I will come right out and admit that I never finished Resident Evil 7. The game was just scary for me, but I plan and go through it now that I have finished this game. Resident Evil Village is the direct sequel of RE7 where you play as Ethan Winters trying to save his daughter Rose that was taken by Mother Miranda. You end up in a strange village full of new evil villains and a bunch of places to explore.

The entire game is played in the first person again, and the game’s settings and scare factor is set right off the bat. You end up in a seemingly abandoned village and eventually you end up running away from Lycans. I don’t want to spoil too much of the story, but giving away details about each area, but I will describe them. You spend a good bit inside the village acquiring your first couple of weapons and learning the layout and controls. As you meet villagers and try and escape the Lycans you end up in Lady Dimitriscu’s castle, one of the only areas that have been shown in great lengths for months leading up to the game’s release. This is where you learn to explore, solve a few puzzles, and understand that the entire game revolves around exploring an area and acquiring a key or item that unlocks the next part. This may involve a mini-boss or onslaughts of enemies. 


Lady D’s castle has her three daughters chasing you and they end up becoming mini-bosses. Lady D stalks you through the castle eventually like Mr. X or Nemesis in previous games. You spend too much time in one room she will come through the door in her 9′ glorious beauty. She’s a fantastic character, as all of them in this game are, but sadly there are only two cut-scenes with her and you don’t get to know her well enough before you finish her off and move on to the next area. There are three more areas that end up being the boss’s lairs. A marsh, a machine factory, and an old mansion. Each area is unique and a blast to explore, but the scare factor in this game is kind of weak. The game gets scary only in certain areas and the good majority of the game is just eerie atmosphere, but not so much creepy. Sadly, a lot of the environment is static and enemies don’t respawn so the game feels tenser in areas especially with a lot of enemies around.

There’s a lot of action in this game and it ramps up as the game moves on. Just like Resident Evil 4, you can expand your cache storage and buy weapons from The Duke. He sets up shop in each area you explore and has a central hub that you eventually get to. There are many weapons to buy with some that are upgraded over others. You buy things with Lei which the majority is acquired by selling crystals and gems and various rare treasures. Large enemies, bosses, and mini-bosses all drop these crystals. You can buy upgrades for weapons as well as parts just like in RE4. Duke has some limited ammo and explosives you can buy, but you can also craft items by finding parts laying around everywhere. This includes crafting ammo, explosives, and health. At some points, you must make every shot count, but I never ran out of ammo completely and got myself into a bad situation. 


One issue I did have with the game is the confusing level design. You have to backtrack a lot and in some areas, I ran around for 20 or more minutes trying to remember my way back to a particular area because I found the key to move on from there. It got frustrating and the machine factory is an absolute chore to navigate. Nothing but endless hallways and dead-end rooms. Once you do find the key or door you need it’s rather satisfying and there’s a constant sense of progression through the whole game. Bosses aren’t very hard, but they just require you to stay on your toes and learn their patterns and you must aim carefully. 

The visuals in RE8 are pretty damn good and they look great on PC. Sadly, the ray-tracing effects are minimal and not worth the halved frame rate even on my RTX 2080 in 1440p. I noticed no difference with it on or off. The lighting looks great and the textures are well detailed and it runs well on any system. However, as I mentioned earlier, the environment is very static and there’s not much interaction or dynamic things to look at. The game is also very linear despite the areas being quite large to explore. It’s just a bunch of twisting hallways and the village isn’t all that big. There are some extra things you can do like shoot all the bobble-head goats, find all the treasures, and defeat optional mini-bosses for treasures, but most people will probably look past all of this. The sound design is amazing with some really creepy sounds both loud and quaint. Being in the large mansion and anticipating something coming around in dead silence was great and Lady D’s castle is haunting. You expect something to come around every corner. 


Resident Evil Village is an evolution of the series mixing RE4‘s gameplay and RE7‘s first-person shooter goodness. I do have to say that Ethan Winters sucks as a character and I hate him. He’s horribly written and I wanted to spend more time with the main villains, but alas, here we are. It’s sad we don’t get to see more of Lady D or anyone else for that matter except when you have short encounters with them in their respected areas. RE8 is a lot more accessible than RE7, and many people will probably finish this game. The difficulty is just right, it looks and sounds good, and it’s just a blast to play through. The scare factor is all over the place, the main areas can be labyrinthine in design, and the extra modes after you finish have varied mileage.

Survival horror is solving puzzles that are complicated. Puzzles that don’t take a few seconds to solve and may not even be solvable until the second or third accts of the game. Keys are not just given to players because they are progressing through a linear path. Most of the keys in this game are just hanging on the wall, or in the corner of an area waiting to be picked up. 

I’m giving Resident Evil 4 a pass here because 1) it was a radically different gameplay style from previous Resident Evil games, and 2) It has elements that even Resident Evil Village does not have. Like melee strikes, knocking over ladders, jumping through windows from second story buildings. Capcom did not even bother to go back to Resident Evil 4 to see what made that game so great. 

The inventory system; Oh boy- by far the worst in the franchise. Just use what you had in Resident Evil 2 Remake Capcom! Why reinvents the wheel? On top of just being difficult to manage, there’s never a point in the game where you have too much stuff. As a huge Resident Evil fan, I expected a lot from Village, and Capcom delivered in some ways yet stumbled in others. All in all, it is a good entry in the main Resident Evil canon and an absolute blast, but it could've been a better game with a few changes.

Resident Evil games tend to lean more toward more classic survival horror (heavy emphasis on puzzle solving and conserving ammo & healing items à la RE1, 2, and 7) or action horror (more emphasis on combat and action set pieces à la RE4, 5, and especially 6), and while Village is a direct sequel to the excellent RE7, it’s also a spiritual successor to RE4. It takes disparate elements from both approaches and puts them together, and though it works in a lot of ways, it misses the mark in others. There are a lot of good, visceral scares here, an atmosphere with a lot of tension & unease, and some great cinematic set pieces, but you rarely have to worry about running out of inventory space as you're constantly finding ammo & healing items and the parts to craft them (none of which take up space in your inventory). This undercuts much of the sense of dread that makes these games work so well. Using RE4's design of finding currency to spend on upgrading weapons & increasing inventory space and the return of a traveling merchant also ensures that running short on ammo, heals, or space will rarely if ever happen. I cannot decide whether this is a quality of life choice or an element that's detrimental to the game's aim - perhaps a bit of both.

The first-person perspective from RE7 returns and works very well here, immersing you in a larger-scale world of horrors. However, where RE7 was cohesive and progressing from one area to the next felt like a natural series of segues (apart from one specific instance), Village feels a bit disconnected. There are separate areas branching out from the main hub (the titular village), each with their own different aesthetic, enemies, and boss fight. There's certainly variety to be found here, but at the cost of disjointedness. The overarching plot helps to better tie things together, but when you have one area that invokes Silent Hill followed by another that invokes Metro Exodus (and one that goes full-out Call Of Duty), your brain is going to notice that. Most notable (and disappointing) was the fact that one of these sections (arguably the best one) was clearly conceived of by Capcom as something much larger and longer but cut very short due to budget and/or time constraints, and the result - while still great - falls short of brilliance due to this and feels like a huge missed opportunity. I also have issues with the writing - the plot gives you very little for a majority of the game only to have a huge, twisty exposition dump arrive in the final hour. Additionally, many of the characters are underdeveloped and merely caricatures who - while well-designed and brimming with personality - are defined solely by their motivation (or worse, simply their appearance) without a fleshed out backstory to make us care enough about them.

I did enjoy the gameplay very much, but I have some issues about it too. The gunplay is very fun & satisfying, but many of Village's big battles don't make you use your brain as much as previous titles in the series have. Most enemies lack specific weaknesses you must discover & exploit and instead just go down by shooting at them repeatedly while evading their attacks. Dodge & melee commands are noticeably absent; the gameplay mechanics are identical to RE7’s, but this game, being much more action-oriented, often has you facing off against waves of enemies. I felt like a dedicated melee command and especially a dodge command would’ve made combat feel much more fluid & dynamic, much in the way the action-oriented RE3 remake had a dodge mechanic that added a lot to its combat.

Regardless of these faults, Village has a lot of both dread and allure. Exploration here is fluid and filled with puzzles (much like most RE games, they’re fun but not very difficult), and the branching hub-based world has a Metroidvania design that keeps you revisiting the titular village and seeing how it changes over the course of the story as you unlock previously inaccessible areas. Returning from the RE2 & 3 remakes is the map design that turns rooms blue once you’ve found everything in them, further reinforcing exploration. After you finish the campaign, Mercenaries (a single player arcade mode) opens up as well as a slew of incentives to replay the campaign apart from simply wanting to (I began a second playthrough immediately after my first ended), including achieving specific tasks to earn completion points with which you can unlock concept art, 3D figurines, and, most importantly, new weapons & infinite ammo. The variety of weapons are very fun, and you can shake up combat by mixing your standard pistol / shotgun / rifle loadout with mines, pipe bombs, a grenade launcher, a sniper rifle, various melee weapons (including an unlockable lightsaber!), and the almighty magnum (of which there are three variations, as there are with most of the gun types here).

Resident Evil Village is a balancing act of action and survival horror that, despite some conspicuous missteps, is a very good game and enjoyable experience overall. It blends varying elements well and does many different things at once competently. There were many moments that made me think “Wow, I can’t wait to replay this so I can experience that again,” and I even found some set pieces so anxiety-inducing that I needed to stop playing and take a breather. I highly recommend this to fans of Resident Evil and survival horror, though I think RE7 and RE4 - the two games it merges - are better. Village is a couple steps shy of being the brilliant blend of action & survival horror it tries to be.

If Resident Evil 8 is your first foray into the series, please be aware that this is a direct sequel to the events of Resident Evil 7. Despite being the 8th numbered title in the series, Capcom has rarely made direct follow ups to each game; for the most part, there are time skips with different protagonists (Resident Evil 6 being the most egregious example of time skips). Upon starting the game, you will be given an option to view, then or later, a video summary of the events prior. I recommend you play 7, or at least watch the summary before starting as your experience will be met with much confusion otherwise. That being said, there will be references to characters and lore from past games that will be lost on you without having played those - and Ethan Winters, your player character, will probably make less sense.

If you're a series regular, you may have had reservations jumping into 7 due to its abstract gameplay and design choices compared to the rest of the series - especially given the fact that Resident Evil: Survivor, the first game in the series to go first-person, was abysmal. Not only do I recommend playing 7, I wholeheartedly recommend playing 8 as it adequately ties together the old lore and adds quality of life to 7's gameplay. Additionally, I cannot properly stress how pretty this game is to look at - if you have the hardware to support it. Even with hardware better than the recommended (I'm running an RTX 2080), don't be surprised if you encounter frame drops when getting attacked by Dimitrescu's daughters or sheltering from Moreau's acid rain; the processing demands spike dramatically in those instances and I can only hope that Capcom has a patch in the works to better optimize the game.

My only other legitimate complaint is that Ethan Winters is a veritable walking Deus Ex Machina - moreso than that Boulder-punching ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥™ on the cover of this game.

Resident Evil: Village is a continuation of the series of Ethan Winters from Resident Evil 7: Biohazard so if you like RE7 it will be highly likely for you to enjoy this game. In order to get the most out of this game i recommend that you play RE7 before jumping in. 
RE: Village is a great blend of Survival Horror and Action, its like the modern first person child of RE4. The game expands upon RE7 by adding more action, more boss fights and more varied areas. 

As an avid fan of Resident Evil franchise i enjoyed my time with Village, the game starts in a very creepy chaotic snowy village with amazing view of the Castle, the game looks amazing, Art Direction is top notch, inside the castle and outside, the details are super gorgeous to look at and appreciate, you can see the beautiful architecture inside the castle, i wasted a couple of minutes in every room just looking at those details. Same with the second section, after that though it takes a small drop as usual with the series, the first areas reign supreme. 

The Sound design and the Soundtrack itself is fantastic, the Duke music in particular is a pleasure to the ears, its very atmospheric and mysterious, suits the character very well. The music does a good job with chase sections, horror sections and action sections. The sound design was also pretty good. Shooting and fighting effects improved from RE7. 

The Atmosphere and Scare Factor takes a seat compared to 7, the game is less scary overall but surprisingly it managed to craft the scariest section in all RE games to date with the notorious Baby/Fetus. (No Spoilers) See for yourself. However it has to be noted again that the game is less scary due to its more focus on action gameplay and boss fights. 

The Gameplay is still Resident Evil style at its core, its closer to RE4 (except in first person) than to classic RE1-2-3. The puzzles are good, the gunplay is good, the level design is good, there is very little tedious backtracking or inventory management and more focus on fighting and exploration, its in a way kind of semi open map, you can find areas and find loot that will help you, solve puzzles and open paths. Boss fights are decent, they could have been better especially Lady D. But i appreciate the variety in this one, compared to lets say RE3 or RE7 where you basically fight the same stalker/boss all the game. 

Characters are interesting, its not news that Lady D and her daughters created such a buzz around the gaming community and the internet due to their character designs and personality, its a shame their screen time was very little and i hope we get more of them in a DLC in the future, the models look fantastic as usual with Capcom (Great Job! Best in the Business). and Oh boy, Sir Chris Redfield is back! 

Story is my biggest issue, while by the end they explained a lot of the threads created earlier, the story still feels like the weakest link in this one, its so over the top but its kind of expected, I still think they could've nailed it much better on the story had they slowed it a bit down with all the over the top villain unnecessary pose and talk, and the plot armor even if it was explained. Usually this is what happens when action takes over, the story suffers a bit from it. Its entertaining as an action horror flick but dont think too much about its writing. 

Replay value is decent due to the amount of unlockable weapons and difficulty, it could be higher if there was different paths to the game itself which could lead to another interesting ending, kind of similar to RE2 Remake with Scenario A and B and true ending, but nevertheless the replay value is still there due to the amount of cool weapons you can unlock. And ofcourse soon with the E3 Capcom may announce some DLCs. 

Overall: Resident Evil Village is a very good game and if you like Resident Evil franchise in general you owe it to yourself to give this one a try, its a very good game and an enjoyable blend of Action and Survival Horror.

TLDR: Resident Evil: Village is a first person survival horror game. It's really good, dumb fun.

  Ethan Winters and his family and his hands have been through hell and back, but finally he and his family and his hands have escaped the creepy Louisiana location the previous game is set in to find peace and happiness in some not at all creepy, non-specified (but heavily Transylvanian-tinged) Eastern European location. But dumb things are afoot, my friend, and soon Ethan Winters and his hands are fighting for their life and family again. You may already know this: things do not go well for his hands.

 Resident Evil games have never had any use for subtlety, and Ethan's poor hands are a prime example of that. Because they're front and center in the game's first-person camera view, the horrors visited on them really are something else; The amount of punishment has been rightly celebrated/ridiculed everywhere in the internet, so I won't go into any more detail except to say that at one point one of them is sliced clean off, only to be glued back with a magic potion that also repairs the cut jacket sleeve. Hold that image, we'll come back to it later.

 The game itself is basically a first-person shooter with an emphasis on exploring suitably spooky places and shooting monsters in the face while conserving ammo. And I'll say it now, the exploration is GLORIOUS. The locations are gorgeous, varied and complex, with lots of secrets, shortcuts and surprises... and there's an in-game map that tracks which places have been cleaned out and which ones you might want to revisit later. Other than a nasty tendency to block out areas so you can’t return to them, this is easily the best thing in a good game. Shooting is good, if a bit unwieldy (do yourself a favour and play with mouse and keyboard,) and there are several ways to upgrade your arsenal and yourself. The usual set of features.

 Where the game doesn’t do that well is in the horror department, but that’s to be expected; the genre is survival horror, after all, not horror, and it’s hard to be scared when you have effective weapons and magical severed-hand reattaching potions. Like most action horror, it's more about the grim fun of creative gore, or straight-on action spectacle. And it gets more action-y as it goes along.
Scares consist mostly of jump scares and tension over low ammo reserves. There’s an excellent part where your weapons are removed, but it’s (kinda) ruined when the game goes all Charles Band. YOU NEVER GO FULL CHARLES BAND.
 
 And that’s another thing about the game: it is dumb. Unabashedly dumb. Extremely goofy and dumb, but never overtly self-awarely dumb. This is no surprise – the Resident Evil series has been stupid from day one, but there was a while during the 7th game, before its madness really kicked in, where along with the perspective change it seemed to be positioning itself to be a bit more serious, more ‘proper horror’, but Resident Evil Village basically says 'Ehhh… nah, screw that' pretty much from the outset. The villains are over the top, their plans face-palmingly stupid, the game’s whole story is basically an [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiot_plot] idiot plot [/url] (one of the characters says as much later on). And I may be being too kind to this venerable and venerably stupid game series, but this time out it feels like it’s in on the joke, kinda; smartly designed dumb fun, and without too much nudging to show that it’s in on said fun. That severed hand, with its severed sleeve, just glued back on? All good. All good.
 Welcome back to the top tier of dumb video games, Resident Evil. Gears of War, Call of Duty, and the rest of the gang have missed you.

Wow... I was not amazed by Resident Evil Village. Unlike RE2 Remake or even RE1 Remake on Gamecube, I have no desire to go back for a second playthrough and I know some people will say if a Resident Evil is good by speedrunning standards. For speedruns, you need good level design and chances to deviate from the typical progression path. I'm no speedrunner, but I'm someone who went through Zero Mission in the past and I can always appreciate a title with good, tight level design and interesting enemy variety to compliment the areas. RE8 falls short which is unfortunate.

I've yet to pinpoint if I was feeling some dread at any point since I could carry so many weapons, ammo and all key items, crafting components and basic stuff had their separate sections. Village is such a departure from what made RE7, RE2 Remake, RE1 Remake and make me appreciate RE3 Remake a little more even though the game was a disrespect to the design philosophy of its predecessors.

Village is exactly what happens when you get carried by marketing and listen to the wrong people. Sure, RE7 was scary, but it was helped by the VR component. Key items for exploration had to be found and took a slot in the main inventory. The Baker were well-established in the introduction as well. All of that is thrown away in RE8 which is a shame, because the game functions and plays well. It brings nothing new mechanically since every new element is a throwback to Resident Evil 4 from the survival segment in the opening sequence to the merchant, the inventory as well as the setting in Europe.

The writing is taking a nosedive since Ethan Winters keeps stating the obvious as well as asking too many questions when the answer is straight in front of him. "What the hell" is becoming the new "Long time no see" and you never want to be compared to Sonic the Hedgehog in terms of writing. Yes, this game's writing is Sonic-level bad. The guy is presented as your everyday joe but is capable of carrying 4-5 guns at a time, changes them in his inventory in a pause menu, quick switches like the Doom Slayer and we must take his reactions seriously? Wow...

Castle Dimitrescu was a terrible section due to the false sense of exploration and how easy it was to just run away from Alcina, except once when I was going down with the elevator: she just happened to appear without prior notice (this is a reason why T-00 worked so well in RE2, by the way). Heisenberg Factory was exactly what I expected from the game with tight corridors, strong level design involving the foundry area and a clear objective. This was, for me, the game at its best and I applaud Capcom for this section.

The rest was either irrelevant or just boring. That includes a terrible platforming segment. Oh and Alcina's design was pushed so much by the marketing campaign that she wasn't that special anymore to me as soon as she was introduced which is a shame because anybody would fall for her, whether you are male, female, transgender, any color of skin, etc. She's no Tyrant in mechanics and she clearly has no subtlety in the likes of a creature from the Resident Evil Remake that I actually appreciated in design. It wasn't helped by fans since they cosplayed the crap out of her even before we knew her role in the game which is proof of strong marketing... but to me, this is deceptive marketing.

I can only appreciate her voice actress being as over-the-top as she can be, [spoiler]but Alcina is indeed pointless to the main story since you learn she is just used as a potential vessel for Miranda's reborn daughter instead of having her own agency like Karl Heisenberg who is also a potential vessel. Donna Beneviento's section was a facade and the segment with the Baby was some inconsequential body horror that worked, but your weapons are gone until you destroy Angie. Salvatore Moreau was a bad attempt at redoing Ramon Salazaar. How bad? Moreau keeps victimising himself instead of being a threat. Since he's deceptive, there's no sympathy to be had for this guy. Oh and Mother Miranda being linked to one of the core antagonists of the series prior to the events of Resident Evil Zero is a terrible attempt at rewriting the story. For me, there's nothing before Zero except the very origins of Umbrella and what led to the unfortunate abomination that is Lisa Trevor.[/spoiler]

For me, the biggest sin is how modern this game feels in terms of writing, tension, dread and in player agency which make sense because the writer collaborated on Dead Space and this is a shock because Dead Space is a better game. Despite the presence of typewriters, there are no ink ribbons making the failure state inconsequential except for being annoying. RE8 is more afraid of itself than you being afraid of the game.

Disclaimer: A Review from a total Newbie to the franchise.
I never played any of the other Resident Evil Games, I only watched a bit of RE7 Gameplay and thought it looks great. I never got around to play it myself though.
So when this game was announced back then, I was immediately in love with the setting. "A small Village in the ice-cold mountains haunted by a virus? Hell yeah!" So I was always up to date with it. Played every demo and watched every trailer. 

In short: the overall game is great. For people that didn't play the other games, like me, have the option to catch up with a little flashback cutscene. The graphics are stunning with beautiful designs in all places. Like the Castle, one of the first places you'll end up in, is just so visually impressive with all of the details, but it still has this kind of eeriness about it, making it a frightfully perfect design/place.
The Horror aspect, which is probably most important actually, is not to be underestimated. The game emphasizes the atmosphere greatly. It's not just like most horror games that you run from one jumpscare to another. The scariest things in this game, is what the atmosphere makes your head think... And a certain basement in a certain house.

To mention something negative about the game: The second half of the game can be tiring, because the first half is heavily focused on the horror, whilst the second half is rather action packed with a lot of shooting and less "helplessness" in situations. Of course, as I've heard, this is for people that love the old RE games more than the newer one's, since those are a lot more focused on the shooter aspect as I've heard. So, the second part can be fun, but it's probably letting down a lot of people a bit. 
Nonetheless, the story really saves this. It really pulls you into the character of Ethan Winters and their anger. Being brought to this Village of Shadows and needing to save the innocent daughter from these monstrosities of people.

In conclusion: It's a great game overall, but there are stronger and weaker parts of it. It depends on the individual which scenes please you more than others, but this helps the game being more accessible to all kinds of players. But it's far from perfectly balanced about these aspects. Still a must-play in my opinion.

Played through every difficulty now, and I must stay this game is a masterpiece. 11/10

Gameplay: 7.5 / 10
The game is amazing It's like 4 horror games in one. First part with Lady D and her daughters is like Amnesia, scary navigation through a giant castle. Second part with Donna is a first person psychological horror, just like P.T. Third part I'm not exactly sure what it fits in  but I guess it's kinda like Bioshock (Never played it so I'm just assuming from what I understand about that game.) And the last part with Heisenberg is in a steampunk action horror style type of game.

Story: 6 / 10
I mean I kinda get the story, but to be honest, it all felt like a big ass Jigsaw puzzle. Go through different areas and collect a flask at the end of each one, then combine them and get your daughter back, that's kinda it. Sucks that we didn't get an option to side with Heisenberg though, hopefully that comes as a DLC someday.

Graphics: 10 / 10
Graphics are amazing as per usual with the RE engine and RE games, some things that sucks was the bugs from the daughters which has caused frame drops to everyone I've seen playing the game.

Music: 10 / 10
The soundtrack was stellar, especially towards the last hour of the game, starting at the battle with Heisenberg. Everything after that was epic or heartfelt sounding. And in my opinion the safe room music in the castle is my favorite safe room music of the entire franchise.

Voice Acting: 8 / 10
The game had very solid voice acting, but some of it felt very forced, particularly from Ethan and Mia, but the worst part of the voice acting is Ethans one liners, they are straight up solid radioactive cringeium. However fricking CHRIS, DUKE and HEISENBERG, their voice actors did an AMAZING job, Heisenberg's voice in particular is one of the coolest voices I've heard in a video game in the past 6 years or so. He did an amazing job a well deserved 11/10 to him. Other good voice actors were Angie, Monroue, Miranda, Chris's squad... actually everyone did an amazing job, I can't find any flaws other than the sometimes cringey Ethan one liners, and ~3 times where the way some conversations were being spoken didn't fit the situation they were in.

Scaryness: 5 / 10
Game honestly isn't that scary It's more of an action horror than straight up horror, which I'm okay with. The truly scary part was the Donna Beneviento house, which like I said played out like P.T.  With Donna takes away all your guns puts you in a position of weakness and defenselessness. And then the baby, true horror nightmare fuel. And then those butt clenching moments when it's coming up to the elevator and you're waiting for the door to close. Other than that, there are a few jump scares, including when the daughters appear out of nowhere in the castle.

Bugs: 8 / 10
There are honestly not a lot of bugs, I noticed in the first week there were a lot of them, for example Lady D's AI standing still for 4 seconds then starting the hunt. And when Monroe knocks you into the water you get thrown there very unrealistically instead of teleporting once you fall in the water. But I guess they aren't really bugs, just moments that felt weird and immersion ruining. And I found maybe 5 other bugs while watching YouTube videos of the game, but I can't remember what they were so they probably patched them or they were hard to create.

Ending: 11 / 10
The ending was amazing, the battle with Heisenberg, Miranda killing Ethan, then finding out she was the old lady, getting to play as Chris, finding the real Mia, finding out Ethan died in RE7 and is just mold, him coming back to life in Duke's carriage, Ethan's fight with Miranda, when he sacrifices himself to save rose and everyone on the helicopter, Chris finding out BSAA Europe sent bioweapon's instead of soldiers, and then finally the ending with rose going to Ethans grave and being driven away by what I think is someone that works with Chris. A person coming up to the car far away in the background and the car stopping, and where went to the car with a freecam mode and found out it was Chris standing at the car (however it was probably just a placeholder) And then the father's story being done. It was all just the best ending ever.

Overall: 8.2 / 10
Some people will just complain because they have a hate boner for Ethan and the game is centered around him, but I honestly don't care, game is worth every single penny.

The plot is incredibly well written, self-aware of any issues and is what is honestly the perfect sequel to the previous game, Resident Evil 7. Definitely watch a walkthrough of/buy and play Resident Evil 7: Biohazard first, it'll make a lot more sense.

It's always hard to follow up a masterpiece. It's probably why Valve just doesn't really make games anymore or why they start and stop production on games if anyone on the development team so much as gets a whiff of excrement. The RE developers bottled lightning twice with 7 and then with the ReTWOmake, but they stumbled a bit with the ReTHREEmake; a good game, but not AS good. Here with "th evil age" we see the developers again try to reach for the gold, delivering an excellent game, a truly great game, hitting the best of the previous expectations they set, but not keeping it there from start to finish. 

The Village continues the unfortunate tale of Ethan Winters and his ridiculously crappy family life. It's pretty well known at this point that the entire plot is premised upon a sizeable "GOTCHA!" moment from the opening onward, and you, didn't get the memo because there never was one. But whatever, you're not here for the great plot, you're here for the great scares and seething chills. The game starts off delivering terror in buckets and droves, including some of the most memorable fears in the series yet--dollhouse, but then somewhere after the half way point, the fear and loathing switches to running and gunning. The change is so abrupt that it feels almost like a DLC tacked on at the end or an entirely new game all together. I was really enjoying the pace and dreadful horror of the earlier part of the game. It's what I loved best about RE2 and 7, this tense uncomfortable feeling of unknown dread--your resources are finite and limited and death is awaiting you around the very next corner. After the first half of the game spent in the fetal position, the pace picks up greatly and so does the amount of resources they throw at you. At one point, I was literally selling bullets to buy other things, because I had so many. Square that with the only three magnum rounds you get in the entire RE7 game. Zombies, Werewolves and Vampires, nothing is really as scary with an auto-rifle and a full metal jacket. On the plus side, it is a long game. The longest since RE4 actually, and while it claims I played thrice for only 28 hours, Steam says otherwise at 47 hours, and that feels more accurate to me. So thumbs up for value. To be clear, I really love the game and respect it's contention for GOTY, but I just wanted the whole game to be like dollhouse. 

The best way to play the game for maximum pants crapping is the Village of Shadows difficulty. You need to NG+ it, but it really made the experience a lot more enjoyable for me as a whole, because it completely eliminated my nagging complaints about pacing above. On this difficulty, even the assault rifle can't help you. The meekest of enemies will laugh off several explosions from your infinite grenade launcher and you can expect to employ a volley needed to take down an aircraft carrier against your "slightly" more challenging foes. So in a word, "Yasssss!"

I liked Resident Evil Village, but I can't say it's a step forward for RE. If Village was a Fallout game, I would call it Fallout 4. Village has very good graphics, above average to even fun combat and exploration, and plays like a modern game (some may find 60 FOV annoying, but there are mods for that). However, 3 things that really turned me off were the walking sequences, mediocre story, and a lack of variety plague the game. 
     Firstly, the game uses the 1st person pov in what I would call gimmicky cinematic walking/running sequences that really suck after the first play through. It really ruins the pace of the game and takes away from the immersion by trying to be too immersive. Second, in terms of story, it has the same kind of cheesy writing that you expect, but it doesn't deliver with any of the charm of previous games. It feels like it's trying to take itself seriously, but it falls very short of what it is trying to achieve. Lastly, I think that the game feels very bland, with all puzzles taking the same level of brain power (none) and combat encounters feeling very similar because there is a slight lack in enemy diversity. I liked the combat, taking down enemies and shooting the weapons all felt satisfying, but none of the situations they put you into were very memorable. 
     TL;DR Pick this game up on sale, whether you are an RE fan or curious. We don't know how good Re:verse will be, but hopefully it is average.

     Obviously this is my personal opinion and I'm not gonna hate on anyone for enjoying it. Okay, look. I wanted to enjoy this- and I did..for the first "act". The first part of the game is very intense, suspenseful, and has a decent amount of horror elements. Everything building up to and including Castle Dimitrescu are pretty great..but that's about where it stopped for me. The rest of the children of Miranda just didn't feel very fleshed out. To me it really seemed like so much of the work was put into Castle D and the rest was an afterthought.

    Beneviento was a chore and while it did have some decent horror elements it didn't make up for how slow paced it was. I was really expecting more with the big ol' fetus but just running around from it was neither fun nor suspenseful. You finish Beneviento's "act" so quickly you're left wondering why she held any significance at all- and Moreau faired similarly. His character has such little development besides "he's pathetic". That's it. He wanted Miranda to favor him, but nobody likes him. Then he turns into Fishman and blow him up. All this can be done in a little over an hour. I tried to take my time with the game and explore as much as possible, especially given the fact that the map will flat out tell you if you missed anything, but eventually I just wanted to move on and see if things improved.

   After Moreau is where things really just became frustrating to me. It felt like they wanted to add game length by throwing wave after wave of lycans at you. There were points where it felt like I was spending 20 minutes or so just in the same room while the same lycans spawned over and over. It wasn't fun. It was an ammo- dump, and felt more like I was playing CoD Zombies than an RE game. Heisenburg seemed to have more effort done into his character, but dragging myself through his factory was so infuriating at times. The enemy designs for this area were very silly too. Take the shambling "zombies" you've seen a million times but slap metal on their face/body. Ta da! 

  I think I've spent enough on the story and this review in general. The Duke was an interesting character but like the Merchant from RE4 his character is a mystery- which is totally fine. Shout out to Saul Moldman Winters and his moldy hands that Capcom apparently hates. He's a damn loser. The dialogue is hilariously cringey at times but that's to be expected with RE games. I'm sure this will piss people off but again, this is just my opinion. I don't think it's necessarily a BAD game, but so much of it felt underwhelming and not thought through that I personally wouldn't recommend it at $60. You may now commence the hate.

The latest entry in the RE franchise is a weird one, where it feels as if the devs tried to make two games in one. I'll say right from the beginning that I did enjoy the game, short as it was (beat in 10 hours on hardcore with additional exploring). I just think there are some bizarre pacing issues and a surprising lack of real horror for a series that built its reputation on it. 

The game has an interesting gauntlet style story, where you take on a series of bosses as you move through the stories as Ethan Winters once again. Unfortunately, the now famous Lady D is the only one with any real substance, thanks in large part to all the marketing that was based around her; as well as the Hunt Showdown reject boss Heisenberg. Aside from them, the other bosses all feel half-assed and forgettable.

While the actual plot of the game is an interesting attempt to link together the entire saga, the actual dialogue and some of the voice acting is mediocre at best. There are a number of decisions made by the characters that will leave you scratching your head. 

The gunplay itself is largely the same as RE7, so take that for what it's worth. However, it is very clear that the devs put a much greater focus on providing faster paced combat, to the detriment of the horror and survival elements of the game, which are honestly almost completely absent here. The game has it's moments and is by no means bad, but for hardcore RE fans who prefer the tension of the classic games and to a certain extent RE7, Village will leave you disappointed and wondering what the devs will choose to focus on moving forward. I think newer players to the series will definitely feel a greater sense of enjoyment for a game that is definitely intended for a wider audience than in previous entries.

This was the first Resident Evil I ever played, while I know the series since its origins, at the time of the first RE I was playing "Alone in the Dark" another survival horror series which is in fact older than Resident Evil...

While Resident evil was more to do with Viruses and Bioweapons, Alone in the Dark had more to do with HP Lovecraft and Cosmic Horror... at least on the first 3, then it tried to resemble other survival games and I lost interest in it.

Resident evil was not appealing to me while still being a good game and good at what it wants to be.
Come 2021, Resident Evil Village, and yeah, besides your truly lovely Lady "D" what also appealed to me about this one was the new setting, mainly the vampiric castle, the architecture, the mood the light and the darkness, but also the eastern European village, the strange characters and also its first person perspective which could be interesting (for this game).

All this I found in spades, and while Castle Dimistrescu is a good portion of the game (one of the main things for sure) it’s far from being all of it. In fact, there’s much more. From the beginning its clear what the main zones for the game will be, one of them being the Village, which comes and go between the other main levels, but this Village is very well done, and I enjoyed discovering new unexplored places across my playthrough.

The best thing about Village is how it introduces you to its characters, and by characters I don't mean only "The enemies" which will be the main boss fights for sure, but the other characters: The places you explore. Castle Dimitrescu, The Village which gives this Resident Evil its name, and also a couple of more places which I won't say to maintain the surprise. Each setting has its own strong mood, and each level doesn’t let you in all at once, but you have quiet places, silence and then.... well, you have to play to find out!

The game is not hurried in showing you its face, first, it lets you wait, and think, and ask you "What the hell is going on?" by not showing you all at once, it makes it so much better. At least on the first half of the game, Village is so moody, and also has smart amusing puzzles (along with the shooting of course, but all in moderate measure). This combo of shooting some enemies and solving puzzles and exploring some more, reminded me a little to the old Alone in the Darks, the good ones, but in this case it’s not HP Lovecraft, but Vampirism, Lycans, Strange experiments, some steam punk horror and... all mixed with a good dose of Resident Evil..ism.

Now, the game still is, very much a Resident Evil game, and has its weapons, modding, upgrades and inventory management, and this is also a fun part of it and a very addicting one. This become especially relevant on the second half, which features more shooting and more action. This is not bad, in fact even during its first half, the game tries different genres and settings and it all works very well. 
Maybe the second part by contrast has a more sharp hard turn towards action and shooting enemies, so while still good I very much preferred the first part with its strong mood, dense atmosphere and slow build ups.

Finally, the game has a New game + which lets you not only continue upgrading your existing weapons, but also get some new ones, and try different playthroughs. The game is very fun to play so you'll probably end up replaying it once or twice, and (re)experiencing also some of the best moments it has.
The story on the other hand, even coming with low expectations... it's half of the time a little corny and the other half total nonsense (even with some of the explanations its throws at you) but again... I wasn't expecting a lot...it didn't matter really... and it didn't stop me from just enjoying the game from what it is, a really well designed and enjoyable survival horror adventure.

Overall, Village is a fun game that I sunk a bunch of hours into, but it just doesn't match the other greats in the series. Village constantly begs to be compared to other games as well. It starts off in a small European village like RE4. The structure of the game is very similar RE7. It's first person, and it's got family members that are the different acts of the game that play out in distinct ways. However, the problem is that each time Village is compared to the other games it mimics, it always compares unfavorably to those past greats.  

The beginning of the story starts off slowly. The first maybe 20 minutes of the game there is nothing going on. This is where the first unfavorable comparison is. RE7 started immediately tense and creepy entering the Baker mansion with a chilling, foreboding Texas Chainsaw Massacre vibe that had me immediately on edge. 

Village starts off by rummaging through some trashed houses with monsters quickly darting in and out of view. Then the village inhabitants all start attacking. This is where the next unfavorable comparison occurs; this time to RE4. When RE4 villagers attack, there is a sack-headed psycho with a chainsaw that breaks down the door of the house you're barricaded in and will decapitate you asap! In Village, especially starting on the regular difficulty (as most people will experience), the werewolves will just stand around  looking at you and then kind of deciding maybe to attack if they feel like it. There was no sense of urgency that I was about to die if I didn't act fast. 

After the attack, there are some boring exposition cut-scene-heavy parts that have Ethan driving a truck,  like a nod to the first fight with Jack Baker in RE7. Once again, though, this is just a reminder of a much better sequence in RE7 and how this isn't as good. The failing to measure up to RE7 happens during each section of the game. On that note, the boss battles are terrible across the board in Village. There's nothing here that wasn't already tired a decade ago. Often times they were just running around a small confined area alternating between taking shots and hoping to avoid attacks. The most tense part of the game was during a sequence when I had to sneak my way around part of the village while a gigantic wolf was stalking me. 

The different sections of the game did have some variety to them and were generally decent. The industrial section near the end is easily the best section. The HDR really shines through in this part giving a spooky atmosphere. The game does look pretty darn good generally and ran smoothly on my rig. 

There are some decent exploration puzzles in the actual village part of the game that took some time to figure out how to get to places. Throughout the game there are secrets off the beaten path that reward astute explorers. 

Village does some actual typical puzzles that were a complete joke. They seem really dumbed down from previous games. The lowest of the low was the piano puzzle where you just need to mash keys until you hit the right note and repeat until all the notes on the music sheet were struck. 

The general combat in RE8 is well done. The guns are fun to shoot. There is a decent variety to the types of enemies. The inventory works a lot like in RE4. There is a merchant who will sell you all the things you need including ammo, magic med tonic, weapons, and weapons upgrades. As in previous RE games, there are excellent weapons to unlock (with unlimited ammo) that will keep the momentum going to get them so you play through the game with over powered artillery that are really fun to mow down the enemies you cowered from on earlier play throughs. Unlocking one will make it easier to unlock the next most powerful weapon and so forth. 

Another really fun as always feature is Mercenaries. It's basically the same as it's always been (excellent fun!) with some unique flavor to it. I'm still early into it, but it's a challenging good time. 

As of posting this review, I've played it for approximately 45 hours and beaten the campaign three times, including on the Book of Shadows (hardest) difficulty. So, it's a fun game that I did enjoy. It's just plain not as good as the other RE games that it's clearly trying to invoke, though.

I found that Village was Resident Evil coming a bit back to it's creepy/fantastical mid-franchise roots. 

The fairy tale-esque setting played really well into this one, it gave the series a bit more of what it was missing from RE7, although RE7 was a fantastic survival horror of it's own. The cast of antagonists in Village felt noticeably more unique and fun to learn about. 

The biggest thing for me with Village was it's pacing. It felt like there was no real bad downtime in between bosses/areas. In Castle Dimitrescu you're back to a familiar "chase" type bosses, with Dimitrescu and her Daughters, similar to the Mr. X/Nemesis bosses we face in the remakes. With House Beneviento we get a more Outlast style horror segment, then onto a couple more action oriented boss fights and areas.

The biggest grievance I can find with Village is that it really does feel as if the difficulty was butchered more, I was fortunate enough to play my first playthrough on Hard and it felt like a decent balance of things, but I can't help thinking that the Hard difficulty should have been what Normal was supposed to be, or at least somewhere in between. A few friends who had played from normal told me about how easy the game felt. It's not a deal breaker for me but it felt odd, and I would only suggest most people looking for a decent challenge attempt from Hard on a new game.

Overall, Village had my attention from start to finish and I never felt a moment that took me out of the fun. Hopeful on some good quality DLC like RE7 was given, and if not will be patiently waiting for the next installment.

Introduction:

Overall, my experience with Resident Evil Village was a positive one. After being disappointed with the RE3 Remake, I was cautiously optimistic about this one (that, and I was curious to see what all of the Lady Dimitrescu memes were about). Resident Evil Village did not disappoint for the most part as it has a great story, (mostly) great level design, and decent gameplay.

Story and Gameplay Discussion (Spoilers):

The game overall has some great level design, but it has one level that I was definitely not a fan of, more on that later. For starters, the first and my personal favorite was Castle Dimitrescu. This level does a great job of setting up the base mechanics of the game and giving a great introduction into what the game is about. Also, Lady Dimitrescu is one of my favorite characters in the game, and it is not because of the memes. She and her daughters have very interesting backstories and personalities, and she is just a really fun character overall. My only complaint is that this level is too short. This is a recurring issue that I found with all of the other sections throughout the game, except for one, more on that in a second.

After longing for more of the first level, we move onto House Beneviento. Another issue that I have is how linear Resident Evil Village is. I know that Resident Evil as a whole is a linear game franchise, but I feel like this game could have taken a few liberties with Village and gave us a bit more of an open environment. Anyway, House Beneviento is another fairly decent section of the game. Being chased by the demon baby was one of the most tense experiences I've had from a game, and I like it. This section gave me a lot of Silent Hill vibes. Sadly, this section of the game does fall on its face at the end with the last encounter with Donna Beneviento and Angie. I'm almost hesitant to call it a boss fight as all you do is chase Angie around the house while all of the other dolls in the house proceed to do next to nothing. The only way that you can actually get attacked is if you stand in one spot for several seconds, so there wasn't a lot of tension during this encounter. Overall, a good section of the game with a slightly disappointing ending. Unfortunately, the next section of the game is worse.

After that, we go to my least favorite part of the game, Moreau's Reservoir. This section of the game was incredibly annoying and I did not care for Moreau as a character. While Donna Beneviento might have been a bland character, Moreau is incredibly one dimensional. His entire personality solely revolves around "Please notice me Mother Miranda." Also, this whole section of the game is filled with annoyance. There were many instances where I died in this part where I thought that I was safe, only to get smacked into the water and get killed instantly. Then there is the boss fight with Moreau. Moreau has a lot of really cheap attacks, including where he spams his acid breath every few seconds. I would run away to heal myself and then turn around to fight him again only to take more damage as he was charging me, rinse and repeat. This section is a prime example of why I don't like water levels.

Once that misery is over, the game picks up with my second favorite section of the game, Heisenberg's factory, but first we have to fight Urias. Urias is a giant Lycan that has been chasing you throughout the game, but when you actually fight him he is actually a really easy boss, especially if you have the Wolfsbane Magnum. After dropping Urias, he go to the factory to face Heisenberg. This level is actually a lot of fun. I really like the industrial environment that we are in and the enemy designs here. I also really like Heisenberg as a character. His backstory made me feel kinda bad for him, but he still had moments that remind us that he is evil. The boss fight against Heisenberg is a lot of fun too. He basically turns himself into a transformer and you fight him with a tank, which is a phenomenal section of the game, but there is some dialogue that raises some questions. [spoiler]He does mention Chris Redfield's boulder punching moment from Resident Evil 5, which raises a question. How does he know about Chris punching a boulder?[/spoiler]

Finally, that brings us to the end of the game. Mother Miranda is the hardest boss in the game if you don't count the optional bosses at House Beneviento and at the Citadel that were ripped straight from Dark Souls. Honestly, I have a fairly neutral opinion on Mother Miranda, as she does not have a lot of screen time. The first section of the final part of the game was really bizarre. You first play as Chris Redfield as the game turns into Call of Duty. This was a really jarring change, and I don't think it belongs in this game. Thankfully it doesn't last long and the game goes back to being Resident Evil during Ethan's final fight with Miranda. This was a great way to end the game and I was nearly brought to tears when [spoiler]Ethan sacrificed to save his family, great end for the character [/spoiler]

Final Thoughts (Spoiler Free):

Resident Evil Village is a great game, but it has a couple of flaws that taint the experience a little bit. TLDR: Good but not great.

Normal is too easy, especially for a veteran player. I found myself never running out of ammo or healing items, only ever being slightly inconvenienced or annoyed. Hardcore setting levels out the difficulty for a much more tense and enjoyable experience. 

I am not puzzle savvy, but I can only recall one or two puzzles that stopped me for a minute. More often than not, the game doesn't trust the player's intelligence and tends to have hand holding 'puzzles' where the solution is within arm’s reach or spelled out for them. No need to piece solutions together. IE – ‘Here is the combination, now open the lock.’

Combat with weapons feels the same against enemies, however enemies tend to embrace grabbing you more often, which can lock you for 3-5 seconds in a pseudo-helpless state with no built-in escape mechanic. This gets old quickly. There is a new block-counter push mechanic that is supposed to help with swarms of enemies, but it is difficult to perform effectively. I do not think I succeeded in pulling it off until my second campaign where I did it by accident.

This game relies on the spectacle of the first play though but suffers heavily on repeat campaigns. The atmosphere and combat become tedious and repetitive, and I do not think I have ever seen ‘the door is locked from the other side’ this much in any other Resident Evil.

A lot of concepts are teased and dabbled in but are not thoroughly fleshed out. The vampires and lycens are barely explored, certain boss fights feel anti-climactic, two of the four main houses in the game feel rushed, and some dialogue choices seem out of place even for Resident Evil.

My suspension of disbelief was often interrupted in this game with certain sections arbitrarily being locked off due to the player being unable to traverse terrain unless it is interactable. (example not being able to climb over a tractor blocking the road.) Also, enemies in cutscenes have the 90s villain syndrome of being able to kill you while you are in their grasp, but they opt to chuck you to safety instead. 

The more you play through this game, the more you think some things were either added in last minute or partially left out due to lack of time, and I do not know which is worse.

The game is very forgiving with difficulty; No matter how hard you make the game’s difficulty, saves do not become scarcer, and healing items and ammo supplied throughout the game are not diminished. Unlimited ammo is easily unlockable making 'Village of Shadows' a breeze.

Speaking of which, the highest difficulty is catered toward NG + items, meaning if you try like I did to take your knowledge and experience of the game into the 'Village of Shadows' difficulty with a clean slate, you will be wondering why the basic enemies seem insurmountable as they bullet sponge your entire arsenal. Do not be a hero and just get your unlockables.

The graphics are the only thing that hold up with repeat play throughs, boasting some of the best I have seen, but that is all I have to say about it is praises. My expectations going into this experience were neutral, however the game feels disappointing even then. This game is worth a play or two, but nothing more. It is average, about a (6/10) score. Unless you are a die-hard RE fan, I cannot recommend this game to you.

RE7 surprised alot of people after the cluster that was RE6, going back to its roots and creating a true survival horror game as its predecessors once were. It had its silly moments and such, but it was still a solid and all around fun game. RE8 takes what already made the seventh entry great and improves upon it.

The story is its three years after the events of RE7. You're living with your wife once again and you've given birth to a beautiful baby girl. However, things turn south when Chris Redfield, the longtime hero of the series, makes a malicious return with his actions leaving you in a remote, unknown village with your daughter stripped of you. Barely armed and severely outmatched by the locals, you march forward to uncover the mystery of this village while saving your daughter

Graphics wise the game doesn't disappoint at all. The game looks beautiful from the glimmering sunrises to the foreign feeling cottages to the layouts of the various strongholds to the grotesqueness of the models. Each and every environment and model is treated with love and care and it truly shines through the RE Engine.

Gameplay wise is also a romp and a half. The game takes more of an action based stance compared to it predecessor and it has a fun time doing it as well. It feels great to defeat a group of bullet sponge lycans, servants, etc while barely surviving through the conflict, especially on the hard difficulties. Speaking of enemies, they up the variety of enemies in this game, which is a welcome addition. Granted there isnt a huge variety, but its better than the single mold monsters you would see. Puzzles in the game are relatively simple but also never waste your time helping you get to the next areas sooner rather than later. The bosses of the game also each have their own unique way of scaring the piss out of you, whether it be Demitrescu's sharp claws, Moreau's grotesque fish, Heisenberg's monstrous machines, or even Beneviento's horrifying experience that I dare not spoil, but you know what it is (Hint: I have a new found fear for babies)

Progression also feels very satisfying in the game as well. You start out helplessly with a knife, but as you explore more and talk to your good friend The Duke (easily the best character in the game) with his wares and upgrades, Ethan will go from a helpless hack to a fully armed Umbrella Corp-like soldier. Granted the game doesn't always make it easy to find certain items since you have to be in an exact position in order to pick up items. This can lead to some slight frustration for completionists when they see a red house or room that they want to complete.

All in all, with a few flaws here and there, if you are a fan of the RE franchise, I implore you to play this game. Its got great storytelling, some fun combat and progression, some seriously scary moments, and is an overall beautiful game to look at as well. You won't be disappointed.

WIthout further ado, let's get into it:
[b]Story:[/b] one thing I must mention here - if you didn't play through RE7, play it first. You will understand the whole setup much better. RE8 is a continuation of the RE7, letting you play as Ethan Winters, It is good, even very good. However I feel it a bit lacking (only a bit). You recently moved with your family to the new house, your daughter gets kidnapped and here we go, you run after her for the whole game. I don't want to spoil the story here, so I won't go into details, but let me say this - some twists in the plot are nothing like you would imagine :)

[b]Graphics:[/b] RE8 uses almost all new gen techniques, while still keeping very good optimisation and high FPS. On bigger screens, especially ultra wide, this game looks astonishing. We have open spaces, with great views, shrouded in snow and/or fog. A big middleage castle to explore, almost taken from Castlevania, and a lot of underground places, so dark that even with your flashlight you are just barely able to see. To sum it up, it's top of the cream if you can support it with a good hardware. 

[b]Sound:[/b] To sum it up ... it's almost gone. Like in RE7, you will be playing most of the time in quiet environment, without any OSTs in the background. Old RE games had great background music, that given additional sense of suspence and builded up nice climate. Here, It pops up from time to time, mainly during cutscenes, but that's it. It's strange that Capcom thinks that silent could be used for most of the game and still keep the suspence of the horror survival ... 

[b]Mechanics:[/b] Nothing new, or revolutionary here. If you played RE4 or RE7, you will feel at home. You get all the inventory space you would ever want, a huge number of weapons that are upgradable and a lot of treasures to support your expenses. Some treasures are can be combined to create a more expensive items, so you could feel a bit of accomplishment. 
Ah, sorry, we have one mechanic that is new to this series, but not quite revolutionary, I'm talking about cooking :) Yes, we finally have cooking in Resident Evil. There are few dishes to choose from, but to get the ingredients you will have to run quite a bit and explore some areas, that you would think are 100% done, or are hidden and accessable only after some point in the story and are missable.

Overall the game is very good, but it's one of the easier games in this series. Also, it doesn't have the vibes you would get from old RE games, because it's no longer so hard to manage your ammo and health. You get huge inventory (this one is a plus for me) and all the riddles are childishly easy. I would even say, you get the answers on a silver platter, so there's almost none of that filling of accomplishment. After clearing it I feel a bit of insufficiency, some things could be done a lot better. Plus that lack of background music during almost 80% of the game ... This seems a new trend in horror games, but it's a step in wrong diection in my opinion. As for replayability, there is a NEW GAME+ that you will unlock after completing the story once. Aside the items you will carry over from your first playthrough, nothing changes. You may play it few times for the trophies, but nothing more. 
So, do I regret buying this game now, for 49€? No ... but I feel it a bit lacking here and there. I spent almost 20h on my first playthrough, exploring what I could, trying to get as close to 100% as possible and I'm not far. For 20h of play time it's not a bad price, plus I'm during my second playthrough now, so add to that another 20h ...

Resident Evil Village is interesting, especially after returning to it for the first time in about fourish years since its release and the DLC expansion. All in all, I still really enjoy it, at the time it was one of my favourite Resident Evils. After having gone through 7 again and the RE remakes, including the masterful 4 remake, I can see why some people were not impressed with this one.

It controls fairly differently from the other games on the RE engine, movement is more precise but also floaty. Weapons and fighting lack a lot of weight and everything goes by so quickly. The pace of the game is simultaneously fast, but it goes through the best parts almost too quickly. Meanwhile, the less than stellar and by far, the utterly unfun party, linger on hours more than they ever should. I think Heisenberg's section is what stops me from replaying this game more frequently. 

All that being said, I have done everything in this game besides an achievement 100% run. I have beaten it on all the absurd difficulties and even aced the mercenaries mode and its a game I know intimately well, yet I still never get the 4 hour-run achievement because of the slog of the last quarter of the game and some of the middle section.

I enjoy it, narratively, a lot more than 7, but not everyone will be along for this ride. I, personally, like Ethan Winters as a protagonist even though his character is genuinely barely there. To the point he is still somehow faceless and he turns to avoid the player's line of sight on his face even in the somewhat janky third person mode. 

The characters in Village are great, but they get far less screentime thank you would hope. I personally really love the first two major areas and compared to previous Resident Evils, the back tracking and labyrinthian elements are not as intolerable as usual. Gameplay wise, everything feels great but has poor presentation and impact. 

The RE engine has some a great damage retention system and this game feels like its still on the older engine. Enemy bodies completely lack physics and are confined to present poses and animations, coming off as stiff. Guns lack impact, lack oomph and generally are very underwhelming. All in all, combat encounters except for the grand and exciting boss fights and pursuit sections, lack teeth and tension. You really don't feel much fear at all as Ethan, whereas even controlling Leon in RE4 remake still made you feel vulnerable to mistakes, despite Leon providing far more confidence than he did in RE2. 

My opinion of the game would be higher (although not near what it was upon release) if I hadn't just replayed so much of the series again. Village is still great and has an iconic cast, and I personally really enjoy how the lore ties everything back to the beginning of the franchise and it provides a lot of necessary closure to what exactly is the origin of everything, including Umbrella. Although, the implications that all these viruses and plagues are some natural occurrence that has only merely been weaponize by Umbrella over the years, really does steer the series more toward supernatural horror rather than the more iconic "supernatural incidents through somewhat grounded science-fiction/fantasy" that the previous entries did so well. 

Chris really steals the show near the end and the Hound Wolf Squad has some major balls. The game is best when it returns to milslop tacticool ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ squads fighting the BOWs and in many ways, I think we are glad to see Ethan retired and with such a great send off in favour of what is to come.

The DLC that provides more closure and what not, definitely is better as a DLC and not a full fledged game. I think everyone can agree we are glad with the direction RE9 ultimately went. 

All in all, this is one of my most played Resident Evil games and for good reason. The game still has far more positives than negatives and it feels like it truly knows what Resident Evil did best, all without trying to fall back into trying to recreate the perfect lightning strike that was RE7.

I won't be the first one who skipped RE7, it just felt too disconnected from what Resident Evil meant to me at that point, it felt like Capcom was trying to fill a hole that PT left behind itself. And even after watching a few playthroughs, I never got the urge to play myself.
Village came out and out of curiosity, I checked the Steam page, very positive reviews made me buy it in the end even if I wasn't expecting much out of it myself. Man was I wrong.

[b]Story[/b]

I feel like the story here is quite strong, it even had a "I actually did not see that coming" twist waiting towards the end of the game. Characters are well written and thought out. Even some unbelievable moments are later explained so they make a bit more sense, maybe you heard about the "magic healing water" and "severed limb" thing already, which made me just laugh initially but it's explained later on. And I mean come on, RE series always had monsters gaining 10 times their body mass in seconds, it's not a biology simulator, we have to look past some things and accept it's a video game.

[b]Gameplay[/b]

I was not expecting much but everything about it feels really good. Guns handle really well, minor gripe would be, if you don't actually aim down your weapon, looking through the scope and what not and shoot off the cuff, the guns feel too inaccurate. You could aim down your sniper rifle, shoot a spot, not move with your camera an inch and try shooting again not aiming down, the bullet will end up way too off from where you were aiming. This probably becomes an issue only if you're trying to run the game fast however. There are not many moments in the game where you'd be required to run and gun down hordes of enemies like a Rambo. There's a good mix of action and horror in here. First major location in the game is somewhere inbetween, second is pure horror and then third and fourth are more action focused. And each of them are really well done. Towards the end of the game you get to play a real, guns blazing section, defeating hordes of enemies with near infinite ammunition, thankfully it's short lived as I feel with RE7, Capcom was trying to get away from this type of gameplay. It just doesn't really seem to fit well in the "survival horror" genre. Bosses and mini-bosses both feel challenging enough but none require multiple re-tries to figure them out, you won't feel frustrated by an arbitrary wall a boss presents. You get just about enough ammo to kill almost every enemy you face in the game if you chose to do so, at least on normal difficulty. On higher difficulties the enemies become more bullet spongy and you will have to chose your targets wisely. For those seeking challenge, go Hardcore difficulty+

[b]Graphics and level design[/b]

Graphics are top notch as we can expect from Resident Evil, there were a few instances where I noticed like a 1px big white line between textures, but you kind of have to look for those and it's not a wide-spread issue. It's hard to find a game where there are not flickering textures or something like this anyway. Motion capture brought us amazin animations as well, enemies look and move brilliantly... If you can even say that about monsters. Ray Tracing support is there and it's safe to say that as a whole package, it'll make the beefiest systems sweat a little.
As for level design, I applaud it, there were many moments where I thought mid-game that the level design is really good. Every random house you enter really feels like it's lived in and overall it just feels like you're in real-life places all over the game. You get a glimpse of every location you'll visit really early on and everything is really well connected. You'll encounter many locked doors that you'll later unlock from the other side which will give you the old "aaah, so this is what the door connected to" feel. There's enough secrets around so a completionist will find satisfaction from scouting every area and sweeping everything he can.

[b]Additional thoughts[/b]

If I were to describe this game as fast as I could to an RE fan, I would say "Imagine if Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7 had a baby" and I don't think I would be very far off. The setting is similar, the European village, the castle... And we have a very similar progression system in the form of weapon/inventory upgrades with added ability to craft ammo. Now all we're missing is the purchasable one-shot RPG. There's a lot to unlock with achievement points in the game, ranging from infinite ammo to concept art. Replayability is there. Casual playthrough on Normal difficulty with many "I am too big of a chicken" moments had me finish the game in 9.5 hours based on the end-screen. Speedrunners are finishing the game in 1h50m ish currently. For someone who's not scared easily, I'd say you have about ~6 hours of gametime on your first run, which is about on par with other Resident Evil games (Besides RE6, that game felt gigantic). 

[b]In conclusion[/b]

I did not have this much fun in a Resident Evil game since RE4, I thought RE2 remake was the peak for modern RE games, but even that one did not make me feel like "I want to play again" after finishing it, which this game managed. It's a well crafted world, with a well written story and a fun progression system. I hope to see more of this in the future.

First and foremost, I do agree that this game needed perhaps a month or more in refinement before releasing. It's disappointing to see the trend of unfinished and rusty games coming out before they were polished. Anywho ; 

[h1] Story [/h1]
The story was beautiful, following along from RE7 nicely and answering a few questions from the previous game. Although confirming the theories you might gather throughout the game in the last hour or so, the hints and lore tidbits throughout really hammer home and allow you to slowly discover the twist for itself before it confirms it. 

Pacing however is where the game falls short. Each area felt fleeting, with the last being the longest in my opinion. With how they marketed the castle and it's lovely Mother, you would expect for a longer story within it. However the castle and two of the other areas were incredibly quick and glossed over the characters quickly without any delve or dive into them. I didn't like that part of the story, as I enjoy trying to figure the world and lore out - especially when playing a game that is so rich with lore and story. Such a letdown. 

[h1]Graphics [/h1]
A beautiful game. I couldn't stop looking around and appreciating the constant cold and grey tones. Wherever a warm toned was used it was with power and meaning, making the colour composition just beautifully dull on the eyes. Blood was definitely meant to stand out in this game. Ontop of this, the weather effects and creature designs were gorgeous and reminiscient of the previous games. Nothing felt too out of place, and yet everything felt amazingly refreshing and new.

[u]Character Design[/u]
Holy cow the DESIGN. [spoiler] Miranda's endgame fight appearance was gorgeous and delicate, with her animations flowing and twirling like the Black Swan ballerina. I loved the choreography of the fight and her mechanics, with each transformation being absolutely beautiful. [/spoiler] Ethan's hand was beautifully molested throughout the game. It's not really a RE game without it being shredded. All of the House leaders were beautifully done, describing their story and area with just their appearance and mannerisms alone.  The only complaint I have is the lack of lore to go with them. There's vague callings to backstories but nothing felt wholly fleshed out.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The gameplay was . . . janky and sometimes painful. From crashes to bugs, and even getting stuck for a solid 5 minutes. The unrefined bugs and glitches definitely impacted the gameplay greatly. But when it worked it was great. The last area did feel like a constant hard grind and shoot-em-up, which is reminiscent of any RE game's finale. But for people who enjoy more of the story-side / horror to the game, the last portion might not be your favourite zone. 

Overall I would reccomend this game, especially since it's getting patches. I cant wait for what's going to happen next in the story.
