So, I have to say that this is probably my game of the year. 

I have about 50 hours on the PS5 and I'm already 16 hours in on PC. I purchased it on PC even after having it on PS5 just because I mainly prefer Mouse and Keyboard for First Person games, also I felt like having a "fresh start" again without having access to shop items and infinite ammo. That aside, let's get into a brief overview of the game without any spoilers. 

You'll probably hear that the game is very much like 4 and 7 mixed together. For those who haven't played either, I highly suggest playing 7 at least before playing this one. To grasp a good idea of easter eggs, theories, and story, I'd suggest playing the previous games as well. Whether that's before or after you play this one, I don't think it matters. Should you pass on playing 7, the game gives you a small recap of 7's events so you're not left too much in the dark. The horror elements are still there but definitely not as much as I felt with 7. The game tends to have more of a mix of horror and action which I feel is executed very well. My only issue that in Mercenaries, enemies can spawn literally right in front of you. (This are scripted, it seems, so it doesn't matter where you are on the map, once the condition is met, the enemy will spawn) I don't recall this happening in RE5's mercenaries mode that I played quite a bit of when it first came out. 

Inventory is alright, they tend to separate scraps or ingredients that make ammo so those don't take up space. It's not like previous games with gunpowder. Same with Herbs for Med Kit stuff. Switching weapons looks funny in this game as it looks like Ethan has 2-3 arms, once you get more weapons, see for yourself and rapidly switch weapons. You'll have a good laugh. Aiming in this game definitely doesn't feel like as you would in let's say maybe Call of Duty or any traditional FPS, and I think it's made that way to make it a little more difficult in fighting enemies. I could be wrong and it's just bad, but I still prefer that over playing on controller, so there's that. 

I've ran through the game maybe 7 times now across both platforms and I can say that I'm not tired of going through it again. Personally, Mercenaries is quite fun compared to the previous games that had it. I do miss being able to hit enemies with a haymaker or stomp their head in but it's understandable that, that mechanic makes sense for 3rd person/over the shoulder. 

The story is well done and while I can't say much without giving spoilers, I have to say that there wasn't any disappointment for me or anything that I would have changed. If you're taking your time, I'd say the story would take about 6-8 hours. My first playthrough, I was taking my time but I definitely didn't hit every nook and cranny which took me 6 and a half hours. 

I foresee myself flushing more hours down the drain on both platforms, so I give this game a 10/10.

The game is interesting and a unique departure from the typical Resident Evil game while at the same time still maintaining its key characteristics, with a protagonist battling evils and achieving his/her goal through solving puzzles and killing foes. You can collect treasures and sell them to the Merchant (who actually has a personality, unlike RE5's merchant), and upgrade and modify your weapons to a great degree. You can even buy custom parts for the weapons which is a new feature as far as I know. The environments are interesting and varied and have an eerie atmosphere despite the game being more action-focused. To those who complain about the lack of horror clearly haven't played the game, because there is one particular part where the horror eclipses even what is considered "the scariest" RE game (RE1), in my opinion. There is great action throughout the game and a good amount of puzzles that require more than an elementary schooler's logical skills (cough cough, RE4 and 5).  I also like that they took inspiration from RE4, which in my eyes is one of the best RE games at least in terms of everything but story (story is nothing special in that game). The inventory system is great and crafting items something I like too. Moreover, killing the game and then having the Duke make you a dish to gain permanent buffs is a cool idea. I also like the Duke in general. It's just nice to have a merchant with a personality again. He's a nice comforting, corpulent presence in a world full of enemies who want to kill you. He is definitely a welcome addition.

It's a well balanced game, but there are definitely flaws. Ethan's lines and his delivery is pretty corny and downright stupid, as if a twelve year old wrote his lines. Moreover, the game has a weird difficulty curve. Standard is pretty easy because you are basically constantly getting bullets and once you upgrade your guns, you can pretty much take out any foe with ease, even though the enemies AT first seem very much like bullet sponges. Hardcore on the other hand (at least at the START), was so hard that I couldn't beat the first village ambush. You die in two hits, and unloading your whole clip does basically nothing to the Lycans as if they're getting hit by BB's. 

I would say that Dimitrescu and Beniviento are very easy boss fights. The doll boss fight is barely a fight. You figure out a puzzle, and then you run around finding her and then Ethan stabs her in a scripted sequence and she dies. Dimitrescu's fight is very easy. You get a ton of ammo, and all you do is shoot her when she is exposed from her weird mold monster dragon form. She's very easy to dodge and kill.

The other two boss fights aren't really challenging either, but they're at least a bit difficult. Mother Miranda is not really hard or really easy but it's really due to the fact that she's just a bullet sponge. It's the same with most enemies, particularly those big mini bosses like Urias or the werewolves. They just take a lot of shots to kill, but they're very predictable and easy to avoid. It can be kind of annoying knowing that you're gonna face this mini-boss and monotonously shoot him over and over and avoid his telegraphed hits. 

The story is interesting in my opinion. I thought it was a cool twist and pinning Redfield as a red herring bad guy was an interesting idea. However, Ethan isn't really the most likeable protagonist, and I'm kinda glad his saga is over. Moreover, at the same time, the premise is so simple that it seems like they didn't even care about the story that much...

Ethan was cool for a bit, but I'd rather have Leon or Chris as the next protagonist. Where has Leon been?

Anyway, this game is really pretty good. It has its flaws, BUT, I still recommend it definitely. I would give it a 4/5.

Reminds you of so many of the other entries in the series. Resident Evil 1 for the puzzle solving and how it impacts the story, Resident Evil 2 & 3 for the menacing Tyrant-like sequences, Resident Evil 4 for the treasures, weapon upgrades and the merchant, and of course, with it being a continuation of Resident Evil 7, the story feels very much in line with the previous entry.

However, while this is all fun and games, I would like you to keep in mind that none of this feels particularly fresh for the series. The inclusion of Vampires and Lycans felt rather lazy, and too fantastical for this particular game. I do realize that there are various viruses that Umbrella is responsible for, but there is hardly any mention of Umbrella this time. I don't actually think they had anything to do with the village and Miranda's antics, and if they did, I didn't catch it being mentioned anywhere in the game. Either way, it feels like a cheap addition to the story arc as opposed to going all in on the Mold virus and how Umbrella is truly responsible for it, which Resident Evil 7 merely hinted at.

I will say, the combat and scavenging aspects of the game are fun and can be quite exciting, especially towards the end when your guns become more powerful. There's also great replayability with this game as there are many challenges that will take you multiple playthroughs to achieve and a lot of unlockables to unlock. So, all in all, I can't say it was a bad game. Fun, not too repetitive, enjoyable story, replayable, some of the best creature design I've seen put in a game and some of the biggest and baddest boss fights yet in the series. I just wish those creature encounters were made to add a little bit of weight to the story as a whole, from all of the games, as opposed to being serviceable for just this one entry. 3.5/5 Crystal Skulls, would recommend if you're a fan. If not, you're not missing anything by waiting for a sale.

Edit: Would bump it up to a 4/5 on the PS5 specifically because of the seamlessly intuitive controls and how the game interacts with the DualSense controller. The adaptive triggers feel so great when you're pulling the trigger and the pressure varies from gun to gun. It feels amazing. Plus with the mix of that and the haptic feedback, the game is a delight in your hands on the PS5. You can get a similar experience on PC with the DualSense controller, but they have yet to emulate the adaptive triggers, and that's most of the fun about the controller, to be honest.

RE: Village gets a tentative recommendation from me. If you prefer action over horror, you'll like it more than I did. I much preferred RE7. It was a lot scarier and felt like genuine survival horror. RE:Village feels like that at first, though it quickly loses that as you become powerful and enemies become trivial to deal with. Leaning into the action really exacerbates Village's weaknesses as an FPS, especially with boss fights. Most of the bosses are just big annoying bullet sponges with slow attacks and obvious weak spots. Dodge the attack, shoot the weak spot. Rinse and repeat until the boss eventually dies. The boss fights in RE7 were far more varied and interesting.

Boss fights aside, Village is mostly enjoyable. The environments are fun to explore and there are lots of secrets to find. On Hardcore difficulty, the early game is pretty tense and requires a lot of careful resource management. There's one really great horror segment that feels unique. I just wish there was more than one. The story is decent enough, though the characters didn't have as much depth as they did in RE7.

I enjoyed Village enough to complete it so that warrants at least a 7/10. That said, I'm worried that Capcom is repeating history and steering the series towards action again. AAA action games are a dime a dozen, AAA survival horror games are not, so I really hope that Capcom moves back towards horror with the next entry.

While 7 focused more on traversing tight spaces, minimal lighting, and close-quarters combat; this was more open, more vibrant with faster gameplay.  What you miss out on is the intimate horror of Biohazard, but in return, you get a very intricately designed world with some truly grotesque enemies and bosses.  It doesn’t completely shy away from horror (one part in particular terrified me), but it’s definitely not the focus.

This game is more like a Resident Evil, or a survival horror game, anthology. There is a RE game in here for everyone. Parts of it are very reminiscent of RE 4, other areas are similar to RE 2 or a certain part of Nemesis, there's a little RE 5 and 6 in there for those who like the more action-focused RE games, and there is one section that is probably the scariest thing I have seen in any RE game. It's all compartmentalized and never overstays its welcome. For reference, I did not enjoy all of the RE games, especially the ones that had our protagonists morph into early 90's action heroes (I am looking at you, RE 6). Capcom really started to lose their grasp of what RE was all about imo. Personally, I was more a fan of the slow-paced, more focused RE games, especially the ones with the tank controls a la RE 1 and 2. Then I really started to love RE with the RE 1 remake (or remaster? I forget exactly) on GameCube. 

Then RE: Biohazard (7) came around and it really blew me away. The RE 2 remake was amazing. Those two games are easily among my favorites of the franchise. I would say my top RE games in order (but kind of interchangeable) are:

RE 1 (GameCube)
Code Veronica
RE 2 Remake
RE Village
RE 7

I am still working out the order. My intent is that a little back story as to which RE games that I like - and the ones that I don't - might help you decide if this is worth your money. If you agree with anything that I have said so far then it most certainly is!

Resident Evil Village combines the best horror elements of classic games in the franchise with the action-packed scenes from later entries in the series. While I've heard that the game suffers from stability issues on PC compared to PlayStation 5, I in my 10-hour playthrough of the story had little to no issue except for a few minor frame rate drops here and there. (For context, I am using an Intel Core i7 with GTX 1060).

Hello dear players. If you don't have time and wishes to see if it's a good game or no, just look the first part of the review "gameplay".
This review is from a player who played all the existing resident evil game and who's a big fan of it.
So seat back, take your glasses, some pop-corn maybe and enjoy your reading.
My review only attente to be constructive. The comments are allowed but with constructive agurments. I don't want to have childs that throw some hate at me just because 
they love the game so much.

[h1] PART 1: THE GAMEPLAY [/h1]

This part will be divided into pros and cons categories with a conclusion at the end and a slide comparaison with RE7.

[u] PROS [/u]

- Better inventory systems.
- Merchant where you can buy guns and ammo, upgrade weapons and sell items.
- Treasure Hunt mecanic
- Wild life hunt with cooking (upgrade player health).
- Detailed graphics and enviroment
- Giant 2 feet tall, huge boobs, vampiric & glamourous lady that you wish you do not have to kill.
- A good overhaul gun variety.
- Good audio (recomande the use of headphones) and good soundtracks.
- Good horror scenes.

[u] CONS [/u]
- Weak guns (even upgraded)
- Fast moving ennemies with buffed health
- VERY SMALL ammount of lootable and craftable ammo
- Controls not optimized for pc (controller recommended for playthrough)
- Poor crafting mecanic
- Poor ammount of crafting meterials
- Too much bosses to fight
- Event that takes up in 2021 yet your in a medival like enviromnent (personal point of view).

[u] Conclusion [/u]

The game itself is not that bad. The scenes are great, good looking and very horrorific. The difficulty is, however insanly hard. You got poor ammo, the ennemies gain more health
overtime and more dammages, but your guns feels weak all the time. Plus the ennemies can dodge your bullets. The crafting mecanic is lacking has you have hard time finding 
materials and the ammount crafted (aka for ammo) is low. You will learn how to use your knife lol. Futher you go in the game, the more mini bosses you will have to fight and they
are sucking your ammo real hard!
My note is 5/10.

[h1] PART 2: RESIDENT EVIL AND THE IDENTITY CRISIS [/h1]

[u] Context [/u]

Not long ago, SILENT HILL was announced with a nice FPS mecanic and created a GIANT hype around it's demo. But, the compagny behin the title decided to cancel their game leaving
a lot of fans sad. BUT CAPCOM saw the hype behin that game a decided, to use it.
Soon after, seeing Resident Evil has their horror franchise and knowing that they already have a huge fanbase (like me). Announced that they are working on a new resident evil game
and said that the franchise will be [b]rebooted[/b]. A huge hype created around the next resident evil game. Soon after, to add up with the hype, Capcom release a demo of a game
called Resident Evil 7. The demo let's you play in full FPS (has the franchise is only knowed for TPS and Angled View). The hype was real. The the game was released and a LOT of
positif critisim surround the game. But this is when think started to be complicated. During the gameplay of RE7 very small details of the Resident Evil univers appeared
(mostly 1 or 2 notes, Chris Redfield at the end plus the umbrella logo). The gameplay mecanic was totaly deffrent of any other resident evil games before. From this game
The fanbase was divided into 2 categories, The one saying "it was better before" and the others saying "it's better now". I'm myself in the first categorie (yet I stay open minded).
Capcom is a compagny that listens to its players so, here comes Resident Evil 8 Village.

[u] Trying to fix the division: Nostalgia [/u]

Seeing the huge fanbase of "it was better before" Capcom decided to keep the mecanic of RE7 (and improved it). But in order to gain that fanbase, they diceded to add a lot of
mecanics of one particuliar game that a lot of fans loved: RE4. You don't know what I'm talking about? Here is the list:
- Treasure hunt with jewel that can be combined togeither in order to form a more valuable item for sale.
- The return of a merchant (The Duke) that openly quote RE4 merchant's "What are ya buyin'?".
- A village that use to leave peacefully until big lords arrived and they had to worship him/her.
- That same village where the event occur in modern times yet they live like it's mideval times.
You get it now? :p

[u] Trying to fix the division: Not much of a reboot [/u]
Most of the criticism of RE7 fanbase was the lack of links between the event and the resident evil univers. So now, in the beguining of the game, you have Chris Redfield, aged 50
who carries the past of previous resident evil games, The BSAA, the umbrella logo very present in the game and [spoiler] Mother Miranda was close to Spencer, the founder of Umbrella [/spoiler]
All of this details that says, this game is far from being a reboot. It's actualy, not a reboot. A reboot would have been possible if they first started with the title of the game
has Resident Evil : Village (and not V.I.I.IAGE), same goes for RE7. But still, the game is here, searching for identity in the middle of a crisis capcom created. Yet they don't care
that much since they gained a lot of money. And we both know that now, compagnies don't make games for players, they make them for money (#EA #Bethesda as they are the popular trend this days lol).

[u] Conclusion [/u]

A great game? Well see the first part above. A Great Resident Evil? No. Resident Evil doesn't have to search for it's identity. Resident Evil wasn't a FPS game and should not be.
And also, if they want to make a reboot, why not, only don't call yourself RE7 and RE8. That's no reboot. It's worth if you had up stories of previous games. If you want to make a rebbot
cut and paste what Call of Duty Modern Warfare did. Because they did it flawlessly, they where no complains, and the fans of COD (which are far superior in numbers that Resident Evil) did not complain
And they devs where happy to rewrite Modern Warfare's history.

[hr][/hr][b][h1]🎮Gameplay: [/h1][/b][hr][/hr] 
Although the plot is a direct continuation of the previous game, no prior knowledge of the events is needed. There's a nice recap at the start that tells everything you need to know and still manages to keep it short in case you haven't played it yet. Three years after the meeting with the Baker family, Ethan and his family lead a quiet life. 

One night, after the bedtime story (foreshadowing the events in the game), the legendary hero Chris comes knocking at their door. This is no friendly visit. Before he can ask questions, Ethan gets knocked out. He wakes up in the woods after a car crash, someone or something is there with him. By following the trail in the snow, he ends up in a village.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2498742666

The first hour in the village is unsettling. Everything looks abandoned, there are dead animals everywhere, and whenever you enter a house, you always hear floorboards creaking upstairs. It doesn't take long until a lycan bites off a nice chuck of your hand. Lycans, which is just another word for a new kind of zombie, or werewolves in this case, are your main foe in the village. 

They come in a variety of shapes and sizes, ranging from fast and vulnerable to armed and nearly unstoppable. Since the reward for killing them isn't worth it, it's better to just run past them and save your ammunition. But killing weaker enemies is a lot of fun, particularly once you learn their moves. They have a tendency to jump away the moment you press the trigger, so aiming a bit to the left or right is the way to go. And you don't want to waste ammo because even a basic enemy requires an entire clip from a pistol. Sometimes I felt like the battles were staged; you rush in loaded with ammo, but by the time the carnage settles down, your pistol has only 5 bullets left.

Village is the first game in the series that tries to explore the open-world concept. Unfortunately, this only works for the titular village that acts as a hub. The other stages you visit in a linear order become off-limits once you complete them. As you collect new tools and keys for locked doors, each trip back to the village reveals a new path to a secret reward or a new monster. Because you're aware that this is a video game with its own set of rules, you don't pay attention to things that don't make sense. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2497854548

All defeated enemies drop lei, the game's main currency, as well as materials for crafting various types of ammo and medicine. Since this is a survival game, there is a limited amount of inventory space with the ability to expand. Items and weapons come in various sizes; the bigger the gun, the more squares it takes. Even if you can rotate items to make them fit better in your briefcase, you'll still have to juggle and decide which valuables to sacrifice for that brand new antique pistol. 

Despite the fact that the game brings back the old typewriter-based saving system (don't worry, there are still checkpoints), it neglects to include its companion, the storage box. This means that stuff in your inventory is everything you "own" and you can't switch weapons whenever you want.

Your main source of new weapons and objects, the Duke, is willing to assist you for a price. He accepts lei and buys things you don't need. He can also upgrade your weapons and grant access to a special kitchen. Here you can cook meals that give you permanent perks, such as increased health or decreased damage. However, the ingredients need to be found first. 

Village, unlike other games in which you collect plants and prepare mainly plant-based meals, jumps right for the meat. You'll see chickens, pigs, and other animals being slaughtered. There are also a few rare creatures. But be careful. Since meat is in short supply and can be traded, you might lock yourself out of these perks.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2498740843

Upgrading weapons can hurt you too. Because there's no way to save them, you might waste resources on a nice gun that will turn itself useless once you find a better weapon. You can sell it to the Duke, but most of the resources will be permanently lost. 

[hr][/hr][b][h1] The Lords: [/h1][/b][hr][/hr]

Since each of the four lords reside in its own distinct environment, you will have to adopt different approach. One environment requires you to use stealth, which becomes totally pointless in the next, which brings back the suspense and horror from the previous game. The fist level, for example, includes a mechanic that has been implemented into every new Resident Evil game: an enemy that can appear at any moment and chase you relentlessly. Except that it's almost a joke in this game. Lady Dimitrescu is so big she has to bend down to go through a door. While she's busy getting back up, you can easily run past her and into a save room, which is apparently off-limits to her.

The inevitable boss fight awaits at the end. With the exception of one, they all take a lot of punishment, so you probably won't have enough ammo with you to take them down. That's why you need to run around the arena and collect valuable resources. The bad news is that bosses have several stages with different attack patterns. These hurt and you'll probably die several times before learning them. Although you can kill the bosses just by shooting at them, you'll run out of ammo long before they die in a satisfying fountain of goo. 

Battles feel like an excuse to waste all the best grenades and ammo you're been saving all this time. Instead, you have to pump enough bullets into their body to reveal a weak point. Even those, however, can survive a few hits from the most powerful gun and prolong the combat until it becomes a chore. Half the time you don't even know if your weapons are doing any damage. 

First-person view doesn't work well. Unlike the old third-person games, where you can keep the camera on the enemy at all times, here you're constantly running away from the boss without being aware of its position. When you stop to take a look, you usually get hit by something you never see coming.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2498737379

By completing in-game challenges, you earn CP points that can be used in the shop to purchase special and infinite ammo weapons, character figurines and even a new game mode Mercenaries. This is basically a time-attack mode in which you need to score points and clear stages as fast as possible.  Unlocked stuff can then be used in the main game.

[hr][/hr][b][h1]🙋‍♂‍Final Thoughts:[/h1][/b][hr][/hr]
After going back to its horror roots and slow gameplay with the seventh game, Village adds more action and goes for the spectacle. I'm afraid this doesn’t sound like good news for the next main game in the Resident Evil franchise. If we take a look in the past, action came to the forefront with each new game. So, if we follow the same trend, the series will turn into a first-person shooter with zombies. That's when the series loses its identity. And there's no going back after crossing that point.

Overall. Village is a good game, but it has a few issues. 

[h1]Performance[/h1]

Denuvo's a piece of ♥♥♥♥. I've gotten heavy performance drop for no reason in certain areas unless I turn my graphics all the way down. If you are concerned about whether your rig can play, buy the game on steam, try for 2 hours, refund if it doesn't work out.

[i]But past RE Engine games were fine. What's wrong with this one?[/i] ♥♥♥♥♥♥ if I know. That's what I'd like to know too. Don't make that stupid assumption like I did. 

[h1]Game flow[/h1]

It's not ♥♥♥♥, but it sure as heck is awkward. I've seen the "dungeons" being compared to theme park attractions in reviews. I agree with that sentiment. Each lord's domain feels loosely connected and the gameplay experience feels very disjointed in each area. Especially if you got off the vampire ride and went right to the haunted house. Unfortunately, Dimitrescu's castle is the high point of the game. Everything afterwards just slowly tapers down. Even more sad is that the vampire lady's domain is the FIRST domain you go to. So the best part of the game for me was over in the first 1-2 hours already.

Village/8's gunplay is fine. It's cool. WHEN you are not in the slow and plodding section such as the unskippable prologue section, and the bit right after the castle... The flow is awkward. This is an issue where it becomes especially apparent after playing the campaign on multiple playthroughs with varying difficulty. It is IMPOSSIBLE to skip the house scene and Ethan's slow and painful walk towards Village. With all the scene skip function, I wish they would just dump you right in front of the first enemy of the game instead of being forced to slog through this tedious prologue every, single, time I start a new game.

[h1]Enemies[/h1]

This is still going to loop back to the issues with the flow. But the first enemy you encounter is the fast and ultra annoying Lycan. Like a wild animal, they dodge and weave out of your line of sight in the blink of an eye. From start to finish, Lycans are the fastest and most nimble mook you'll encounter. Surely shooting at their knee cap or head can stun or make them stumb- ♥♥♥♥ you no such things. For whatever ingenious design reason, you need to survive against a wave of Lycans in the prologue section. This is literally the start of the game when you have barely any ammo or other types of resources to hold out against such an enemy type. Surely you can ladder cheese like in RE4... Nope, fuzzballs can just leap on top of roofs. You also don't have invincibility frames when climbing ladders. Moroaica, the second type of mook to be encountered in Dimitrescu's castle: is slow and shambling like a classic zombie. The perfect, classic, beginner mook monster to throw at the player. But you encounter them later instead... The final variety of mook is Soldats. They are basically beefed up industrial zombies and only appear in the last dungeon of the game. Despite being the last mook type, they are still easier to kill than Lycans. WTF?


[h1]Story[/h1]

Village takes place some years after the events in 7. You play as Ethan Winters again, out to save his abducted family member, again. And a certain boulder punching ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ may or may not be involved in the abduction. 

Minor spoilers ahead

The writers did the characters dirty. Chris is a jerk. Ethan's a moron. We got actually new and interesting RE villains squandered in one single game. Many thought Dimitrescu would play a more important role in the game because of all the hype generated from the demos. But she's the first boss you fight and then that's it. She's dead within the first 1-2 hours of the game. Heisenberg is also another villain who's rather atypical for your standard RE bad guys. Writers had ample opportunity to do an alternative route with Heisenberg, like what they had done with Zoe in 7. But they chose to make Ethan a freaking idiot and close off that opportunity. What the ♥♥♥♥ were you smoking?! 

Originally they planned to do more with the NPCs in the village. But since so much got cut out already, they honestly could've just removed that sob fest and nothing of value would be lost.

[h1]Chris' involvement[/h1]

I am not that big on Chris' section in the game. I get flashbacks of Revelations 1 when I'm forced to play other characters with none of the cool customized gears I've collected and a disjointed story. I would have preferred that they just take out Chris' assault on the village altogether. They probably did it for story purposes, but they should've just made a separate scenario ala Ada's Separate Ways in RE4. I didn't feel like I was on a power trip when I was playing as Chris the gorilla. It wasn't fun. I had to fight a giant mace man in a tiny pit by crouching and shooting at his left leg. Yeah. [i]lots of fun[/i] if you think frustration = fun

[h1]Mercenary mode [/h1]

You only have control of Ethan, period. Each main map will have additional mini maps, and at the beginning of each section you will start in the merchant's shop. If you don't like your peashooter LEMI you can buy other guns. The enemy doesn't spawn the way 4's does. You need to chase down and figure out how the enemies are spawning in order to rack up combos for that SS level. ... 4's merc mode is better.

[h1]Overall impression[/h1]
On the whole, an ok game barely held together by good gunplay but bogged down by disjointed theme park rides. The story was a wasted opportunity. DLC might be able to fix this but I highly doubt it. Also needs a better mercenary mode. Wait until Denuvo's gone or a good sale unless you really enjoy the series.

RE8 has basically village as hub region from which it separates to each bosses regions that can be quite different in play styles. Other might be solving puzzles, getting around and finding the way along with occasional combat, second with puzzles and horror or then very battle heavy region that throws enemies as obstacles on your way one way or another. Start of RE8 is quite story heavy and goes for a while bit slow, but it's basically how 4 and 7 were, then after a while it's more free to go where you can gameplay as usual.

First combat section is really heavy one and you will most certainly get slapped around, as Ethan is quite ill equipped for the fight and even with finding potential help from surrounding buildings, it's still merry slap Ethan around moment. There is 2nd very battle heavy lycan phase closer to the end of the game, but at that point on should have better gear on besides LEMI pistol and ye olde knife.

Visually it was very impressive looking and each of the regions had their own theme going on, day passes by and you experience very real looking village from break of the morning to it's night time. Gameplay is tad more faster and fluid from RE7, as it was game that was influenced very highly by Alien: Isolation that was magnificent horror game like RE7 was. There are horror sections in RE8, but it's not with as heavy atmosphere of horror as RE7 was, but has it's moments.

Resident Evil Village is not just an excellent sequel to Resident Evil 7, but an excellent Resident Evil game in general. Okay it's now story time.

It has been 3 years since the baker incident and things have finally settled down for Ethan and his wife; they immigrate to Europe and now have a baby named Rosemary.

But after settling down Mia is killed by Chris Redfield and before Ethan can do anything he and rosemary are taken. it's not over yet after coming too from being knocked out, Ethan discovers the transport he was on destroyed, a guard dead and his daughter missing, but he soon finds a loan almost abandoned Village in the distance.

But he also hears strange monstrous wolf-like howls, what is going on, where are all the people and what is this talk about Lycans? That is what Ethan must find out every as he searches for his daughter in this accursed Village.

Alright then it's time for the likes, the story is really good as it not just answers questions from the previous game it also presents new ones while adding so much to the Resident Evil series as a whole. They also have plenty of great and shocking moments. Another good thing about the story it pays homage to the classic works of horror like vampires and werewolves to even Frankenstein and a bit of HP Lovecraft. The Story theme about parenthood is also incredibly good as it shows what a parent will do for their children both good and bad.

The game's graphics is very good, nice to look at have you wander through a village or Alcina Dimitrescu Castle, there just many moments and scenes that make you stop and stare. The levels in the game are really good and very diverse as we go from a village to a castle to an undersea Village to even a factory and the levels are all very detailed and very nice to look at and explore.

The atmosphere in the game is good and spooky it definitely has moments that keep you on edge of your seat especially when you're at Lord Heisenberg’s Factory. While the game is not as scary as the previous Resident Evil games it definitely does have its fair share of scares. There have been people that have compared this game to Resident Evil 4 and yes there are definitely some similarities, but it also does its own thing and has many differences that helps separate the two.

The music in the game is really good and the new characters in the game are also very good, my two favorites is Heisenberg, he has a cool look, he's charming and charismatic while also being dangerous, plus his boss fight is really good probably my favorite in the whole game. The second favorite character of mine is Donna Beneviento, her whole level is just so spooky and she herself is such an interesting and mysterious character and even sympathetic.

The gameplay is very good definitely fun with plenty of great weapons to try out and to upgrade. The enemies in the game are really good way better then 7’s, with their own interesting looks. The notes in the game are also really good as you know I'm a big fan of notes in the game because they help with the world-building and these notes are no exception.

Probably the best were the enemies in Heisenberg’s Factory; I don't know I'm a sucker for Frankenstein like creatures. The bosses in the game are all very cool and interesting looking again my favorite is Heisenberg's but all the other bosses are pretty cool as well. The puzzles in the game we're good, not too hard to figure out and pretty fair, the treasure and combinable treasure was nice to see again.

Alright then it's time for the dislikes, the only thing I can say I dislike about this game is the fact that Donna Beneviento’s whole level was too short for such an interesting character and we didn't even have a proper boss fight with her, so I'm hoping a DLC were we get to have more time with her is coming.

Now that I have told you all this, Resident Evil Village is not just an excellent sequel to Resident Evil 7, but an excellent Resident Evil game in general. With a really good story, very good gameplay and very good characters, so if you liked Resident Evil 7 then you are definitely going to love Resident Evil 8 and I highly recommend getting it.

First off, if I have to hear one more "hot vampire lady" joke review, I'm going to lose it. Like gee, did you come up with that all on your own?

As for the game itself, it's interesting. People say that it's a combination of RE4 and 7, which I agree with. However, I find myself being reminded of RE6 when playing this game. In my opinion, the best part of this game is that it succeeds at doing what 6 failed at. RE6 tried to feature both horror and action in its multiple campaigns, but in practice just featured different flavors of over-the-top action. In contrast, each area of this game is essentially its own horror subgenre. Castle Dimitrescu feels like a classic RE environment with puzzles, enemies that you're usually better off avoiding and a terrifying invincible stalker character. Without spoiling the particulars of the other levels, one of them feels like P.T, another is a massive RE6 style set piece level, another is an RE4 style tense combat arena, and the final areas are like a combination of different RE games. 

Some people may dislike this direction, for the reason that the game takes on a jack-of-all trade approach. While exploring Castle Dimitrescu is fun, the puzzles and enemies are kind of underwhelming and simple when you compare it to, say, the Spencer Mansion or the RPD building. In the same vein, the combat areas are pretty engaging, but they're few and far between. 

I can understand people not liking the fact that the game features smaller sections of different styles instead of just sticking to one and refining it, but I personally feel this is a "glass half empty" way of looking at it. This isn't like RE6 where the slower moments felt forced and tacked on, everything flows together pretty cohesively in this game, and it pulls off each style of horror well enough to make the overall experience a positive one.

I also feel its important to mention how excellent this game's post-game unlocks are. RE7 left me pretty disappointed when it came to its special unlocks, and this game more than makes up for that. Not only does the well-loved mercenaries make its return for the first time in this new generation, you can unlock a good variety of new firearms to spice up future playthroughs. Not only can you give each of your guns infinite ammo and unlock previously unique one-off weapons for an entire playthrough, there are also some more outlandish choices. You can go through the game with a rocket pistol (which is actually a real thing, look up the "gyrojet rocket pistol"), and even a freaking lightsaber.

Overall, this is a fantastic game, though I would highly recommend people play 7 first, as the story is very heavily tied to that game.

If steam had an option between Positive and Negative for reviews to choose from I'd definitely pick it for this game as it's definitely a mixed bag in certain areas that feels underdeveloped or generally just rushed.
I'll still recommend it for Resident Evil fans or for those who solely enjoyed RE7, as the gameplay in this one is pretty similair to 7 but this time around more action packed, to some degree.
Took me like 70 hours to 100% the game, all challenges and getting max rank on Mercenaries mode. The rest is pretty much just me trying out different challenge runs, like limiting myself to some weapons or no upgrading, stuff like that which ended up being quite fun. 

[h1] Optimization [/h1]
Guess I'll start out with the game's technical issues, which are quite bad. Game's not really well optimized in some areas which can ruin gameplay at times. Headshot explosions on enemies often gives you a micro-stutter for a slight second, even from just killing enemies this problem is present for some reason. Moreau's vomit rain and the daughter's fly swarm attack will pretty much kill your FPS, sending it straight down to zero which can be really annoying on harder difficulties. There are some mods that fix these issues fortunately and it seems like the modding community are doing a better job than the developers themselves when it comes to fixing sh*t in general. Like a FOV slider which isn't even a thing in the game options, pretty damn baffling I have to say especially for a first person game in the year 2021.

Then there's the looting system that seems downright broken at times, picking up stuff can be one of the most jankiest and frustrating things in this game as it sometimes won't let you pick up stuff depending on how you're positioned. At times you can pick up stuff from a mile away without even looking at it, then there are times where you're directly looking at it while being close to it and you get no prompt for picking it up. It's an inconsistent mess. 

Also I'll add that loot not dropping instantly by enemies as they die in Mercenaries mode is so dumb because the way they drop loot in this game is heavily dependant on their death animation. So the longer it is the longer you have to wait which can really mess up your ranking as their loot counts toward your overall scoring in the end. 

[h1] Gameplay and Combat [/h1]
So how's the overall gunplay, gameplay and enemy feedback? It's okay at best I'd say, sometimes satisfying but at most underwhelming in my opinion. The Lycans probably end up being the most fun enemies to fight, they're the only enemy in the game that has some gore present when you kill them, they can have their head explode upon shooting them and for some reason it's completely absent from other enemy types in the game. Like why? 

Visual feedback is very lackluster as well, there aren't even bullet wounds or flesh wounds as you unload a shotgun blast onto an enemy, so the weapons you use end up feeling quite weak in some sense, not very powerful sounding either which is a shame (the explosions comes to mind here, they are really pathetic both sound and visual-wise). Considering this time around it's pretty obvious there were more focus on gunplay and combat, given the fact there's a lot of enemy variety and more weaponry, which I really like. It was something RE7 were severely lacking at and I'm glad they adressed that. 

Too bad the gore is nowhere to be seen as I think they nailed it with RE2: Remake really well, a game that's not as much dependant on combat in the first place like Village. I honestly think they could've used it here as it's the same engine and all. To some extent at least, could go a long way to have dismemberment for some enemies and would add a lot to the replayability this game has. 

Where the overall gameplay shines is in the animations, knocking back an enemy with a shotgun blast feels quite satisfying, if close to a wall they'll crash into it then fall onto the ground and it does look and feel satisfying whenever it happens. Same with staggering enemies, they'll stumble around if shot in the leg, you can interrupt them with a headshot, flashbangs will have them fall down on the ground wailing around like cry babies, shooting their melee weapon off their hand if timed correctly, you can line up enemies and penetrate them with a sniper rifle shot or a magnum shot. 

Saving ammo in efficient ways are well rewarded, landing headshots consistently with a handgun feels quite rewarding too as it's pretty tough to land a headshot as enemies are constantly on the move. Especially lycans which can use dodge tactics against you if you take too long to aim and shoot. All good and dandy in that department I'd say and provides for some challenging combat at times, at least on Hardcore difficulty which I'd say is the optimal difficulty for this game as Standard ends up being too easy as soon you get through the ambush segment early in the game. Hardcore in general has a pretty good flow throughout the entire game and ends up being the most fun in my experience.

[h1] Inventory System [/h1]
The inventory system from RE4 were something I was kind of excited about coming back to a modern RE title, unfortunately it's non-existent in this game from a gameplay standpoint. It provides barely anything to the core gameplay of managing your items and feels more like a homage to RE4 than anything else, a half-assed implementation for sure. What I think ruined it is how generous it tends to be when it comes down to space. It's very cheap to buy the next upgrade because of how much treasure the game throws at you throughout the game, so you never really end up having money issues here. The fact that your crafting materials (which is very similair to RE7's system) doesn't take up space in your inventory, makes it easy to abuse space as you can just craft healing items whenever you feel like you need to heal up. Same with ammunition. 

This time around weapon attachments don't take up any space when you apply it to said weapon, explosives like pipe-bombs and mines stack up to 5 and they're really powerful tools to use which make them feel a bit too overpowered and easy to abuse to a point it doesn't even feel like a survival horror game. The mines can basically be used as a strong melee weapon as they don't inflict self-damage to the player which is stupid. So yeah, don't even know why it's there to begin with.

[h1] Graphics and Visuals [/h1]
When it comes down to the graphics, the overall atmosphere and ambience I think the game nails it. Quite an immersive environment and some areas in the game has some really pleasing aesthetics, Heisenberg's Factory comes to mind here and ended up being my favorite section of the game. Its claustrophobic level design, its tough and intimidating looking  enemies lurking at almost every corner made it feel both unsettling and intense to get through at times, I aboslutely love it. The castle and the village itself were also pretty great from a level design perspective, pretty good pacing as well and ends up being fun to go through on repeat playthroughs as the game heavily encourages it for unlocking extra content.

In the end it's a neat survival action/horror game with pretty solid replayability, but falls short in certain areas that probably needed more development time and polish to feel like a complete experience. I would personally wait for a sale to purchase this game if you're now interested in playing it.

Resident Evil Village is phenomenal! An exciting next chapter in the Winters' story to be sure. 

If you enjoyed RE7 but considered it perhaps a little too slow or methodical Village will undoubtedly tickle your fancy! 

Time and time again you'll find yourself facing multiple enemies. Not so much run from this main enemy, follow that one; get that other ones key but after they turn that corner. Although there is still a bit of that "sneak around and try not to get your booty button eaten by crazy so-and-so" aspect it certainly does not take up even half of your story game play.

It is a relatively quick play through.. But! This is not a one and done sort of story mode! Not only does the game encourage you to replay and up the difficulty, they make it simply a must! 
Playing through your first time you will become familiar with the types of monstrosities lurking about in the different nooks and crannies. You will become familiar with the much improved inventory system as well as the market. And you should get a feel for the sort of weapon you may prefer to upgrade for more efficient monster plowing. 
THEN! When you've completed the story, you have the opportunity to start again within the completed save. Carrying over your acquired weapons, money, and wisdom! As well as earn new and improved sorts of weapons for purchase and upgrade! 
Once you have played through a few times Village very much becomes about chasing that 100% challenge completion. And once you've broken into some of the games arguably best weapons, speed running becomes a hilariously good time.

I very much recommend the game to anyone who has enjoyed the tremendous story and detail that CAPCOM has produced in its past RE works. 
To those who are stumbling upon RE for the first time, Id suggest playing 7 beforehand. Although the game is more than fine without the back story, I cant imagine having been as attached going into it as I was having played 7.

Oh, and its certainly worth mentioning, complete the story at least once and you open up another way to play! Like a sort of "rush", 'time trial" type challenge mode. Its an absolute blast!

Resident Evil Village feels like a melting pot of various gameplay mechanics from previous games in the series. The new shopkeeper, The Duke, sells you resources and upgrades to your weapons like the "Whaddaya Buyin'?" merchant from Resident Evil 4. The sultry Lady Dimitrescu and her freaky insect daughters stalk you throughout their castle very much like Mr. X from the Resident Evil 2 remake. Village weaves these familiar mechanics with a fascinating world that's really fun to explore, and even though some portions aren't as strong or memorable as others, the bulk of the game is very well done.

Village takes place in a small, isolated settlement somewhere in eastern Europe, and the entire map gives off the same vibes as the Spencer Mansion or Police Station from the first two Resident Evil games, only outdoors. Right away you'll find locked doors with distinct symbols and barred paths that can't be reached without a specific key or tool. You'll be syphoned off to specific, linear areas to fight the game's main antagonists, but you’ll come back to the settlement fairly often. The game is definitely less spooky and more combat-heavy than Resident Evil 7, and some fights can get stressful at times—I was definitely sweating in some intense encounters when my ammo got low. I do wish the game controlled a little better, especially when you're fighting a sizeable group of enemies at once. There’s a new block button that can reduce damage if you time it right but it felt a little too slow. I definitely don't think the combat is the game's strength, but you're given lots of weapons and tools to play around with.

Out of all the bespoke areas you'll explore throughout the 10-hour-or-so adventure I enjoyed the earlier-than-expected castle portion the best, but most of them are pretty good. There's a couple of locations near the end of the game that are excessively linear though, and not very much fun to explore—there's one particular unapologetic action sequence which I very much disliked. The game is brought to life with awesome, occasionally grotesque visuals and steady performance—the castle’s interior looks particularly nice. I did have some hiccups when killing enemies on PC and some performance drops when a lot of insects are on screen at once, but hopefully these get fixed in a future patch.

Village weaves a collection of familiar Resident Evil mechanics with a fascinating world that’s fun to explore. Not every portion is perfect, but the bulk of the game is strong.

This is my favorite Resident Evil game so far. Let me explain why.

I really love the first three Resident Evil games, and I really like Resident Evil 4... we won't talk about 5 and 6... 7 was absolutely fantastic and a return to form, until the end with the stupid ship section. The thing that I didn't like as much about 4 was the absence of the Metroidvania style exploration. I found the game to be very fun, action packed, and with just the right amount of horror shlock that makes the series great. But that sense of exploration was just not there.

Eight does everything that 4 did right, and tacks on that sense of exploration and discovery in just the right way. It's the perfect balance between what I love in the original games, and the action shlock that we all crave. I remember going through Castle Dimitrescu, and I found I was often going to save room, then opening my map and figuring out where I need to go, plotting my course, and then booking it while chased by a giant lady with blades for fingers. I love that aspect of world design. Now, the rest of the game lacks that same sense kind of design, with much more linear levels afterwards, but it makes up for this by constantly sending you back to the village, now with new things you can unlock. Thus, once again, giving that Metroidvania feel to it, and giving you some satisfying back tracking.

Those linear levels, aren't bad though. They're really fun and engaging, and the combat mechanics are honed in enough to make just going through a barrage of enemies a fun challenge. There's also a lot variety in the areas. From a slow burning horror fest where all your weapons are taken away and you're forced to hide from the most horrifying giant fetus you could imagine, to a gauntlet of seemingly infinitely spawning enemies as you make your way through a medieval strong hold. All of it's good, and all of it's very different. Which is great.

The only weak point is that the two middle areas suffer in replay. I'm on my fifth playthrough trying to complete all the challenges, and the areas that are less combat and exploration focused feel a little tedious when you go through them again, since you pretty much just have to do them the same every time.

The story for this game, also turned out to be much better than I would have expected. Resident Evil 1 established a formula of starting with slow survival horror and leading to a ridiculous action fest near the end. Which is great, and I expected much the same with this, thinking that it would just get ridiculous and over the top, but instead I found myself feelings things. Damn you Resident Evil for making me feel things.

Resident Evil Village is a MASTERPIECE. Well done, CAPCOM! You guys really outdid yourselves with RE7 & RE8.

The Story & Characters: Really splendid plot with very interesting characters that will be remembered for years to come. The plot is the sequel to RE7 which adds to the characters and gives us more depth into what happened at the Baker's plantation and the plot takes an interesting twist towards the end. Well done!

Environment and Setting: Everywhere you go in this game, it gives you the feeling that you would expect in a horror setting. Creepy village, castle, dolls, you name it! The environments are so damn detailed and beautiful that I found myself taking screenshots all the time and just staring at them like paintings. The artists have really created a living, breathing scene for us all to enjoy. Truly a work of art!

Enemies: Every single enemy, mini boss and boss was so damn fun to fight. They kept you on your toes and jumping around in your seat just to stay alive. There is so much variety in enemy behavior. It's overall a really well thought out concept and execution.

Weapons & Items: Although well balanced, the game does go easy on you (on Standard difficulty too). The items and ammo almost never ran out or is that just me? I didn't find myself healing often or buying healing items or ammo from the Duke.

Gameplay: By far the most fun and interesting way to play Resident Evil. First person perspective (FOV was a bit weird with this one though), interesting and fun puzzles, helpful block and kick mechanic, and the much needed crouch mechanic.

Overall the game does an excellent job justifying what CAPCOM meant when they said they were returning to their roots with these games. i got a lot of Resident Evil 4 vibes playing Village and it was nostalgia hitting just right. With RE4 being my first and one of my all time favorite RE games, it was good seeing the Duke (like the merchant from RE4), shooting treasure so that it falls to the ground, shooting crows to get rich, and the list goes on! 

TLDR: If you're a Resident Evil fan or are simply looking for a survival horror game to pick up, I'd definitely recommend Resident Evil Village. Although, I'd suggest completing RE7 Biohazard first if you want the full experience.

Having beaten Biohazard only recently, I can clearly see where some of the criticism comes from. Village balances out some of Biohazard's psychological horror with more action packed sequences. Some thought this change was a departure from what made 7 good and I agree. What Biohazard did, it did PRETTY good. But let's be real, this is still Resident Evil. You're always due some ridiculous action sequences and some cheesy "DIE DIE DIE" stuff. Capcom also listened to the major complains from 7 like enemy variety and weapons and they improved on that. 

Graphics: I won't even delve into graphics. The game on ultra settings looks ridiculously good. I can only call it out on some (sometimes annoying) performance issues where the game just tanks its fps down to a crawl. It happens spontaneously when entering certain areas or after getting involved in some heavy sequences. I found it has something to do with RT but I'm not sure what's really going on, so really waiting on a patch on that.

Story: the game wraps up Ethan's story pretty well. Actually, I loved how they tied the 7/8 Ethan saga to Umbrella and the whole RE universe. It'll also be interesting to see if Rose takes the helm as the new lead (that would be fantastic). The pacing is pretty damn good. Like... wow. The way you're thrown into the Village at first, then entering the lush castle (most Biohazard-esque area), then Benevento's house. Lovely, just lovely. Voice acting is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 10/10 too.

Gameplay: general combat feels pretty good, the enemies are not too spongy. I'm only disappointed in not having different ammo types for the basic weapons, which are pretty good by the way, not taking anything from them. One thing I can only concede as not being that good are boss fights. Biohazard boss fights weren't that good either and I think they struggled a bit improving there. Lady Dimitrescu's boss fight was a bit disappointing, although Heisenberg's was pretty fun with the tank and stuff. It had that ridiculous charm RE is known for and I think the shooting felt pretty great.

What else. Is it worth the $60? Absolutely. Is the game ♥♥♥♥ because it's not 7, which is what some people on YouTube or Reddit would want to make you believe? Absolutely not. It's a damn sequel. It's supposed to build upon the previous game. This game does that in both gameplay and story. Definitely recommend.

(Light spoilers ahead.)

RE8/Re: Village, where to start... In full name, Resident Evil 8/Village is a first-person survival horror game similar to its predecessor Biohazard, in the vein of getting to explore several interconnected areas, along with being in first-person view instead of third-person like those before the two. You play as the same protagonist as before, Ethan Winters, and instead of trying to find your wife, the goal is to find your daughter, Rose. The game begins innocently enough in the Winter's household, with what seems to be your wife, Mia Winters, and then takes a turn for the worse. After this encounter, the game takes place in five areas, including the Village, which is located somewhere remote in Romania, Europe. The other four areas are Castle Dimitrescu, the Beneviento family house, Heisenberg's factory, and lastly, Moreau's swamp type area. There are various hidden locations and of course, the save rooms we all know of and appreciate.

The maps are interconnected in the sense that you must go through one first to unlock the next, and you must backtrack a lot. The village, whilst usually quiet and unassuming, is infested with fodder Lycan-type (werewolf) enemies, and sometimes their scarier, bigger, four-legged brethren. You must revisit a lot, and right outside the gates in the midst of it all is your usual merchant for this game, at least in later stages of the game. [spoiler] The four lords (Dimitrescu, Donna Beneviento, Heisenberg, and Salvatore Moreau) [/spoiler] are all interesting enough, but the Duke has his own intriguing ways and features, besides his readily available new weapons, ammo, & food dishes: as long as you can pay the price, amongst other things, like micromanaging your inventory.

Each microcosmic area is as horrific & beautifully rendered as the next, taking inspiration from real-life Eastern European castles, hallucinogenic plants, human experimentation (which is a running theme), and simply gut-wrenching environments (in a nauseating way.)  Some characters will excite you, others will remind you of stories like the Hunchback of Notre Dame and Jekyll and Hyde. Even the most predominant seeming villains are victims in a sort of way, at least once you realize what's really going on, and who's orchestrating everything behind the scenes; and while these antagonists are bioweapons, the Umbrella Corporation isn't pulling the strings this time (although there are easter eggs referencing the ways in which they are related.) There is a final boss for each area, being the lord of each area, and a conclusionary boss, [spoiler] who you'll come to know as Mother Miranda. [/spoiler]

The game can take as little as one hour if you're a speedrunner, and as many as 10 to 13. The difficulties range from Casual  (which is also known as easy) to Village of the Shadows, which is the absolute hardest. I'd say it has plenty of replayability features because there are tons of achievements, aforementioned secret areas, things to collect, & once you finish, there is also a game mode called Mercenaries waiting for you. There is tons of extra content to peruse as well, such as 3D models of characters, case files entailing information on the Baker family incident, concept art, and a shop where you can purchase things like infinite ammo for whatever weapon you prefer. The game is a love story to both Slavic folklore (which I believe we need more of in the video game industry), the RE Universe, and its lore in its entirety.

If you liked Biohazard, this game is a [spoiler] continuation of that story after a few years, [/spoiler] and supposedly less scary, although that's up for you to decide. It has gorgeous photo-realistic graphics & tense survival horror elements, as well as hide-and-seek horror reminiscent of the old Amnesia games. RE8 is sure to keep you hungering for more as you play through and investigate the happenings of this derelict town, satiating you once and for all as the credits roll. The game is brilliant, and I'm eagerly bestowing it with a personal score of 10 out of 10. Play this game, I adore it, and I'm sure that you will as well.

So after completeing Valley of Shadows and even beating the game under 3 hours for Dashing Dad, unfortunately not much changed my opinion of the game, I was hoping a harder difficulty would have made a world of difference but sadly it only added to things that made the game feel worse. The lack of FOV is huge on higher difficult playthroughs, so much that it feels like the real enemy is the camera itself, and let me explain that. in VoS difficulty the enemies not only have more health but occasionally it will throw the upgraded version of the Cadou at you, as well as ranged enemies, generally this wouldn't be an issue if you could adjust the FOV to take into account of your surroundings but since you can't you run into situations where the game will have a group of armored Cadou swarming you, archer Cadou firing at you, and normal physical Cadou trying to sneak in and grab you. Truth be told if you played any other FPS this is a typical situation where you need to move fast and bait enemies, but you need to be able to see where things are going so you have clear lines of sight to navigate. This comes to ahead when you play as Chris and he fights the leader of the Lycan pack (despite you killing him twice if you do it during the first Lycan swarm and again during the Stronghold boss fight) you're in a very small room, the boss likes to jump, charge, and go berserk. So having a small FOV in a small room, with a giant boss that swings around a giant spiked maul, becomes way more frustrating than it should be. This was probably the biggest issue I had with VoS mode and it was purely because of the camera. 

Now another thing I mentioned in my first review is how the game has missed opportunities, that is taken to a whole new level after my 4 playthroughs.  Moreau (who I referred to as Mermaid Man's drugged out brother) is criminally under used based of articles and dialog you learn in game. He is a scientist who is doing experiments with the Cadou, but his area has zero unique enemies unlike the Castle, House, and Factory. This would have been the best opportunity to reintroduce a old enemy of the franchise, the Hunter. If you're not familiar with the Hunter it is a giant amphibious BOW, it's like a combination of a Frog, a Crocodile/Alligator, and basically a Cheetah. They're fast, they have claws, they can leap, and more importantly they're deadly. Since Moreau's area is as quick and easy as House Beneviento, this segement of the game just feels overly rushed, conversely House Beneviento isn't that much better but it has uniqueness to it that isn't present in any other area of the game which I touched on in my original review. After 4 playthroughs this game really only has 3 main areas of combat and exploration, the Village, Castle Dimitrescu, and Heisenbergs factory. The Stronghold, House Beneviento, and Moreau's area are just quick pit stops that all feel like second hand design ideas. 

The writing in the game is also inconsistent, something I didn't pay attention to during my first run, this has nothing to do with the voice actors as they all sound pretty well, but the lines they speak are very inconsistent. For example, after you kill the first Dimitrescu daughter, she runs into her bathroom and screams "What have you done to my daughter!" This sounds like it's projected to the player but you can't be certain because it's said off screen. This line seems like it should have been used in a cutscene or during the interaction where Dimitrescu cuts your hand off. Then when you encounter Heisenberg, he and Ethan have a conversation about taking Rose, to which Ethan responds "You take Rose? Not a chance!" But, they already took Rose? That's the whole point of the game, they already have his daughter, why does he need to say that line when his daughter has already been drawn and quartered? There are a few more instances of bad writing but you get the point. I just feel the game had a lot of missed opportunities that weren't realized. And because of that I couldn't fully enjoy the game.

I'm going to be brutal with this review. I'm playing in progress and on Heisenbergs factory everything below is a collection of my time playing this.

This game is probably more removed from the "Survival Horror" genre than any of action based Resident Evil titles. This game is what I imagine Konami would do if they wanted to make a FPS of Castlevania, you have vampires, possessed ghost dolls, werewolves, a mutated man fish, a guy who has Magneto powers, and the latest version of "Zombies" called the Cadou. The Cadou is responsible for all the enemies you fight, in the Village you either fights Werewolves or flying bat Cadou, at the Castle it's either the bats, or the extremely emaciated undead with swords and sickles, and later in the manufacturing site "Zombies" are equipped with cybernetics. See what I mean about it sounds like Castlevania?

Now the boss areas, the first is the Castle, it looks nice but there isn't much to the exploration of this place, everything is basically linear and exploration isn't really allowed, for how big the Castle is you go to very few places within it. You would think you would have hidden passages at every nook and cranny, maybe switches that open secret paths, or maybe faux paintings or bookcases that reveal new areas, but you get none of that. Top it off, Lady Dimitrescu just walks around a very linear path, she is not even remotely threatening, the same can be said for her daughters, who all fight you in rooms where you use the environment to kill them. It's very lackluster and a huge missed opportunity.

Now the second area, House Beneviento is the only and I mean THE ONLY area in the game that has any elements of survival horror. You lose your weapons and you have to deal with literal failed abortion turn undead monster at the start of the area. The atmosphere here is exactly what survival horror should be, creepy, intense, and panic inducing, while this area has all this, it ultimately fails because of the mentioned "boss, it's on a linear path, it moves slow, and if you have more than half a working brain you can easily out maneuver it. Later in the House you have to find the Beneviento doll, this is the final boss fight in this area and it consists of you walking basically in a circle to find the doll, that's it, that's the whole boss fight.

Third area, you go to a giant lake, find Mermaid Man's drugged out brother, drain his lake and fight him as a giant fish. Nothing really extraordinary happens here, and the boss fight is also as forgettable, you'll walk in circle, tear down algae barriers, shoot exploding barrels, and hide under conveniently yellow painted buildings when the boss does it's AoE attack of raining down acid. Again, if you played ANY other FPS this is a walk in the park, as is most if not this entire game. 

Now because I haven't gone through Heisenbergs Factory yet, that's where I left off prior to this review, I'm going to cover the technical stuff about this game. As a FPS it's incredibly lack, you can't adjust FoV without a mod, the aiming feels clunky at best, like many players I get massive frame drops throughout the whole game, and anytime you get grabbed by a monster it launches into a animation that really slows down the pacing of the game. I run a 2070, with a i7 9700k, and 48 GB of ram, and I can watch my frames drop to as low as 45 when fighting a Cadou, I can go from 130 in one area to 55 just by looking at a blade of wheat, it's so inconsistent and jittery that at times it feels like the frames are the true monster I have to survive. If I were to stack this game as FPS against other titles like Doom Eternal, Call of Duty, TF 2, L4D, Halo, or any other game that actually has refined FPS mechanics RE Village falls so short of these titles that it really takes away from the experience.

(edit2: Capcom really needs to patch this to fix a few things not least the fact that temporal anti-aliasing doesn't work as intended and leaves the game both overly-sharp, due to the TAA sharpening filter still working, and overly-aliased. It looks harsh. There are probably more issues given that the demo hard-locked my system four times and left a 114MB shader cache file on my computer after being uninstalled, but I didn't encounter them thankfully even if other people evidently have.)

(edit: after playing through hardcore, I think the game is a little better, though there aren't really enough options for the player compared to something like RE2 — you can shoot things, maybe run around ghouls, that's it for the most part)

I don't think it can be overstated how little they actually do with combat encounters in this game. For almost the entire game there is one enemy type (zombies), and a faster version of said enemy type (werewolves), and they almost always appear in front of you along a narrow path, and your weapons all have a very specific utility— you use the pistol for best DPS in mid-range, shotgun when ganged (btw the shotgun is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ and insultingly still takes about five years between shots) and rifle at far distance. You have a grenade launcher too but there are rarely enough enemies to make it worthwhile to use outside of boss fights. Ultimately almost all encounters have one way of dealing with them (use prescribed weapon for range as enemies approach) and it makes the combat sections feel not much more engaging than the sections where there are no enemies at all. There isn't really any resource management since the game spoils you with ammo and crafting (ugh) resources, which you turn directly into ammo at any time (so why does this exist?)

You'd think the problem is that the game doesn't respect the player at all, but when they actually do put you into a series of arena encounters that resemble something from RE4 (they even add ranged enemies to force you to stay within certain areas or otherwise to keep moving while dealing with melee enemies, which is an actual example of ~encounter design~ that I haven't seen since) you realise that it's impossible to stay aware of your surroundings with such a tiny field of view. These kind of arenas would obviously benefit from a third person perspective with a wider field of view, but then you'd be playing Resident Evil 4 instead.

Like RE7 there are a lot of sections that are back-to-back scripted events and bad "puzzles" with no gameplay. I dread the idea of replaying this. During the early sections of the game you have to watch about ten different cutscenes of Ethan getting attacked by villain characters; it's ridiculous and doesn't really pay off with any feeling of triumph in the end. And those puzzles... Particularly egregious is the piano puzzle where you have to read some sheet music to play a tune. Instead of including instructions somewhere on reading the sheet, the game overlays a mark on the sheet to show where the key you hit is. Am I to assume that Ethan can read the notation and the mark represents his knowledge? That seems too weird for an RE puzzle.

Pretty good. I have a lot of complaints, but at the end of the day, I did have fun. My main issue with the game is that it's just not really scary! Even though I loved the setting of this game, I still prefer RE7 because I come to these games to be freaked out, the action doesn't do it for me as much. Like, the [spoiler] baby segment in the dollhouse [/spoiler] made me nearly sh*t my pants and it was maybe my favorite part of the game. Just wish there was more of that. My two big issues with the game are tied together - poor writing and poor pacing towards the end of the game. I really hate unnecessarily drawn out and sluggish endings to games, and while this game doesn't suffer from that issue nearly as much as its predecessor, it's still an issue. My brain just kind of starts to go numb with these things and I just start wishing I was playing something else. Of course, this isn't helped by the fact the writing takes a nosedive at the end of the game. When the game is goofy and Ethan's being a pissed off little manlet (He is a manlet, right? like it's not canon as far as I know but it would make so much sense!) it's a fun but when it tries to get emotional and deep it just falls flat on its feet. This is also an issue with the voice acting to a lesser extent. Whoever does the voice acting for Ethan makes a great lovably angry little doofus but isn't so good at selling [spoiler] a husband/father's grief and slow death [/spoiler]. One last minor complaint before I get to the positives: some of the sound effects for certain guns really don't sell the impact very well, especially whatever the second shotgun you get is called. I have a lot less to say about the stuff I loved, but even if it's simple, there's a lot of it, so believe me I do in fact like this game! First off, god the movement and combat in this game is smooth compared to 7. I started this game not long after finishing 7 so I could really feel the difference in movement speed and weapon proficiency right away. Also, the puzzles in this game are usually pretty good! I liked how the physics engine was incorporated into some of the puzzles to make them feel less rigid and give a sense of freedom in solving them. Speaking of puzzles and the rewards you get from them, man the inventory system in this game is nice! Having a dedicated limitless inventory for key items and valuables is such a relief and for the stuff you do need to take up space with, the inventory tetris is a good time too! I do wish there were more uniquely shaped inventory items to make the stacking a little more complex, but it's not a big deal. - Performance: flawless. Admittedly a 7700K and 2070Super should make it easy, but the port itself is so well optimized that I manage to stay above 80fps almost all the time with RTX on and the highest settings..
- PC specific: really complete Graphics settings, but there's no FOV slider and the default one is pretty low, therefore if you suffer from motion sickness, install the FOV patch from nexusmods first.

Overall: 9.5/10
