So don't play this just for the story, it's really not worth it. But to be fair every RE story was bad and cheesy. You are a liar if you say otherwise. (And I say that as a huge RE fan.)
At least the characters aren't that terrible even though you don't get much backstory for them and a lot of characters just act stupid in the game. (Including Ethan.)

In fact the whole game is very cheesy and over the top. But this doesn't have to be bad for you. I didn't had a big problem with it. RE7 was rather modest with over the top stuff and I loved the game, but I also love this game.

Sadly the game is not scary at all except one part, but at least the atmosphere is really great in the village and all the other parts. Same with the graphics, the sound design, the voice over and the performance. (Except 3 minibosses where my performance dropped a lot when I got too near. This seem to happen to a lot of players. But it's still not that big of a deal.) In my 53h of playtime I also just had one crash.

Then some could argue that the game doesn't really seem to know in which direction it wants to go. The different sections of the game are very different in style and also kinda gameplay wise. On the other hand you could say that the game has a lot of variety. I tend to say the latter.

Now the best part of the game by far: the gameplay. It's just awesome. Pretty much classic RE gameplay, heavily inspired by RE4 with another merchant, buying/finding weapons and upgrades. What I didn't like with that is that the game misses an item box but it's also not really needed as most items don't take place in your inventory away, only weapons, ammo and hp items, so you don't have to worry about crafting, treasure and key items. On one hand I like that because less annoying item management, on the other hand you basically never have to worry about inventory space in the game.

The game has also quite a lof of content. The game is quite long and after beating it you unlock the boni shop, just like in RE3R, where you buy additional weapons or infinite ammo for a certain weapon for other runs. There is also the option for NG+.
And then you also unlock Mercenaries mode. As this was announced I wasn't really hyped for it because I am not really into the arcade modes of RE. But after playing it, I have to say it was quite fun even though definitly not as fun as the campaign, also there are just 8 stages for it.

Fov: Yes, the game has a quite low fov and you can't change that ingame. You have to manually change that in a game file but I didn't do that. So many players complained because of the low fov and that they get motion sickness by playing this. Of course I can't say if they are saying the truth or not, but personally I never got motion sickness by playing a video game. I mean maybe I could get motion sickness with some VR games but with desktop games? Come on. And I easily get motion sickness when being in a car or bus and just reading a book. So, no I did not get motion sickness by playing RE8.
And overall I did not have a big problem with the low fov. You get used to it pretty quickly.

And a quick word about Re:Verse. I really don't get why Capcom still wants to give us those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RE MP games. Seriously, no one wants those. At least give us RE coop games but  not that. But for me personally, RE is about singleplayer, and very occasionally with coop.

Not Quite as Good as RE:7, but Still Very Good.

One of the few single-player games that's actually compelled to me to play it multiple times in a loong time. 

First, the things I really liked:

1.  The Presentation and Level Design.  It's hard to describe how well they did with this in words.  There were only 2 sections in the game where you would have a transition, otherwise the entire game flowed and revealed itself to you in a very organic way, which is amazing considering all of the insane places this game takes you to.  You're never lifted from one area and plopped onto another, you are fully with the protagonist at every moment (except those two transitions I mentioned).  Also the flow of the levels gives you a good sense of exploration without a lot of double-backing.  The RE developers are true masters of level design and bridging the levels together, imo.

2.  The Graphics.  The game looks amazing.  Even better than RE:7 somehow.  They really did a great job of using the RE Engine to play with the lights and shadows in the game to give you incredible moments of dread and wonder.  This game doesn't just look good, it looks "beautiful".

3.  The Voice Acting and Sound.  I mean, if you've seen the trailers you can hear it for yourself, and that top notch voice acting pretty much carries throughout the entire game (with one exception which I will address later).  The sound engineers also did an incredible job.  From the snap of a twig to a feint rustling of the leaves, there are so many great bits of sound all over the place.  Sometimes it's pleasure to just stand still and listen.

4. The Game is Very Polished.  I did not experience a single weird glitch or non-sense.  My immersion was never broken.  Granted, there are videos show glitches and wall breaks, but those are speed runners intentionally trying to break the game.  If you're just playing the game normally, it's a very tight and finished experience.

Now, there are a few things I didn't like in the game:

1.  One of the Characters is Unintelligible.  While overall voice acting is great, there is one character that is impossible to understand without subtitles, which is sad.   To have such great visuals, but be forced to focus your eyes on lines of text during that character's cutscenes (or worse if you already have subtitles turned off: to have no idea what he's saying at all).

2.  The Game Was Quite Short.  You can say the game is divided into 6 sections, the intro, the 4 main chapters, and the final fight.  The first chapter (the part they showed in the trailer) is about 40% of the game in terms of play time.  I really took my time tagging as many collectibles as I can, explored every side area, fully watched every cutscene, and enjoyed the view in my first play through, but it still only gave me about 15 hours of game. Intro (about an hour), Chapter 1 (about 7 or 8 hours), Chapter 2 and 3 together (about 2 hours), Chapter 4 (about 3 hours), The Conclusion is about 30 minutes.

Overall, the game is quite excellent.  It's not as creepy as RE7, but it's way more action oriented.   With the excellent graphics and sounds, it's a feast for your sense.  If you enjoy single player games this is one you don't want to pass up.

I am so blown away by how good this game is that I decided I should write a proper review. 

Gameplay: 4.5/5 

The first-person perspective, first pioneered for the series in RE7, adds tremendously to the atmosphere and overall horror of the game. Each area is themed and has its own quirks that are either call-backs to original entries in the series or straight-up references to other popular games in the horror genre. (Ethan's repeated beatings are reminiscent of Outlast 1 and 2 and I get serious Silent Hill Homecoming vibes from the Dollhouse). The return of the treasure, gun upgrade and the implementation of the cooking mechanic are more than welcome and bring back the flavor (no pun intended) of what made previous entries so wonderfully engaging. What's more, the return to form for the series' penchant for mind-bending puzzles is a welcome one - even if the puzzles are scarcely difficult, they are always satisfying.

The only thing that could make this a perfect 5 for me would be the inclusion of more nuance to the enemies. They are all basically just bullet-sponges in the outer world. I liked the idea in RE4 where specific tactics were required to take out some enemies. There also seems to be too -few- enemies to contend with. I don't want a constant stream of enemies, but I feel a little too crystalline in terms of safety for a survival horror game.

Design: 5/5

This is the most beautifully laid-out Resident Evil games in the franchise. I love that each area has a different take on horror and certain references to older titles. The character design of the enemies is fantastic and gruesome (loved the Dollhouse enemy and Lady Dimitrescu/Daughters). The environmental design is one of the best I've seen in any video game, let alone a Resident Evil. The design team has really outdid themselves in every aspect, from the treasures you unearth to the weapons you upgrade. 

Story: 4/5

This I may need to re-evaluate after completion (as of now I'm confronting Heisenburg). The narrative so far is deeper than any of the games historically, but the writing team still has a lot to learn about what makes a stellar story. That being said, and without spoilers, I will say that this is the strongest entry for story for the series - ever. However, it falls flat when it comes to meshing with previous entries, and the introduction of Chris into RE7 and his continued role in RE8 as a type of anti-hero/antagonist continues to vex and overall does not seem to serve the overarching story. 

Overall: 4.375/5

This entry is absolutely worth the full price tag. I have not enjoyed a Resident Evil like this since I played REmake 2 or Resident Evil 4. Where these are all very different entries, I have no doubt in my mind that Resident Evil Village will go down in history for fans in the same way Resident Evil 4 did: as an emergent outlier, trend-setter and love-letter to everything the series has come to mean to the player base.

Review contains spoilers in so far as I mention characters outside of Tall Floppy Hat Vampire Lady existing.

Overall the game is excellent.  That's all you really need to know at the end of the day, isn't it?

Complaints are to be had, though.  It could of used a lot less combat and a lot more horror.  They leaned to hard into "enemies are cool and not scary" as Lady D and Heisenberg are too milfy/dilfy to really come across as a threat and Moreau is just...pathetic and sad by design.  It's like reading a story about a Lovecraftian monster with teenage angst and low self esteem.  It...it uh...doesn't exactly bring terror to my heart.  Donna and her section are the closest thing you get to "horror" in this game but it lasts all of 20 minutes and it's over.  It's not only incredibly short but what goes on in this little horror segment is predictable.

The lack of horror is a nitpick, however, and the latter half of the game being combat-heavy is more of a personal preference.  The combat itself is surprisingly solid for a game like this and can have some tense moments of ammo conservation vs waves of constant enemies (depending your difficulty).  I just wish there was less of it.  It wasn't fun enough where I wanted to keep engaging and by the time I got to the last 1/4 of the game I actively just ran past encounters just because I couldn't be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ anymore.

The biggest actual flaw in the game is some cutscenes will have severe audio desync with even the most minor of FPS changes.  Running the whole game perfectly smoothly?  That's great.  Hit a cutscene where for a split second the FPS dropped so little that it was imperceptible?  Yeah the audio is going to snowball from lip movements not lining up to lines being spoken half a minute early.

And no.  This isn't an issue with "you must be running it on a potato with 10 FPS", the gameplay and cut scenes are smooth, the audio is just abominably done and I don't feel like spending an hour fiddling with whatever arcane eldritch setting will fix it though I've heard it's possible.

A very fun and super campy game. It's not as good as the Resident Evil 2 remake, but I think it's more fun than Resident Evil 7. RE7 nailed a very Amnesia-esque horror atmosphere that was legitimately scary, but for 8, Gameplay trumps atmosphere.

So I decided to wait before I make my review for when I complete the game fully. And now that I have fully 100% completed every challenge, bought and maxed out everything there is. I will now make a review.

First of. I absolutely love this game, it was so much fun to play through its unbelievable, I personally played through the story 25 times to complete everything because it was so fun, I do not regret playing it as much as I did. On to the game.

The story follows the protaganist Ethan Winters from the previous game. Resident Evil 7 or Resident Evil: Biohazard. Village takes place 3 years after the events of louisiana after Ethan escaped the bakers family with Mia. If you want to understand Village, I definitely recommend playing through Biohazard first. If not, then you'll kind of not understand what's happening and stuff.

The game overall is very well designed and the continuation of the story is just amazing. When I first saw the trailers, I was super hyped and so ready for it. It looked absolutely amazing. And when it finally released, it was even better than I expected. I am honestly out of words for how good this game was. There is so much more details that makes it look so realistic, and the way they make everything happen makes it feel like you're Ethan yourself. It's so good and amazing experience.

The puzzles and keysolving are kinda meh. I liked the ones in Biohazard way better. In Village there isn't much puzzles and stuff, there is a few. But those are simple and easy to find out how to solve, while Biohazard had a bit more difficult and more complex puzzles. But they're still pretty cool and fit the game.

The enemies are so much more cooler and stronger from the previous mold monster we had in Biohazard. The new Lycans being the most common mob in the game has so many different unique styles, some of them rush towards you and grab you, some use hammers and spiky sticks to kill you, some of them have bows which are really powerful, and all that sorts. There is other enemies and stuff, but can't really talk much about them since I don't want there to be any spoilers. Tho I can say, there is soooo many different enemies to fight against and they all have different abilites and styles of killing you.

The bosses are fun and cool to fight against, tho the 2nd boss fight is kind of boring, the 2nd part after the caste is just too easy and kind of boring to do. I really got tired of that place after my 3rd playthrough, but it's still one of the scariest parts of the game in  my opinion. All bosses are different and have different ways of killing then, tho most are just spamming them with bullets. You can easily run out of bullets if you're playing on either Hardcore or VoS (Village of the Shadows), with VoS being basically Madhouse from Biohazard.

The Difficulties. Casual is just for players that want to experience the story and not die all the time. Standard is for the players that want a hit of a challange. Hardcore is even harder challenge. And VoS (Village of the Shadows) is just pure pain and death, that is for the people that really want a hard challenge. Me myself played through Standard first and then worked my way up from there. VoS was my main focus, I even attempted to go through the whole game on VoS without taking any damage from enemies, or healing at all. It took around 10h to do but, it's definitely possible with the right weapons and items.

What do you do after you finish the game? Well, this is where the fun begins. Once you complete the game, you unlock the Bonuses where you have challange points, what those do is, in the Extra content shop, you can buy a new weapon or infinite ammo for a weapon, and another extra mode called The Mercenaries (more on that later). With challenge points you can buy a lot of different things, but before you can spend it all on infinite ammo and new weapons, you need to unlock it first. For new weapons you need to complete the game on a certain difficulty or get a certain rank on a another mode (The mercenaries). For infinite ammo you need to fully customize your weapons with all attachments (You can buy most from the merchant or find them in treasure chests hidden on the map) And you also need to fully upgrade your weapons to max power and efficiency. To do that you need to get something called Lei. Another thing you unlock is New Game+. And what that does, is it gives you all your weapons, items, money and all that sorts you had left from when you finished the game. Now how do you get New Game+?. It's simple. Once you defeat the final boss and complete the game, you get the option to save on a new slot. Now if you save and open that slot, you can choose a new difficulty and start all over again. Just this time, you have your weapons, items, ammo, and everything else you had from when you finished the game, it will be very useful to use those weapons on the hardest difficulty to kill the enemies faster and get through easier. Trust me, it will be very useful if you load a New Game+.

The currency. In the game when you progress and kill enemies, there is something called Lei, basically it's the currency you can use to upgrade your weapons and buy new items from the merchant. The best way to get Lei is to search treasures and sell those at the merchant, you can also kill enemies to get Lei there as well. Having a lot of Lei will be mostly used to fully upgrade weapons to get them infinite ammo. Other than that, you can just buy recipes for different ammo and explosives from the merchant, or healing items, ammo, or explosives itself for that matter.

The other mode. Once you finish the game and unlock the bonuses and go to content shop, you can buy The Mercenaries mode for 100 challenge points. Challenge points are easily earnt from completing challenges in the challenges menu, just find a challenge and get the points to buy it. Now the mode itself I didn't really like. There is a specific rank you need to get on all stages to unlock a certain weapon to 100% the game. For me, this mode took 13h of doing over and over again to get the weapon and complete the challenges for it, but it was worth it in the end. The mode is pretty simple and straight forward, you kill enemies for points and higher combo for even higher points. Those points is what you need for a rank, if you need to know the point amount you need to get that rank. Just load in a level and read the book on the left side when you spawn. The maps are different places of game and 2 of them are very difficult. It starts of easy, but gets harder and harder from there. Me personally had problems with the 3rd and 4th stage, since those are difficult to navigate and find enemies in time to keep your combo. All levels have a different amount of stages you need to go through before you can complete the level itself, don't worry about dying if you have enough points for the rank you want, it gives you the rank even if you die and you can move on with life. Tho the 4th stage has a challenge where it requires you to beat the whole level. The 1st level has 3 stages, the 2nd has 4, the 3rd has 2, and the 4th one has 5. The first 4 levels are put on casual difficulty, but once you finish those. You have to replay them again, but this time on VoS difficulty (The hardest). This is what is the hardest part and is what I personally struggled the most with. But good luck.

Overall. This game is absolutely amazing, and I'd definitely recommend   playing it whenever you can. I had so fun much playing through it and would love to see what they do next. I'll probably play through more just to have some fun. Try completing the game yourself, it's challenging and really fun to do. Tho it can be stressful and annoying some times. Just don't give up,  you'll get it eventually.

That's all I have to say about this game, and I hope to see more in the future. I can't wait for DLCS if they have that in store, but for now we'll just have to wait and see. :P

DISCLAIMER: I am not a fan of RE7 or its story, and the fact that it moved to first person. That being said...let's get on to the review.

Resident Evil Village is delightful call back to the game that made it so popular, RE4. 
RE4 is by far one of my favorite RE games for it's fun, action packed gameplay, intense moments, and many different weapons to use and upgrade. Resident Evil Village tries to captire that lightning that RE4 struck with, in a bottle, and on some levels, it's succeeded.

Pros:
 - Story feels more compelling and grand in scale than RE7. Has a lot of revelations that are important to the lore of the Resident Evil universe. 
 - Gameplay has more action without compromising on tense and creepy atmosphere. The gunplay is still slow by modern FPS standards, but definitely faster than RE7. Enemies get faster and harder with each increased difficulty level. Again, reminding me more of RE4
 -  Varied gameplay. The game has a stalking section, a walking simulator section, encourages exploration to find treasure and upgrade parts for weapons, action sections more on par with RE4. There's definitely  something here for everyone, and it feels natural, unlike RE6 where it felt like an bunch of different games put together and gave the game a disjointed feel.
 - Replayability. There's new game plus, more weapons to be bought and upgraded. Fully upgraded weapons get an infinitely ammo version. Getting accolades/achievements grant you points to purchase in a bonus store so you can make additional weapons available and their infinite ammo versions. Oh and Mercenaries mode, which is an arcade like mode that has you blasting monsters for points.

The bad

 - (Personal Opinion) Still in first person. RE2 Remake showed that horror can still work in third person. Plus, RE's pedigree is in third person. While I didn't mind it in Village, I would have liked a third person view option at least. Many games have done it in the past, why not this one?
 - Walking simulator section. This is where the game dips for me. I'm not a fan of walking simulator horror where all you do is play cat and mouse and can never fight back. There is an entire section (albeit short) dedicated to this kind of mechanic. Resident Evil 7 fast became one of my favourite games of all time, with how it mixed various styles of horror into one compelling, terrifying, heartbreaking narrative. I was so excited for a continuation of that story, and RE8 didn't disappoint. It feels like 7, but on a grander scale, and taking down the four lords - who each embody different horror tropes - was highly reminiscent of dispatching the Baker family. In fact, House Beneviento was perhaps the most shocked and scared I've ever been by a video game. You might just want to wear a diaper for that level.

As has been well documented - by the developers, no less - Resident Evil 4 is also a palpable influence, mainly in its European mountain setting, its treasure hunting and merchant system and situations in which you barricade yourself in a house while fending off unholy hordes. It's a delight to watch the clockwork way in which the game unfolds, allowing you to access new areas of the village as you acquire new items and abilities. It almost feels like an open world or Metroidvania title in that regard.

That said, the game does lose some steam after the halfway mark - around the time you defeat Moreau. Things take another dip into action horror, which was a welcome thematic shift towards the end of RE7 but kind of outstays its welcome in RE8. The factory is foreboding but becomes a bit of a chore to navigate (props to its freakish Silent Hill-esque mini-boss though) and culminates with a ridiculous OTT fight sequence that feels like it belongs in the dreadful RE6. Things improve for the last boss though, and I had something in my eye during the final scenes. There were some big shocks and revelations, mainly around how RE8 ties into the wider Resident Evil story.

I haven't decided if it tops RE7 yet, but it's a terrific title in its own right. If you liked the previous game, this is an essential, no-brainer purchase. If you didn't like RE7, this *might* convince you otherwise with its more diverse cast and heavier action focus - plus there are also zombie-esque enemies again, which seems to be a deal-breaker with so many fans. I can't wait to see how 9 continues the story - it's got a hell of a lot to live up to.

The best way of describing Resident Evil Village is that it's all the best aspects of Resident Evil 4 combined with the best of Resident Evil 7.

That is a big deal to me because Resident Evil 4 is not only my favorite game in the Resident Evil series, but also one of my favorite games, period. Or it was until I played Resident Evil Village. While Ethan Winters is no Leon S. Kennedy, Village is truly the spiritual successor to RE4 and an absolutely perfect blend of horror and action.

I will admit RE7 was a bit (or a lot) too terrifying for me, but a return to the survival horror roots of Resident Evil with a switch to a first person perspective made it a great game. Village tones down the horror enough to still have terrifying moments without feeling like you're constantly about to have a heart attack, and ups the action with a lot more guns and a merchant, The Duke, to buy and upgrade those weapons a la RE4. If RE4 was your jam but RE7 was a bit much, give Village a try.

Lastly, I rarely, if ever, finish or replay a game in my library. At the time of this review, I have beaten Village five times so far and have started my sixth playthrough. Yup.

I don't know. I'm a huge RE fan. I just finished beating the RE3 remake on the hardest difficulty (insane mode or whatever), and even though the remakes also felt kinda clunky, I still found myself engaged the entire time without too much repetitive gameplay. With this one, not so much. Maybe it's the setting--I wasn't really a fan of 4, either, it's so gray and dull and depressing. Graphics:  8/10 
RE8 looks good. The textures do look alike in a number of areas but they keep a realistic feel and I don't expect Resident Evil to look cartoonish any time soon. Still, titles such as RE4 and RE2 remake have textures that work so well together without looking cartoonish. 

Level Design: 5/10 
RE8's level design connects paths and makes shortcuts at the player's convenience at all times.  It becomes almost comical how often a short cut will practically create itself for Ethan Winters. In some games this is fun. In RE8 it feels stupid.

Gameplay: 5/10
You simply point and click when you need to kill something. Each gun has it's effective damage output and cool down reload. The way enemies react to gun play has much to be desired. Enemies often tank bullets like they are pellet gun ammo and you get so much ammo to use. This doesn't add to the the difficulty thankfully because most enemies move at a crawl, but playing is boring with no sense of peril. QUICK REVIEW. MAY CONTAIN LIGHT SPOILERS. 

Resident Evil is my favorite gaming franchise of all time. The anticipation for 8 was almost so high that I was worried it wouldn't come close to my expectations, but thankfully, its another solid entry into this franchise, following the excellent 7. 

If straightforward Horror is more your cup of tea, you might be slightly bummed out with this offering. Its not completely devoid of scares, and is packing some excellent jumps, but for those looking for a regularly uneasy atmosphere, you probably won't find it here. There is one smaller portion of the game that focuses more on Horror, and it excels greatly for that brief moment, but unfortunately its short run time and odd placement can bog down replays of the main story. 

Puzzle wise, this game s*its the bed. I would be lying to say they aren't in the game, but whats on offering here is trivial at best, and far from the old days of Resident Evil brain busters. Its no secret that puzzles in RE games fell to the wayside after 2005's Resident Evil 4, but with the series having what almost resembles a  soft reboot of more old-school Survival Horror in RE7, I still feel its worth mentioning here as a let down. 

For difficulty, I highly suggest starting on Hardcore instead of Normal or Casual. I did my first run on Standard and deeply regret it, even going as far as to avoid crafting items or upgrading guns to try and create more of a challenge. If Survival Horror is what you're here for, start on Hardcore. 

A few other small gripes include some poor item interaction (some items do NOT what to be picked up/ interacted with), a story that is, for the most part strong, but goes a little too far off the rails in the last quarter, the writing included. In my opinion, the game regains its posture in the last few minutes, buts the stumbles are still worth mentioning. 

Finally, lets talk about the positives. 

The REngine games have all been shining beacons of great optimization, generally playing very well on the beefiest and budget PC's alike. I don't know how they pull it off, but the engine is very worth of praise. It looks fantastic, sometimes even photo-realistic, and besides the odd muddy texture, some semi-common pop in and strange framerate interactions, I am happy to say that this is a fantastic engine and one that I cant wait to see other games made on in the future. 

Gun play is also very good, feeling just agile enough for the amount of enemies, but just clunky enough to cause stress when missing shots on the games assortment of enemies. You have access to quite a few weapons thanks to the game having multiple versions of most guns that look and play slightly differently, and they always feel great to shoot. Weapons can also be upgraded with mods found from exploring the village and browsing the merchants shop, as well as things like damage, reload speed, fire rate ect. being upgrades the merchant will apply for you, for a fee of course. 

Speaking of the Merchant, he is a very present character in RE8, allowing you to sell treasures found exploring, upgrade weapons as previously stated, buy/ sell supplies, and even cook you food with performance enhancing capabilities. Yes, on top of being an arms dealer, the merchant is a top-tier cook, who is more than happy to make you all sorts of delicacies, provided you go out and kill the different animals need for the meals yourself. I won't comment much more on the merchant, as he is one of the better characters in the game, and should be experienced with as little information as possible in my opinion. 

Once the credits roll, the amount of replay potential, as per usual with this franchise, is through the roof. Unlocking achievements in RE8 grants you points to spend on in this games "Bonus content" shop, and after the first run through the story you can unlock the series famous Mercenaries mode, a time-trial gauntlet of enemies for you to combo through with increasingly powerful weapons. On top of Mercs, you also gain the ability to purchase Figures, Art and my personal favorite, powerful new weapons and unlimited ammunition variants of those weapons, along with old ones too. These can be carried into your next story runs, and make replaying the game again a blast. 

I beat the game 3 times myself, first time on Standard, second on Hardcore and third on the brutal Village of Shadows mode, and I will probably start speed run attempts sooner than later. 

Overall I highly suggest looking into Village. It was well worth the money, and I can't wait to see what Capcom pulls off with RE9 in the future. I would say this is a solid 8/10. 

Thanks for reading and feel free to let me know if this was at all helpful, cheers!

TL;DR As a Resident Evil fan who has played all the games since the original, I can safely say that this is a must-play not just for any RE fan but any horror game fan in general. I'll go as far as to say that this might arguably even be the best RE game ever made.

I will try to keep this review spoiler free but there still might be some things that certain people may consider spoiler material. I waited to write this review till I had experienced everything the game has to offer. Now that I have gotten all achievements, completed all in-game challenges, received max rank on all Mercenaries stages and unlocked every reward in the game, I do believe I can give you a review based on a complete experience.

So starting off I'll be the first to say that I was very skeptical after seeing all the promotional material for the game, wondering what werewolves, vampires, witches, ghosts, magic etc. are doing in a Resident Evil game. But long story short: there is nothing supernatural in the game, everything has a logical explanation. For example, the werewolves are just a type of mutation caused by a parasite, that makes humans gain animal characteristics. So if you had any concerns there then do not worry, this is nothing new to RE.

Now that we got that out of the way, important to mention is that Village puts a way bigger focus on horror than any other RE game has done so far. This is partially thanks to the First Person perspective which players may be unfamiliar with as most of the recent REs have been over the shoulder third person but I feel like this is the perfect style for a more horror focused RE as you will never know what is behind you. This works perfectly with the next topic which is the sound design.

This is the thing I personally was the most impressed with. The grass moving in the wind, footstep noises, growls, all of these sound so natural and I've never heard a game do such a good job with sound design, and trust me I've played a lot of AAA games. The random noises will make you jump naturally without it feeling forced as enemies may be lurking closeby without you even realising it.

Probably needlessly said the visuals are incredibly impressive and without a doubt one of the best in the business but more importantly the RE engine manages to deliver them with minimal system requirements. In my 50 hours of playtime on max settings the game did not crash or even stutter once and everyone who I have talked to also said they are impressed with how much they improved the technical aspect of it over RE7.

The gameplay is challenging but rewarding. There are plenty of optional areas to explore, treasures to discover, puzzles to solve and even hidden bosses to find. It will definitely make you reminisce of RE4. Every time you return to an area you may even find something new so backtracking is encouraged. Speaking of challenge, there is a difficulty for every type of player but for your first playthrough (especially if you are like me and love taking your time exploring every room and just taking it all in at a slow pace) I highly recommend going with Standard or even Casual if you don't have much experience with FPS games as higher difficulties can be quite tough (they are mostly designed for a second playthrough as enemies have a lot of extra hp and yes, there is a new game+ option). There's also tons of replay value here with challenges and many unlockable rewards, that will give you reason to go through the game over and over again.

And speaking of replaying, The Mercenaries makes its return in Village and is as fun as ever even though different than what we have seen in RE4/5/6. This time around the mode has a more mission based style a lot like the original Mercenaries from RE3. It almost feels like Capcom is making up for not including Mercenaries in the recent remake of RE3 and they do an amazing job at it. Challenging stages will keep you coming back and working your way up the ranks, unlocking rewards along the way to eventually get that top SSS rank.

As for the story, it is a direct sequel to Resident Evil 7 and these two games form kind of a substory in the RE universe but it does also tie into the rest of RE story in a quite surprising way. And I have to say it definitely is the best story a RE game has ever seen, by far. Without going into detail, it will keep you guessing and on the edge throughout and till the very end.

For anyone who is completely new to Resident Evil: I do recommend getting the "Resident Evil Village & Resident Evil 7 Complete Bundle" here on Steam and play through Resident Evil 7 first and then Resident Evil Village for the full experience as these two games are directly connected. Needlessly said there are many more RE games but if you don't have the time to go through all of them before Village then RE7 would be the best starting point.

My one and only complaint about the game is regarding the voice acting and that is not to say that it is bad, it is actually great but there is one big problem. If you are planning to play the game then I suggest NOT reading this part till you actually beat the game, especially if you have played the recent RE3 remake. Why you may ask? Quite simply because you might NOT even notice the issue. [spoiler]Capcom hired a few of the same voice actors they did for RE3 remake and I would have no issues if they played minor characters but that is not the case for Jeff Schine who plays both Carlos and Chris, as well as Neil Newbon who plays both Nicholai and Heisenberg. All of these are leading characters in their respective games and hearing two different main characters of the same franchise have the same voice does break the immersion to a certain extent. If you have not played RE3 remake this will not be a problem for you and even if you have played it, this may not even bother you but it did bother me quite a bit during my playthrough. It is by no means a deal breaker but just feels a bit lazy of Capcom not to search for more actors.[/spoiler]

In conclusion: the game is most easily described as a mix of two of the most beloved titles in the Resident Evil franchise: Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7. The gameplay part is a lot like RE4 and the visuals and feel of it is a lot like RE7 so if you enjoyed either of those two titles, you are very likely to love the newest entry in the franchise.

It is a very well done level and is a very traditional RE level with many enemies, puzzles, and eventually, a patrolling MR X type in the form of Lady D.  Next you have the dollhouse area and the dollhouse basement is by far to me the most disturbing and scary moments in all of RE. This review contains SPOILERS for Resident Evil Village.

Resident Evil Village is Resident Evil 7 but in a European setting and with much more gun-play (and questionably improved). Just like Resident Evil 7, it is not a “Resident Evil” game but a FPS with the namesake slapped on top and just so happens to include Chris Redfield for a bit. It is visually stunning with some interesting designs for the characters and environment, including some of the best moving water graphics I have ever seen. If you like good visuals and FPS then you will like this game.

STORY TIME

The story is really, REALLY poor. The characters are not developed in any intriguing way. Dimitrescu is pretty much sadistic “MILF” vampire mommy and her daughters are just there. Then we have the puppet master lady who is the obligatory “feel bad for me” backstory character. Moreau is meant to be a pitiful/annoying character. Heisenberg is actually the only interesting character in the game with potential but was completely neglected. Ethan (Bradberry) Winters gets some development as the father of Rose but honestly, they tried to pull off a Subject Delta and Eleanor from Bioshock 2 which did it much better. Then we got mother Miranda who basically is Ultimecia’s final form from Final Fantasy 8 and nothing else. But hey! Apparently she is SUPER important because Oswell E. Spencer was her student and he was inspired to create the Umbrella Corporation due to her. Yeah. Fun and developed lore, all discovered from toilet paper notes scrambled throughout the game. Enjoy!

GAMEPLAY

The gameplay is literally RE7 with just different enemies and more ammunition. The merchant from RE4 is back as an obese aristocrat and bosses are all the same with reskins: bullet sponges. That is all about gameplay. Puzzles were “find X and put it in Y”.

CONCLUSION

Is the game good? Not really. There is no story, there is no fun factor since everything is just a sponge reskinned, visuals are great and sound design is not bad. Should you buy it? If you find it for £15 or £20 and like FPS zombie games it is alright. Full price is totally a disgrace for what they are actually selling.

I think some of the best Resident Evil titles are those who tend to pull away from a previous game's style and themes. Resident Evil was an amazing survival horror game, Resident Evil 4 was also amazing, updating the controls and combat mechanics of the game. Resident Evil 7 was great because it felt like they were taking the better aspects from all the games and returning to that old creepy horror vibe.

	Resident Evil 8, for all intents and purposes just feels like Resident Evil 7, just with a change of scenery. The problem with that scenery is that it largely matches very closely to the same as RE7.

	Many of the mechanics are the same, there's some sort of twisted family and you have to deal with them. They even roam the halls looking for you like in RE7, although their hunting mechanics don't feel good, they generally just pace around in specific areas and that's about it. 

	There's also a stupid amount of backtracking in this game. The world may feel very big, but that's because it's built like a rat maze. If it were built more organically like an actual village and castle, transversing the grounds would be far too easy and quick.

	There are some puzzles I really don't like, the best example being the stupid fish boss in which you are trying to drain the lake. You have to move these levers in order to raise platforms out of the water so you can walk on them. But they have a timer and will sink after a few seconds. It's incredibly frustrating and if you aren't perfect on your execution, you won't survive. 

	Is Resident Evil 8 good? It's an okay game and I had fun playing it. Is it a great game? No. Is it better than RE7? Absolutely not. It feels like a copy cat trying to recapture the success of the previous game.

When I found out your stuff carries over to a new game, I decided to try the standard difficulty level, needless to say the game is so difficult that I cannot play it. The aim assist feature the game offers also apparently gets turned off, even when you turn it on with this difficulty as well. Okay, so first things first. Not everyone is going to be a fan of this one, just like not everyone was a fan of 7. That's the pitfall with long series, and that's what Resident Evil has been since 5. A long, multi-entry series constantly trying new things.

So what did they try new for this entry? Not much. Not much at all.

Is that a bad thing? No, it's not. Because they picked and chose what worked from the older games in the series and put it together in what is very obviously a labor of love. So, to put this in the simplest terms.

If you liked the original third game with its bullet crafting system, the fourth games attache case, gun customization, limited chase and hide mechanics, and most of all...big tiddy vampire mommy gf...you'll like the mechanics of this game.

If you enjoyed the more human tone that Ethan brought to the series by not being a full on superhero (but an obvious damn freak) and some time away from what was considered 'the main cast', you will enjoy this also. It teases at the main lore and story of Resident Evil Earth, while being disconnected just enough that it feels fresh. All the way up until the end, in which...the connections become way more apparent, and not in a bad way.

Overall, get this game. If not just for the new mercenaries mode which works so well with all the new blocking, first person, and upgrade mechanics.

Despite [i]Resident Evil: Village[/i] perhaps having the best integration of roman numerals I’ve ever seen, It's a wonder that this game isn’t called [i]Resident Evil 4: 2: Village[/i] may as well be wearing the skin of RE4, yet it pinches ideas from all over the franchise. And by no means am I complaining. [i]Village[/i] is an amazing action horror game, and although it doesn’t quite hit on all of the potential found in the franchise, it’s still a heartfelt tribute to every game in the series.

[h1]A VILLainous Setting[/h1]
[i]Village[/i] has a decent plot hook that carries the game along fine, but the events are  serviceable purely for gameplay. [i]Village[/i] delivers finely on most of its initial ideas, but there are some odd plot elements introduced fairly late into the narrative I didn’t entirely mesh with, and remain under-developed by the finale, likely an intentionally inconclusive incident to set the stage for sequels. It’s not an impactful or well thought out narrative, but it's not to be expected from this series.

I found the file system felt stronger than ever in this title, and helped fuse the large jumps between each major area of the game. The village feels greatly developed through the perspectives of many citizens encountering the horrors that now inhabit their world. Likewise, each villainous foe serves as a great archetypal horror to confront, all of them given detailed attention to ensure their phenomenons fit naturally within the established universe, interesting yet optional information welcome for the players who seek it. 

The excellence of the characters carrying the story make up for its mediocre content. Ethan, once again, is a fantastic everyman, who fits right in as a catalyst for the player, as he conveys his initial inability to fight and eventual chaotic actions beautifully. He delivers some amazingly cringey one liners from time to time, but after all the suffering you experience with him, the lines feel earned in a cathartically relieving way. 

Each villain too, brings a great energy to their respective section of the game, paying homage to various famed horror movies along the way. They feel a lot more detached than say, The Baker Family’s shared antics, but it's enjoyable how they sell their unique chapters of the game. Heisenberg's unexpectedly immature and stylish energy was probably my personal favourite, but each provides their own fascinating appeal to explore.

It’s hard to talk about the visuals while keeping it brief, but let me assure that this game is simply phenomenal looking. The gothic european setting is perfect, and adds a haunting snow stained ambiance to every area you traverse. Each area has its own carved visual identity, from the grandiose yet hauntingly abandoned Castle to the diabolical horrors of the Factory serving as [i]Resident Evil’s[/i] best commitment to an industrial finale. All of this is enhanced by jaw dropping modern graphical features such as RTX lighting and incredible textures, all of which are optimised for performance to create a jaw-dropping world of beauty.

[h1]The “RE” Formula Returns[/h1]
As per the previous entry, the gunplay here is pretty fantastic. [i]Village[/i] is more action focused, so your access to a larger arsenal is appreciated greatly when facing large numbers of vampires and werewolves, embodied with brilliant advanced A.I. There are some very prominent returns to RE4’s formula, such as the weapons being managed through a merchant, and the tetris-like inventory. These offer a lot of player customization in terms of what weapons you want by your side throughout [i]Village,[/i] and it’s great to see these mechanics implemented into a game with such responsive shooting.

The invincible stalkers found throughout the franchise are another returning mechanic, although they don’t quite feel as fleshed out in this entry. Dimistrecu and her daughters are completely invulnerable to damage and can body block you into corners, a far cry from the refined balance of fear and strategy that Mr.X and Nemesis gave us. The stalkers are such a small throwaway part of the game this time as well, it seemed this mechanic could’ve been used by Heisenburg or even Moraeu, but alas, their absence in this regard was a tad disappointing.

Whereas RE has traditionally had a tumultuous relationship with boss encounters, I have to say they were pretty fun here. None of them blew me out of the water, and there are still a couple mediocre entries, but they were all engaging, with each boss's mechanics well communicated. I liked the scale and awe of these encounters too, while they’re still just the dodge and shoot formula, some of them felt massively destructive and satisfying to fight.

However, one classic RE element that feels lacking are the puzzles. I like that  there’s no irritating ones blocking progression, but what has been implemented are mostly just brief hindrances. The hidden ball labyrinths were a fantastic addition, even if they’re just for a cash reward, it would’ve been nice to see a couple more secrets like that.

Returning to the titular village after every climactic encounter makes for some great quiet time. I appreciated how many secrets were hidden in this village, opening up a little bit more with each visit. I wished other open areas had gotten this treatment, but most areas in the game will be locked off from the player upon leaving them. I’d advise fully exploring each area until you’re truly content with it, as the phenomenal environmental design holds many uncoverable delights.

[h1]REplayability[/h1]
[i]Resident Evil[/i] has a tendency to prioritise replayability over length, however that's not the focus here. There are still some excellent ideas such as upgrading your weapons via the shop and slowly building an absolute powerhouse Ethan over each playthrough, tackling enemies with gradual ease. However I do wish this upgrade system was a bit less linear, there's no logical reason to use the early weapons once you’ve got the endgame guns, lest you merely want to impose custom challenges on yourself.

The in-game achievements make a return in the vein of RE3’s completion points allowing you to buy items of your own choosing. There's not much to buy that affects the gameplay unfortunately, as well as very few “challenge runs” to attempt, but there were still a couple fantastic surprises, and a plethora of behind the scenes content that made ploughing through this treasury more than worth it.

One of these treasures is the revival of The Mercenaries, a game that's been missing from the RE franchise for 9 years, finally making a glorious return. Reincorporating the environments from the game into enemy gauntlets gives you a satisfying mastery over the forces that once taunted you, and turns the game into something closer to [i]DOOM[/i]. New additions such as abilities and the shop make this interpretation of The Mercenaries really stand out from its predecessors, providing a great amount of customization to get plenty of mileage out of this bonus.

When it comes to the campaign’s replayability, it's still very fun to return to, but it does feel a bit mismanaged. I found myself missing the higher difficulties that changed the formula in interesting ways, particularly Madhouse mode in [i]Resident Evil 7[/i]. [i]Village’s[/i] hard mode equivalent still provides plenty of fun with it’s stricter ammo management and brutal enemies, but it has no major overhauls to surprise the player. Likewise, although some areas of the game are packed with more than enough secrets and challenges to warrant multiple playthroughs, the middle of the game hinders replays by being far too restrictive, as certain encounters will always play out identically no matter the player's actions.

[h1]8/10[/h1]
[i]Village[/i] is undeniably a fantastic title and a great homage to the series. A couple rough spots aside, I cannot recommend it enough as a worthy sequel to this ever evolving franchise.

RE8 is a beautiful and fun game to play but as of writing (5/22/2021) has numerous glitches and issues that ruin the experience. Although I have beaten the game in HC mode without a guide, explored the hell out of it and enjoyed it somewhat, overall I am pretty disappointed with the experience. 

TLDR; Overall, it's NOT a Cyberpunk, but its still a rushed release that could've been better. Definitely not worth 80 dollars.

1.) NO MATTER WHAT YOU DO, You may have constant stutters and sometimes crashes in many of the game areas. This is shown in cutscenes (Village visits, Castle fights, Places where the Vampire sisters spawn, etc.), sections of the game and will even CRASH your Mercenaries game in the Mad Village Sections and the like. No amount of setting changes will fix this, and it may or may not hit your PC. A lot of users with high-end rigs have the same issues. Fix still needed, and Capcom is VERY SILENT on it. Same feeling as the first month when RE7 released and the SSE issue prevented players from progressing through the sewer in the game and it took the devs such a long time to release a fix.

- I will state, however, that as a scumbag way of winning, the FPS tanking randomly from 50-60 to 15-25 during certain cutscenes and actual boss fights did help me easily beat the enemies. Knifing and blocking so EZ when you can see them coming XD :D 

2.) THE GAME DESYNCS and SLOWS DOWN in cutscenes, too. Imagine trying to play the story mode in slowmo with Lady Demitrescu lol and wait for almost 5 mins just for a cutscene to finish. Good view,but no, its horrible. Pressing ESC and waiting for the sound to catch up works for a second or two, but after that, nope. No Capcom fix either.



3. Fight-wise, the game itself is fun in terms of the overall fluid fighting and gunplay mechanics, but the Merchant system / Duke's Emporium is CRAP compared to the RE4 it was paying homage to. There are limited amount of guns (3 pistols in first story run, 3 shotguns, ONLY 1 SNIPER RIFLE ATM WTF, 2 magnums in the base story and plus the end-game unlockables. Which is awfully limited.) 

Worst of all, not all guns are fully customizable, and WHEN YOU DO FULLY UPGRADE THE GUN THERE IS NO SPECIAL unlock like extra crit, firepower, piercing, etc. Very limited at best.

4.) Content-wise? Story is nice, but.... I kinda hoped they wouldve fleshed out the characters and plotlines more. As much as I hate to say it, Resident Evil Village and the newer ones in general do poorly in this aspect. Going back to RE1, 2, 3 in the PSone days and to Code Veronica and Outbreak, they all had lore tidbits in the environment and you can interact with a lot of things too and feel really immersed in the story. See a table? Unusual device? Your character could go to it and you can see his/her thoughts when you interact. RE8 barely has that, probably just in the initial part of coming into the village. Not immersive at all.

A lot of lore was left out. Questions unanswered that only DLC (Hoping they dont charge you to the teeth for it) would most likely remedy.

- Settings also are lacking at the moment. No FOV slider, so some may experience really uncomfortable motion sickness issues. Mods are available to circumvent this for now.

5.) THE POST GAME CONTENT THEY PROMISED YOU ABOUT THE MERCENARIES? IT IS A DAMN DISAPPOINTMENT. For one, so many bugs. Worse off, is that IT IS [u]NOT the mercenaries I wanted at all. You are dropped into a "stage" or part of the game to eliminate a SET amount of enemies that at many points, WILL ONLY SPAWN IF YOU TRIGGER THEM by running there or activating an invisible condition (kill everything else in another area). Sounds simple, right? No, its not. You can literally play so well by killing things so quickly, but YOU CAN MISS AN S or SS RANK just because ONE CREATURE did not spawn or was hit and there is NO INDICATOR where it is.

Sure, you get a merchant and you can pick what you want to use on Mercs before going into a session, but its super limited! In fact, its a joke, really. Situations arent as interestingly varied to present much need of a diverse loadout. You can't customize them as fully as you would want, either.

Overall, it's NOT a Cyberpunk, but its still a rushed release that could've been better. It's a nice game, BUT DEFINITELY NOT WORTH 80 CAD. You'll waste your money if you think it is like I did after playing it. Wait for a sale. A really big sale. Until then, it unfortunately breaks my heart to not recommend a title from my favorite series to other people at the moment. 

Hopefully they don't charge to the teeth for new ones and better features.

I WONT HIDE THAT. GOD. Waste of 80 CAD, that one.) and have finished almost all of them in all kinds of platforms except the pachinko ones. RE fan since the dawn of time here. RE: Village is a very good game, and at times feels the most departed game from the rest of the franchise, while also having many classic RE moments. It is RE4 + RE7 on the surface. Obviously, the characters and camera angle from RE7 are here, so it feels like that and a lot of the mechanics work like in RE4, like the locations themselves, enemies dropping loot, merchant, etc. So it has more horror elements than 4, and more action than 7, and the balance is fairly decent. There are different parts of the game where the action and horror are in different amounts so it almost feels like you are playing a variety of different games, which keeps the game fresh. The atmosphere is great. I felt the pacing of the game a little bit fast personally, but given the length of the game, I think it is well-paced. The game length is more than the last few titles, but as it is always with resident evil games, I always end up wanting more game length.

[b] Locations/environments [/b]
All the environments in the game are great. Each environment acts great for the mood or other tone of the current part of the game and doesn't feel just there, it adds to the vibe. The village itself is nice, and there are many things to find and explore, you can miss out on a lot of optional stuff, like [spoiler] treasures and new weapons [/spoiler] apart from the ammo and supplies. The castle is also very great, though feels a little short. [spoiler] The factory part was also very well done, it reminded me of the lab areas from the original 90s games and island from RE4. [/spoiler]

[b] Story [/b]
The story is good for a resident evil game. There is enough mystery to keep you going throughout. The last hour or so of the game was a little bit off for me, mainly due to story reasons, but everything else is amazing apart from that. It ties up to earlier games in some interesting ways, and playing RE7 is highly recommended before playing this. There might be some questions left unanswered at the end, but that happens a lot in these games, I hope they explain some stuff in the sequels/DLC.

[b] Gameplay [/b]
The gameplay is very fun. Each section of the game is done very well and is different from the others, which prevents it from getting repetitive. The gunplay is satisfying enough and easy to get good at, but there are tense moments in the game that will test you sometimes. Choosing what weapon/side weapon to use and when is also a big thing and fun to do, and can make fights from easy to very tough. Weapon upgrades, ammo crafting, and [spoiler] hunting [/spoiler] are all basic and good enough to keep you busy. Exploration is important in this game and can help you a lot down the road in tougher parts.

[b] Enemies [/b]
The basic enemies are good and reminded me of the Ganados from RE4 in how they hunt in coordinated packs and can use basic weapons. They are kinda hard and intimidating at first, like all good enemies. I wish there was a little more enemy variety among the regular enemies. On paper, there is a decent variety, but some of them felt very similar, like [spoiler] the dungeon zombies in the castle and the ones outside Benevientos house [/spoiler]. The boss fights are all good, and on higher difficulties can be challenging.

I wanted each section of the game to be slightly longer so that a maybe 10-11 hour playthrough could become 13 hour-ish.

Visually it is the best-looking resident evil game. On my relatively weaker PC, playing on low settings, it still looks amazing, I can only imagine what it looks like at max settings with RTX. There were huge frame rate drops while fighting against certain enemies when they got very close. That said, the environments are really great, especially at the beginning and at the end of the game. The overall setting and the atmosphere are the games' greatest assets.

For what the game is, I'd give it 9.5/10. I am a big fan of the franchise, so maybe that makes it slightly biased. Less horror and more action than 7, but unlike RE3 remake, it didn't feel bad. And I did not miss the slow-burn horror of 7 as much. If you are a fan of the series, then definitely play it. Even otherwise a very very good action-survival horror game.

Honestly, I could probably give this a thumbs up if I was feeling generous - it looks good enough to make even the dull sections entertaining, and there's some fun puzzle-solving and gunplay that pops up. But the overwhelmingly positive reception blows my mind, so I'm going to give a thumbs down just to counterbalance everything. This game has a lot of problems, and the "RE7 + RE4" sales pitch is 100% not accurate.

Here's the fundamental issue with this game: It's basically a walking simulator, even during the firefights. Half of the time, you'll just be stumbling through an environment, solving some pretty straightforward puzzles, and occasionally an unkillable pursuer will appear to annoy you. There are very few "fodder" enemies to deal with, and the ones that do pop up go down incredibly fast. Combine this with a relatively weak amount of enemy variety, a giant inventory where healing and crafting items don't take up space, and the ability to create or buy ammo on demand, and there's just no challenge. None, whatsoever. 

I promise, I'm not some stuck-up purist who needs this to be an extremely punishing horror experience where you're always moments from death; my favorite game in the series is RE4, for goodness' sake. But RE4 still had me worried at times, whereas this game is almost comically free of any real tension. This is especially true during the "boss" fights, which are one step above a QTE. There's nothing more disappointing than watching a massive mutated freak of a creature burst through a wall, scream about killing you... and then stumble slowly around a small room while your absolute idiot of a protagonist fires potshots while walking backwards and doesn't take a single hit. It's just hard to believe any of these villains are a serious threat to you or anyone else when they all seem incapable of doing more than just slowly following you while you shoot them repeatedly in the head.

And this really ties back to another issue, which is that Ethan Winters is an idiot. An absolute idiot. He talks like an idiot, he makes idiotic choices, and he seems totally incapable of understanding what's going on. It's annoying on its own, but it's especially jarring to see this guy who seems to have the intelligence and common sense of a 12 year-old essentially breeze through the game without any worries. You can have an average guy for a protagonist who is constantly struggling, or a super-capable guy who gives you a power fantasy. But you can't have both, and at some point all the tension disappears as a result.

Like I said, the game isn't awful - there are some really cool setpiece encounters, some fun puzzles, and the gunplay is solid. But the entire thing feels more like a haunted house than anything that would really terrify you. And without the scares, the gunplay isn't enough to pick up the slack. After all these RE4 comparisons, I went back and played it to make sure I wasn't misremembering. But sure enough, I had killed more enemies, taken more damage, and just been more excited in the first half hour than I was through this entire game. Maybe if you're a big fan of RE7, this will be a better fit, but I was really disappointed.

(Also, not to "get political" or whatever, but man does this game have some problems with women - every character seems to be some kind of sexy and/or disfigured woman who is battered or killed in horrible ways. I didn't have any, like, "feminist issue" with it, but it got to the point where I really didn't want to keep living out some weird Capcom employee's repressed fantasies. RE4 had some really fun weird stuff, but this is just... gross.)

The gameplay is much more fast-paced and action-oriented than say RE2, RE3, and even RE7. Regardless of how you feel about this shift in pace, one area where the game excels is creating an atmospheric world, that makes you feel isolated and watched at the same time. 

In terms of negatives, I'd say the default keyboard controls are a bit convoluted (especially for the menus),
and that this game feels like it could've been its own thing, rather than an RE game. But I understand why Capcom wouldn't want to give their own horror series competition.

After watching an RE7 playthrough and seeing what that entry did with the series, I got more interested in trying a game, and so was looking forward to the next game. Resident Evil Village, with its gothic horror and slavic folklore inspirations, was right up my alley! I almost couldn't not buy it.

And disappoint it did not, the setting of this game was truly amazing! The titular village with its patron saint and four lords create such a living atmosphere despite the horror creeping beyond every corner. Every major area in the game had a unique look and feel to it, and the atmosphere throughout the game was absolutely amazing!

The story is nothing too deep, but has enough mystery about it to keep things interesting from start to end. The protagonist was a bit annoying, but never got in the way of me enjoying the game. At some point groaning at this stupid comments became just another part of the experience.

The gameplay is a healthy mix between puzzles, combat, and running for your life. The puzzles (with one incredibly silly exception [spoiler]"No you're supposed to [i]shoot[/i] those fire chandeliers of course!"[/spoiler]) were pretty good and provided a nice change of pace. There was enough variety of guns to keep the combat interesting, and having to scrounge for ammo led to some interesting moments where I had to switch to guns I was less familiar with.

There were a couple of minor bugs, but nothing game-breaking. One did make me reload an earlier save, but luckily that wasn't too long ago (save points are common enough if you think to use them). The other made me miss out on some buffs because the game wasn't very clear what I could do with certain items, only explaining it after I had already sold them with no way of getting it back. Both of these were more minor annoyances than anything that really ruined (parts of) the game for me.

With tons of collectibles, in-game challenges, achievements, and the bonus store where you can buy bonuses and special content after finishing the game once, all lead towards a ton of replayability! I beat the game this week, and am now already on my third playthrough.

Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game, despite some minor hiccups. If you're at all interested in playing a horror game, Resident Evil Village certainly is an enjoyable experience!

I can't recommend this game enough. The "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews are very much deserved (its not just because of the 8 foot tall dominatrix hunting you down I promise).

tl;dr 
Village is a fantastic singleplayer horror experience. The story kept me hooked despite being a newcomer to Resident Evil. The gameplay is satisfying but not dark souls hard. The bonus content is also just as, if not more, fun than the main game. I highly recommend it.

This game is a continuation of the "Ethan Winters" story from Resident Evil 7. Village is quite friendly to newcomers to the Resident Evil franchise.... buuttt if you haven't played the last game, look up a summary of RE7's story to catch up as there are some important plot points in the latter half of the game you'll need. I never played RE7 but I DID know the story beforehand and it really helped.

You play as Ethan Winters. A man whose wife was murdered and infant daughter taken from his own home, and he has no idea why. He must track down his daughter's kidnappers and piece together what happened to the small village, plagued by monsters, he finds himself in. 

This game has a perfect blend of genres with there being a number of distinct locations with atmosphere, gameplay and just the general vibe being different between them. Most games struggle to implement this but I believe that Village does it extremely well, as they use a kind of "hub" system using the Village itself, where you must go back there each time to progress to the next area. Each time you go there, however, the village is slightly different with new enemies and areas to explore, giving it quite a dynamic feel. Another review mentioned that the story would be nowhere near as good without the village as one might experience tonal whiplash without it since it provides an excellent transition between locations. 

I found several sections of the game to be quite difficult, namely the first few encounters and the last few encounters, but this was most likely because my first playthrough was on "Hardcore" difficulty (which I highly recommend. It really felt like I was one man against the apocalypse as every minor enemy could kill me in only a few hits, and ammo was extremely scarce).

The graphics in this game are also spectacular. I never had a single moment where I saw a poor texture, or a lighting glitch or anything. I am playing on an RTX 2060 GPU with an AMD Ryzen 9 3900x CPU (with 24gb RAM) and had consistent 150 fps throughout the whole game on max settings. The only criticism I have would be that there are certain areas which can (in a small number of players) cause memory leaks and thus massive fps drops. This is easily fixed however, by closing and reopening the game, so you'll just have to play for a while with 20-30 fps until you find a save point. That happened to me only once though, however one thing which happened multiple times was freezes. The game will sometimes freeze for 3 - 10 seconds. It usually doesn't matter as all the enemies will freeze too, except in cutscenes where the audio will continue as normal but the game will freeze in place, causing a delay of about 5 seconds for the visuals to audio and resulting in an immersion break. But this only happened a few times. Other places it happened were in the the bonus content which consisted of (minor spoilers) [spoiler]time trials where you need to kill as many enemies as possible in a certain amount of time. When freezes would happen, I wouldn't be able to move for about 3 - 10 seconds but the in-game timer would continue as normal, meaning I lose those precious seconds. It wouldn't normally matter but I tend to go for perfect scores so it caused me some trouble. [/spoiler] 


(Minor spoilers for bonus content, but nothing to do with the story)
[spoiler]Once you complete the game, there is an additional mode for the player to try called "Mercenaries". I mention this because i haven't seen many people talk about this in reviews. Mercenaries is an entirely different game to Village as it feels a lot more like Doom than Resident Evil, with you mowing through enemies with increasingly powerful weapons to a killer soundtrack. All the levels in Mercenaries are based on the in-game locations, so there is nothing you won't be unfamiliar with but that doesn't mean it won't feel new as the Devs really throw everything they've got at you, sending the most difficult enemies throughout the game at you. Then it gets even harder, as they make you do everything you just did, but with the starting weapons... As of writing this I'm still making my way through it and I'm having an absolute blast. [/spoiler]

If you're up for a game that essentially combines Resident Evil 4 with Resident Evil 7,  this is a bit of a no-brainer. I myself was both excited and wary, but it wasn't far into my first playthrough before I found myself saying: "Hey! You know what? I'm really [I]lycan[/i] this!"

   Okay, so there's a bit more to it than just RE4 meets RE7. In fact, mythos- and enemy-wise, this entry blows the castle doors wide open. Gameplay-wise...nah, not really. But if you're a dyed-in-the-wool RE fan, is this liable to bother you? Of course not! Unless you're one of those old-school purists who demand that at least a third of the game's monsters be [I]zombies[/i], in which case...um...I did mention Resident Evil 4 and 7, didn't I?! (Actually, there [i]are[/i] zombies, of a sort, but you'll have to wait a wee while for that particular itch to be scratched!)

   I for one welcome the odd variation or two in a franchise that's been going on this long, and to that effect this game delivers just the right amount of change and the right amount of familiarity. I won't lie: I don't have nearly as much to say about this entry as I did about RE7, 'cause it's much of the same thing in a different setting. 

   The only notable differences I can cite? Well, the merchant from RE4 has finally returned to the series - though he's a bit chubbier this time! - and melee combat is at least a tad more effectual than most RE games (though I still wouldn't rely on it [i]too[/i] much)! I'd also opine that it's one of the least "scary" RE games overall, but it more than makes up for this with constant thrills and insane epicness and some of the craaaaaziest characterisations we've seen in quite some time (pretty sure that's an Outlast 2 influence I detect, haha)!

   So it's pretty much what you expected, with a few less scares and a tad more wackiness. Long-term RE fans are unlikely to be disappointed.

   Oh, and you get the upcoming Re:Verse "deathmatch" game for free, a bit like we got Resistance with the RE3make. Let's be honest, though: does anyone really [I]give[/i] a toss?!

   Verdict: 10/10.

[h1] NO IMMERSION [/h1] 

 The game just doesn't feel immersive enough. If you want your game to take place in a foreign country, add stuff from that country's language and culture. Yes, the village looks stunning and close to a Romanian one, but it feels dull. The peasants speak a perfect English (at least let them have a silly Romanian accent if you don't want them to speak their language). The road signs are written in English...It isn't that hard to replace things like "Castle Dimitrescu" with "Castelul Dimitrescu" or "Ceremony Site" with "Sit ceremonial". It's intuitive, you know? Yeah, I know, "ciorba de legume" or Romanian dishes in the Duke's shop, right? No, it isn't enough. Listen at how Lady Dimitrescu pronounces her name...she's not even close to a good pronunciation. Place the game somewhere in the United Kingdom if you want to make it English and away from the United States.

[h1] THE CASTLE PART IS WAY TOO SHORT [/h1]

 Seriously, did you see how big that castle is? It could have its own game if you ask me. It feels like they rushed this part, but I can't give a verdict since I just reached Benevento's house. What makes me say this is the fact that the mini bosses fights against the Lady's daughters are anticlimactic (you just shoot/blow up/open a couple of windows or walls and load entire clips of ammo into the girls). The puzzles are basic and easy. You spend way too much time on the rooftop or in the courtyard for a castle with that much potential of indoor action. The main hall looks exactly like the one in the Raccoon Police Station from Resident Evil 2 and 3 with the two sets of stairs connecting in the middle, the locked rooms from upstairs, the balconies etc.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

 In conclusion, for now, I would say it's a good game with some potential, stunning graphics even if I don't play at the highest settings (big thanks to the miners for not letting me buy a decent graphics card), some good scary moments etc. but lazily made. 

Maybe I will come back to write a full review after I finish the game. Or maybe not...
