Serious question: who is this game for? RE8 is a strange, incestuous mix of Resident Evil 4 and 7, but it isn't as good as either save for graphics. Being a sequel to 7, it takes place after that game and uses its first-person gameplay, but with several thoughtlessly-repeated mechanics and concepts from 4 without any understanding of why they were implemented in the first place.
 
The inventory system is the big one. RE8 initially presents itself as more of a survival horror title, but it has no real inventory management. Space is never an issue, so you can pretty much carry whatever you want at all times. Having space at all is basically rendered pointless because crafting materials for healing fluid, ammo, and explosives don't take up any space. The created items do take up space, but you can mitigate that by only crafting them when you need them since you can carry unlimited crafting materials. I only ran out of space ONE (1) time and that was solved by rotating one item. In RE4, weapon attachments took up space and continued to do so even if you had them equipped, so you had to sacrifice space if you wanted to use them. The attachments in RE8 only take up space so long as they are unattached from their corresponding guns. Once you equip them, they're removed from your inventory and can't be removed from the gun or sold; the decision makes itself. Furthermore, you're never strapped for ammo since you can just buy it from the merchant. In fact, I was literally given free ammo and a healing item as pre-order bonus. The purchasable resources and practically non-existent inventory management really take away from any tension during gameplay. There's literally no point in having inventory space like this if you aren't going to be limited by it. 

On the topic of combat and weapons, every new handgun or shotgun you get is a flat-out upgrade over the previous ones. They don't have different abilities or characteristics that would give any reason to utilize them like in RE4 (piercing, spread, speed, crit chance). People still argue about which is the superior handgun between the blacktail or the red-9 and make legitimate arguments for both. The same cannot be said about RE8's weapons. RE7's combat was mediocre at best, but it was perfectly serviceable for survival horror. I think even the staunchest defenders of RE7 will agree that its last third is the weakest due to increased linearity and focus on combat. Instead of fixing that, RE8 literally doubles down on the worst parts of 7 for its latter half. The combat is just not a good fit for RE4-style shooting galleries. You aren't spending the majority of time in one interconnected area and resources are abundant, so you never really need to make a choice about whether to engage in combat or not and clear out a specific area. The best option is almost always to kill every enemy in a given area. In RE8, there are no specialized melee moves, the guns aren’t satisfying to use, and there are few (if any) context-sensitive enemy reactions (shooting enemy legs to make them kneel, making enemies drop dynamite or torches, shooting enemies by ledges to make them fall). I occasionally made some Lycans fall off ledges, but the opportunity rarely ever arises. You can set enemies on fire, but I only remember doing this once to solve a puzzle (admittedly a pretty clever one). The point is: these systems are in the game, but aren't utilized nearly enough. Ultimately, RE8 can't cement itself as either solid action or survival horror. 
 
In terms of areas, the village, castle, and doll house are all great. The other areas, while graphically-impressive, are quite bland. The game makes a good first impression in the first half. The initial village assault is frantic and intense, as you have to fend off several Lycans similar to the opening survival bit in RE4. I feel that a lot of people will find blasting Lycans off of a rooftop and barricading doorways to be a highlight of the game. The castle is what I expected and wanted the entire game to be: puzzle-like progression in a semi-open map with stalker enemies. Dimitrescu and her daughters aren't that difficult to avoid, but things can get pretty nerve-wracking when they start appearing unscripted, especially when two of them show up at the same time. Puzzles here aren’t challenging, but it's acceptable given that the area is early and at least attempted classic RE level design. The dollhouse is a change of pace, but it is expertly done. The emptiness and initial lack of any music is really eerie. I was super tense during the segment and was intentionally walking slowly. You have your weapons taken away for a majority of the segment and solve some more admittedly-basic puzzles, but the incredible atmosphere and sound design of that area make up for it. Although, I can see why some may find it tedious, especially on repeat playthroughs. 
 
The reservoir, though, is extremely dull and uninteresting. Kind of hilarious how the giant fish can only get you on specific boards, which basically kills all tension. I won't compare it to the giant fish from RE4 because that isn't gonna end well for RE8. This area also lacks any original enemies, which is highly disappointing because aquatic enemies could've been really freaky (like some zombified anglerfish or mermaids). Stronghold is just a forgettable, linear action sequence without anything going for it. Factory is the only other major area after the castle. It looks decent and some of the enemies are cool, but it’s so far removed from the tone and aesthetics of everything prior that it literally feels like a different game at that point, and not in a good way.
 
RE8 has a mercenaries mode, but it's easily the worst iteration of it. There are no extra characters or loadouts; you buy/sell what you want between fights. You have to move around to different part of the map and can only kill a set number of enemies on a generous timer instead of an endless horde. The best strategy is always to buy a single weapon and upgrade it as much as you can. It's braindead and offers no flexibility. In previous games, you rarely had to actually look for enemies to kill. They would always come to you. Most enemies in RE8's mercs are those Dark Souls-wannabe zombies(?) that aren't fast or aggressive, so you have to actively go and look for them. It's not so bad in early levels, but this makes the factory an absolute trash fire. It's incredibly easy to miss a single enemy that you didn’t see behind some random corner and lose your combo looking for the ♥♥♥♥. In previous games, if a story level didn’t work in mercs, they would just make a new level built for the mode using the same assets, but we don’t get that here. Part of the appeal of mercenaries was getting to play as characters unavailable in the story like villains. RE8’s first-person perspective may not make the idea seem novel, but it would’ve been a better way to handle special abilities rather than giving randomly-selected, boring upgrades. Chris could have an expanded melee system or one of Dimitrescu's daughters could do quick dodges or special attacks by turning into a swarm of insects. Hell, I would've settled for even less. If they just swapped the player hands and voice lines, that would've made me spend a little more time on it. I'm spit balling ideas here, but it's pretty clear that RE8's mercs mode is bare-bones and half-assed. It also accentuates how weak the combat is. #notmymercenaries
 
Again, who is this game for? There's no real inventory management, resources are never scarce, the few puzzles are basic, and the game stops trying to be scary in any capacity halfway through, so it's clearly not for survival horror fans. The gameplay is a straight downgrade from RE4 in every regard, so it isn't good action either. It isn't even a bad game, but it’s not worth full price. In fact, for the full price of RE8 you could probably buy both RE4 and 7, both of which are better purchases.

I must say, I'm pleasantly surprised by this game. It's a perfect blend between RE4 and RE7. One of the best RE games in general. That's a tl;dr. With that said, here are my thoughts:

[list]
[*]Difficulty

I completed the game on hardcore. Honestly? Perfect difficulty for a first playthrough, it feels like a classic RE game. Constant lack of ammunition and items in general makes you search every nook and cranny. It also teaches you how important block is, because enemies hit very hard. But, there is one thing you should know. The intro of the game, well... hard as ♥♥♥♥, frustrating even. You will die a lot. After that, well, it's much more smoother. 

[*]Visuals

Locations look great and is very fun to navigate and explore. The game in general looks very good, RE Engine is some kind of a miracle, I tell ya. 

Some moments in the game are pretty scary, not gonna lie. I was scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ a couple of times. I wish some segments were a little bit longer though. 

[*]Guns and baddies

Shooting feels nice. Weapons are impactful, even your first pistol. Speaking of weapons, there is pretty good variety of guns. There is even more in NG+! You can also upgrade your guns.

The game has good variety of enemies. Bosses, well, they are pretty fun, but not very unique except for one. Classic modern RE "shot the weak spot and dodge ♥♥♥♥ until it dies". Design-wise tho - fantastic. 

[*]Story
Story is good, especially for a RE game. Some moments genuinely made me tear up a little. It gets kinda all over the top, but it's a Resident Evil game after all. I liked Ethan character a lot. Villains are cool too! Heisenberg especially.

[*]Performance
This game is pretty well optimized, my PC is far from great, but I got mostly stable 60 fps. There were some hiccups tho. Just reboot the game if you have problems.
[/list]

In conclusion, well, I do recommend the game! I hope Capcom will continue to deliver quality games like this.

This is the best marriage of RE7 and RE4, with elements from other RE games sprinkled in.

A much more action focused Resident Evil game with emphasis on a more arcade-y combat, straightforward boss mechanics and even including a few horror focused sections.
Since everyone and their mother knows this game for the big vampire mommy Lady D I do have to warn you - she and her daughters are only about 10% of the entire game. So if this was a selling point to you then sorry to disappoint, and if it's the opposite then you're in luck!

Now RE4 was a somewhat controversial title due to it being a more direct transition into the action genre, with RE3 being an experimental slightly more action oriented horror game. This might feel similar coming from RE7, you will most likely be running and gunning half the time, with some sections even throwing enough enemies at you that you'd want a minigun. Which brings me to a negative point here: NG+.
In previous RE games New Game+ was a fun way to discover new unique weapons and interesting ways around encounters. Here you just get more powerful weapons of the same type you've been using before, with the one truly unique weapon locked behind a Mercenaries mode grind.
The mercenaries mode is a lot of fun, you can even find random power-ups around the levels which almost turns it into a rogue-lite, until you try to get high ranks in the Hard Mode maps though, then it starts becoming frustrating. It would be interesting to see a more open-ended mode like this, with all the maps combined perhaps, to see how a long run would look with you becoming ridiculously overpowered.

Overall a great game, if you are looking for a true Resident Evil experience you might be disappointed, but if you're fine with a bit of action in your RE games (if you liked RE4 and beyond) then you'll love it.

The hidden items you can find to sell to the merchant, upgrading yourself and your weapons, etc. Once you get to the point where you're selling items and upgrading, you just want to find E V E R Y T H I N G, and it's pretty addictive. Some parts of the game (especially boss fights) can come off as "safe" or "basic", but they're still a great deal of fun IMO.

Especially by the time the game wrapped up as it makes connections with previous titles, and ties it up neatly.

Once again another solid game for the franchise. Extremely creepy but very fun to play. Much longer than Resident Evil 7 and also many more bosses and places to explore, things to do and just a great first person survival horror game overall. The graphics are great, voice acting pretty good, music very good and immersive, cool guns, cool enemies and a great story. 

It definitely reminds me a lot of Resident Evil 4 where there's a shopkeeper who you can buy weapons and items and upgrades from so there's a lot of opportunities to run around the village finding collectables and other little things to sell in order to make some cash. You can also hunt for animals to give meat to the shop keeper so he can cook you up some meals to give yourself permanent buffs which is pretty handy. Only issue with this is you're able to hunt and sell the animal meat before you unlock the cooking so I ended up selling stuff before I knew I needed it which was extremely annoying, cooking should have been introduced a little sooner. 

The game runs quite well on pc, I had most of the settings maxed and I was able to get a good 100-144fps most of the time (on GTX 1080 & i7 7700K @ 1080p) although playing at high framerate puts the cpu usage up quite a lot which is a shame but maybe once denuvo is removed it won't run so hot. I didn't experience any crashes and I didn't really notice or experience any bugs so very well optimized and play tested.

There's a whole bunch of just enemies and bosses to fight and they're all pretty cool and unique so don't have any complaints there. The map design is pretty good as well, very creepy looking environments. The village itself is quite fun to just roam around in, unlocking new parts of it as you go along and finding more treasures, very fun. 

There's maybe just a handful of things I didn't like about the game, like I said earlier about the high cpu usage and the cooking unlocking a bit late but aside from that there's quite a lack of puzzles in the game, there's not really many around and the ones that are around are extremely easy and since I was playing on hardcore I guess they don't change based on difficulty so yeah. The game itself was a welcome challenge on hardcore mode but if you're an experienced player I imagine playing on an easier difficulty would just be a breeze and maybe not as fun or engaging so it would have been nice to bump it up a bit. 

Overall pretty damn good game and a great new entry to the series. Very interested to see what they'll do next and how it'll play out. Didn't really have many problems with it and I had a blast through the whole thing. 9/10

From the moment I had beaten the game I was as quiet as one can be. Whilst the end credits were rolling and whilst I was still thinking about what I had seen in the ending, I couldn't say another word about the game for the rest of the evening. 
Man is this game good. 
I do want to get some things of my chest though, for anyone who is still planning on playing this game in the near future. Don't worry, I'll try and keep things as spoiler free as possible, since that would be the biggest buzzkill you'll ever experience in your life. Getting spoiled for this is game is absolutely the worst thing they can do to you. 
With all that being said, here are my pros and cons of the game. Which I'll wrap up with an overall score. 

Pros: 
- The graphics. They're beautiful. And this is coming from someone who doesn't have the pc power to run things at maximum if I want to stay above 30 fps during the most intensive parts of the game. I played this game at a combination of medium and low throughout and it looked (for me) absolutely gorgeous. 
- Speaking of graphics, let's talk about performance. Once again, just like any other Resident Evil game, the optimisation is wonderful. It runs fine, and you won't encounter any crashes or critical freezes like you might experience in some other games. 
Don't get fooled by the "recommended specs" either. Whilst their estimations on what you need for 60 fps @ 1080p holds true to some extend. Considering this is a single player first person shooter, 30 fps will be totally acceptable. So as long as you have something like a 1050ti, you'll be good to go. (Worse could also work, though then you'll drop below 30 fps in intensive parts of the game.)
- Story. The story of this game is clear, not to complicated, but most importantly, wonderful. It is obvious what's going on by the end of the game and the connections between Resident Evil 7 are definitely there. (This pro could be 10 times longer if I was allowed to tell spoilers ;) )
- Gameplay. The way they made the gameplay truely stands out as something special. The limited FOV makes it feel like you are never safe from any possible threats and there are puzzles to keep you occupied at all times. The backtracking that you'll have to do extends the game in a positive way too. Because it's not like the game becomes a 30 minute walking simulator if you have to go back and do something. There is always something coming after you. 
Yes I know, I said I like the FOV and I know a lot of people will say that this game sucks because of it. Whilst I have to agree that the FOV is smaller than in other games. Saying that it is the equivalent of using binoculars in front of your monitor is simply not true. They claim that bosses move way too fast for you to follow with the limited FOV and that some parts of the game are just really difficult because of it. I don't consider this as a con, nor did it bother me in anyway, but just in-case you are easily triggered by small FOV's. THIS IS YOUR WARNING. 

Cons: 
- Minor stutters. I know I said this game was perfectly optimised, which it is, but that doesn't take away the fact there are some minor errors. 
Once again, whilst I didn't really mind all that much, everytime you kill an enemy you get a minor stutter. It isn't a freeze for like 2 seconds, but it is worth mentioning for those who want games to be stutter free. The good thing about this though is that you'll never shoot more bullets at an enemy than needed because you know when it dies. 
- Frame drops. This doesn't have anything to do with optimisation, but the Lady's daughters seriously drop your frames. For those who don't know, they're made out of flies and when I say flies I mean A LOT of flies. This means that when one of them starts chasing you in the castle, your frames will drop if they get close to you. (In my case they dropped as low as 15 fps). Something to be aware of.
 If you want to get rid of this problem, you're going to need mods. One of the first mods I saw on nexusmods was one that removed all the bugs from the daughters. I now know why. 
- No option to change FOV. "But I thought the FOV didn't bother you!" You're right, but that doesn't mean they should remove the option to change it all together. It didn't bother me, but that doesn't mean it doesn't bother others. If you want to seize this problem, once again, you'll have to use mods. 
- Sensitivity. The mouse sensitivity in this game is a bit odd and takes some time getting used to. Yes you can set it higher but it is still a bit iffy. 

That pretty much wraps it up for me. Though I will give you one final overall conclusion.

You are still going to have lots of fun though. Resident Evil games are never bad, but this isn't the direction I wanted them to go. Getting 7 and RE2make made me hopeful they would do the modernized version of the old school labyrinth-horror we've seen in those two games. I think the game I wanted would've taken place in the Castle all the time with some moments going outside to the village and then trying to solve the labyrinth there. The fun of old Resident Evil games is trying to figure out how you are going to navigate through the mazes and where what items goes, but Capcom doesn't have much faith in that game-style.

RE4 is still fun and that's mostly because that game is very varied and keeps the action fresh for a very long time. This game has a lot of variation too, but not as much as RE4. The biggest crime this game does is having a few of those ENEMY-WAVE AFTER ENEMY-WAVE-moments. Because whenever we get those we get those instead of more chases, more labyrinths or something new and interesting. I wish Capcom would just ban that concept from their game development teams completely. 

But as a consumer I am powerless. "Vote with your money" doesn't work because companies will always chase the mainstream because there are simply more potential buyers there. I suspect it will take like another RE6-flop until we get something interesting and more old school-ish from Capcom again.

First off I am a long time fan of RE and have played most of the games (yes even the bad ones lol), Since RE 7 the series has had somewhat of a new lease on life and Village is another strong entry for the series. 

The graphics are amazing  and with everything maxed out except texture vram (high 1gb) and ray tracing off the game looks stunning. The lighting, the textures, the insane level of detail all combines for a palpable atmosphere. 

I am not that far in yet and I am taking my time a lot staring at the scenery, for me the first run of a new re game is always super slow  as I explore everything and gawk a lot. 

I will say though in terms of game play flow the first few hours have been amazing, the game can be suprisingly intense and is a bit more weirdly supernatural then 7 which I love. 

The statement if 7 and 4 had a baby it would be 8 is pretty acurate to how this feels and seeing as I loved 4 and 7 I am happy as I can be so far. 

Will update at the end of my playthrough. 

Edit 16/05/2021 - Finished my paythrough and I loved it, real solid mix of styles with the different boss domains all tied together with the village as the central hub, The story flows well and escalates at a nice pace, I feel the balance of action and horror is handled well, it switches back and forth at a nice pace between horror, tension and more action packed moments. Only at the end does it really go full action (but still in a solid horror setting) and to be honest I loved it, at that point in the story it was really nice to be told hey don't worry about ammo just go nuts, it was fun. I like the way they have done the unlockables, its the same as RE3make you earn points by completing challenges in game and spend those points in the bonus content store. For infinite ammo weapons you have to have fully upgraded all of a weapons stats and unlocked all the modifications which for some of the rarer weapons is very expensive. So it feels like there's a good amount of effort required to unlock a powerful game play tool. So far I have the infinite TAC shotgun and Dragoon assault rifle and its really fun. Will probably play through a few more times. Finally I never really got in to mercenarys mode but here in an fps it is really fun and I like how each level is broken up in to stages and you can upgrade weapons at the duke between stages and unlock powers as you play (no damage when blocking, extra shotgun damage ect) which stack over the course of a level. Its really fun and I will play again. 

Overall I like it slightly more then 7 (which I loved) The graphics are stunning, the gameplay is as refined as its ever been, the pacing is sublime and it somehow manages to homage all the different styles of gameplay Resident evil has tried over the years in to one cohesive package.
It has a few really scary moments but for the most part it feels like most resident evil games, lots of horrific imagery but over time you go from being scared and tense while counting bullets and searching for ammo to carrying multiple weapons of death and destruction and feeling like a badass. This gameplay progression means RE games have never been the scariest games out there because its hard to create the tension of Outlast when you have a grenade launcher and automatic shotgun but I am OK with that. And to be fair this game try's really hard to sometimes mess with that formula to create a few moments of real dread throughout, it doesn't change the formula completely but feels like a nice evolution of it.  I love it 9.5 out of ten.

I just like what can we do that isn't a Zombie virus and how that ties into the original plot). The gunplay is fun but nothing to write home about. Significantly more action oriented that RE7, feels like what RE4 was doing to the series only in first person.

The first area is wonderful: Castle Dimitrescu with it's vampire ladies and the opening of the story is just fun, and well done. The second area is a non-combat based zone, that feels very Silent Hill which had me really happy they were trying to include both. The puzzles overall are VERY easy which is a little disappointing. The third area is a complete wash, the BBEG is a sniveling, unsure, unlikable wreck to begin with and the area is neither interesting nor challenging. The fourth area is fun, because it breaks up the style with some heavy Dieselpunk / Tetsuo: Iron Man style elements but abuses the player with needlessly narrow / poorly designed environments in order to create artificial tension (the enemies aren't hard, just frustrating and you're jammed into narrow corridors). The boss battle is needlessly over the top with some Akira vibes and they give you a ridiculous superweapon for part 1 of the boss battle. They break up the time between the 4 minions and the main baddie with a short overpowered romp through the areas you've already been as "That boulder punching bastard" Chris Redfield - but it's a bit clumsy it feels like it's just holding you up and adding some filler before the end rather than being truly enjoyable. The ending battle is a fairly standard multi-part multi-form boss battle, which if you've been hoarding all your magnum / grenade ammo, in true RE fashion you can just rush through with a little bit of maneuvering. Similarly in RE fashion, the story is ludicrous and all the emotional responses to everything are 1000x over the top with characters taking wild illogical leaps sometimes. There's an amusing amount of self awareness (commentary about how much damage Ethan has taken and survived leading to a major plot point, the self referential humor of Chris punching a boulder in a fury in RE5, etc) that is a nice nod.

6-7/10: better than meh and competently executed, but nothing stellar - I did enjoy myself because I like RE despite all my gripes. Recommend it on sale 20%+ OFF for sure, and I'm hoping the multiplayer game is solid when it released. Really wish we could get another RE: Outbreak though.

If you grew up playing Resident Evil in it's infancy, when it defined a genre and you loved it's slow methodical gameplay and tank controls and you hated where the series went with and after 4 because it "wasn't survival horror" then there is a good chance you won't like this game. Luckily, I'm not one of those people and I love this game.
   
I love that this game treads a thin line between intense action and tense horror for the majority of it's runtime and even dips into both at different parts of the game without the game leaning heavily into either. So you aren't playing Resident Evil 6, but you aren't playing Resident Evil 1 either. Sound familiar? It should if you've played Resident Evil 4 except this game doesn't have QTE's so 1 point for Village. In all seriousness, I like this mix of action and horror where I consistently feel engaged and tense save for points that serve to break up the pacing to either give you a break or go heavy into either action or horror to keep you on your toes. 

Gameplay aside, The world and level design is great. The game is divided into set pieces that are each well designed in layout and aesthetically as well as bringing a feeling of isolation. The gothic horror motif is refreshing for the series and the graphics are beautiful. The layout of each area also keeps some staples of the series like backtracking and opening new paths that gets you familiar with each area. Resources and treasures are hidden all around so that you aren't mindlessly walking through room and corridor, though enemies (both killable and patrolling invincible ones) also do a good job with that. And the enemies too are deigned well, they aren't generic zombies or big boring mold monsters. They are all pretty inspired and scary takes on classic gothic horror monsters like werewolves, vampires, and Frakenstein-like monsters. And then there is the giant fish monster with tons of eyes, can't have a Resident Evil game without a giant fish monster or a monster with way too many eyes and this one has both! In one monster! Wow so cool. But for the most part, I love the enemy design. 

Although it isn't all good, Resident Evil games have always struggled with story and writing and this one is certainly no different. If you are anything like me, you will probably be laughing at every single stupid word that comes out of Ethan's mouth as well as some weak and downright stupid plot twists. And I think the game could've benefited from some darker, scarier environments that you actually fight in. If you are in an area in this game that is so dark that you need your flashlight, you probably aren't going to be fighting in it, save for a couple. 

And yes the game is short, but it is tight, doesn't meander and if you take you time with it, it doesn't feel short at all and even if it does, go back through with some of unlockable weapons, complete challenges, or go back through on Village of Shadows, which is a good challenge that changes some enemy spawns up a bit.

Overall, I love the game, the tall vampire lady and her daughters are indeed very hot, and I would not mind at all if the Resident Evil series stays this course for a while.

I'm bias in that I love these games, however I will say that RE7 was the better game in terms of scariness and actual horror. This game however, is better in every other aspect, which while a positive, not the kind of positive you want to hear from a game franchise that prides itself on being a horror series. Now while expressing my main concern, I will go on to say that the fun factor is pretty high up there. If you aren't a huge fan of horror, but love zombies/sci-fi, this game is right up your alley. 

The weapon customization aspect is quite fun and gives a fair amount of longevity to this fairly short game. Even 44 hrs in, I still have yet to unlock every weapon and every customization, and every upgrade for each gun. A downside, but interesting thing that's done, is that they did away with the storage box, meaning you're stuck with your inventory, it adds to a possible mechanic of selling old weapons to upgrade new ones.

Speaking of inventory, it is much less of a hassle here, as there is much more raw inventory space than there was in 7. Another aspect that has been simplified for the sake of QoL is that quest/mandatory items now exist in there own place in your pocket dimension, so managing inventory is super easy. Personally, I didn't prefer it, as the challenge of deciding whether to keep some spare ammo versus a key needed to progress was a fun mini-game in of itself.

The last topic that's worth talking about, is the story, which to me, would have been far worse if there hadn't been text documents, which while not the best- since they aren't too terribly long -is still an unenjoyable way to understand the story. Throughout the story, you are teased, and it's never a good tease, but when the tease is finally revealed in it's entirety, it's very satisfying, and adds a lot of depth to the story overall- harking back to RE7 -, and sets up for a lot of potential.

I found it enjoyable. Overall, I loved the experience. In most games, when I replay them, there are moments where I just say to myself "Here comes an annoying part." I've played this 4 times now and never really felt it like that. I just have a few critiques about this game:

1. The graphics are amazing, until it comes to water and the slime-like substance from Moraeu - it turns into a blurry mess and at times, just looks like a color with no texture. Speaking of graphics, I noticed that there is dynamic resolution. I don't know if it's because I'm using Ray Tracing, but even at 1080p I can see textures pixel-ate when I move around. When I stop moving around, it becomes high definition again. It's not always noticeable, but it is more often than I'd like.
2. The performance issues are quite annoying. Most of the time, I maintain a good 50-60 FPS, but there were moments where it would drop to 10-20 and would remain there until I reload the game.
3. For being a "survival horror" game, it sure lacks the "horror." Don't get me wrong, it has it's moments that made me a little scared my first play through, but only at the beginning. Mainly the introduction to the Village and Beneviento. Everything after that just felt like action, especially the end. After Beneviento, all horror seemed to disappear. I thought I was playing Call of Duty for a minute. One way to counteract the horror part is to play on Hardcore or "Village of Shadows." Enemies are actually a threat on those difficulties, and it brings the terror back into the game when you're being attacked.
4. When you beat the game on "Village of Shadows," you're able to get the Rocket Pistol from the Extra Content Shop. I felt is was a bit under-powered for shooting rockets. It would still take 7 shots or so to kill a Lycan on "Village of Shadows." On standard, it took 2 rockets to kill a Lycan. 

It was a great experience, I would definitely recommend it to a friend.

Great graphics and performance. I have a GTX 1080 and can play at 90-100 fps almost maxed. The models and atmosphere were achieved very well. Mediocre story, and terrible voice acting (I mean, the dialogues are laughable, I don´t really blame the actors). The bosses feel somewhat lackluster, as do the enemies. When I think about my experience in this game, I think of two other games to compare it to, which might seem weird.

The first is Half life 2. HL2 was a game consisting of many setpieces that linked together. The trainstation, the canals, the airboat section, Black Mesa East, Ravenholm, Highway 17, Sandtraps, Nova Prospekt. I remember them vividly, though that's partially because I've played the hell out of Half Life 2.

Resident Evil Village also has some fantastic setpieces. The village, of course; the castle, the dollhouse (and the basement underneath), Moreau's section, and the factory. All of them fit together and lead from one to the other perfectly. The progression of areas in the game didn't feel too rushed or forced. I only wish I could go back to completed areas to get things I missed.

The other game I think of is Dead Space 2. Funnily enough, Dead Space was heavily inspired by Resident Evil 4, and if you've played both, you can clearly see that.

I think you can compare RE 7 and Village to DS 1 and 2. If Resident Evil 7 was Dead Space 1 — a slow paced, scary, haunting experience where power is taken from the player constantly — then Resident Evil Village is Dead Space 2 — a more action packed sequel that strayed away from horror and toward thrills to broaden its audience.

The devs for DS 2 said in interviews that EA wanted more sales, and forced them to go in a more action-oriented direction since horror didn't bring in the massive audience they needed. And, wouldn't you know, Capcom ran into similar problems with RE 7, saying that it was too scary for a lot of players. So they made RE Village more empowering, still giving it the scary moments and tension, but overall straying from the horror aspect (barring one area in particular).

I don't mind that the game isn't as scary as RE 7. In fact, I think it might have been the right way to go, since a lot of people don't like horror.

- Easily and by a huge margin, RE8 is the best looking RE game ever. It's INCREDIBLY detailed, well designed and STUNNING to look at.
- Very atmospheric, and its got a lot of variety in that aspect as well.
- Sound design is also the best in the series. The intro is horrifying!
- From the first few hours, you'll quickly notice how big and diverse the game is.
- Levels are intricately crafted, with more ways to explore them. Really liked how the village was structured with more ways to explore and search its houses.
- The game INSANELY nails the interior design of its levels; I find myself stopping every 5 mins or so just to absorb the beauty of it all.
- The game's setting really makes you feel like you're playing in a horror themed amusement park.

If there was ever a time to get re-introduced to the Resident Evil series the time would be now. People will talk about Village/Biohazard the same way those of us reminiscence playing Resident Evil 1 on Play Station 1. The amount of effort Capcom has put into revitalizing this series has been a proven success. They took calculated risks by deviating from the standard game-play design/mechanics of the first six games, and took the series into a brand new fresh original direction. 

Both Village/Biohazzard can standalone apart from the original titles. I think this is a good thing. You will find small references that hint at the previous titles but generally speaking I feel Capcom kept that to a minimum on purpose. I'm happy to see different characters, setting, and a totally new original storyline. I was worried that Biohazzard was a one off game for them to experiment with and we would never get something like Village. 

Without revealing too much here but once you finish Village you will discover that Biohazzard was made with Village pre-planned and already in mind. I don't mean this in a cheap sense where "Oh that character that was good is actually bad all along. And that person you thought was dead was really alive this whole time." You won't find that kind of cheap writing, and style here. There is a well though-out planned design you will discover behind the Ethan character and how the ending of village introduces to us to the next chapter. These characters are here to stay for years the same way Leon, Wesker, and Jill did for us. 

As for a review of the game itself... I don't know even know where to begin... amazing visuals. Thrilling action sequences that give you a rush. The horror themes are present with you in most of the game, but not anywhere as horrifying as Biohazard. The game was fluid and responsive through in and through out. I'm overly impressed with how well polished the game was on PC launch with little to no bugs. 

The amount of detail you will find in the game and not just visually, but how layers of the story are riddled everywhere around you for to explore shows that Capcom took great effort to leave no stone unturned. 

My biggest takeaway was amount of challenges put in front of you. I can't remember having to deal with so many boss fights in the series as I did here. What I found most impressive about these fights is how amazing the character models looked in the final transformation stages of the villains. You think after years of playing games that you had seen it all and this is another boss fight transforming into his final form but I felt like the design put behind these character models were stunning.

Highly recommend +++++

Resident Evil 8 is by no means a bad game. In fact, it does a lot well when it comes to rectifying the issues that plagued RE7 for example there's much more enemy variety, weapon variety, better pacing, and overall story arc that doesn't leave as many loopholes at the end (regardless of the story's direction). If you hated RE7's helplessness and hated RE4's ultimate lack of horror elements, you'll think this game is pretty neat.

However, I do think this game was unsuccessful when firing on all cylinders. First to mention, the PC port is surprisingly lackluster, the menu UI as well as the overall lack of an FOV slider, I am utterly surprised that some of these things weren't added by the release date. Another thing is that despite everything the game portrays so well, it still feels like it's trying to be something it's not, whether that be a piece of nostalgia bait for hardcore fans who wanted more RE4 or a title that wanted to be an amped up RE7. It just does not seem to fill it's own shoes with it's own content and that feels somewhat disappointing and makes the rumor that this was previously a new Revelations title a little more relevant to truth. 

So from someone who adored RE7 for it's originality and atmosphere, applauded RE2R return to form with a modern style, and at least appreciated RE3R for existing, It just was not for me. Despite it's obvious lack of weaknesses, it doesn't really have many strengths to make it what it is. HOWEVER, I refuse to tell you that this is a bad game, it's great, it's just not for me or people who might think like I do.

The game has a nice blend of Resident evil 7 and 4's play style and and level design.  Although the beginning of the game is a little slow once extensive tutorial is finished the game opens up.  I like the easy to use crafting system with the extremely limited items.  
        The cooking system though very limited can be completely undermined early on by selling key ingredients collected from animals in that there is only a set amount of crafting items and only "1" unique crafting items.  Despite that frustration, its a one time lesson and easily avoidable in the future.  
       Combat is fluid, fast and mostly intuitive.  Close range combat is very stressful, yet hugely rewarding with weapon attacks landing with a satisfying impact and sound.  Long range combat is fairly easy with large windows of opportunity to apply damage.  
       The aesthetics of graphics, level design and music give a very immersive visceral experience particular to each location.  This creates a collection of smaller Resident Evil experiences with a localized hub at the core.  The bulk of the game is unfortunately early on, a great deal of upgrades and items are acquirable early as well. These combine to further accelerates the rate of progress shorting the expected length to a few hours.  The fastest I am aware of is an hour and thirty-eight minutes to beat the game although 15 - 18 hours is fairly normal for a first play-through.  
       All and all this adds up to a fairly fun, surprisingly forgiving yet intense game.  I highly recommend this game for those who enjoy a challenging survival horror First Person Shooter with a flair for legendary monster.  
      As a final aside, I played this game listening to Castlevania Lords of Shadows 1 and 2 official sound tracks with varying degrees of appropriate music to game play -usually fits the game perfectly-.  I kinda wish we could have Gabriel Belmont or Simon Belmont costumes for Ethan.

SCORE:  4.2/5
METRICS: 
FUN FACTOR:  4/5
STORY: 4.5/5
QUALITY: 4/5
AUDIO: 5/5
REPLAYABILITY: 3.5/5

PROS:  The variety of different enemies to fight throughout the game is astounding.  I love the pacing and selection of different enemies in the game.  From the Lycans that are loud and move quickly all the way down to your typical zombie that makes relatively low noise and moves slowly will certainly keep you on your toes as you turn around just for one of these guys to sneak up on you.  It feels a lot more like an action game than a resident evil game to be completely honest.  But it does a great job building a good atmosphere by creating really awesome biomes to mess around with.  The dollhouse had me completely on my toes, and for those that get far enough there is a surprise in the basement of the house if dolls aren't enough to freak you out by themselves.  

CONS: The responsiveness is pretty rough on PC.  For example, when I try to pull up the map it says to move the map around simply move the mouse under the tooltips.  This does not work.  For me to be able to check the map I have had to attach my controller and use the controller to navigate the map while using mouse/keyboard.  There were also some issues regarding the enemies clipping through objects, and grabbing me through buildings.  This was pretty frustrating which forced me to always be in the center of a room at any given time.  The only other negative thing about the game is the shortness of it.  It felt way too short for me, and after 7 hours or so I was able to beat it and find most of the secrets of the game.  

SUMMARY:  This is a good game.  I do encourage the developers to make some changes to the game as it does have some bugs on the PC version.  All in all.  I still recommend this game.  The visuals are great.  Sound quality is very well done.  The story is compelling and feels new and fresh.  It does lack replayability and the story is relatively short making me question whether or not the game is worth 60$.  But all in all I don't feel like I've wasted my money.  The journey itself is worth your time and if your considering this game I would wait for a sale.  20% off?  Hope this guide helped someone make a decision to purchase the game, and as always. Cannot recommend this game enough. it not only captures the essence of Resident Evil it also learns to do its own thing and experiment with gameplay that we would not normally see in the series, and makes it work! 

Pro's-

Huge map for great chances of exploration
Merceneries Mode was a good bit of fun that plays similar to RE4
Story was well done with some great twists and memorable moments
Visuals were very high end with some spectacular creatures and evironments featured
Boss Fights were each unique and challenging in their own ways
Atmosphere was excellent with us jumping from being calm to anxious to terrified in the blink of an eye
Ethan greatly improved with his character work and having more chances to bounce off other characters

Could be improved-
Photo Mode was a little limited and the copyright watermarks were irritating

Cons-
2 of the areas visited can be completed too quickly. Could have done with being longer
Some plot elements that were carried over from Resident Evil 7 were still not explained
A couple of characters were over exposed and hyped during the trailers and demos so they  lost some of their appeal when playing.
Evidently some cuts to the game were made that made some parts of the game a little disjointed

Final Thoughts-
Overall an excellent game which learned from past mistakes from Resident Evil 7 and the 2 and 3 remakes. Still had a couple of niggling problems but they are outshined by alot of the brighter spots in the game. The exploration and resource/item management was great and the return of currency and a shop to by supplies and weapons was excellent. Looking forward to seeing where Capcom goes from here with the inevitable Resident Evil 9.

After the success of Resident Evil 7: Biohazard (RE7… or should I say Resident EVII?), Capcom continues the Winters family story with Resident Evil Village — or Resident Evil VIIIage (yes, they did it again).

The entire game takes place in a remote European village. I get that Ethan and Mia were looking for some peace and quiet, but it really does feel like the setting existed partially just to make the Roman numerals work. Subtle? Not exactly. Effective? Absolutely.

Jokes aside, this is a major step up from RE7 in terms of gameplay. There’s a wider variety of weapons, far more inventory space, and enemies that don’t feel like complete bullet sponges. Combat feels more balanced, and the pacing leans more into action while still keeping the horror atmosphere intact.

The Resident Evil Village: Winters' Expansion adds even more value, including a new campaign where you play as Rose Winters and the option to experience the main story in third-person mode — something fans had been asking for.

Overall, this feels like a confident evolution of RE7’s formula. It keeps the tension, expands the combat, and fully commits to its gothic horror setting — Roman numeral puns and all.

At the time of this review, no DLC has been planned or announced for Resident Evil : Village. The multiplayer game included RE:Verse has been put back into development to work out issues, and has no update on if or when it will be released. 

Resident Evil Village, is the perfect blend of Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7. Two of the best selling games of the franchise. Elements of Resident Evil 4 were melded into the style of 7, and it worked out wonderfully. Elements such as no item boxes, a merchant, and a new treasure system are all back from the Leon-Led game of Resident Evil 4. While story elements, characters, and mechanics of  7 were carried over to Village. While a lot of the Resident Evil games stand a lot of their own, Village really benefits from having played Resident Evil 7’s main story. 

The main story of Village is broken up into segments, and is based around the lore of Mother Miranda, the “Priestess” of the Village. Having 4 children, having segments of the Village’s surrounding areas, which are known as the Lord’s. Each Lord is a boss segment in the game, and each lore has a unique area that goes with their theme. While some areas such as Castle Dimitrescu (Tall Vampire Lady, that broke the internet), and Heisenberg’s factory take up the majority of the game. The other two lord’s House Beneviento, and Moreau’s Reservoir, while shorter in length, both hold up wonderfully. However some of the pet peeves I had with the game, is that you are not allowed to go back to segments. After finishing the castle, you can’t return, after both House Beneviento and the Reservoir there are missable treasures to where if you simply leave, you don’t even get the option to go back. If you didn’t know they were there, you would just never know. 

For long time fans of the series or newcomers that came in with 7, this game is wonderful to play. The game should take anywhere from 10 - 14 hours, based on watching cutscenes and getting lost. While playing through it a 2nd time it’s noticeably shorter. 

Following this segment, we will be talking about the segments of the game -

Village Visit One | This is the longest time you spend in the village at one time. Going through the demo’s area as well as unlocking and visiting the house. The game also has a horde section in which it is timed rather than by kills. Overall the segment felt more like the Village in Resident Evil 4, and it was lovely. 

Castle Dimitrescu |  The 2nd Longest Lord Segment in the game, and has the host of Lady Dimitrescu, herself. Having three mini-bosses, a wealth of areas to explore and a final battle with the Lady of the house herself. Castle Dimitrescu fits right in with classic Resident Evil and feels something straight out of the Veronica House / Spencer Mansion with a Gothic Feel. 

Village Visit Two | This visit is rather short, but rewarding if you explore. Getting access to parts of the villages, where you couldn’t go before and unlocking more treasures for going off the beaten path. This part really rewards backtracking and doing a full look around! 

House Beneviento | This is one of the strongest segments, going more lines with traditional horror and escape room. Locked in a room, with no guns or weapons forced to take apart a doll of your late wife, and lead to puzzle after puzzle. This one was a real trip and one of the best segments to experience for the first time! [spoiler]After beating the house, if you go to the graves in the village, the one mausoleum opens up in which you get a piece of a puzzle to go back to the house/grave for a treasure and mini-boss. [/spoiler]

Moreau’s Reservoir | Classic monster in the lake, and having to run from point a to b, while dodging the lake monster. While it was good, the actual segments were short and rather lack-luster. The boss fight, while annoying, was kind of cool and one of the only boss fights outside the last one that gave me any kind of trouble. [spoiler]After beating the boss of the area, the water is drained and you can go to the first part of this segment where you first road the boat out. With the water drained you can go down a new path for a goat and a treasure. [/spoiler]

Village Visit Three | The clean-up, basically with the way to go cleared it’s the final time to really go over places you might have missed, gather last minute items. 

Factory | This felt like the longest segment in the game, constant back tracking, close quarters and a lore dump. New enemy types keep you on your toes, and the constant feeling of being lost is a real issue. The first time I was here, I had to take a good 5 - 10 minutes trying to figure out how to backtrack to the  foundry. 

Last Stand | After the fight with the last lord, you take over Chris on a hell path to destroy the mold and the Village. This segment felt like Not a Hero but forced into the main game. Which is needed, but it’s basically going to point a to b while fighting hordes of monsters. 

Final Fight | The last fight with Mother Miranda, was the hardest in the game and straight up from Silent Hill. (Yes Silent Hill) The fight phases were nice, and the lore/cutscene with it were exceptional.

I'm a big fan of the Resident Evil series and this one stands out as my favorite so far. With pretty much every other RE game, I complete it and that's that. They're great games, but for some reason never stood out to me as replayable (this is just my opinion, my brother loved replaying RE 2 and RE 3, I just personally didn't want to). However, this one is different. The gunplay is very satisfying in my opinion, which makes me want to replay the game with my newly unlocked weapons. The upgrade system to make your weapons more powerful is also quite enjoyable. Because you obviously can't unlock every upgrade for every weapon in your first playthrough, you're more inclined to replay the game to discover what your favorite weapons would be like fully upgraded. Besides that, I really love the look of the weapons themselves. This is purely subjective, but I really enjoy the aesthetics of tricked out guns or just sleek looking classics and RE 8 delivers hard on this.

Beyond that, the game itself is quite fun period. The story is interesting and while I thought they were veering away from the established RE story thus far, it was revealed to me that this could not be more wrong. [spoiler] For instance, it reveals that the village is where Umbrella started, explaining why the Umbrella symbol can be seen on these ancient ruins. This was something I found incredibly cool because I just love finding out about the origins of anything. [/spoiler] Also, it explains things that were simply glanced over by much of the fanbase, proving to be a satisfying twist for some. 

This is also by far the scariest RE game I've played yet. Specifically (spoilers for one of the Houses in the game) [spoiler] Donna Benevenito's house had one of the creepiest monsters and scariest challenges. It steered the game away from the action and delved into psychological horror, which I personally love and dread at the same time. [/spoiler]

All in all, this is my favorite Resident Evil game because of its satisfying gunplay and subsequent replayability, the story, and the fact that it's the scariest one thus far (at least in certain parts). I highly recommend this game even to everyone who enjoys horror games or would like to try a survival horror game out.

After the end of Resident Evil 7, I wondered how they would make a sequel to the game and what direction the series would take. All of my questions were answered with Resident Evil Village. RE8 had the gunplay and 1st person perspective of RE7, with the village theme, inventory system and traveling merchant of RE4. Upon noticing this, I was very excited to play the full game because RE4 is my favorite Resident Evil Game and RE7 is easily top 5. Village didn’t disappoint with its memorable characters, detailed zones of the game and well written plot to wrap everything together. One thing that bugged me a bit was I felt as if I was given a bit too much ammunition, making the conservation of ammo little to no worry at all. Resident Evil Village divides itself into 5 sections with the village being somewhat of a hub area. 

BUGS:

Microstuttering after kills and cutscene audio sync issues 

ZONES:

Alcinia Dimitrescu’s section is the beginning part with the castle. This plays a lot like Resident EVil 2 with the fear of Dimitrescu hunting you down, for better or for worse, looming over you. This seemed to be the only section Capcom advertised. All I would see is the ads with the tall lady time after time. 

The next zone of the game is Donna Beneviento, or as I like to call her, the doll lady. I really enjoyed this section as it reminded me a lot of the evil brother from Resident Evil 7 and his birthday cake puzzle. It felt a lot like a reimagining of Silent Hill.   

After the doll lady you come across Salvatore Moreau who’s section is pretty lame. THe giant fish in the sea is a lot like Resident Evil 4’s sea creature which was cool. But the final fight of the zone was pretty lame. 

Karl Heisenberg really stole the show for me with his zone of the game. The enemies, which reminded me a lot of the Regenerators from Resident Evil 4, kept me on my feet the whole way through. 

SPOILER SECTION

[spoiler]The big reveal of Ethan actually being dead at the Baker house was completely unexpected and I loved it. When Ethan died one too many times and finally started to disintegrate was a good transition to finish Ethan off to make way for Rose. Changing Resident Evil’s story in favor of this new plot development was a welcome one. Having this family with bizarre powers adds a sense of mystery as to what abilities they have and where the story will go. Overall a great rework of the formula to pave the way for new Resident Evil games in the future.[/spoiler]

RE7: Biohazard crossed with RE4 sums up this game fairly well in one brief sentence. 

With that said, the scares compared to its direct predecessor, RE7: Biohazard, are diluted (according to Capcom this was deliberate based on fans feedback... *sigh*). But much more like RE4, there is a further emphasis on action and getting your hands on weapons and ammo that would put your playable character, Ethan Winters, at the sort of skill level you would expect from series favourites Leon Kennedy and Chris Redfield.

The village itself, whilst overrun by Lycan-type creatures, serves as a hub to branching areas, ruled by biohazard nasties that are as unique as the areas they reside in. The villains are some of the most iconic the series has introduced since the original trilogy (with our favourite vampiric madam getting an obvious mention). The varied levels themselves feel like tributes to previous titles in the series, from a luscious mansion to a dark rusty factory. There's a reason Capcom referred to Village as "a theme park of horror"; each level/area sets a different tone and even play style (with the more psychological-horror direction of House Beneviento being a particular highlight), which offers variety and intrigue for what will come next.

Although the more open-world approach of exploration is a welcome departure from the previous game's, the puzzle-solving is pretty damn lacklustre, which will leave long-term fans pretty disappointed.   

Without spoiling anything, the plot is decent and tie's in to the wider Resident Evil universe fairly well. However marks have to be taken away in regards to Chris "boulder-basher" Redfield and how he goes about things from the very beginning of the game.

Overall though, a very worthy main instalment in the most beloved survival horror franchise out there.

I took my time completing Village, stopping to admire the vast set pieces and graphics that the RE Engine has to offer. In that regard, Resident Evil Village is certainly something to admire. The game plays well too. The first person combat is engaging on a level that first person shooters tend to struggle with in modern times. All of the fights are engaging and will keep you on your toes.

Where Village struggles the most is in it's name: Resident Evil. This is not a new argument. People have been asking "how is 'x' a Resident Evil game?" Of course, "x" is any number of Resident Evil titles from 4 - 8. Resident Evil 4 showcases an arsenal of weapons and ammo unlike it's predecessors, Resident Evil 5 leans into the action, Resident Evil 6 becomes an ensamble action movie wannabe, and Resident Evil 7 takes things a back to the roots - but only with regards to the limited resources while changing perspective to first person. 

The biggest hurdle is in Village's story. I admit that I was scratching my head in the beginning when Chris is made to look like the bad guy, but we later find out that he was acting in Ethan and the world's best interest by shooting Mia. After Ethan's "death", Chris says that he just didn't have time to explain to Ethan what was really going on. Really Chris? You couldn't utter the words "That's not Mia, it's a clone - I'll explain later, but you have to trust me?" Anything along those lines really would have sufficed? And while that doesn't have the biggest impact on the outcome, it's these nuanced story moments that confuse the hell out of me. The Cadou makes them into lycans if the host is rejected. What a convenient way to work vampires and warewolves into a Resident Evil game. Then we're introduced to Heisenberg, a super-being with powers reminiscent to Magneto from X-Men. Without going into tons of detail, I would just ask fans of the series if you're really okay with Resident Evil turning into a Wizard show.

There aren't many big connections to previous games, aside from 7, and that's okay really. I view 7 and 8 as their own entry into the franchise that should be an open and closed chapter into the franchise. I get a bit more confused why they are proper numbered entries into the series and not called something else. Even Code Veronica is not a proper numbered title into the franchise.

The story does have some nods to previous games, like Spencer getting his inspiration from this village and Ethan actually having been dead / turned into a mold monster. The payout on the Ethan story line is satisfying, while the nods to Umbrella are simply met with my reaction of "that's neat, now moving on..." What I am intrigued by is the BSAA using bio-weapons. I don't trust Capcom to follow-through in a very meaningful way with this, but I want to be proven wrong on this point. Their insistence to add all kinds of Gothic lore tangled with super-powers and more final form monsters perplexes me.

Why I would not recommend this game to other players: Assuming you're a fan of the franchise, you're already on board to buy this game and play for yourself to make up your own mind. Many with disagree with me, and I would assume that those who disagree regard Resident Evil 4 as the best game of the series (it is not). To me, Resident Evil Village further drives a very confusing and convoluted narrative apart from it's roots of survival horror. While it does prove that some well timed action sequences can serve a purpose (playing as Chris), it also proves that more isn't always more. Having more guns and ammo never gives me the sense of losing, and on that same token you're never truly scared. When resources are limited, saves are few and far between, and you never know what's lurking around the next new corner is what keeps Resident Evil fresh.

I'm hopeful, given the resurgence of a spotted zombie, that Resident Evil is working it's way back to what made the franchise a household name in the first place. I would absolutely love to see an open world Raccoon City style game. The T-Virus mixed with some of these other bio-weapons getting let loose on an urban setting would be a new and exciting direction.

This was played in 3 sessions, finishing on 13 hours of gameplay on hardcore and exploring everything.

I am REALLY happy with the game, it feels like an overall love letter to the RE franchise, 
In the first few hours you go up against everyone's favorite lady, Dimitrescu.
It is very reminiscent of RE 3 and 2 where you have in the early stages more scripted encounters, tho it gradually shifts to a more RE 2 feeling, where the AI is let lose on you and honestly, the developers put all the thought and sound design into it, to make it possible to be fully immersed and have great scares and other than their second and third games counterpart, the lady and her 3 little witches have tons more character in terms of personality, which is not to say that nemesis and Mr.X were bad, since it was their character to be Machines, created solely to destroy.
My only problem here is with the witches, as they are known to cause massive frame drops, we talk about from 60-120, all the way to 10 frames a second, tho oddly and relievingly, those are the only moments in the game where i had them, so i would assume that, unless you really overestimate your PC, they will be your only moments in this game as well, which is a minor portion of the game.

There are tho other threats, which are also present later into the game, tho i will word things without spoiling much.
What i will say tho, is that you should not get to attached to the lady, as she is not the only one, you'll get the pleasure facing.
Later on, the game feels very different, which at first, was a great displeasure for me but the developers made sure, that you will enjoy the later parts, as if they knew that they have to impress.
My main gripe is the second enemy you will meet, as for me it was a very boring fight compared to others, tho as said, every main enemy is supposed to represent a different part of RE's franchise, which in this case, was a lot about psychological horror and another genre which i can not explain or tell, without spoiling something

The next one felt a bit more like resident evil 4/5 in all honesty, tho they did their best to remove everything that made 4 and 5 bad, at least to my feelings. I will just suggest to activate subtitles for this one ... cause boy was that one hard to understand.
Overall, it is a very adrenaline pumping section, that also focuses on body horror as well as another fear which i yet again can not mention, without spoiling a thing. Tho overall it made me feel uncomfortable for some reason this whole section which i think is a good thing, since this is what the developers seem to try to achieve, again very good execution in every way. 

Next is a genre i can not completely put my finger on, tho it is by far just as stunning as the first time you get the village in view. The visuals in this part of the game are really breathtaking, i mean by all that we believe in, this must have taken weeks if not months to create. This and the castle seem like they were the ones with the most work put behind by a large margin, which is not to say that other parts of the game look bad, in contrary, they look very good, if not stunning, if that is to give a scale on how immense and grand the design of the level is. It took me literally half an hour, just to take in the view.
It again, has a lot of Body horror with again another main genre which i can not name without spoiling most of it.
What i can say tho is that this enemy is just as good as Dimitrescu. He is charming and a showboater, tho has the skill to back up his demeanor. Ontop of that, during the last fight in that section is a quote packed up as an easter egg which should make some RE5 player chuckle, i know it made me laugh a little so hold out your ears for that one.

The last section is a full on RE6 feeling, which hold your horses, is fine here, since it is the climax and it just fits in and does oddly enough NOT betray the franchise given the context. Also there is something elseyou get to do during that, which is pretty sick in my opinion and gives you lorewise a huge intel on how strong Ethan is in comparison to the other good guys in the RE franchise, again a great story telling tool made manifest and used for said purpose. The ending likes to pull on your heartstrings and the music in the last section is just immense.

Other than that i will talk quickly about difficulty. 
If you want a true horror experience with anxiety inducing moments, cause you worry about your ammo and have to be worried about every single shot and care on when to shoot and what to craft as well as be VERY cautious about taking damage, play hardcore. You WILL feel like prey at first that gradually becomes stronger, which again, fits VERY well to the stories progression and i can only recommend it. That said no one should feel feel bad to go lower on their first playthrough, as it can be frustrating and stressful and if you do not like that, i would not recommend it and tell you to go normal/easy on the first time and hardcore on the next one.

But wait there is more, this game literally wants to make you play again, this is due to really cool and nice rewards on your second playthrough like a really strong weapon which will help you beat the insanely difficult "village of shadows" difficulty and by all means, if you feel like more, definetly play more or play the mercenary mode, as this is another piece of content for this game. This game was made by developers who understand their community and made a game for them. It is not only a love letter to the franchise, but to horror it self in many ways, it often makes fun of you by scaring you in another way when you are oh so sure that it will happen in another way. They knew how to design the sounds and the scares, just .. wow .. i rarely had so much fun in a videogame.

My conclusion, this game is Masterpiece, not a flawless one, tho a Masterpiece nontheless. 10 out of 10

Like a normal Resident Evil game, it's like 70% stupid that is held up by the 30% of it that's cool.

[h1]The 30% that's Cool[/h1]

The game's structure is pretty cool. Hub with four spokes. The village is the hub, each of the four spokes is one of our Dark Souls Lords.

The hub offers the most exploration. It's pretty fun coming back to the hub, noticing a new path has opened up and then scouring that path.

The fourth spoke, Heisenberg's, is my personal favorite. Frankenstein/Golem inspired, it's dark, grimy, rusty and it contains the most dangerous enemies. Only times I felt anything like panic were in his section. His boss fight is moronic in the good RE-style way, too. So that's fun.

The broad strokes of the story are cool. Ethan's a special guy. Miranda is using him like a Champion of Ash. Umbrella ties in. Mia's evil. Village and Dulvey, Louisiana have some things in common. Pretty cool.

[h1]The 70% that's Stupid[/h1]

Mia's evil, but nobody seems to care (including the writers) and she totally gets away with everything.

Ethan's a special guy, but why on Earth isn't Mia? The thing that happened to him also should have happened to her. But for story-convenience reasons, it didn't?

The story is childish. It will look like some messed up interesting things are happening. But don't worry. This is RE Village. Everything's fine, because the writers opted for the safe way out every single time.

Most of the game is actually pretty boring. Castle Dimistrescu is really popular among other players, but I don't understand why. It's a railroaded collection of narrow corridors. Alcina and her daughters are stalkers. The daughters are just walls of fire--they show up in the direction you shouldn't run so you can run down the progression hallway. Alcina is a more permanent stalker, but she's an imbecile. She walks 1 mph, she pauses for like 5 seconds after she successfully hits you, and she just forgets you exist if you run into certain rooms or if you put like 1.5 rooms of distance between you.

Beneviento's house is just an escape room. But it's Resident Evil, so there's no challenge to it. Obvious but coy hints are scattered around on notes, and there's usually only one interactable in every room. The greatest crime that section commits is that the story it tells isn't real. It's all crap Beneviento is making up to scare Ethan. So the story doesn't even move during that section.

Fish man is fine, but his zone is just a boss fight and that's it.

Mechanically, blocking solves all of your problems. Alcina shows up and extends her claws? Just hold block, tank the hit then run around her during her following 5 seconds of derp. Seriously. She's supposed to be one of Miranda's great Lords, and in cutscenes she's very threatening. During the game, she's a complete incompetent.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

Basically a cool overarching story. Very stupid story details.

Heisenberg's section is fun and tense. The others are easy (sometimes pointless) slogs.

Resident Evil is always stupid. This one is also childish, so I find it to be the worst of the RE Engine games so far (2,3,4,7,8.9 are currently out).

But play it, if you like Resident Evil. I'm sure the story told will be referenced in future games.
