What a waste of potential.

It seems Capcom decided to go for a cinematic experience above all else when they created this game, as the incredibly claustrophbic FOV will attest to. Puzzles are basically nonexistent and especially simple to figure out, often with solutions presented to you in the same room mere steps away, and any complexity you might expect also stripped away. The handholding is immense - the yellow tape / paint of handholding is back, but in an extreme sense, and guides you every step of the way, and then you have big white prompt circles that appear based on proximity and where you are looking in order to guide you even further down the plot. As a first person game, you'd expect there to be an emphasis on actually exploring your environment up close and actually carefully examining the area, but nope - no need. Just look for yellow and white, and you're golden!

It really annoyed me that this game is in first person. Not because I think this game series belongs squarely in the fixed camera or third person perspective, but because of the absolutely abhorrant waste of potential and lazy use of creativity involving a first person game in general, which was also demonstrated with how Capcom decided to handle RE7 and there hasn't been any improvement, only a downgrade. You can't lean, you can't low crouch / prone, you can't stretch up on your tip toes to look on top of objects, you can't do anything but crouch and look around. Even with the ability to crouch, there is never any need to peek under a desk or a table, never a need to peek inside a cannon to find a hidden object or lean behind a suit of armour to find a hidden switch, no need to stretch and look on top of a fridge or something, nothing. Beyond looking up at the ceiling for shiny treasures or a bright yellow bird cage to shoot down, there's no other interesting first person gameplay at all. 

Not even the puzzles benefit from first person persective, except one of them - and it's boring. You look out of a window and see three numbers on three different objects and, without even having to figure out the correct order or the colour of the numbers themselves, you just read them left to right and you have your very basic padlock code. I can say with certainty that the first person perspective is purely used to attract the same audience as those who enjoyed the glut of oversaturated first person horror games that were in their height of popularity during the mid 2010's, and so the game can provide a cinematic experience rather than a mechanically interesting gameplay one.

It saddens me what this game could have been if they had used some spark of creativity and not focus solely on presentation and story elements. You've got this world, the characters in it, even a passable story to involve yourself in, but there's little for the player to actually do beyond following set pieces so rigid that any thought of replayability or options provided for "player agency" is completely impossible. The intro alone before any gameplay begins is at least 10 minutes long (replaying) of what amounts to just holding forward and skipping cutscenes, it's REmake3 all over again.

They favoured immersion, seemingly, but then decided to give every character in this unspecified Eastern European town an American accent. Not even a hodgepodge of interesting accents from across the continent, instead it's some generic boring plain and clear accent devoid of any character in almost all cases. Not that it matters anyway because most of the NPCs you meet will be dead within 5 minutes of showing up because...why exactly? What was the whole point of the section where you visit Luiza's house anyway? Just another linear interactive cutscene and a boring time waster for any future playthroughs. Every NPC you meet there dies in the same breath and have absolutely no bearing on the rest of the game. 

The world is set up to completely discourage exploration. Typically you'll find areas that present a lot of options to you, but then you'll discover all of the doors are locked except one. You'll quickly realise that this is always the correct way to go, no side paths (except one noticeable one involving a mini-boss with some treasure and meat as loot) to get lost in, it's just constant point A to point B gameplay. You don't have to worry about all the other doors if you find the unlocked one first, don't fear you might be missing something, because you aren't. 

There's so much I want to say about this game and its flaws and I know I'm going to run out of room in this review to do so. I'll move swiftly on to Lady Dimitrescu. Another implacable pursuer type enemy for you to avoid, only this time as dumb as a bag of rocks. She walks slowly after you, can't dash or jump over objects / up a flight of stairs, and has a lengthy animation where she exposes or conceals a clawed hand when you get too close or too far away, easily exploited to simply run past her while she's stuck in the animation. She appears for a very short amount of time and in no serious capacity, as soon as you get around her she's left in the dust. No fear, no suspense, no chasing you throughout the entire area either - just hanging around the main lobby to harass you as you move through, despite the fact she's wailing at you and vowing to destroy you for the offences you've committed against her, etc. What a waste. 

Oh, and a personal gripe I suppose: reused assets. I can understand doing this sparingly, but when you see the same rug in the same position five times in the starting house, and then see the same cheap bottle of "Regina Rose" wine copied and pasted throughout the whole game, among other assets like pots, pans, rotten potatoes, slashed cushions etc, it starts to grate on me a little. The absolute kicker is the Boltcutters though - remember those? First appearing in RE7 and then being used in REmake2, and then REmake3, and now again in RE8, the EXACT SAME item used for the EXACT SAME THING for the fourth game in a row. They didn't even take the time to make them look different, changing the colour or the texture to be rusty or old, just a pair of brand new bright red boltcutters in this dilapidated village. It's insulting that Capcom clearly doesn't believe it's worth the time - or you, for that matter - making new assets for a new full priced AAA game.

Also consider the "Trauma Pack" DLC which is just a bunch of already created assets from RE7 being sold to you for the asking price of 20% a full priced AAA game! What the hell is even that? Why would you not include that for free as a pre-order bonus or an unlockable item if the game detects you have RE7 saved data on your system? 

Similar in scope are the recycled concepts from older games. For example, the inventory. It's a clear homage to RE4's attache case, but without any of the charm and honestly necessity. Since crafting items are stored in a separate menu like key items and treasures, the only thing going inside your inventory are weapons, ammo and health - and some meat and lockpicks, which honestly make no sense if they're going to have a separate inventory for key items and such, but oh well. It's a nice homage but a thoroughly pointless one, as unless you're storing 5+ weapons you're not going to have any chance of filling it up.

Other concepts like how the game retains an early game attack you need to survive against in a village, then you visiting a castle, and then visiting a lake to fight a giant fish boss, and then visiting a stronghold and factory with many enemies present, and even a final boss that resembles Saddler with a body supported by spider legs can be pointed out as being a distinct lack of something new. You could even almost change a few characters to RE4 ones and call this a reboot or a remake, thanks to the similarities it wouldn't even be that much of a stretch - we've already seen worse offences from a remake to the source material, look at REmake3.

But aide from this one mission, most of the time it's quite clear what you need to do: either you know the objective, or you have some areas left to explore.

The game feels like the previous installment, Resident Evil 7, but it's more shooty than that one was. There are a few main areas that you will visit and they can feel very different in gameplay. The castle is like the house in RE7, where you investigate to find items to open doors for short-cuts or progress, while (eventually) being hunted by the Big Lady, then here is an area that's a lot more horror-hide-in-the-closet and even a full-on First Person Shooter area, where you get so much ammo you don't need to think about shooting or avoiding. Personally, I think Resi 7 was the superior game in drawing you in to a creepy horror atmosphere, a new take for the Resi series. Resi 8 puzzles feel quite trivial, seems a bit too easy on Standard (recommend going Hardcore) and only a rare few moments of really creepy tense bits.

With that out of the way, I think I am hooked into the story of Resi now. Played RE 2 remake , a dash of RE 3 remake because it was bad, and Resi 7 (skipping 4, 5 and 6, though waiting for 4's remaster). Resi Village looks beautiful, the atmosphere is immersive and can feel creepy at first until you get your head wrapped around the game after a few hours. Despite not being as a bit more free form than Resi 7 in terms of the boss encounters, Resi Village is worth the ride especially if you have been following the series this long. One of the game's strengths is that it doesn't feel like it overstays it's welcome as I clocked 10 hours on finishing my first playthrough, which I feel is a decent length, not too long or not too short, although I'd say once you play on harder difficulty you'll take a bit more time.

Resident Evil Village is a lot like Final Fantasy IX, in that it's a celebration of the series as a whole. There are influences from and call outs to other games felt throughout, and is wonderful to spot all of them. The ramped up action is very reminiscent of RE4, so if that's what you like in an RE game, this is for you.

The game also does a lot with a smaller space. The village is the perfect size for this game. The smaller space is more intimate, and the devs did a great job implementing environmental storytelling in each of the game's locations. Every time you complete a section of the game, a new part of the village opens up, letting the familiar feel new again. There are constantly new places to explore, treasures to find, and Easter eggs to locate that really bring the series together in both lore and game play.

There are a couple of downsides, however. Two of the villains don't feel properly fleshed out in terms of character. As well as this, their sections are far shorter than the first and last sections of the game.

However, despite all that, the game's length still feels good. Your first playthrough could be anywhere from 8-13 hours depending on desire to explore. There are some optional areas and treasures that are great for completionists, as well as at least two optional bosses. There is also a side activity to hunt to boost Ethan's health, guard damage reduction, and movement speed.

All in all, I highly recommend this game for RE fans and survival horror fans alike. The game is very replayable with optional items that can be purchased with an endgame currency (only accessible after your first completion of the game), as well as The Mercenaries, an arcade challenge mode.

This is such a unique entry into the RE franchise. While the game feels like a mix between RE7 and RE4, parts of the game feel completely different from either entry, which I believe to be a good thing, as it separates itself from other titles while still retaining that RE feel. I was worried that this game would end up with a "boat section" like in RE7, but none of the areas in the game felt like that, though I will say I think the factory section dragged on longer than I would have expected. Village also doesn't skimp out on the RE fan service, dropping references to many other scenes in other games, some more obvious and some very subtle. Overall, I think this is a fantastic game and a great entry into the series, as it feels familiar yet completely unique at the same time, and more importantly, the gameplay is fantastic and there is a ton of replayability with New Game+ and Mercenaries, as well as the Bonus Shop with a ton of things to unlock. I will say, however, if you're expecting that classic RE survival horror feel like RE1 Remake, you are going to be disappointed, as this game focuses much more on action than horror, though there is some horror at certain parts.

I've been playing Resident Evil games for 25 years, have made fan websites and groups - enjoyed most of the movies, made youtube videos about the franchise for years.
So going into this I knew what to expect from an RE game, 
They're have fast thinking gameplay, with a mix of horror and action, with gorgeous environments, puzzles and terrifying monsters to compliment it. 
With those expectations, Resident Evil Village did not disappoint - it's environments are like none before it, the monsters are awesome, imaginative puzzles are scattered everywhere and there are even side missions if you look hard enough.
The combat starts off with a village segment similar to RE4, the enemies are always eerie, lurking around and stalking you.
The Village itself is one of the most immersive environments constructed by capcom to date.With it's sound design amplifying it's atmosphere. Small snaps of wood, bottles rolling down the beaten paths, monsters growls heard from a distance. 
Capcom has made a truly realistic feel to Village and it's inhabitants, but just because everything is pretty doesn't mean it cant get obscenely ugly - there are countless grotesque creatures to be found in REVIII.
There are vastly different parts of the village to explore so the limits of the kinds of enemies you encounter are numerous.
Go into Resident Evil village with high expectations, it will not only meet them but surprise you with it's experimental nature as well. 
Resident Evil Village is about 10-12 hours if you take your time, but naturally there will be speedrunners and I believe it's speed runner friendly. With all that said, RE Village is easily an 8.5/10

Resident Evil 8 can be seen as a combination of the survival-horror gameplay elements from it's direct predecessor, Resident Evil 7, with themes and mechanics that mirror Resident Evil 4. RE8 is a solid sequel to 7 that offers an interesting cast of characters and steps up the action while still walking that thin line between going *too* action-heavy and keeping the stress/horror aspect that is critical to RE games. Graphics are incredible, the voice acting/writing feels like a step up over 7, the music is very atmospheric, building a lot of tension for encounters, its done well but doesn't offer anything that particularly stands out. The game is incredibly atmospheric, creepy, and disturbing at times, but I wouldn't necessarily call it 'scary'. It's an empowering survival action game and it's a lot of fun.

RE Village's negatives aren't that bad in my opinion but while puzzles in RE games have been easy for many games, these are far easier. Most of the game for me ran flawlessly but the bugs that are on the vampire sisters did cause frame drops when they got close. Finally, there's no FOV slider. Graphics are very pretty. Lots of details on the enemies and each location looking really nice. I saw a few muddy textures here and there but it didn't exactly distract me from the overall presentation.

I've played all games from RE0 to this one, including the remakes of some of the titles. 
Cleared the game in 7 hours in hardcore (first playthrough), with skipping a few parts of the village because I was very much intrigued in the story. Currently taking my time now in my 2nd playthrough.

Having played previous titles and specifically RE7, the game that preceded RE : Village, this entry is definitely a huge improvement from RE7, and overall a very good entry in the franchise. RE : Village, comapred to RE7, leans more towards gunplay and action, but still a very 'classic', slow, and methodical approach when it comes to movement and gunfights. 

I can still call RE : Village a survival horror, since that is the genre of the RE series. If RE7 was more horror than action, and RE4 being more action than horror, RE Village brings the great parts of both titles. Action/gunplay feels great, but not the 'best' course of action for every encounter. Avoiding/dodging and enemies and just 'speedrunning' several parts feels very rewarding and cool, but some segments require precise gunplay if you want to go through as unscathed as possible.

I don't want to spoil the story because I found it to be one of the best in the series, but several plot elements in the game just wow'd me. Of course, like true RE fashion, some parts are cliche and need a bit of suspension of disbelief, but overall, the writing is great.

If you were disappointed in RE5, RE6, RE3R Village more than makes up for the shortcomings of those games. It feels complete, well thought, and greatly executed.

Having said that, I have a few problems with this title.
-There are performance issues when fighting the Dimitrescu Daughters, specially when their bug swarm shows up and when they bite you.
-A little nitpicking, but while Ethan and other characters have splendid voice acting, some segments of the game have...odd direction/choice when it comes to voice lines or lack thereof.
-FOV feels a bit too low. I wish Capcom added (or at least add it in the future) an FOV slider. It can be disorienting at certain areas.

After playing this title, I'm very much excited for the ending of this trilogy. I hope you are too, after finishing this game!

[h1] [u]Quick Overview[/u] [/h1]
"Resident Evil: Village" is a first-person survival horror game set three years after the events of "Resident Evil 7". We play as Ethan Winters as he wages against Lycans, blood-sucking monsters, and the undead to save his daughter, Rose. It is more action-oriented than its predecessor, but it does not take away from the survival horror experience we come to love in a RE game. Highly recommended for fans of the RE franchise and/or survival horror in general.

[h2] Pros: [/h2]
[list] 
           [*] Intense, survival horror action
           [*] Amazing atmosphere and sound design
           [*] Gorgeous graphics
           [*] Fun boss battles, varied enemy types      
           [*] Great performance, no bugs/glitches
           [*] Lady Dimitrescu's "performance"
[/list]  
 [h2] Cons: [/h2]
[list] 
           [*] Framerate dips during certain encounters with the swarm of insects
            
[/list]  
-- --

[h1] [u]The Gist of the Story [/u][/h1]
Ethan and his family were relocated to Europe upon the request of Chris Redfield. Ethan was ready to create new memories with his wife, Mia, and daughter Rosemary until tragedy struck them. Redfield ambushes Ethan at his home and kidnaps him and his daughter away for reasons unknown. En route to an unfamiliar destination, the transport Ethan was in crashed, and now he must fight his way through this hostile land filled with wild beasts to save his little daughter.

[b] [u]My Thoughts[/u] [/b]
In terms of the story as a whole, it was an amazing journey. I enjoyed it tremendously. I found myself eager to reach another plot point because I was anxious to discover what is going on with this remote village and its denizens. I scoured every place I can go to for documents and note pages, so I can gather more intel about anything related to the events unfolding. The ending was bittersweet, but it made sense because of what occurred throughout the game. It also opens up a new protagonist for future Resident Evil games, so I am highly anticipating what will happen next. 
-- --

[h1][u] Gameplay [/u][/h1]
During the first half, it is more slow-paced horror with some action bits strewn about. However, it gradually shifts into a more fierce action-oriented game, akin to "Resident Evil 4", during the later parts. I certainly don’t mind the shift, but later on, resource management becomes more difficult because you are crafting ammo or healing items more often than not. 

The game is also more open than RE 7. There are more places to explore and detours to visit. These exploration sections were a nice break from the usual stressful moments of the main campaign, and I found them worthwhile for the most part. 

[b] [u]Crafting, Inventory, and Resource Management [/u] [/b]
Crafting has its own tab and a separate inventory from your main items. This was a welcome change because it allows you to craft ammo, explosives, and curatives in a more organized fashion. You are able to buy blueprints from the merchant so that you can put resources you find, like scrap metal and gunpowder, to good use. 

Inventory management seems to be easier as well since you can rotate your items and weapons to arrange your belongings around, but I would have also appreciated some kind of auto-arrange button for more convenience. There is no storage system but more inventory space can be bought to the point where I didn't think about space anymore. 

Since this is a survival horror game, resource management is key to survival. Prioritizing what to craft first will depend on what you think is needed. Some items require the same ingredients to make so players will sometimes have to decide which items they would need in their given situation. 

[b] [u] Weapon Variety and Customization [/u][/b]
Ethan must survive countless attacks from horrendous monsters and to stay alive he needs a particular set of weapons to fend them off. He has a variety of weapons in his arsenal, ranging from handguns, shotguns, and a sniper rifle. You can upgrade them as you progress through the game and find modifications to improve them beyond their normal capabilities.

[b][u] Hunting and Cooking[/u] [/b]
Cooking and hunting are new additions, and that encourages exploration because you have to search for a few local animals to cook with the aid of the merchant. Cooking permanently boosts Ethan’s stats/abilities (i.e. health pool). Let me just say that I got way too excited when I saw the boosts. I think this is another great addition, and hopefully, Capcom expands on this a bit more in the future.

[b] [u]Bosses [/u] [/b]
The boss battles are pretty fun, and memorable as far RE bosses go. They have their patterns and gimmicks that you should learn to make the fight more manageable. They aren’t too difficult, but you still have to be mindful of their attacks because they can still rip Ethan to pieces. I also appreciate the different types of enemies each new area provided. It keeps the game fresh since the enemies have their specific movesets that can surprise you.
-- --

[h1][u] Scare Factor[/u] [/h1]
I must discuss the scare factor. I would rate it a 9/10. The tense-filled atmosphere, coupled with amazing sound design in some of the locations Ethan will traverse was intense. From the hostile “Lycan” turned locals to the blood-drinking daughters of Lady Dimitrescu’s, they kept me on my toes and my gun ready to shoot.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2482315985

As I previously mentioned , the first half is where the horror lies. I felt more apprehensive and terrified during this section. The enemies do not come at you in droves for the most part, allowing the atmosphere to take center stage and make its players feel uneased. The foreboding sense that something will jump at you at any moment crops up. Castle Dimitrescu and the House of Beneviento (the first two larger areas) are where this is amplified the most. These two areas were my favorite. 
-- --

[h1][u] Graphics and Technical Issues[/u] [/h1]
For context, my specs are RTX 2070 Super, i7 4790S, 12 GB ram. Playing on 2160p resolution.

The game is beautiful. I love what a friend said about RE Village. They said that you can just take a random screenshot, and it would still look good. I would have to agree with them, as the vistas of the locales are gorgeous. This is the best looking RE game at the time of writing this.

I encountered no bugs and only have some slight performance dips. I noticed these dips in framerates occurred when I was fighting with Lady Dimitrescu’s daughters. The swarms of insects they summon to attack Ethan are just too much for my pc, I guess. Other than that, my playthrough was a smooth 60 fps, and I played on very high.
-- --

[h1][u] Wrap Up[/u] [/h1]

Resident Evil: Village was more action than what I was expecting. It took me about 14 hours to complete. The end game content is robust, and there's always Mercenaries to play. All in all, Resident Evil: Village was worth the hype it received. If you are a fan of RE games and/or survival horror games in general, I highly recommend this game.

I heavily recommend this game. Although it relies upon the past lore the series has established in its long running, Village proves a worthy successor to both the absurdity and survival horror that the series has long trademarked. Technical issues relating to a lack of FOV settings and inconsistent frame rates in some areas provide some frustration. However, the design of the game from its gunplay, puzzle elements and environments provide a much greater experience that easily offsets the negatives. Some of the early game is confusing/frustrating, especially on harder difficulties, but didn't prove too annoying to deter me. Thankfully, there's depth to the combat with a newly added parrying feature and the typical guarding and shooting. Speaking of shooting, all the weapons feel great to use and have their purpose within the greater game, even if it is not necessary to use them all. Despite a few technical issues, RE Village serves well on the design portion and provides a mostly optimized experience for a game with such a strong graphical fidelity and scale.

Narratively, this game follows RE7's Mia ending and takes place years after as the Winters family establishes their
home in Eastern Europe. Their home is full of references to the series and provides a jumping off point to drag Ethan back into the horrors once again. Returning faces such as Chris provide a sense of uniformity with the greater series, despite the newer games being relatively separate from them. All the villains are well-characterized and serve their own role in understanding the village, from the famously known Alcina Dimitrescu to the grisly body horror of Salvatore Moreau, the psychological horror of Donna Beneviento and the freakish creations of Karl Heisenberg, a personal favorite.  However, as a note, the game's marketing and emphasis on the Dimitrescu family is misleading and it should be noted that the game moves towards many unfamiliar characters, so if that is exclusively your interest, do not expect much more content with them than you've already seen. 

Also of note is The Mercenaries, an incredibly fun and fast-paced arcade mode that is a long-held Resident Evil tradition which tests map knowledge, routing and aim. This mode comes with unlocks of its own and ties into the challenge shop, which unlocks concept art, models, and weaponry to use in further playthroughs as well as the traditional infinite ammo weapons. Together, these incentivize multiple means of playing, from achievement hunting to recording breaking as all helps with obtaining points to unlock these rewards.

If you have not, play Resident Evil 7 before playing this one for narrative reasons, but both serve to provide some of the best survival horror this generation and show that Capcom is willing to experiment with the formula for the better of the series. I have a strong appreciation for this game and am eagerly awaiting the RE team's next game.

RE Village has satisfying combat, superb visuals and audio, and a fun story. Ammo and resource management keeps things tense, and the combat is fast paced as enemies now dodge and weave much more erratically compared to those in RE7. The bits between the frantic combat sections have a nice sense of exploration as you unlock new areas, collect more goodies, and hunt for ammo to restock for the next battle. The different areas you'll visit in your play through provide a nice sense of variety, while keeping a decent enough connection to the game as a whole. Some people say the story is kind of crap but I enjoyed it, particularly how off-the-rails it goes towards the end of the game. The over-the-top action set pieces ramp up quick, and they're fun as hell. Village definitely leans a bit into the more action focused entries like RE4.

I can only think of a couple negatives about Village. The first is the arbitrary locking of areas after you leave them. This prevents you from going back to loot-hunt for no other reason than: a piece of debris fell in front of the door and now it's closed forever. It's frustrating to learn later that you missed a goat or some cooking ingredients, and now they're gone forever. The other thing I didn't love is that a couple of the main antagonists aren't as fleshed out as I'd prefer. They're still decent, but I'd have liked longer sections or more story for bosses two and three. I will say though, the second boss area was really creepy. Probably my favorite section in the game.

RE Village is overall a very good entry into the series. I'd put it right up there with RE7: better in some ways, worse in others, but a great continuation of the story. It took me around 10 hours to complete the campaign, with plenty of loot hunting included. If you liked RE4 and RE7, this game is well worth your $60.

I think a big issue was the villains themselves. The main villain Mother Miranda is nowhere to be seen until the final hour and when we do get her she's just a boring cliche villain with no personality or charm unlike some of the lords like Lady Dimitrescu who we should have gotten much more of. She has her own little segment in her castle which lasts a few hours and then you move on. The other lords don't hold up as well. 

The core Resident Evil gameplay is still here which is why i can easily recommend this game to any fan of the franchise. The satisfying exploration is still here, but uncovering the village and the locations around it is not as complex or involving as the mansion from RE1 or the police station in RE2 was for example. The puzzles also leaned too much on the easier side, was kind of hoping to have to use my brain a bit more. I did like the switch to more action focused gameplay. Much bigger variety of enemies to fight and weapons to use and i like the homage given to RE4 with the inventory management, currency, the merchant and of course the setting of the game. Overall i enjoyed the game quite a bit, i was never bored throughout the 10 hour journey and i am going back on a higher difficulty just like the other RE games, i was just hoping for a bit more out of the game.

The graphics, oh my god, the graphics. I have rarely found myself wondering in awe at a Game that much. For me Resi 8 joins the ranks of Horizon Zero Dawn, Control, Cyberpunk, Tomb Raider and AC Odyssey/Valhalla. (I know there are more, but those were the most stunningly looking that Ive acutally played). Its not only that the textures, the lightning, reflections and all the technical shenanigans are great, but its the balance of light, shadows, coloring, reflections etc. that makes this game truly shine. Capcom managed to find the sweet spot to set the perfect tone for Ethans second Journey through the Marcabre.

The sound design, for me is always the special child. From the roaring of the beasts or the sound of the guns to the little rustles, snaps, creaks and cracks. All those litte details that were added, Capcom absolutely nailed it. I found myself all too often cramped up in my chair holding my breath in tense situations, to a good portion thanks to the superb sound design and muscial composition.

Last but not least, the gameplay. For the most part Resi 8 follows the same phases. Get to a new area, kill boss, explore for extra loot, upgrade stuff, repeat. Sounds simple,.. and, well it is. But you dont really need much innovation, when the structure you built is filled with Quality content. E.g. the balance of loot and currency/treasure for upgrades. I never felt having an excess of either, but also never felt like there was an all too threating shortage as long as i played it smart (on Standard difficulty). This kinda stands symbolic for the whole gameplay experience. Also got to mention, in my almost lifelong career as a gamer i have probably killed a thousand bosses, but after some of resi 8`s bosses I was just smiling, thinking:"F**k, that was awesome.." Capcom has to have done something right achieving this. I guess, its a mixture of all the things ive stated above.

Conclusively, Resident Evil 8 follows a simple recipe, but a simple recipe done right.. and that all the way. The sound, gaphics, story, map, riddles, gunplay etc... the whole feeling of it. And sadly nowadays you have to state that (at least in my exp.) they did it bug free. *looks over at CDPR with visible dejection*

[h1] First impressions [/h1]
Another great installment into the series. Has experimental ideas implemented and allows for more insight into the lore of the story. Great use of ray traced lighting, and very high detail model scans that create very beautiful environments and characters with an ever higher level of detail than before. The Reach for the Moon Engine (RE Engine) really shines. You can even see your own foot prints that have depth and shadow in the snow. Has a good length to the story with replay value. Even though the sorting boxes are removed it has not effected my play through with not having enough space for items. Much like all Biohazard / Resident Evil games you will revisit areas for items or loot, I do like this and it never felt stale to me. It really feels rewarding after searching a room for minutes to find a hidden gem then clearing that room. Some of the puzzles were fresh and was nice to be able to figure them out, it never frustrated me. I feel like the Normal difficulty was a little easy, I only died once when I did not hit something in time in a boss fight and the boss fights didn't require much in normal.
[h1] Some Technical Issues [/h1]
One issue I've had was on the Labyrinth Puzzles on Keyboard specifically the Heisenberg's Factory Labyrinth Puzzle there seemed to be input delay even on a mechanical keyboard or some weird physics delay when rotating. To complete this puzzle I had to plug in a controller then it allowed me to have better control of the puzzle with a lot less delay. Some optimization issues I've had some of the times is when you walk into areas it loads them in but I've experienced engine timing issues that drops frames/slows the engine. Possible with the shaders as I am running the game off of a NVMe M.2 PCI-Express 4 SSD. It stops when you walk back to the previous area or exit and reload the game. Also if you set Anti-aliasing Transparency in the Nvidia control panel to a value and then set it off again it breaks the engine and makes the textures look very dull and pixelated so I have to keep it on / off the default setting if it has been changed. Also had issues with engine timing if you alt-tab and then return to the game but it is known for me at least on the RE engine. Smaller things include models clipping through the ground in some areas and enemies sometimes initiate an animation that makes them clip through the environment but its not often that it happens or is seen. Sometimes I've also been hit when i'm far from the attack range. This happens in a lot of games however.

E-Series of the new Virus. Ethan had to kill Evelyn, then Chris Redfield and his soldiers showed up and rescued Ethan and Mia. Now we can jump to RE8.

A few years after the events of Resident Evil 7, Chris ordered Ethan and Mia to move to Europe and undergo military training and be out of civilization. However, one day Chris reappeared, shot Mia and took Ethan's daughter Rose, took Ethn to the Test Room, but during the trip there was an accident and Ethan found himself somewhere in the middle of the woods and had to get somewhere safe, he came to the village, but it was all crawling by monsters, also known as Lycans or Werewolfs, attacked Ethan and so he had to survive and get to the Village and get some answers, his task was clear, to save Rose and leave this village, but unfortunately everything gets complicated and Ethan meets the four Lords of the village.
Lady Dimitrescu, Donna Beneviento, Moreau, and Karl Heisnberg, each of these Lords has a Village section, Lady D has a Castle, Donna Beneviento owns a house further from the Village, Moreau owns a mountain and a water section, and Karl Heisnberg owns a Factory under the Village, each of Lords is represented by Bosse, who is not exactly simple and you never have a certain chance that you will get away alive.

So, I have done three runs of the game already at the time of this review. Two standard and one VoS, and I'm going to be doing a couple more runs for achievements. So is this my favorite Resident Evil game to date? No, but it's still fun. Why have I played it so much if it's not my favorite? I have no life and this came out when I needed a distraction. Why isn't this my favorite RE game? I honestly preferred the more horror driven RE7. That game was much tighter and more rewarding to beat. In this game I already got the most overpowered items by my second run. Plus I preferred the story and concept of RE7 much more, with you being a normal guy getting trapped in an RE scenario and being forced to survive. With less ties to the main franchise, it was a nice change of pace. Without getting to far into spoilers, this game tries to insert itself into the wider RE universe and that kind of ruins the experience, with the ending being a slow descent into mediocrity. In my opinion, the first two sections are the strongest in the game and then they slowly descend in quality. It's not the worst, but it is far from the best.

And yet I still have put most time into this game for some reason.

But this game does have a lot of positives. Most of the sections are fun, there are plenty of achievements to keep you coming back, mercenaries is a blast (although I hear it's a "shell of it's former self"), and there are some genuinely good horror elements. The game is great, just not as great as it's predecessor.

An okay Resident Evil game, but with that said, it's not the most impressive game in the franchise sadly.

I started the Resident Evil franchise with Resident Evil 4 and played every game since, so I was very pleased to see a back to the roots (atleast MY roots) Resident Evil game!

[h1]Story[/h1]
I liked the story very much. Without spoiling anything major I loved that at the end the game combines trough journal entries of the main villian every other big entry in the series. I loved how the new Vampire enemies has been explained the plot twists around them, I enjoined the Werewolf enemies too but less then the vampires because those have been more "impactful" and the zombie/ghul enemies were nice and atmospheric too! For me the strongest part of the story was the castle part and the ending of the game, the by far weakest part was the domain of the 4th boss because it was much like the Military guys from Resident Evil 4. I dont like the majority of act 5 in RE4 so I also disliked the 4th boss area and it was also not very logical because there was way to many "specimens" for the population of the village.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Most of the time the Gameplay revolves around fast passed combat/action and only then around horror. Then gunplay feels very good but the balance between the weapons is more bad then good. In RE4 nearly each weapon had the opportunity to get a special upgrade if upgrading everything that would give the weapon sometimes a unique property e.g. the weakest pistol would have a 50%crit chance even though it is 3,5 weaker then the strongest pistol it could potentialy kill enemies faster or the "Punisher" pistol that would shot trough 5 enemies eventough its the weakest pistol it could CC a group of enemies. In RE8 every new weapon is just better then the old one and weapon upgrades besides damage are pointless and you dont have enough money to do it anyway. Unfortunatly the knife in RE8 is very bad  compared to RE2Remake or RE4 (Best Weapon in RE4!) and the ability to CC enemies in RE8 compared to RE4 is also lackluster. There is enough ammo and healing in this game on Standard difficulty but I would not recomend to play on any harder difficulty because that is not a game that is so well balanced as RE4, the enemies are just bulletsponges and your health is low there is now fun CC aspect or knife play as in RE4.

[h1]Horror[/h1]
Many people criticize that the game is not scary at all atleast compared to RE7. I dont understand that argument at all. I think the only Scary part of RE7 was when Mia would jumpscare you from around the corner and thats it! Besides that RE7 was not more or less scary then RE8 is! If you are concerned if RE8 has any Jumpscares then the answer is: NO. There are no jumpscares at all! But jump scares is not the aspect of horror anyway! The best kind of horror is the one that happenes inside your head when you doubt things and are waiting for something that might not happen. I think the Horror part is not and never was the strongest part of any RE game ever.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
This game is gorgeous! The visuals are incredible. Everything is handplaced and looks very nice.

[h1]Performance[/h1]
I got 90 fps with 2070Super on highest settings for my 1080p monitor the only fps-lag spikes I got was around the Dimitrerscu daughters and their insect swarms which would break it down to 30fps but everyone has this problem right now even people on 3090. Other then that not a single Bug in a AAA game! This is very special in our time, I dont remeber when was the last time a new game was not a complete failure the last time.

[h1]Overall[/h1]
I loved the story, gunplay and atmosphere! I think that Lady Dimitrescu and her daughters have been the strongest part of the game and I wish for more content around them! The other boses have been less impactfull and the 4th boss I disliked! I wish they would have done more vampire stuff and I hope that in future games or DLC we can somehow return to Dimitrescu castle. With that I am looking forward to RE4Remake very much!

[h1]Another hit from Capcom[/h1]

Resident Evil is my favourite gaming series of all time and Capcom lately have been producing great game after great game, not just in the Resident Evil series but nearly across the board. Resident Evil Village continues that trend of extremely high quality games. This direct sequel to Resident Evil VII: Biohazard, which you should play first if you haven't, is an incredibly focused an well tuned experience, short intensive games like this are hard to come by these days with games like Assassin's Creed opting for unnecessary bloat over a honed experience.

[b]PROS[/b]

- The character and boss designs are fantastic, Lady Dimitrescu is just one of 5 main antagonists and they are all great in their own way
- Great enemy variety, an area REVII suffered
- Gameplay and gunplay is very solid as it was in REVII
- The level design is exceptional and exploration is well rewarded
- The merchant return. I love having lots of options and the merchant is helps that, The Duke is a great character too
- Very well paced generally, downtime after intense parts. The game does not outstay its welcome like far too many modern games do these days. 10 hours of focused, well designed gameplay
- The story is actually pretty good as it was with VII and I enjoyed the ending
- Huge amounts of replay value with mercenaries and lots of unlocks to chase

[b]CONS[/b]

- Why is there hardly any music? One of my favourite things about the older RE games are the amazing soundtracks. What music is there in Village is good, but less silence and more amazing music while exploring would be very welcome.
- Some enemies and bosses go on too long and take too long to put down
- The castle at the start is the best part of the game and the rest of the game never really hits that dizzying high despite it all being of high quality
- There is a section near the end of the game when you get rushed by loads of enemies and it just isn't very fun. I can't go into too much depth due to spoilers, thankfully it's only short. Weakest part of the game by far
- Ethan is still a bit of a nothing main character, but the surrounding cast is great as with REVII
- The merchant return was great, but in RE4 you could pick a gun and that would be viable for the whole playthrough if you decided to stick with it. In RE8 there is no reason to not upgrade your handgun and shotgun each time a new one becomes available as they are obviously better. No reason to stick with the default guns which is shame as there's not really a choice, just a perception of choice

Playing on hardcore and having no ammo in the beginning was just frustrating. I almost quit there. But I'm glad I didn't because once you pass that everything seems pretty fair and balanced. You just have to stockpile ammo and avoid enemies if you want a decent amount by the end. Also, the gun play was fun... but WHY CANT WE ADS! That seemed soooooo silly.

The story: This bih starts off at 100 and pretty much maintains that velocity the entire game. At first I was like "what?" then I was like "WHAT?!" then I was like "OH NO! WHAT!" and then I cried. Masterful game by the team at Capcom.  Village is a compendium of Resident Evil history compiled into one experience and for that reason I can say there's something for everyone.  If you are a fan of the FPS Resident Evil style then this game exceeds its forebearer in most regards.  If you like the eastern european setting and enemies dropping loot like RE4, it's got that.  Big crowds of aggressive enemies like RE5.  Exploration to find key items to open the next door like RE1-RE:CV?  More straightforward, but yes it's there.  It's a jack of all trades.  What is masters is the action combat.  It is TENSE.  I've completed the game on hardcore, and I've heard the unlockable Village of Shadows difficulty is so difficult you'll want to start with your carried over weapons from the previous playthrough just to get by.

All in all it's a very well tuned experience, expertly paced.  Amazing graphical design.  Among the best looking games I've played.  It's closest visual relative in my mind if Half Life Alyx.  A game where you'll get caught staring at the wall textures because they're so lovingly brought to life.  The detail poured into this game is phenomenal.  It's a carnival fun house roller coaster ride.  And also it's scary AF in certain parts (one in particular comes to mind); but the overall tension works for the Survival Horror genre and gives you the thrills you come for.  I don't have a lot bad to say about this game.  If I had to pick a criticism it would be the story.  A lot of it feels like an excuse to lead you through the locations it does.  But can I complain when the locations are this great?  It's a game at the end of the day.  It's priority is sticking you in tense situations in beautiful locations, and in that regard it's a 9.5/10.  Story wise I'd give it a 7/10.  That averages out to an 8.25 but since it's a game and I love it I'll move that up to a 9.0.  I have a feeling that score could go up after my second playthrough.

Thank you Capcom for another stunning adventure.  Your games are a work of art and we appreciate your hard work bringing them to life!

Resident Evil Village follows the RE recipe: cheesy story, a collection of strange monsters, scarce ammuntion, lotsa running, some back tracking, easy key riddles, small inventory, a bit of crafting, herbs, some collectibles.

I really liked the atmosphere of a far off Transylvanian village. Trade zombies for Lycans and Vampires and some odd monsters and you get the idea.

Graphics are fine and I got 60 FPS at 2k with high (3rd texture settings) to maxed settings and RTX. The game didn't like ALT+Tab that much, if FPS drop hard, it's best to restart the game (preferably after saving).

The boss fights were a bit disappointing, it's mostly bullet sponging, not much finesse or tricks needed, just fill em up with lead and explosives.

The story is another weak point, it's not very coherent and there's but a loose connection to the RE universe (Umbrella & Co.).

The game is most enjoyable on a 2nd run, when you unlocked endless ammo cheats and some of the better weapons early on (scarce ammo was always the part I hated most in RE). Some merchant called Duke allows you to tweak and improve your equipment further which is very welcome.

All in all, it's a decent title but not that good as the mainstream press rates it. I was far more impressed by the recent (free for standard owners) RTX-only Metro Exodus Enhanced edition.

Given how secretive Capcom were with the marketing and build up to this game, it was difficult to know what to expect from this entry of Resident Evil. Being the fourth game in the series utilising the RE Engine and following on from three quality releases left expectations very high. Having beaten the game I can happily say that "Resident Evil: Village" is a fantastic experience, meeting many of the high expectations I had for it. A wonderful Survival Horror game that includes a huge variety of enemies, environments and characters that had me invested from start to finish. 

The setting of RE8 was at the forefront from the moment of its announcement. The titular Village of this game is a beautifully designed labyrinth, an interconnected world that is a joy to explore and offers a number of challenges. Throughout the game there are a number of unique environments; A Castle which feels like a homage to the original Spencer Mansion. A Swamp-like area with huge RE4 vibes in both its design and gameplay. A spooky house utilising similar horror techniques to those seen in RE7's Baker House. A gigantic industrial factory, displaying the grand scale of RE games like 5 and 6, without losing identity or flow. Each of these areas provide a distinct experience, displaying the various aspects that make up the Resident Evil brand of survival horror. 

The variety of enemy types is a vast improvement from RE7; There are a number of variations of Lycans, Ghouls as well as other bizarre and terrifying creatures throughout the game. Each of their designs are beautifully detailed. Crafted to be monstrous and threatening, each of them posing unique challenges to the player. The "4 Lords" acting as the main bosses of the game are interesting and intimidating characters, each of them tormenting the player in different ways. I would have liked to see some more development given to these characters, however, as quickly as they are introduced they are defeated. Lady Dimitrescu and her daughters I particularly would have liked to see further background on. Given their heavy presence in the marketing of this game, its surprising how little development they have and how quickly they are dispatched from the story.

From a technical standpoint, the game is phenomenal. Graphically its marvellous, the sound design is top-notch and I absolutely adore the art style. Each of the weapons sound perfect, the monstrous roar of the Lycan enemies as well as the raspy calls of the Ghouls are wonderfully crafted to send chills down the spine of those with good speakers/headphones. Voice acting, animations, lighting and all the small details are excellent.

Narratively, I have some mixed feelings. Overall I think the story is solid and emotional, its a father driven to save his daughter. Chris' involvement is well done although he seems to appear at random moments in seemingly random locations just when its appropriate to do so. There's a small segment where you play as him that is an action packed romp that I thoroughly enjoyed, however it is a massive tonal shift. I also found the explanation for Ethan's strange healing and reattachment of limbs to be rather contrived. I honestly preferred the bizarre vibe of limbs being casually "stuck" back on and felt this didn't need explaining, especially not in the way it was done. That said I don't think it was a deal-breaker.

The game offers more beyond its initial playthrough. Offering a wide variety of bonus content that adds a great deal to the formula. Unlockable weapons, abilities and the return of Mercenaries mode. There is a large amount of replayability to RE8. Attempting to beat the game on the highest difficulty is something I plan on attempting, as well as trying out some of the bonus weapons. Mercenaries is a fun arcade style mode that I find to be great fun and infinitely playable.

In conclusion, Resident Evil: Village offers an amazing blend of horror and action. It perfectly blends the two genres into what is a horrifying experience that both makes you feel powerless and like a one-man army. Taking down hordes of enemies at one moment but being at their mercy at the next. I thoroughly enjoyed each of the different areas I explored and found each of the enemy types to be challenging and unique. While I think the boss fights could have offered more in difficulty and spectacle, with most of them feeling rather "DOOM" like in "the shoot it till it dies" way, I had fun defeating each of them. A quality title in the Resident Evil franchise.

As I've been expecting since the game's announcement, it was great. The story expands Resident Evil's lore and explains quite a lot of stuff. The gameplay as always is awesome, it's clunky but super satisfying. I like the concept of having to defeat 4 lords in order to face your main threat and i like the way it was implemented in the game. There are 4 areas and each area has it's own bosses and enemies.

First one is Castle Dimitrescu. I loved exploring the castle and i think they did a great job with the design and the atmosphere of the castle. Fighting the daughters Bela, Cassandra and Daniela and killing Alcina Dimitrescu herself at the end happened a little sooner and faster than i thought since they were hyped a lot but it makes sense since there are many more areas to go through in the game.

Second one is House Beneviento and i think i can say that this one is my favorite! It's like the Silent Hills game we never got to play and i freaking loved it. There are no common enemies in this house because it's more based off with puzzles and horror elements. I was shocked and terrorized by some of the things in the house but i won't spoil it because i think it's better if you go in there totally blind, it was an amazing experience playing through this part of the game.

Third one is Moreau's Reservoir. It was a disgusting place just like Moreau himself lol, I don't think it was the best but it was definitely interesting to go through, I liked the general atmosphere of it and Moreau turning into a giant fish like the one in Resident Evil 4 was fun to fight against.

Fourth and the last one is Heisenberg's Factory and even though I like this area I think it overstayed it's welcome. The concept of it is not the most interesting but also not the worse so i thought it'd be okay but since it's one of the longest parts of the game i remember thinking 'okay I've had enough let's leave this place now' but it has some interesting enemies and boss fights so it wasn't that bad.

Apart from all these areas there is the Village which is where the whole game is set in and i must say that i love it! The design of the village is amazing and i liked coming back to it as a hub area after every once in a while and there was always something to do before leaving again to go for a different location.

The game wasn't too hard, at least on the standard difficulty. My biggest complaint is that the puzzles were too easy, most of them didn't even require you to think carefully about what you're supposed to do. The game also has lots of replayability with the weapons, extra game modes and a new difficulty you can unlock by completing challenges which is great!

Overall, this game has great graphics, an amazing optimization (works in 60 fps on my GTX 1650), great bosses, some scary and intense moments and a decent story to tell. As a die hard fan of the Resident Evil series for a long time I strongly recommend you to experience this game, I don't think you'll regret it.

I really enjoyed it.  Played for about 12 hours to the end (perfect length) and did just about everything to be done in a single playthrough, but there's plenty of replayability here.  Seemed highly polished, ran great, I adored the "connected" nature of the various areas - made it all feel fairly grounded, kind of like the first Dark Souls.  I found the environments to be pretty immersive, the "village" was a fun little playground.  The sound design is top notch - I loved all of the little bits of sounds and noises in the various environments.  They sounded great, especially with headphones.

I found the combat to be pretty fun from beginning to end.  Lots of cool guns - the shotguns were sufficiently "shotgunny," which is more than I can say for most modern games.  Loved exploring the areas - lots of nooks and cranies to find stuff and stay well-supplied throughout.  I never ran out of ammo for any gun and killed every enemy I found.

Game isn't perfect though - in fact I would rate it as "above-average."  The story is highly predictable and pretty out there.  The voice acting ranges from pretty good (Lady D.) to bad (Heisenberg) to comical (Ethan).  The script throughout is just awful.  But none of that really bothered me, much like it didn't in RE4.  The puzzles are...not puzzles?  The bosses are gimmicky and dumb and predictable.  I absolutely hate how little of Lady D. was actually in the game...I mean WTF was all of that marketing about anyway??  The actual main baddies all suck except for her.

Worst of all - there isn't any "survival" or "horror" in this "survival-horror" game.  There is exactly ONE part that had me on edge - ONE - and it lasted for about 10 minutes...of a 12 hour game.  The rest was either not scary at all, or I could predict exactly when the "scare" was supposed to be coming.  And survival?  Ha.  No.  The game is about shooting ♥♥♥♥ and the longer you play the more badass you feel, but it does that pretty damn well - much like RE4.  Indeed, this is not a survival-horror game, it's an action game with horror elements sprinkled throughout.

There is one big series-self-deprecating reference near the end though - one line of dialog - that made this whole damn game worth playing.  I won't spoil it...but it was...incredible.  I laughed out loud.  There's also some fun tie-ins to past games and the greater "RE" universe/story as well that work nicely enough.

6.67...8232 out of 10.  No regrets. Would let Lady D. murder me again.  I recommend it overall!

I'm writing this literal minutes after beating this game for the first time, so there's going to be a bit of mindblown bias, but not much because this was an absolute experience, start to finish.

All in all, 9.5/10. Keeping this short-ish and spoiler free so I don't write here all night.

The TL;DR of what makes it great is that it takes the best parts of RE 4 and 7 and smushes them together. As those are my favorite Resident Evils, I had an amazing time. If you like 4 or horror/action at all, you will probably like this game. The aspects of 7 are few and far between, but there is light stalking, and the story is very, very heavily tied together. Also, this is one of the only games with a crafting system that doesn't make me want to projectile vomit (looking at you, Horizon Zero Dawn, that I have yet to touch). From the moment I loaded in to the moment the ending finished, I couldn't wait to keep playing.

Critiques:
As spoiler-free as I can be, the main reason most of us (at least I, at the time of this writing, a sad, single guy who loves goths) bought this game is... not... featured as much as you would think.

The other two critiques are more Resident Evil in general, rather than this game: if I shoot something in the head 8 times that doesn't have Plot Armor, it should die. That is a hill I will die on, apparently without ammo.

This part is not a critique because... I wouldn't change a thing about this game, but in most Resident Evil games, you basically finish the game, then they send you through the longest and most boring part of the game to pad it out, then and only then can you beat it. The final "dungeon" is a bit long and is definitely an ammo dump and backtracking nightmare, but everything after that? Absolutely blew me away.

I can't give it a 10/10 because of the smallest critiques, but this is far and away my favorite Resident Evil game. I would recommend it if you do like RE or if you don't. It is simply a fun, intense action shooter with enough horror to keep your pulse racing.

What a fun follow up to a surprising turn for Resident Evil.
The last Resident Evil came as a bit of a surprise. I thought it was just going to be a VR gimmick, but then it turned out to be a legitimately interesting new direction for the series. Even with some of it's frustrations it's mostly a decent and fun survival horror game, and now in first person which gave it some interesting new angles.
With RE:Village I feel a little like they again played with the formula in some interesting ways to make for another intriguing experience. I played through the game in 3 sittings across three days. Some kids may think it's short (I beat it in 19 hours trying to get everything), but it's longer than the first game by a little and they have Mercenaries mode to play with when you're done. For me it is sufficient.
Graphically I think the game looks fantastic. I don't quite have it at max, but I have it about what I would say is mid and at 1080p (about average for most gamers I would guess) and it looks fantastic. The only thing that stands out to me is there were a handful of frame rate hitches (where the game would stutter freeze for a second). This only happened maybe... seven times in my playthrough and it doesn't crash the game. It also didnt happen for me at bad times or cause issue when I was in combat. The framerate wasn't entirely stable (it was mostly 60 but at times it did dip- especially when loading in new areas or particle effects). Any of the frame rate issues were not game breaking, tho. It could also be my computer as I do not have the best computer out there. Still, the game looks amazing.
The gameplay mechanics are well done. I feel with this one it's mostly a first person shooter. I played at standard (which was the default difficulty and possibly the highest for first play- I don't remember because it unlock new difficulties when you beat the game). While I don't know if I found all the possible money there is, I found a ton and upgraded ALOT. I did not always have ammo, and did feel a need to conserve and strategize, I mostly also felt that as long as my shots counted it was ok to shoot almost everything because you're rewarded often with loot that you can use or sell.
They took away the storage chest in this one and instead gave you more storage capacity with the added benefit of still being able to upgrade your capacity. This takes away from the "realistic" nature in some ways, but it adds new depth to the inventory as well. While you still have inventory Tetris from RE4, if you keep up with everything you will have more than enough space when playing normally. I think this is an interesting idea and well executed.
Combat is still frenetic, but the guns feel weak. The hits smash, but (and I'll get into this more later) the sounds feel muffled and it comes off weaker than you'd expect. Even so, the combat is still cool, intense, and you have to fight different enemies differently which brings a strategy to fights that keeps it fresh.
The exploration in this game is great. It feels rewarding, and interesting. You can go around any location you're in, and it doesn't feel like you've only been in one place for too long. It also gives you a lot to look at.
The game isn't all combat, and in this they leaned into puzzles maybe more than I remember RE7 doing. There are a lot more, and even long stretches when you're solving puzzles, or environmental scenarios, rather than fighting. I really enjoyed this. My only complaint there is the way they do this (no spoilers) makes the game feel like it's split into different game types you have to beat. This sections will be combat focused- this section will be puzzle and no combat. It's strangely implemented and I feel it would be better served to mix it up more all the way through.
There is a cooking system in this that serves as a sort of upgrade system. You get more health and guard protection when you have the merchant cook up certain meals. I love this system. I wish, though, they had added an animation to him cooking rather than just a sound. This was rather old school of them to do, and it would be neater to see him cooking I feel. Also, I found it frustrating at times. There are a few ingredients you can only get within certain locations and at certain times of the game each location will get closed off. You can never go back, so if you miss anything- it's done. You can never go back to get it. This means there are things you can miss and never do. This kind of goes with the exploration as a whole, but this part of it was incredibly frustrating. Not only that, but this can happen when you're still playing a location and just beat one certain part- it locks it off and you can never go back and get something you missed. This is one of my biggest gripes I hope they think about and work on for future installments.
They have a great map system they developed with RE2 Remaster where it tells you what rooms are completed and others still need to be searched. If they're going to use this, and these upgrade systems, why close off locations so we can never go back again? There's no way the first time you play to know that's going to happen. It's not done in a way that even feels fair.
The story starts off just plain bad. It's really going to be up to the player on whether or not you think they redeem themselves. I felt they did some interesting enough things that I was actually very happy with where it went even though a lot of the way to get there was really really stupid. It did a good job at explaining itself though, and that goes a very long way for me in video games.
The acting is uneven. I was actually ok with most characters, but there's two in particular that are really awful. Again, I felt the game kind of fixes this by the end, but one of these characters is almost entirely pitched down and on top of the bad acting it sounds really awkward. It's strange. I only forgive this because of notes and things you read that kind of give an explanation to this, but it's still really bad.
The sound in this is messed. I suppose this could be because it's relying on surround sound, but it has an option for "headphones" surround or something like that. On my computer for some reason this just causes the sound to break and it mutes even if I turn it off. Also, just altogether, the sound seems broken. Stuff sounds right in your face even when it's far away, sometimes music cues just stop or cut out, guns don't sound powerful (they're very muffled), and overall the sound is very strange. I know it's not just me because even streamers I watched play this also have sound issues. It's just something about the way they code the sound on this engine is very odd. I don't know why. It does not ultimately break the game, but may give you a ton of unwarranted jump scares- maybe they intended that.
Speaking of which, this game is not scary. I would say for the first couple hours it's a little creepy, especially in the first major location, but the game doesn't lean into this a whole lot so if you're not easily scared you definitely won't find this game scary, but you may still get some jump scares if you're skiddish. I actually think it was creepy for most of the game, but by the time you get to a certain point the game is no longer even trying to be scary. Even Ethan is clearly not scared at all by then, and he jumps at everything when the game starts. I don't know. I kind of like that. It felt like the game was evolving and as the character you play becomes less scared- you do too. I thought it was an interesting conceit- if done intentionally.
Overall, I highly recommend this one. It's got some bad parts, but if you like a certain kind of horror (that I would liken more to Freddy Krueger than paranormal activity) then this might be of interest to you. It's not entirely scary, but I'm not sure it was meant to be and by the end I thought they did a lot of interesting things.
I recommend you check it out.

Resident Evil games are always tough to review because fans of the series are often very particular about what style of RE game they like. The best way I can describe Village is as a hybrid of RE4 and RE7, with many of the basic mechanics of the latter, but the pace and attitude of the former. It is definitely more action-oriented than the classic games and RE7, and out of the action-oriented mainline games—RE4-RE6—I like it better than 5 and 6 and probably roughly the same as 4. That aside, segments of this game feel like other entries in the franchise and like other horror games entirely. Almost like an RE: Greatest Hits. The story gets absolutely bonkers (more than even Code Veronica or RE6), but I enjoy that about the game. Your mileage may vary.

A first-time play-through on Standard difficulty took me about 9 hours (in game time) with some pretty thorough exploration. For reference, my first RE2 Remake play-through on Standard took about 8 hours. After the first completion, you can unlock The Mercenaries, which is a fun arcade mode where you try to string together combos of kills and max out your score. It's similar in theory to the one in RE4, though it trades the novelty of playing as different characters with different abilities for giving you randomized abilities that make you stronger—stronger headshots, pistol damage, execution damage, double ammo capacity, etc. I personally prefer the one in RE4, but this one is still fun.

The game also has the same kind of unlockables shop as RE3 Remake, where you earn Completion Points for completing certain challenges in both Story and the Mercenaries and can purchase special weapons, infinite ammo, etc. I'm working on unlocking these now and they certainly add a bit of replay. 

So far I'm happy with the game. I liked it more than I thought I would, and I think it's a great addition to the franchise. I'll have to let it sit with me a while to know where I would place it in my rankings, but I already know I like it more than RE5, RE6, the two Revelations games, and most of the other spin-offs. Hope this helps.

So the short of it is that this game is ok. I would recommend it but only on sale really. If you are expecting Mommy Dimitrescu to play a bigger role in the story you will be sorely disappointed. If you are expecting it to be scarier than 7, it isn’t. It has some moments but none of those moments are the best in the series, the game is also very frontloaded in terms of quality. The resolution of the story is good though, if you’ve somehow managed to like Ethan.

Now for nuance. When it comes to Resident Evil I honestly have never really liked the series. I’ve played every game since 5 and have always found the gameplay to be lacking and the overarching story to be a complete mess, a comprehensible one, but a mess all the same. I bring this up because my opinion of this game does not come from any nostalgia or deep rooted love for the series, I don’t hate the games but I have never followed the series closely because I find the ‘game’ part of resident evil games to be extremely lacking. I want this series to improve, I’d love to love it but it keeps disappointing me.

Anyway, I decided to give Resident Evil 8 a try because the character trailers (everyone's favorite vampire dommy mommy specifically) were really captivating and the art/stylistic choices were really giving off a very creepy and character driven vibe. I was expecting it to be as good as that first half of RE7 but hopefully through the entire game. I was wrong. In terms of scariness, the game isn’t very scary. I know for some that's not a deal breaker but for me it definitely was. The gameplay of Resident Evil, especially 7 & 8 is just weak. The enemy types are not difficult to fight, firearm feedback is limp, and combat encounters usually just revolve around either blocking everything with a bare minimum effort or obnoxiously swinging your camera around and sprinting around enemies to avoid incoming attacks. There’s also the issue of the game being centered around Ethan, possibly the most milquetoast character ever. It is really hard to empathize with such a blank slate character. The four lords minus vampire mommy and kinda-maybe Heisenberg are also really shallow and honestly kind of underdeveloped. The game is also incredibly short if you don’t feel like engaging with the mercenaries mode or grinding the main story a couple of times on the higher difficulties; I beat it in 8 hours just for reference. Pretty much, after the castle the game really just falls off. 

I will give credit to the game being absolutely gorgeous. Graphics can’t save gameplay though but I know a lot of people will probably weigh graphical fidelity a lot higher than I would. The main issue though is that while the Level of Detail everywhere in the game is so incredibly high, it just feels kind of wasted; like the detail is nice but none of it really matters. It's hard to explain; when i started the game I was looking at every little thing but then when I realized that the little details didn’t really offer anything other than eye candy I began ignoring most of the environment. It doesn’t help that the environments get considerably less interesting the further you are in the game. 

I mostly wrote this long winded review out of disappointment I guess. I wasn’t even on the hype train but I still finished the game feeling disappointed. I think most people will probably enjoy it which is why I gave it a positive review but for me it felt lacking. Basically, I could ignore the lackluster gameplay if it was scary but it was not very scary, and I could’ve ignored the game not being scary if the gameplay was fun but that didn’t pan out either.

If you love the Resident Evil games, you will love this roller coaster of a game. As usual the level and character design is amazing. Characters and locations feel lifelike, many times I found my self lost in the visuals forgetting I was supposed to kill that awesome looking monster because I was just too focused on how cool it looked. All the horror you expect of resident evil monsters is here. And yes even the larger than life final forms of the 4 main bosses. 

Many different ways to do damage and if you fully upgrade your favorite you can do the damage you need no problem. The usual collection game is here as well so keep eyes and ears open, you never know what you will find and where. 

And personally the vampire feel of Lady Alcina Dimitrescu, her three daughters and the BOWS you find in her castle are right up my alley, I love vampires and seeing the mold take this on with a twist was fun, same goes for Urias and the werewolfs, a new take on a classic is always fun. I did not care for the dolls and big baby holy crap, heart was racing but thats what i came here for and wasn't let down. 

The story line was quite the ride. I went from confused, to angry, to surprised and joyful when I got to the ending, a lot of loose ends were tied up with a nice little bow but at the same time some new questions were brought up that I cant wait to learn the answers too. 

BUT its not all sun shine and rainbows. the story is a little short, It took me roughly 20 hours to finish, and if you know RE games it goes quickly. The boss fights were...well they didn't really live up to other RE boss fights, all three sisters(mini bosses) were exactly the same, 0 variety in how those fights played out. And the 4 lords were even easier, more damage required yes but more of a challenge would have been nice. Especially with the last lord, the unlimited ammo while in the "tank" made the battle laughable. And Mother Miranda oh boy, after the "mostly" let down that the 4 lords were I was hoping this battle would make up for it...and nope.  I got through every single boss fight with my shotgun and the launcher, 

But other than the issues above I do recommend you play this, I know I will be playing it again to get all the collectibles and do the other difficulties

RE: Village is the best new AAA horror game I've played in years. I'm so glad Capcom was able to turn around the series from RE6 and make RE7, RE8, and the remakes of the older games. This game has all the resident evil tropes but still manages to feel pretty fresh and new with unique environments and character. I won't spoil anything, but there is a lot more to the game than the village and the castle, I'm happy they did not show off too much in the marketing for this game. 

As for the gameplay, it definitely feels more action oriented than 7, you will often be taking on hoards of enemies or big bosses with massive amounts of health. Like many others have said, it is like the change from RE1 to RE4. The environments also scale up to match, feeling much grander and larger than the confined houses of RE7. There is also a wider assortment of guns and you can upgrade them at a merchant. Enemies drop loot and there are tons of treasures to collect and sell.


These huge environments also look stunning, I played this will everything maxed out, ray tracing on using an RTX 3080 and Ryzen 5600x at 1440p, the game ran great, it was almost always above 100 fps. My only technical complaint is that they should really have a high res texture pack or option for this game, environments look great overall but if you get close to certain objects or textures they look low res and pixelated, even with max texture resolution. This keeps the game size down to 30GB but obviously the visual quality suffers. I would have liked to see an optional texture pack download to solve this issue. The game also lacks some basic features like an FOV slider, hopefully this is fixed in an update.

Overall, RE: Village is a must buy for fans of the genre or even people who are interested in jumping in. It looks fantastic, is lots of fun to play, has awesome horror setpieces, and great creature design. It feels like a high quality product the whole way and never feels like it gets bogged down or overstays its welcome. The game took about 12 hours for me to beat on standard difficulty, I look forward to continuing to play in the mercenaries mode and doing a second playthrough on the highest difficulty in the future.
