Really good Resident Evil title. 

The game is a well done, polished experience. The main story took me around 12 hours on my first go, with mild exploration. I didn't spend too much time rooting out items in any given area so I did miss a bunch of stuff including a weapon. 

I liked how each area felt like a love letter to a different part of the genre - gothic horror, psychological horror, body horror, eldritch horror... it felt like this game touched on a little bit of everything. This has its downsides of course, I wanted more of some themes and less of some others.

I did not like how weapons were handled. I was hoping they would be more like Resident Evil 4 in which each weapon had it's own niche and was worth upgrading to see what special traits would unlock, whereas in this title each gun is a direct upgrade from the last. There is no point in upgrading your initial weapons because you'll quickly replace them with better versions and there are no special effects that unlock upon maxing.

They definitely improved upon enemy variety. In RE 7 we had maybe three or four enemy types, in this game there feels like a lot more and they vary by area which is cool to see. The lycans look great and their AI was pretty sophisticated as far as I could tell. They seemed to work together to corner me on multiple occasions, with their groups splitting up to cover multiple exits and trapping me. 
With that being said, there are certain enemies which can be easily cheesed and broken, unfortunately. Lady Dimitrescu for instance, seems to stay on very strict rails and doesn't seem to be able to wander anywhere near as freely as Mr. X could. Certain beastly enemies later on are very intimidating but cannot enter buildings so can be cheesed from doorways. Things like this make the game easier than it should be and can break the immersion and sense of fear and dread one should be feeling in these situations.

The game allows for more action than it's predecessor, but the survival elements are still present. I found myself constantly running low on ammunition and healing, only to find some bullets or mats right in the nick of time. That being said, enemy and crate drops are random between mats and money so my experience may not be the same as the next person.

The village and other environments you visit are all atmospheric and very well crafted. The last area you explore does sort of stand out from the others in terms of theme, but I personally still enjoyed its dark, claustrophobic corridors as much as I enjoyed exploring the rest of the game. They did a great job at hiding items, there were more than a few "red" areas left on my map, much to my dismay.

After completing the game you get special points which you can spend on various bonuses including infinite ammo, new guns, concept art and models, among other things. You can also unlock the mercenaries mode, which I have yet to play but I was a big fan in earlier titles. 
I'm very happy that Capcom did not insert any microtransactions into the game and everything can be unlocked through playing, they're a beacon in the darkness right now.

I'll finish by saying that RE VIllage is a great horror title worthy of the Resident Evil name.

I may revisit this review after playing through NG+ a few times and through the mercenaries.

Truly a fantastic blend of both action and horror, both things the series is well known for at this point, and clearly showing just how much it wears its RE4 inspiration on its sleeves. With it being a continuation of Ethans story as well, it also happens to tie pretty well into RE7 as a whole, and in what feels like a pretty rare case for the series, feels like an incredibly natural progression story wise for the most part, which was probably one of the most shocking elements for me ultimately in just how well the story resonated with me in its final hours.

Of course, the main thing I imagine many skeptical fans and prospective buyers are asking themselves if they've yet to pick it up is just *how* much horror and scare factor the game actually has to offer, especially compared to the previous title? And admittedly, overall? Its less scary than Resident Evil 7 for sure, though, it has sections that easily rival, and are probably even *scarier* than the whole of Resident Evil 7, largely depending on who you are and what really gets to you most. However, while it might lack in horror at times, it still provides ample amounts of great setting and atmosphere, with almost every area being distinct from one another and brimming with character, and many of the scenarios the game puts you in will truly invoke those feelings of tense panic/uncertainty that Resident Evil 4 first introduced us to, with overwhelming numbers of enemies and just very frantic situations on the whole, and even elements of Resident Evil 2 remake sneak their way in for that extra level of intensity. Very rarely does this game ever drop a beat in terms of its overall pacing, though, if you do choose to do certain bits of side content, the game can feel a bit slow here and there, albeit, much of the side content will lead you into interesting encounters, either puzzles to gain new treasure, or even optional bosses/mini-bosses of sorts which can really be tough as nails on higher difficulties, as well as plenty challenging even on the standard difficulty.

All in all though, with plenty of unlocks, the Mercenaries mode making a return, and even a difficulty mode like Resident Evil 7's Madhouse called "Village of Shadows" which mixes up enemy placements as well as certain item placements, the game has plenty of content on offer to keep you playing, and reasons to keep you playing if you need them. Truly a great, replayable experience from beginning to end. If you're a fan of titles like Resident Evil 4 or even Resident Evil 5, this should be a pretty easy pick up for you, and even if you're an uncertain fan of the original titles, I'd still suggest it just to experience some of the fantastic horror segments in the game, though perhaps wait for a sale, and when you do eventually pick it up, play on Hardcore off the bat for some real survival horror elements to kick in. If you're a new, prospective buyer however, I'd say this game is an excellent starting point to test the waters with the series, as it both offers some great action which is iconic to the later games in the main line trilogy, as well as horror that can at times eclipse, and stand right up there with the best the series has to offer.

After the huge comeback with RE2 Remake and RE7, I was excited to get back into the franchise and especially excited for RE Village. It looked like a RE4/RE7 fan's wet dream with the fusion of the two, and it did deliver. There were unfortunately a few annoyances that carried over from 7 that would have been easy to fix, as well as some cut corners and strange decision by Capcom which I'll cover.

GAMEPLAY: Feels pretty similar to RE7, which was surprisingly a lot of fun to play an RE game in first person. The only complaint, which I'm sure everyone has been screaming about is yes, we get it, the FOV is low. It's kinda stupid that a shooter in 2021 doesn't have an FOV slider, but there's already a mod out for it, get over it lol. The Village opening up to the four different houses was pretty fun to go through, especially for those that are completionists. However while this was great, Capcom really slacked off in certain parts. The Demitriscu Castle, Factory and Village itself were fantastic and horrifying in their own respective ways, but the Beneviento house and lake portion were very underwhelming. The Beneviento house was basically a medicore Indie Horror game simulator that lasted about 30 minutes. The Lake portion was pretty much copy pasted from RE4, giant fish monster and everything. The crafting is definitely way better this time around, with more materials and better recipes that improved on 7. All in all, gameplay was fantastic.

STORY: The horror aspects of this game call back to the traditional horror elements of storytelling, like creepy dolls, gears and machinery, etc. The plot twists of Ethan's true nature and Dr. Spencer's involvement in the Village were great to experience and see how it all wraps around Umbrella and the bio weapons as a whole. My complaints are centered around Chris and Lady Demitriscu's involvement in the story. It's pretty blatant to see that they were purely focused on for marketing's sake, as Demitriscu was defeated around the 2-3 hour mark and Chris was only really on screen for his Call of Duty mission esqe portion. Hopefully we'll get some good DLC of the two in the future.

CONTROLS: Aside from the FOV issue, the controls are pretty much the same as in 7. The vaulting mechanic is pretty unnoticeable most of the time, but the shove after the block mechanic is a very helpful tool for large groups of enemies. Playing with mouse and keyboard, I found that the speed needed to be turned way up, but after that blasting enemies with snipers and shotguns feels so satisfying.

REPLAYABILITY: This game is 100% worth replaying again, especially on Hardcore or the new higher difficulty (forget the name of it). I'm already looking forward to my Hardcore playthrough after doing Normal first.

BUY/SALE/IGNORE?: Buy this game if you're a Resident Evil fan for sure. If you're skeptical about short game length (game is about 10-12 hours) then I guess get it on sale but Resident Evil games are always meant to be around that length.

In conclusion, Village is definitely an improvement on some areas of 7, but falls short with some stupid simple mistakes that Capcom could have fixed. But these issues don't detract from my overall enjoyment of the game.

Going with theneedledrop style of rating, I'm feeling a strong 7 to a light 8 on this game.

EDIT: Forgot to mention the puzzles this time around were insultingly easy, even compared to 7. The ball mini-games for the treasure were fun though.

Actual Review update after 28 hours of play: This game is hands-down my favorite resident evil game in the whole series. It has so much character that it feels more like an epic fairy tale, and for a certain reason I think they aimed to give off that vibe. The story is amazing. It follows the hero's journey in it's style of story-telling. It plays off the previous installment in very perfect ways. Ethan is a damn legend after this game. 

The combat is fast paced and brutal. There are a ton of weapons, from pistols, shotguns, I believe several rocket/grenade launchers, machine guns, mines, pipe bombs etc. The environment can also be used for combat. Things like explosive barrels are strewn about the maps, you can use enemy attacks to kill other enemies through redirection, you can also disarm, kneecap, blow up, chop up, block, push, and of course run. The huge variety of weapons, ways to kill, and the combat areas/sequences gives this game the best combat system out of any of the previous resident evils. The firs-person fast-paced horrific chaos that ensues all throughout the game makes this such a memorable experience. Don't even get me started on mercenaries mode. Fight off hordes of monsters as fast as possible, buy and sell at the merchant, rinse and repeat, all while picking up power-ups that give you abilities to kick even more ass and just demolish enemies like a super-Ethan.

The puzzles are mostly basic and quick. Nothing like the earlier resident evils, but they are there. This by no means detracts from the game experience, because this is resident evil trying something completely new and innovative, and striving at it. If you played resident evil 7, expect puzzles a little less complex than in that game for the most part. They were easy for me at least.

Did I mention there are a ton of weapons?

Overall, the game is like resident evil 7 mixed with resident evil 4, as I believe a few others may have mentioned. Every element from resident evil 7 was improved upon, and the intense action of re4 has been added. This game is great. I am on my second play-through right now attempting to get all the unlocks. I never replay these types of games. If you are a fan of the resident evil series and you liked re7, then you will absolutely fall in love with this game.

For context I've been playing resident evil for 12 years, starting with the OG RE2, then RE1, then RE4, and eventually getting through pretty much 90% of the series. Resident Evil has had an identity crisis for far longer than I've been playing it, but this game seems to be the epitome of that crisis.

In short, this game is terrible. I'm baffled when I see these positive reviews because I've yet to experience a single thing that doesn't feel stolen, reused, a demo-piece for REmake 4, or out of place. 
It's fair to say everyone experiences horror differently, so I'm not taking what scares me into consideration. Instead I'm judging this game on its story, the characters, the setting, the enemies, and some of the most inconsistent detailing I've seen in an AAA game.

STORY
The story so far? As bland as any other RE game, with the exception of using a trope that should have died long ago. "Go rescue a relative you spend 2 seconds with at the start". It's not interesting, and the game offers me little reason to care outside of the characters caring. (Spoiler) By the end of the game Ethan magically returns to life by regrowing his heart? The game doesn't feel the need to explain but his fingers didn't grow back so who cares. Also this contradicts the need for Game-Overs in both RE7 and RE8.

CHARACTERS
The characters are also bland. "Everyman" Ethan has literally become an every-man as his personality jumps between ridiculously snarky, to utter coward, to not even a care in the world as he reacts to nothing. Reacting to his wife's death he is less emotional than reacting to some random stranger he's met for all of 30 seconds. 
The Daughters have very generic personalities that don't even get fleshed out, and for me they bugged to all be the same blonde-haired one. I'd complain about such a bug but it's pretty fitting considering that they were already identical in other regards.
Big Mommy Milkers Dimitrescu is just a Karen. She has some personality but upon being chased by her the chase would randomly cut out as her daughter spawned instead. This means any character she does have is made redundant as she proceeds to do extremely little in the game outside of ONE actual chase sequence with her.
Doll Lady doesn't have a character.
Fish Man doesn't have a character.
Heisenberg is as my friend described "A wannabe Nicolas Cage".
(Spoiler) Miranda is given a pity story to justify her actions where she is actually trying to revive her dead child. HOWEVER she then proceeds to tell Ethan "everyone dies eventually" which contradicts the entire plot.

GAMEPLAY
The game is a walking simulator. In between gauntlets of enemies, and a few chase sequences, you just walk around looting until you progress the story. There's never the feeling of being in danger unless you see Ethan say something.
There's no recoil on the guns, which is fitting because the enemies also don't react to being shot. It makes for some of the most un-engaging gameplay in the series. YES WORSE THAN TANK CONTROL SHOOTING.

ENEMIES
The enemies in the free-roam segments are extremely boring. Do you remember your first time seeing a licker, be it RE2 or REmake 2? Those things are terrifying. The hunters? Scared me to death. Nemesis, Mr X, Regenerators, Executioners, RE has had some absolutely fantastic enemies in its history.
The Lycans are all copy-pastes of each other.
Manbats make the worst sound imaginable and their AI is terrible.
Prisoners are just skeletons with weapons and become the second primary enemy.
Lastly we have a weird BIG HUMAN with a drill, who gets more bullet spongey as you progress. Additional note: This enemy uses the moveset and sounds of the Blind enemy in RE4.
The enemy design is terrible.

Lastly I wanna point out some stuff that just annoys me. Ethan's sleeve staying on after his hand was severed is stupid. An old man buried in burning rubble and then climbing through said rubble while on fire retains all of his clothing and no burn marks. Enemies rarely ever react to being shot, and the AI on Standard is so braindead it makes Launch CP77 look like a master piece.
MOST IMPORTANTLY: ETHAN HOLDS UP HIS ENTIRE BODY WEIGHT WITH JUST TWO FINGERS AND A THUMB??? DOES NO ONE FIND THIS EXTREMELY STUPID?

TL:DR
This game is devoid of enjoyment. It feels like a testing ground for the REmake 4, and capcom decided to sell it at full price.

What an absolutely thrilling ride this game has been from start to finish. It definitely is up there as one of my personal favourite in the mainline series. It clearly showed plenty of inspirations taken from past titles (RE4 being the most prevalent example) that have been mashed up into one solid greatest hits package with a campaign that spans easily up to 10 hours if you play it methodically and explore every nook and cranny. I cannot fault it.

The fact that Capcom made it to have each Four Lords' houses/areas to be thematically distinct and different from one another is phenomenal work too. I won't spoil it, but House Beneviento almost made me throw my chair out - and it's not because I chose to start on hardcore difficulty either (although that part was absolute BS during the beginning of the game, somehow I stuck with it and managed to see it through to the end).

The RE Engine just has jaw-dropping graphics especially the lighting with RTX on. I know some people encountered several issues with it on, but I guess I was one of the lucky few for having zero issues throughout my entire playthrough save for one encounter ([spoiler]Cassandra's boss fight in the Armoury [/spoiler]). Other than that the game maintained above 80fps all the way and is excellently optimised. To be fair though, even without RTX and HDR enabled the game still looks gorgeous.

Sound design is top notch and I don't expect anything less from the makers of RE2 Remake which is my personal favourite RE game to-date. Whether I'm using headphones on or using my PC's speakers, thankfully I can tell exactly where an enemy is coming from and if they're above or below me. It really pays to have fantastic spatial audio in a videogame, especially if it's a horror-type genre. It has saved my life more than I can count.

I guess that's all for my review. I am absolutely exhausted after playing on hardcore for my first run, but the ends definitely justify the means. Overall, I will definitely class this as one of my top Resident Evil titles of all time and will play through it again to complete the challenges.

Minor spoiler, I definitely can't wait to see what Capcom does next with the finale with what I'm assuming is a trilogy. Let's see what Resident Evil IX has to offer in the far future - and how Capcom plans to creatively work that title into Roman numerals.

As a disclaimer I don't always have the most typical opinions on entries the series. I don't think my opinion here will be a hot take however. As of writing this I have beat the game one time on Hardcore difficulty, and I typically go back and update my reviews if changing difficulties up and replaying the game increases or decreases my opinion of it.

With that out of the way: As others may have hinted this game is basically if Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 4 had a baby. What I like about that is that RE7 was traditional enough in style to be like the originals, and that did transfer over even if Resident Evil 4 was a huge influence here. Resident Evil 4 while loved by many, lots of the traditionalists thought the series departed too much from the original formula. I can safely say that Resident Evil 8 did not feel that way. This game had plenty of item hunting, puzzle solving, and great pacing with good traditional style atmosphere. One thing it probably did lack compared to the more traditional Resident Evil games was item management. Even on hardcore I found myself never struggling to keep up with inventory space. So in that sense the inventory was closer to Resident Evil 4. 

I think the games ultimate strengths are how many different ways the campaign plays out and how you have to play the game. There are plenty of style switches in the game to keep it feeling exciting. While there is a Mr.X style character, said character does not over stay their welcome. I will say, the threat is no where near as threatening as Mr.X, but I didn't feel myself finding that to be a bad thing. I think the first 75% of the game is the strongest portion, while the ladder portion of the game I didn't find myself loving the atmosphere quite as much. The enemies in the later portion of the game were fun, but the environment just wasn't as magical. 

The bosses  I felt were on the easier side, and keep that in mind because I did play hardcore. Some bosses in particular I found myself not even taking a hit. I do like the ability to play boss fights flawlessly, but perhaps some of them should have been more challenging. 

One of my favorite things about the game is also one of the things I felt like it could have done better. This is just personal preference, but although the collectibles were a blast, I would have preferred if more of them weren't so easy to narrow down using the map. For me the replay value would have been far higher (though it's still high) if I felt there were many more secrets for me to find using my wit and being thorough. I'm sure most casual audiences will appreciate the way it is now, but perhaps the harder difficulties could have made that aspect more difficult (thus more rewarding). 

As far as the rewards go I felt they were extremely fun, just like Resident Evil 4. I'm looking forward to many more play through to experience some of the upgrades I missed. Replay value is high, like some previous games including 3make there is a store that you can use in game CP to purchase new guns and other unlocks like infinite ammo. CP is earned by completing in game challenges. Not only is the campaign very replayable, but the game also comes bundled with Mercenaries mode after beating the campaign. This also has its own unlocks that can be earned by doing well. There is plenty of content to get your monies worth here. 

My campaign took me a little less than 10 hours, but with loading saves to fixed stuff I missed it was probably closer to 12 hours. There was one part in the campaign that took me a painfully long time to figure out, not only was it not obvious, but it was also arguably the only actual very hard part in the campaign in my opinion. Now that I figured it out I don't think it will be an issue next time however. 

As far as comparing this to Resident Evil 7, I think over all 7's atmosphere and scares get the edge, but it's not by a landslide or anything. The story is good and keeps you interested and engaged. I think this was a worthy successor for sure. 

The PC version looks and plays incredible. The only major flaws are some texture issues, and in some rare cases pop in. I played on a 3090 with 1.5x image quality.

Where to start, I guess to put it simply, Resident Evil Village is a very good game, and a very good Resident Evil game at that, too.

Capcom weren’t joking when they said they put a lot of effort into making sure the actual village in the game is a character on its own. But it’s not just the village, really; their marketing team made quite sure not to show us a lot of the game and…there’s a lot of game here besides just “tall vampire lady”, her castle and a village.

It’s simply one of the most unique Resident Evil games so far, with many varied environments and areas to explore. It’s also not a short Resident Evil game, it’s not the longest, perhaps RE 4 or 6 hold that title, I’d say, but it has a decent duration if you take your time or, like me, your first playthrough is on Hardcore Difficulty.

I was never bored by any of the new areas we visit in the game; there are four main areas, each one corresponding to one of the four Lords in the game, but there are also other areas and side zones to discover. 
The seamless transitions between areas in this game (there are no loading screens), make it look like it’s actually pretty decently sized and it feels great.

It was already after I completed Dimitrescu’s Castle that I thought to myself: “Oh yeah, this is definitely a very good Resident Evil game” and I have to say that whoever are responsible for designing this Castle at Capcom did a very good job, it’s an amazing place to explore early in the game and a 120% Resident Evil experience. The amount of detail put into these designs is really something.

Same can be said about the remaining zones in the game, after how incredible the Castle is, it’s difficult to top that, but I was very pleasantly surprised by the areas that we get to explore later in the game as well. There was not a single zone or area that seemed poorly designed or rushed to me, and each new area brought something new and different into the gameplay. One of my favorite sections of the game does not even involve combat in any way, without getting into spoilers: it was incredible, and scary as hell, didn’t last as long as the Castle, but the intensity and tension were off the charts in there, so it really felt longer than it is, because it was so well executed.

I really liked that Ethan has now an actual developed personality in this game, compared to the previous one, the character has come a long way and we get to see so many aspects of him in this game. As in the most recent games, all the characters are really well done and the voice actors and motion capture performers (which are the same for the English audio, mostly, they do the voices and the capture themselves) really once again did a very good job with all of them.

Of course, having played the latest RE games I instantly recognized some familiar voices, and I’m glad because they are all really good actors and I’m happy that Capcom is taking care of their voice and performance talent here.

When it comes to this specific PC version of the game, I found it runs pretty decently on my Ryzen 5 3600 and RTX 3060 Ti setup It is definitely a more demanding game than RE 7, RE 2 and 3 remakes, and we even have the option to use Ray Tracing now, making it even more demanding. But it is also the best looking RE Engine game so far, that is undoubtedly true as well. That’s not to say the game looks bad without RT, it doesn’t, I think it still looks great without it as well.

I did find an issue with the game that should be patched: minimizing the game, or switching settings once we’re in game can lock the game into a very low frame-rate state only fixable by restarting the game and this was already an issue in the demo too. This can be avoided by leaving to the main menu and making the changes in there, but it’s still an annoying issue.

There’s also no FOV slider present in the options, a big oversight, considering all the recent games have it, and I hope it gets patched in soon, but for now there are mods out there that work to increase the FOV, with no issues.

Overall, this game is an incredible survival horror experience from start to finish, that continues the story that RE 7 started, and ties in with the lore of the whole series with some very cleverly placed allusions and clues, and not so subtle ones as well. RE Village is so good that it even enhances all of what RE VII did, making the both of them a cohesive experience very much worth revisiting back to back, and I think that's really good.

The RE Engine once again continues to evolve into the new generation so…good job Capcom, this one was pretty good.

After finished this game 3 times, on Standard, Hardcore and Village of Shadows respectively, I feel like I'm finally able to give my opinion on this new installment of the RE franchise.

During my first playthrough, I found the game to be a bit tedious, struggling to navigate through the different places and constantly getting lost or not knowing where to go, although experiencing the horrors of this game for the first game was truly a great ride and one hell of a rollercoaster of emotions. The environments were unwelcoming and hostile, from the abandoned and haunting village to the eerie castle to the sinister and dark factory, I didn't feel safe a single second. The graphics truly are gorgeous (not to mention well optimized, not going lower than 100fps on average) and stopping by to take a few screenshots of the landscape quickly became a ritual throughout this game, you stay in the same area long enough to not get bored of the surroundings, every new areas felt and looked different. Another thing I enjoyed a lot about this game compared to the previous installment: the enemy variaty. The lycans remain the main type of enemies, which are extremely aggressive and can quickly kill you if you're not fast enough, along with the basic zombies but more enemy types will appear as you progress through the game, adding more difficulty and I'm not even including the mini bosses which add another layer of difficulty to the levels.

However, the game isn't perfect and has some minor flaws didn't really impact the gameplay but were still present. The AI is terrible, few enemies remained blocked in a area or simply couldn't detect me despite being right in front of them and it led to some awkward moments, which basically made Lady Dimitrescu's chases inside her castle ridiculously easy. Talking about difficulty, I found the game to be particularly easy on Standard and Hardcore mode, we're constantly provided with ammo and the resource management becomes less and less present. Only the final difficulty, Village of Shadows, turnt the game into a challenge, for the most part, as some areas still remain fairly easy if you have a good aim and invested in the right weapons and upgrades, boss fights are the only moments I truly struggled playing this diffulty. I also encountered some more minor bugs like like lighting issues and a few rare fps drops.

Overall, this is a pretty solid game, mixing both horror and action elements perfectly, it is by far one of the best RE games ever made and I highly recommend it, even at full price. Really looking forward to learning more about the game, the villains and characters in future DLCs.

Although it may not be considered one of the best games in the franchise, it certainly exhibits a remarkable level of boldness and originality. The carefully crafted ambiance of each area is one of the most fascinating features of the game, with maps creating an intriguing maze that gradually unveils new surprises.

Moreover, the game includes various successful references from other franchises and styles, adding an extra layer of depth and interest. The feeling of wanting to explore each area further is a testament to the game's quality design, which skillfully balances content and progression.

It is important to note that the introduction of new protagonists and the renewal of the franchise are necessary to maintain players' interest and relevance over time. Therefore, the change of direction that the game seems to indicate, with the post-credits scene suggesting a new phase for the franchise, is welcome.

In summary, although the game may not be flawless, its boldness, originality, and quality design make it a fascinating and engaging experience.

After 80+ hours, I've come to the conclusion that this game is an overwhelming disappointment. Let me be clear: Resident Evil Village is a fun game. But it is drastically flawed, in ways that required a lot of reflection and analysis for me to fully realize. The story and substance of said story pale in comparison to Resident Evil 7, despite the more grandiose tone. The story spends a great deal of time bordering on nonsense and suspension of disbelief. The good parts (namely the characters of Dimitrescu, Heisenberg, and Beneviento) of the story receive an embarrassingly minuscule amount of screen time. Karl Heisenberg, for instance, is almost never seen or interacted with, and when he appears, the voice acting and writing are painful (nothing against Neil Newborn, that guy is cool. He just had poor writing and direction, I don't blame him 100% for how bad the voice acting was). Heisenberg could have been the coolest, most fascinating RE character of the decade. His potential was squandered. Karl's character is really an allegory for the video game as a whole. Wasted potential. I'm sure I'll write a full on essay about the game at some point. It has so many awesome things going for it, and so many pitfalls that bring it down. But it's fun, and pretty looking, and it has significant replayability despite my complaints. I'll be comparing this alot to resi 4 (my personal favourite in the franchise), although I'm not a blind fan of the series. There are numerous games I dislike and don't cream myself whenever I see the words "Resident Evil". I also didn't play the 7th so can't compare how similar it is to that game. Also there is no FOV slider, but someone called FluffyQuack made a great fov mod and it works for all games, just look for "Fluffy manager 5000", thanks to this guy you won't need to have a migraine trying to play the game.

The good:
This game is pretty good. It's about as close to resi evil 4 gameplay while not being monotonous (like the 5th game) that I've played. 
The story was good enough to keep you engaged even if it was abit weird. 
4 of the 5 bosses were really good. 1 was pretty meh.
The changes in scenery are really nice. You aren't just stuck in places that feel identical like in alot of resident evil games outside 4. It's not as diverse as 4, but it's good enough. 
Variety of weapons
Merchant who's charismatic. Not a fan of the visual style of him though.



The bad:
Animations range from "industry leading" with facial and movement on enemies, to "absolutely terrible" like 15fps enemies at the end boss, reloading ect.

Gunplay is terrible and unsatisfying. No recoil to any of the guns and they just feel weak.

Graphics range from "pretty damn good" to "this looks like a texture hasn't loaded in". 

Environment building is the same. There's a part where you enter a factory and look out onto fog and intricate mechanisms going off and it looks fantastic. Then I whipped out a sniper for a closer look and found bridges clippings into walls, cranes clipped into buildings, bridges that literally go nowhere ect. and it was like this every single time I looked even slightly off into the distance to look at the scenery. Really disappointing. 

Zombies aren't as satisfying to kill as they were in resi 4 because they are way to tanky IMO (and I played through on standard. 

Movement feels wrong. Inputs don't register sometimes and somehow they managed to make movement feel clunkier than RE4, a game that was designed to have clunky movement. But in that game it feels intentional, this game it feels like it's a bug and they don't intend for it to be as clunky as it is. 

I had some very weird stutters. Running on a 2070s, 3700x and 3600mhz ram without raytracing and when the stutters came, they were very noticable. They also weren't obvious as to what caused them because I would have literally 15 people on screen and it ran like butter, then I would kill all but 1 and it would stutter like crazy until I loaded a different zone. I don't know if there is some kind of looping error when you get close to killing everyone and it is constantly trying to spawn something or do some weird check in the area you are, whatever it was it happened too many times for it to be just a one of bug.

The hardest difficulty is terribly balanced. You basically are 2 shot until you die and they add harder enemies in certain areas (this I have no problem with), what I fundamentally disagree with is buffing the HP of the enemies 10 fold. You need to play this mode following a playthrough or I don't think it's physically possible to complete. The first enemy literally took 20 round to the head of the pistol you get, then proceed to survive 4 or so minutes of me kiting it around and knifing it in the head until I got bored and switched it off. Also it prior games, new game+ (where you keep your previous items in a new game) used to be locked to that difficulty. So if you played a match on standard, new game+ would be standard. That is not the case here, you can continue on any difficulty. This means it's better to play through on the easiest difficulty, get max out weapons across the board and stockpile a crap tone of ammo then just breeze through the game on the hardest difficulty. 

The merchant balancing is terrible. You have the same couple guns for 3/4 of the game, a crap tone of money and nothing to buy then at the 3/4 mark suddenly a bunch of guns to buy. They also botched the upgrade system for guns. You can (like RE4) increase things like the damage of your gun, mag capacity, add attachment ect. which is great. At one point you get a new pistol which at the time you acquire it (pretty early in the game) is weaker than what you can get your starting pistol. This is because you can't upgrade it until you progress. So like in older titles, I held onto it until I could upgrade it to be better. By the time I could, the merchant immediately got a pistol in stock that non-upgraded was better than the second pistol upgraded making it completely pointless. This happened numerous times and even happens with the end game guns. 


There are other issues but the review will last years so.

[h1]In-Depth Analysis[/h1]
[h3]Pros[/h3]
[b]1.[/b]
From an AAA title of this caliber, it was sort of expected to have top-notch visuals. However, cutting-edge graphics are hereby combined with masterful art direction, that consistently creates a bouquet of environments ranging from opulent castles to damp sunken villages and abandoned factories. About anything from smoke, to the plumage of crows and bullet casings, is realized with utmost care.

[b]2.[/b]
Secrets, metric tons of em! In true Resident Evil tradition, more reminiscent of RE4 than anything else, RE8 has potent weapons, forgotten treasures, unique modifications and even dangerous optional bosses scattered about anywhere. Going off the beaten path, scouting every millimetre of every house, shack and ceiling, may be the wisest use of time anyone could make.

[b]3.[/b]
On Hardcore difficulty, Ethan can expect to have his head smashed in by just a few hits from the lowliest enemy, some more if blocking is used correctly. Combat is always dangerous no matter the foe at hand, the challenge is equally defeating the enemy, while doing so in the most conservative manner - careless players will eventually struggle from lack of supplies. Bosses and Elite foes may be a bit on the slow side, sure, but their attacks may very well obliterate Ethan there and then.

[b]4.[/b]
Cursed undead, deformed gargoyles and vampires are just some of the many bizarre and definitely lethal foes on Ethan's path. Most of them are inspired to Eastern European mythology and folklore, while some others are original creations in line with the lore and setting. Save few exceptions, most of them have unique attack patterns, behaviors and their own identity in the gameplay.

[b]5.[/b]
Between Mercenaries, the impossibly brutal "Shadows" difficulty and the Points Shop housing unique guns and gear, there definitely is replay value and more content after beating the main story. Some of that might not be everyone's cup of tea, but for those who like it, it's there and ready.

[h3]Cons[/h3]
[b]1.[/b]
Exception made for the final boss (that one is a REAL son of a-), most other head honchos really don't stand up to their reputation, even on Hardcore. Attacks are mostly slow, predictable, and most bosses can be kited around rather easily. It ain't a cakewalk, but it's not really hard either. Sure they can one-shot poor Ethan, but they have to actually hit him first.

[b]2.[/b]
Not only the first let's say two hours are a bit boring (save for a couple "turnaround" scenes), but also house what probably is the lowest point of the whole adventure, a segment so badly designed and so unfair I wanted to slam my head into a wall, and I did, after dying some 20+ times in it. After this mediocrity though, the game starts to really shine.

[h1]Gameplay Breakdown[/h1]

[b]Exploration[/b]
Is done on foot most of the time, rarely using vehicles such as boats. The global map gives a general layout of some areas, while some others are discovered by hand or by finding a physical Map item. Notably, rooms that have some un-looted items will be colored red, completely cleared ones instead, blue. Open spaces are not subject to this "color coding". Paying attention to each area, opening all containers and taking time to explore thoroughly are vital, to rack up enough resources. Several completely optional areas are present, often they house more dangers but also unique rewards.

[b]Combat[/b]
Plays out in first-person, with Ethan able to carry several guns (depending on inventory size) and equip four of them, or equivalent consumables like grenades, in quick slots for immediate swapping. As in most survival horrors, precision and conservation are the foundations: hitting enemy weakpoints, using environmental elements (like explosive barrels) and being as efficient as possible are the only ways to not run out of, well... everything. Blocking has paramount importance as well, as it greatly reduces sustained damage and enables a stun counter-attack afterwards. On "Hardcore", enemies hit like a ton of bricks, some capable of killing Ethan in a single blow even. 

[b]Character Management[/b]
Is done using the inventory panel, which has a rectangular area containing all of the protagonist's items, weapons and consumables. Quest items and treasures are however excluded and kept separately. Provided one does regularly upgrade the inventory size, the amount of space is rather generous and there won't be major over-encumbrance issues: Ethan will eventually become a walking armory. Excess items can be sold to the Merchant anyway, or picked up at a later time.

[b]Puzzles[/b]
Are rather uncommon, sparsely distributed throughout the adventure. They often involve finding the correct sequence in some layout of elements, or gathering all the required pieces to operate something. None of the enigmas proves much of a challenge, as they are all on simple levels.

[b]Mercenaries Mode[/b]
Is a standalone game mode unlocked after finishing the game. Re-using maps from the main story, it pits players against hordes of enemies in various locations, with the objective of scoring as many points as possible. Unique mechanics are present, such as Ability Spheres that grant powerful passive skills, and also Time Spheres that prolong the ever-present global timer. Killing many foes in a short time triggers a Combo, that gives out bonus points. As missions are completed, points earned and high ratings acquired, more weapons, levels and other bonuses will be unlocked.

Resident Evil 7 was a pretty big deal, as it was Capcom swerving back into their old school design philosophy of survival horror found in the original trilogy of the series. That said, as good as the game was, it definitely felt like it pulled some punches and didn’t go all out with a lot of its ideas. After the overwhelming success and positive reception of Resident Evil 2 Remake, which was far truer to the original concept, the RE7 team decided to take their ideas to greater extremes while also incorporating some of the elements people loved in Resident Evil 4. Thanks to this, Resident Evil Village isn’t just all the better for it, but is in my opinion one of the best entries in the franchise to date.

If you’ve played Resident Evil 7, you know what to expect from this game on a mechanical level, and on a game design philosophy level if you’ve played Resident Evil 4. While Ethan still feels as helpless as he did in the previous game despite the shooting feeling good, there’s a lot more emphasis on action and your resources aren’t as limited as they usually are. The Attache case inventory system of RE4 is back, and only your weapons, ammo and healing items are what take up space in it as key items and treasures do not. The trader is back in the form of The Duke, who not only sells you goods and upgrades your gear, but has way more involvement in the story this time around. Needless to say, the level design is still excellent and on par with the Spencer Mansion and RPD; though it may not flow as well, it’s still incredibly complex and multilayered with a lot more verticality, and you’ll be slowly going back and forth across the map trying to open up piece by piece like a giant escape room, much like in the previous games. The enemy cast is excellent in terms of the sheer variety of them as well as the intelligence of their AI as not only will they run at you but even try to dodge your bullets and hit you with melee weapons. The stalker enemies unfortunately suffer the same issue as with Nemesis in Resident Evil 3 Remake, where they feel less natural in their stalking, they stalk you for very short periods and the scripting is very apparent so things feel more artificial.

Something really interesting is that this time around, the game really takes advantage of its physics as well as being in the first-person perspective. You’ll often find extra treasures and resources if you’ve got a sharp eye and look around really carefully, and while those treasures did exist in RE7, they weren’t as common and the whole idea was ruined with the perception pills that just gave them away. That said, this does make completion runs a little frustrating as you’ll definitely need a guide in order to clear out all the items in the game, as some are really difficult to spot on your own. This also applies to puzzles and you’ll be asked to look around way more at specific angles in order for the answers to align to you. The boss fights are overall excellent, and while it may not be the most apparent with some of the earlier bosses, they keep getting better and better the more you progress into the game, to a point where the last several boss fights are among the best the series has to offer. The enemy encounters are very clever too, as there are instances where you’re in very open areas and you might have to rely on the sniper rifle as you shoot down enemies waiting to ambush you from a safe distance, in addition to one specific encounter taking advantage of liquid physics in a highly engaging way that I’ve never seen done before. I don't discuss these games much when it comes to the story, but I really enjoyed it here especially with its ongoing theme about family and how it's incorporated into almost every facet of the narrative. Overall, the game just screams quality and creativity top to bottom.

With that said, there are definitely some issues with this game with the elephant in the room being the terrible performance. If you’re running on an old machine with a budget graphics card, the game might be unplayable; whenever Lady Dimitrescu is loaded in, the frame rate and the game speed both tank so significantly, and even during cutscenes the dialogue audio will play normally for their normal length of an average of one minute, but the animation still has to catch up and so the cutscene takes a full 10 minutes to finish. It happens so often and it’s so frustrating especially during moments of tension where you’re in a calm scene that then suddenly turns violent as you can hear people starting to scream but the animation has yet to catch up. Contrary to other Resident Evil games, the start of this game is kinda slow and the game progressively gets better the more you play (this might be the one exception when the final area in the lab is my favorite part in a Resident Evil game). Other issues are much more minor, but the default keyboard and mouse controls for navigating the map are incredibly frustrating, and changing them to anything else without running into conflicts is a nightmare. You do get the ability to shove enemies away if they get too close to you, but you can only do so after taking a hit and it’s context-sensitive, thus rendering the mechanic pretty worthless except in very rare occasions. I’ve also noticed a couple of times when the game just eats my keyboard inputs especially when trying to switch weapons. One minor issue but one that frustrated me so much is that the game locks the ability to get meals from the merchant arbitrarily up to a certain point in the game, and you’ll be picking up livestock meat way before that, but you have no idea what to do with food especially when it takes up space in your inventory, so naturally you would think to sell them, which is what I did and on my next visit to the merchant did the option to cook unlock.

Overall, Resident Evil 7 walked so Resident Evil Village could sprint. It’s a huge improvement on the previous entry, and the game is so unbelievably good that I would even rank it after the remake of Resident Evil 2 as my favorites in the franchise if not what I consider to be the best. Definitely check it out, although buyer beware if you’re running on anything lesser than a system with a GTX 1660 graphics card, as the performance drop is so significant it might heavily impact your experience with the game.

I would recommend anyone with fps and RE experience to play on Hardcore as this appears to be the sweet spot for an initial run. As a RE Veteran of the series the Castle was my favorite area and gave me serious Spencer Mansion vibes from the Remake which is my favorite of all the games, its a shame the section is so short and its stalkers ie the tall vampire lady and daughters dont stick around. I always think what was so great about the originals was that they just dropped you in these massive environments and left a lot of the story and puzzles as mysteries to be solved as you progressed, the Castle is a bit like this but a lot of the game and encounters do unfortunatley feel very scripted.

I do enjoy the way in which the game was paced, with each chapter and lord seemingly borrowing from previous games in the series although its not as scary as the originals by a long shot it does have its moments in places and I enjoyed uncovering the lore and mystery as I progressed. I do wish that there had been more lore and exposition with regards to the lords as the four villains and the cult are by far the most interesting part of the game and how they all occupy there own individual areas which are genuinely all different. Capcom have also given us a huge range of new enemy types and I genuinely like the new Lycan monsters and how they react and work as AI. 

In conclusion a much more improved and expanded RE7 with a central hub in the Village itself loaded with secrets and side contents, much more enemy types, a much better plot and lore, more scares and genuinely a great outing for the franchise.

Anyone interested in how this ties in with the initial Universe and games can also find the answers by exploring later diaries by the primary antagonist although if they had further expanded this it would have been great.

Resident Evil Village takes what RE7 did and pushes it to the next level. While there is still an emphasis on horror the game is a lot more action oriented than its predecessor was. Don't let that turn you off though. The game's atmosphere and even some of its mechanics actually feel a bit like RE4.  Like RE4, you are in a remore European village with all manner of creatures about.  Unlike the previous game, enemies have a chance of dropping items ranging from extra herbs to even treasure, which is another similarity it has to RE4. 

The gameplay is solid and plays much like RE7 with its first person perspective. The combat feels much faster and more refined now however. You can still block attacks as always, but now a perfect parry will allow you to perform a counter to push the enemy away.  Gunplay is pretty much unchanged. You still solve puzzles and progress through the story as well. One of the cases where more of the same is welcome depending upon who you are.

Considering RE's history of being campy, the story here is probably one of the better out of all the games. Close to the end of the game your emotions may get a little intense due to the outcome of the story.  I won't spoil it, but let's just say it will leave you surprised. 

While I do recommend this game, I would urge you to wait to buy. The game has some performance bugs that Capcom needs to address.  At the time of writing, the game will experience a nasty performance drop after only a handful of hours of play. This happens even on good PC's. There are fixes for this (well they're more like band-aids as they don't actually address the primary issue) but for the most part you may need to just reboot the game as this seems to solve the issue. Resident Evil took a high risk with the making of RE:7 and it turned out to be the start of something special. This was the "something special". Fantastic game full of unique and interesting environments, really fun enemies and interesting boss battles, a great mix of survival horror, panic, terror, and a fantastic well-written story with lovable character(s) and a surprisingly great ending that I definitely didn't expect. One of my favorite installments in the Resident Evil game series. An absolute pleasure to play

Verdict:
If you liked Resident Evil 7 you'll likely enjoy this too. If you're a Resident Evil fan that didn't like the direction RE7 took, you likely won't like this either. If you're interested in this game but haven't played RE7, go play that first - should be able to get it for cheap. Despite the pre-release press and interviews claiming it's inspired by Resident Evil 4, don't go in expecting first-person Resident Evil 4, you'll be let down.

The boring details:
Story/writing
I enjoy Resident Evil's hokey writing that rides the line between taking itself seriously and knowing it's a game. It's something Resident Evil does well and has grown into over the years. I've seen some people criticising the quality of the dialogue and voice acting, but to me it's on par with previous entries. I think the campiness is very much intentional, and I'm sure a lot of Resident Evil fans will enjoy it.

I can see why the developers talked about growing attached to Ethan. Despite being intended as a blank slate, his vanilla one-liners and constant surprise at all the weird stuff happening (despite this being well and truly not his first rodeo) made him endearing to me. There's also some nice character development, with him going from being scared and angry, to still somewhat scared but determined. 

Ethan gets put through a lot of bodily harm - like a lot - but picks himself up and keeps going. Some people will observe this as over the top, or lacking attention to detail. However it has a story pay off and it speaks to the chops of the writers that they understood this is the reaction people would have and played with it.

Similar to RE7, the story is end-loaded. You're in the dark until the last couple of hours when the Gates of Exposition open wide. I'd much prefer the story pacing to be more consistent overall. There's a twist you can see coming, but the conclusion was overall satisfying with some plotholes here and there. I also think they handled the last act of the game much better than the previous title. It escalates but this time keeps the gameplay enjoyable.

There's something off regarding the pacing overall. For some reason it feels like there's a chunk missing from this game. It could be the hub-like nature of the village and how you always return there - it lacks a feeling of adventure where you end up somewhere radically different from where you started.

Graphics/Art
It's a very pretty game, and runs well. The environments are incredibly detailed and the standout of the game. It doesn't reach the highs of the atmosphere of RE7, but I think that's because that game had a much tighter, focused environment. This one takes you through some distinct environments which aren't in conflict with each other, but don't always compliment each other either.

I found some of the enemy designs weak. The common enemies aren't very scary, and some of the boss designs lack originality (spooky dolls? Come on).  But there are some great ones. Lady Dimitrescu is the obvious mention. The design is creative visually and in practice. It's a scary thing the first time you approach a door and she opens it in front of you, having to duck under the frame, giving you just enough time to turn and run. Being chased by a large, slow enemy isn't new, but the first-person perspective and presentation elevates it. Sturm, a boss in the Factory level, was another favourite of mine, an extremely dangerous looking bio-mechanical body horror monstrosity.

Combat
There's inspiration taken from Resident Evil 4, but the combat and gunplay don't live up to the pedigree. 

A difference can be seen in the first big action sequence. The parallel in Resident Evil 4 is when you have to fight off enemies until the village bell tolls and they leave you alone. In RE4 this is a baptism by fire and you have to survive it. You are introduced to mechanics and then immediately have to use them to survive. It's tense and rewarding and challenging. 

The equivalent in RE8, while intense, is a much less enjoyable experience. It's quickly apparent you don't have enough resources to deal with the number of enemies, and that you're expected to lose so the story can continue (that being said, there are in-game challenges related to this scenario, so it may play out differently on new game+ where you have access to more weapons and ammo). You're introduced to being able to barricade doors but I think I used it all of twice to any effect in my playthrough.

The guns lack the punchiness of RE4. In RE4, hit noises had this crunch noise that delivered good feedback. In RE8, hitting a target is far less satisfying. This lack of feedback contributes to the enemies feeling like bullet sponges, along with a lack of flinching or reaction to hits. After a few hits they stumble or are thrown off balance, but mostly they tank the hits and keep moving. Lycan heads sometimes pop in a satisfying way, but a lot of the time they just throw their hands in the air and fall over when they die, and in the case of the vampire enemies this is all they do. I wished they worked on making the hit feedback punchier and enemy reactions more frequent and exaggerated. It's like they transplanted the system from RE7 without making more considerations for the greater emphasis on combat.

Puzzles
They're way too easy. I didn't feel accomplished completing any of them, and I miss the riddle-like puzzles of previous survival horror games.

Technical Issues
This game hasn't been ported perfectly, and it shows. The obvious issue is a lack of FoV option. I'm sure there's some argument that it makes the game scarier, but it's an unwelcome limitation. For some people a tight FoV makes them feel sick. For me it's uncomfortably claustrophobic, and not in a tension enhancing way. I recommend using the FoV fix available online to increase the FoV and remove the vignette - it makes the game look and feel better.

Keybinds can be customised, but for whatever reason only to alphanumeric keys. I'm not sure why this was done. It's annoying as I bind some extra mouse buttons to symbol keys, but wasn't able to assign them in this game. Another thing to note is I use a Razer mouse and have multimedia controls set up through Synapse, like changing the volume. This didn't work in-game. I didn't put a lot of effort into troubleshooting as it's a minor inconvenience, but this is the first game where I've had this problem.

Conclusion
Overall I really liked it but I hold RE7 more highly. The first-person idea was still fresh and while some of the villains of Village stand out, it's hard to beat the characterful and unsettling Baker family. I feel for fans that haven't enjoyed these entries in the series and want the old style back, but it's good to see Capcom working with this new formula and mostly succeeding. I'm happy to recommend this game Resident Evil or not, because story-focused single player games with high production values and interesting settings are getting rarer, and this one is worth playing.

[h1] Finally completed the game, final impressions of the game. [/h1]

[b] Pros: [/b]

- RE Engine is VERY well optimised. Even playing on an RX 5500XT which is a budget 1080p GPU. I was easily achieving 150+ fps during indoor areas and 100-120 in outdoors on max settings. The game supports Radeon Boost if you need extra FPS, not like it matters too much for single player but it's there if you need it. I did have one crash but I think this was my GPU driver rather than the game itself.

- The gun play feels tight and a lot more polished. I previously played RE7 on PS4 and it felt rather jank. Could be the controller but playing it with a mouse made the experience a lot better.

- Free roaming is fantastic and the game encourages you to go and explore to find rewards that will become very useful later on in the game. No load times. All seamless.

- The Duke is easily my favourite character in the entire game. Very well voice acted. Real hero of the game. [spoiler] The RE4 merchant is mentioned and got a good laugh from the impression! [/spoiler]

 [spoiler] - The doll house segment where your weapons are taken away and have to avoid the blob, easily the most frightening moment in game and gave me a strong PT vibe! More of this in future games please! [/spoiler]

- Ethan actually shows emotion this time when going through a traumatic situation. Considering all the crazy stuff he saw in RE7, he didn't seemed phased at all. He's a far more likeable character. [spoiler] the twist about him being dead and moulded was crazy. [/spoiler]

[b] Cons: [/b]

- The FOV complaints are certainly valid. I am surprised that a game in 2021 hasn't included this as an option considering RE7 & 2/3 remake have this. We shouldn't have to create and use a mod for the most basic settings. While I can tolerate the FOV itself, it does look a little too zoomed in for my liking. Please include this in a future update Capcom.

- Some of the boss fights are very meh. Lady D's was certainly enjoyable, I wished she saved for last. The doll was the most easiest "fight" and the fish... Pretty weak especially if you upgrade your gear earlier in the game and abuse the mines. Not as much fun compared to RE7. And Heisenberg's fight... Different but didn't felt like it should have been in the RE universe. Mother's fight was OK but certainly under whelming.

- While there are more variety of enemies to fight. They do get stale very quickly and can be easily dealt with once you learn their weakness and attack patterns. It can become a chore later especially when you're forced to fight in order to progress.

- Even playing on hard core, it's far too easy. I haven't played Shadow of the Village difficulty but will plan to do this on NG+.

[spoiler] - Look at how they massacred my boy, Chris! I really didn't like the action sequence and could tell that this was to appeal fans of RE6. [/spoiler]

- The story's pacing at the start is very slow.

Resident Evil Village (RE8) is an excellent return to the horror underpinnings of the franchise, but with a new "combined" perspective. It brilliantly continues the path set by RE7, successfully infusing it with the DNA of RE4. But it's not the only infusing they did. Even though its not mentioned anywhere, this game is actually divided by chapters. I don't want to spoil anything so thats why I'm not going to mention details but rather I'm going to explain these chapters by comparing the previous games that this game is inspired from and very similar: 

If we think about it, there are actually 6 chapters. First one is like RE4 where you first enter the village and explore the village for the first time, second one is like RE2R where there is an unkillable boss follows you around while you are trying to figure out the exit, third one is like Silent Hill PT where you lose your weapons, fourth one is like RE4 (again), fifth one is like RE3R where you kill zombies while trying to figure out how to reach your destination and the final chapter is like COD Zombies...

Yeah I know... I'm surprised as well like you from "COD Zombies" part but it was a short and nice touch.

[b]To sum:[/b] As you can see from above, RE Village doesn't offer you anything new or creative but instead they combined the previous successful gameplay mechanics so good that I can clearly recommend this game to anyone. It's not as scary as RE7 and it's also not as fast as the ones with TPS camera angle.

[h1]Resident Evil Village[/h1]

[b]Story / Main Game Overview[/b]

I finished the game in one (very long) sitting which took me about 16 hous with about 10 and a half hours of actual playtime and have to say that i'm overwhelmed by how good it was. So in terms of game length you don't have to worry for the game being another RE3 Remake.

Gameplaywise Resident Evil Village feels like a enhanced and overhauled version of Resident Evil 7 as there are a lot more weapons and mechanics based on the First Person Combat that was present in the last game, more exploration and more puzzles (though still not as many as there would be in a classic RE).

Aesthetically and atmospherically it feels a lot like Resident Evil 4 minus the horrible escort quest and it also uses RE4's legendary Inventory & Merchant Systems with the abillity to upgrade your weapons and put attachments on them. New Game+ Allows you to bring your upgraded weapons and items into an new playthrough to maximize their stats and make it easier to clear higher difficulties, because unlike Resident Evil 4, you can now pick a new difficulty after loading a completed Savefile and prepare your Hardcore or Village of Shadows Run on lower difficulties, though be warned, lower difficulties yield a lot less Lei (Currency) and you will have a harder time upgrading all of your weapons.

[b]The Mercenaries[/b]

The Mercenaries are Back as well, though this time around it's more like.. "The Mercenary", since there are no unlockable Characters or Outfits or anything of the likes. In this iteration of the classic, you once again take the Role of Ethan Winters and start in the Duke's Shop where you'll get a fixed amount of Lei (which you can increase by completing the different Stages) that you can spend to build your prefered Loadout before you start. Once you start you will go through a timed gauntlet of smaller Areas in which you have to defeat a fixed amonut of enemies. Kills and golden Watch Pickups increase your timelimit, Kill-Chains increase your score and blue pickups give you so called "powers" which are passive upgrades that last for the entire stage. Each time you pick up a power, you get to choose out of three and can stack as many of them as you find.
It feels a lot like a mix between The Mainline's Mercenaries modes and Revelation's Raid Mode. There are also Rewards for the Story to be unlocked in this mode. 

[b]Final Verdict[/b]

All in all this is a very good entry to the Resident Evil Franchise and it will mark the finale for faceless protagonist Ethan Winters and storywise this game will probably even surprise the oldest of Resident Evil veterans. Village has a lot of replay value thanks to four different difficulty settings (from which the hardest makes significant changes to most enemy encounters, so be aware), lots of speacial weapons to unlock and the mercenaries mode.

At the time of Review i completed the game twice, once on Standard Diffculty and once on Hardcore diffculty and i'm currently in the middle of my first "Village of Shadows" Difficulty run, which is quite stressful compared to the former two. For now i can't get enough of this game and hunting down all of those special unlocks is lots of fun and will probably keep me occupied for quite some time.

Resident Evil: Village is about a man who is ready to sacrifice everything, overcome any obstacle and overthrow any foe to save his family, come hell or high water.

Sidenote, I feel like RE:V is Capcom telling us: "This is as best as it gets in terms of a RE4 remake because the real remake is gonna suck". Hopefully I'm wrong but yeah...

RE:V feels moderately inspired by Resident Evil 4, everything from having a similar inventory system (inventory tetris is back people!) to having a merchant, buying and finding upgrades for weapons and even one specific boss.

Locations? Very atmospheric and immersive. 
Visuals? To be honest not a lot seems to have changed from RE7 but the game does look nice indeed. 
Weapons? Capcom gets a big plus for adding the FR-F2, my baby from a certain F2P game <3. Otherwise varied and interesting, still lack more oomph in the sound department but maybe that's intended? Feels that way.
Sounds? No complains but like I mentioned the guns could do with more oomph.
Story? Not as predictable as one might think with crazy plot twists.
Difficulty? Assisted and regular are indeed very easy, my first run was on regular and I died around five times due to my own stupidity and not because the game was difficult. I do have a feeling hardcore and village of shadows will grab you by the balls and make a balloon poodle out of them, like always.

Other than that, challenges are quite fun to do, mercenaries mode is fun aswell, first time I actually felt like playing mercenaries and that says a lot. Unlocks are very nice because you can now get unlimited ammo for any gun, not just specific guns like it was in RE2R-3R RE4 or RE7. You have to fully upgrade a weapon to be able to unlock infinite ammo for it though, RE5 style. I mean it extends your playtime and makes you really vacuum clean the map for treasure and enemies to save up for upgrades. There is NG+ to help you with collecting enough money aswell.

Right, treasure. Remember RE4 and the gems you had to shoot down? Or the treasure you had to "assemble"? Yeah, it's back. 

Crafting is also here and guess what? Crafting resources have their separate, unlimited storage! More space for cooking ingredients (yes there is "cooking" in this game which give you pernament HP, and speed bonuses as well as guarding dmg reduction).

There is a lot to talk about here but I'm gonna leave it at that. I think that, if you enjoyed RE7 and want a similar horror-survival FPP (with RE4 vibes) experience, you'll love this.

I want to preface this review by saying that I've never been a very big RE fan. Had the first one on my PS1, but was too scared to play it, played RE2 and 3 (remastered), but was pulled into the franchise with RE7. RE7 was awesome, there were few things I didn't like about the game, so I wanted to put that out there due to the criticism the game's receiving over "not being a RE game".
The game is absolutely stunning, and though I've seen a few complaints on FPS, I'm running it on very high settings, at around 80-120FPS, with no problems at all on a RX5600XT. Another note, the game uses a compelling sense of rule of thirds. Every single area I look at could be used as a wallpaper, so considering how big the game is, it was quite a feat to accomplish.
The RE Engine is quickly becoming one of my favorites, combat is snappy and responsive, weapon animations are well made, and though the spread while moving or firing to quickly can be a bit forgiving, a sense of accuracy is made clear through gameplay. I kinda wish the weapon swapping would've been fixed, but I guess it adds some kind of culture to the game (Octo Ethan).
Gameplay loop can be summed up by; New area with stuff you can't do, fodder enemies, area specific bigger enemies, mini bosses, hidden area that can be completed because of previous said new area with stuff you can't do (usually accompanied by a mini boss or bigger enemy), next zone, sell all your collectibles to the Duke, upgrade your stuff, ♥♥♥♥ your pants when you get to the ventriloquist's zone, rinse and repeat. There's a lot to do and is very well paced which keeps the game fresh. 
In terms of the horror aspect, I can definitely say I've screamed multiple times. But I'm also a massive ♥♥♥♥♥. Comparatively, I don't believe it has as many scares as RE7, but 8 definitely has one of the scariest (or uncomforting) thing I've ever seen in a video game. Overall, RE8 definitely felt a lot more tense, so if you enjoy that kind of stuff, this game's right up your alley.
Overall, this game is a serious breath of fresh air, it's been a while since we've had a AAA title with this kind of quality, and it's definitely going down as one of the better games I've played in the last couple of years. The only people I would not recommend this game to are people who aren't a fan of horror/thriller, and anime lovers.

**Resident Evil Village Review – Action, Exploration, and a Thriving Modding Scene**

Having completed *Resident Evil Village* on my Xbox Series X and now diving into it on PC for the modding scene, I can confidently say that this game is a blast to play, though it's more action-oriented than classic *Resident Evil* horror. That being said, it still strikes a good balance, especially compared to the overly action-heavy *Resident Evil 5* and *6*.

### Action Over Horror – A Balanced Mix
*Resident Evil Village* leans more into the action side of things, but it manages to blend in enough horror elements to keep the *Resident Evil* DNA intact. While it may not have the same spine-chilling tension as *Resident Evil 7*, the action-packed moments are exhilarating and well-executed. The bosses, however, are relatively easy compared to other titles in the series, making them more about spectacle than challenge. The puzzles and codes, while present, are straightforward and won’t leave you scratching your head for long.

### Combat and Exploration – The Game’s Highlights
For me, the greatest part of this game is the combat and exploration. There’s something incredibly satisfying about the game’s gunplay and how it mixes with the world’s creepy, atmospheric exploration. Despite having completed the game twice on Xbox, I’m still finding new areas and treasures halfway through my third playthrough on PC. The replay value is impressive, with a world that constantly rewards exploration even on multiple runs.

### Replayability and Speedrunning
The first time through, the story takes around 8 hours, which feels just right. But it’s clear the game expects you to speedrun it, as subsequent playthroughs can be done in about 3 hours. This adds a layer of challenge for completionists or those who love getting the most out of their games.

### PC Modding – A Fresh Experience
Playing on PC is an entirely different experience thanks to the thriving modding community. While I loved my time on Xbox, the variety of mods available on PC has given the game new life and extended its replayability. Whether it’s cosmetic changes, gameplay tweaks, or entirely new ways to play, the modding scene adds a fresh dimension to an already solid game.

### Final Thoughts
*Resident Evil Village* is a fantastic game with a good balance of action and exploration. While it may not offer the same horror intensity as earlier titles, the engaging combat and rewarding exploration keep it entertaining. The ease of the bosses and simple puzzles may detract for some, but for me, they didn’t hinder the overall enjoyment. If you’re playing on PC, the modding scene only enhances the experience, making it a must-play for any fan of the series.

I cannot begin to describe how absolutely relieved I am that this game exceeded all my expectations. As someone who enjoyed RE7, but did NOT classified it as a main title Resident Evil game, I am blown away with what they took from 7 and turned into a full fledged, truly Resident Evil feeling game. This game is not only Beautiful in Graphics, Story Telling, and emotion itself, but its a clear step forward in the RE series that deserves every ounce of praise it gets.

- It feels like a mix of all the best aspects from RE4, 5, 6, and 7 combined into one fantastic game. Gone are the bland molded enemies and replaced with actual enemies that give you not only a challenge but a feel of "What are they going to do next?"
- The guard feature has been improved upon by simply giving it a knock back feature after successfully guarding.
- Ethan had more lines/character development in the first 30 minutes than he did in the entire RE7 campaign. 
- Ties to the past RE games also come into play here (No Spoilers on what). Thank GOD we are not rebooted!
- Bosses FEEL like Resident Evil bosses! This is a big one! While I love the Bakers for what they were, the only true RE boss in that game was Jack's final forum!
-Gun play and mechanics from RE4 and 5 are used to upgrade weapons and manage inventory that makes the game WAY more exciting! 
- NoneLinear Gameplay, (For the most part) DONE RIGHT! 
- SOMETHING FOR EVERYONE! From hardcore fetus horror to action packed Call of Duty esc gunplay, this game literally is a perfect blend of everything for everyone. 
- I couldn't even find a single bug, (gameplay wise) in my whole play through. Capcom really let those bugs have it! A really good release launch!
- The RE Engine has never looked more stunning! Honestly, RE7 was made as an indoor game, and you could tell outside was NOT the focus with how ugly it looked. But this new RE Engine is just straight up beautiful! And its not that big of a GPU hog either!

For hardcore Resident Evil fans, and people just looking for a good story/horror game in general. You MUST pick this game up! Worth its price, worth your time! Thank you Capcom for not screwing this up!!!!
