Resident Evil: Village is a solid entry into the resident evil series

Pros:
-Clean and well defined mechanics of the series are back including looting, crafting and exploration which has always been what has made a good resident evil survival horror game.
-Characters are all interesting and unique, very different from one another.
-Story is good but it isn't the best part of the game, it's not why I think most people play resident evil.
-Lots of challenges and end-game content to use so replay ability is encouraged (Thanks as well to exploration)
- The duke(merchant) is a great addition to the game, selling treasures to buy upgrades for guns become something to look forward to. A duke's kitchen system also allows to make permanent upgrades as well to Ethan Winters.
- Mercenary mode is a good fun addition but I could only see one possible meta build which was the sniper and shotgun combo. Although the ability system does make for some exciting chaos with more ability's unlocked the better your scores are.

Cons:
-You cannot revisit the castle after leaving which annoyed the hell out of me as I had left it assuming I could come back and explore it later. The game doesn't tell you this which is even more annoying.
-Like resident evil bio-hazard, Ethan Winters walks at a snails pace which is fine when first walking into new areas but if you want to revisit an area it can be chore because of how slow he is. Luckily there is an upgrade to improve his movement speed but that is found pretty late in the game.
-No FOV sliders, which can be an issue for those with motion sickness.
-I'm normally a pretty big ♥♥♥♥♥ when it comes to horror games but I noticed that the first half was scary but the second half was more action than scary which for me was a disappointment.
Awesome game, good pacing in most parts, beautiful maps and an incentive to replay the game.

First things first: This is a very good game. I only played resident evil 4, 7 and the remakes of 2 and 3. And out of all of these it's probably my 2nd favorite game.

The game took me 15 hours to beat as someone who likes to backtrack and find every single piece of loot (I didn't even find everything). That is including cutscenes. I played it on the standard difficulty.

This game is absolutely beautiful. I don't have the best PC specs but the game runs very well. A certain enemy who has lots of particals will eat your frame rate though but that seems to be for everyone from what I've seen. 
The gameplay is also phenomenal for the most part.

The beginning of this game is actually amazing (first 6 hours if you don't speedrun it). It might actually be my favorite start of a game ever. It's really incredible. It does a very good job at making you scared/panic. One area specifically is very terrifying.

The middle part is still very good. You just don't really feel scared anymore because of all the fire power you own at that moment. At that point it's kind of going from survival-horror to action.
Though even with all the firepower you still have to be strategic.

The last 1/2 hours are very underwhelming. It just starts spamming enemies and bullet sponges at you. 
I don't mind action but the combat mechanics just don't fit for that style. 
What I mean by that is that you are pretty slow, your camera's FOV is fixed (you can't see much around you). This is all to make you feel more vulnerable and make you more scared. That works perfect for survival-horror but not for action. It becomes more of a frustration at that point.

The game rewards you a lot for exploring. There are a couple of secret optional areas that you can enter once you get specific key items and you happen to remember a certain door/passage being locked before.
One area in particular was really cool and satisfying.

There are a couple of puzzles and minigames in the story. None of them are too hard. One minigame in particular involving a little ball is very cute.

Without the last part of the game this game is a solid 9/10

I beat the main story in less than 9 hours. Harder modes are unlocked but it just looks like the enemies are just bullet sponges. There is a bonus game you can play where you kill as many enemies possible within a time limit and other weapon unlocks you can get through challenges.

Overall this isn't worth the full price. I would wait for it to go on sale before purchasing it. Hardcore mode is too hard and I usually end up dying after being hit twice. Other issues that I have is extreme fps drops during certain fights.

As somebody who was a fan of Resident Evil 7, but with no prior background towards Resident Evil 4, I had big expectations for this game. However, everything about Resident Evil 7 that made it great was seemingly left out here, and all of RE7's weak points were ported over.

I'll start off with the environment, which is probably the greatest part about this game. The graphics look amazing, especially the village, and each location has its own personality to it. The lighting, whether it be outside or indoors, was perfectly done. The setting was very compelling, and might even be better than Resident Evil 7, so where does this game fall flat?

One problem I had with the game was the lack of a real threat. I played the game on the normal difficulty setting, rather than hardcore, which might have been a factor, but the game seemed as if I was on casual. Not once did I have a fear of dying, as I somehow always managed to have 50 pistol bullets in my reserve while only using a pistol. The pacing of the weapons was off-putting as well. I unlocked the second power upgrade for my starting pistol, only to receive a M1911 moments later that had a higher base damage. This made me wonder what the point of upgrading was if I was going to find, or buy, a better gun anyways. The sniper rifle felt like a pointless addition to the game. With most, if not all, enemy engagements happening close range, there really isn't a situation where I would prefer a sniper rifle over the shotgun or pistol. I never felt like the antagonists were going to kill me, either. They all took their sweet, sweet time doing whatever they wanted with me. Many boss fights were just tedious and so simple. [spoiler]It seemed as though they were waiting for me to put them out of their misery. Another gameplay related problem was with the second house, Donna Beneviento. I solved a 20 minute puzzle, and thats... it? I get a Rose part? Okay, time to go to the next section! [/spoiler]

The story, like many others have already stated, felt disappointing. The pacing in particular was awful. Nothing is explained until you reach the last hour of the game, and what is explained leaves more questions than answers. The majority of the game I was wandering around, thinking back about why I was put in this village. At least in Resident Evil 7 I was looking for my wife. The antagonists have such shallow personalities compared to RE7, like they had to split one person into four different people. [spoiler]The deformed swamp dude section was laughable. It was so funny seeing him say "you're stuck here" only to run away past everything. Heisenberg was the best out of the four, as I kind of felt bad for him and actually liked his character. Meeting Chris and him just telling you "Mind your own business" or something like that made me so upset, like he dragged me into this village after murdering my wife how is it not my business. Another thing is, and I might be wrong, but after completing the game, I was still left wondering how come the van even went to the village. Chris' explanation showed that they wanted to get Ethan and Rose away, but why go so close to the village? The ending with Ethan being dead already was lazy writing. If he can magically regenerate after being injured, how come his fingers didn't grow back? [/spoiler] While Resident Evil 7's story was pretty weak, Resident Evil Village let me down on so many different levels. 

I haven't played Resident Evil 4 so I can't compare any mechanics, but from the new ones added, they really make the game less scary and more geared towards action. I ran into no space issues with the inventory system. Not once did I have to rotate my guns to fit an item in my inventory. I did buy inventory expansions, but only because I had so much excess money (I only used/upgraded the pistol).  The shop system contributed heavily to the resource management problem. There was no resource management to be done, since I knew I could buy more bullets around the corner. If I did run out of bullets for my pistol (which never happened) I could switch guns anyway. Once again, playing on hardcore might have been a different story, but this is just my own experience. Towards the end [spoiler] the factory part [/spoiler] I got so bored that I ran around blocking every enemy, the story being my only motivation. For some reason, I barely took any damage and had to heal once during the entire section.

Time and time again, during my play through, I wanted a reason to like this game. I couldn't find it. If I wanted to look at beautiful scenery I could look outside. For a game under the survival horror genre, I was definitely surviving. The horror elements were mediocre at best. All my expectations went down the gutter the longer I played Resident Evil Village. Overall, as someone who loved Resident Evil 7, I cannot recommend anyone to buy this game, especially at full price. You are better off watching someone else play this game.

I am going to start this off by saying this game was everything I wanted it to be and more. I played the game for 9 hours straight on the first day and then finished it within a few more on the next and besides the last hour and a half the whole thing absolutely blew me away.

When I saw this game was going to be heavily inspired by RE4 I immediately thought high action and a few tense moments sprinkled in between but no real horror sections. Boy was I wrong. I mean honestly the Dollmakers basement section on its own (you know the one if you played the game) is one of the scariest moments in an RE game that I can recall. Other than that though there are so many intense fights that start off from the very beginning, which some call unfair and bad design but RE4 did the same exact thing so if you say RE8 did it horribly then dont say you liked it in 4 but either way I for one like just jumping straight into the mix so it was a very humbling start to the game and really showed me what to expect in the upcoming hours playing it. 

As the game progresses you will be traveling all around the map going through various indoor and outdoor locations which all have a different atmosphere and aura to them that really helps sell the theme of the game. Ah and the theme, this is something that turns a lot of people away and makes them say its "not a real RE game" and maybe its just because I always loved the idea of making a horror game out of fantastical things like witches and other things of that sort, Hansel and Gretel type of ♥♥♥♥ and so far this game is the closest to scratching that itch for me. Also the cherry on top for me in this game was the return of the money/shop system. My favorite thing to do in RE4 was to go around hunting for all the little treasure items to give to the merchant and now its back in Village and its great to be able to do that again. The Duke is a fine replacement for The Merchant and as an ode he even quotes him in one of his lines stating "What are ya buying? Ah its just something an old friend of mine used to say", but The Dukes shop works very much like The Merchant from RE4, you buy weapons, upgrades, and other supplies you may need and also the new addition of being able to cook meals from the meat you can get by slaying some of the animals found all around the map, these meals are the replacements for the shots you would get in RE7 that permanently increase stats which I thought was a really cool way of doing it. So to wrap up the positive portion of this review I'll talk about the story. I thought it was pretty solid but it slowly dwindled and got harder to follow as the game went on until the last hour and a half where I didnt really know what had happened. But even in the last moments of the game they wrapped it up in a pretty touching way but at the same time it makes me nervous for the next new entry in the series which I will expand on later.

Now onto the things I didnt like so much. I'll start with the boss fights because its something that RE never really gets right imo. I'll sum it up by saying the theme with RE bosses is they have about 4 different attacks and once you learn those it all comes down to knowing when to dodge and having enough ammo to finish the job and while I can think of a few bosses where this differs this seems to be the main theme throughout the franchise. This is no different in RE8. The only bosses, and theyre more like mini bosses, who even break the cycle a little bit are the Dimitriscu daughters in the Castle section of the game in which before being able to damage them you need to find a way to let cold air into the room to halt their regenerative abilities and therefore kill them in about 8 or so shotgun blasts. Other than that the other bosses are just dodge, shoot, dodge, shoot, repeat until cutscene plays and this includes the final boss. But besides that another part that really didnt do it for me was the final area of the game, the factory. Throughout the whole game each area has something that sets them apart from the others whether it be the Dimitriscu ladies hunting you down in the Castle, traversing the horrifying basement in the Dollmakers house, or dodging Moreau in his section. All Heisenbergs Factory has to offer is running room to room killing human robot hybrids and finding key molds to open the next door and work your way through the area until the boss fight with him, which I'll admit even though it was still the same shoot and dodge technique it was in a tank thing and it was badass but overall a bit underwhelming. So that leads to my final qualm with Village and thats the entire final hour or so of the game. Incidentally it begins at the factory section so I'll skip that but right after the factory you are thrown into the body of Chris Redfield whose mission is to destroy Mother Miranda and to find out about what exactly is happening in the Village. Its around this point as well that you learn (or you may have figured it out earlier through notes found in the game if you arent an idiot like I am) that the Mia you saw get obliterated with bullets in the first 10 minutes of the game was actually Mother Miranda in disguise as Mia, which because I am dumb was an actual *OH ♥♥♥♥* moment for me, but she did this because she needed your daughter, Rose, to complete a ritual to bring back her daughter that died from the spanish flu over 100 years ago and yes Mother Miranda is immortal as revealed in a note from Oswell E Spencer of all people. But in Chris' section of the game they try to basically tell the whole story of Mother Miranda and the Village through a cluster of notes you find just before finding the real Mia locked up in a cell and returning you back to playing as Ethan where, and this is where it REALLY lost me, you find out from Evelyn in a dream like state that Ethan actually DIED by the hands of Jack in the Baker house and was infected with the mold which is why he is able to heal from all of those HORRIBLE injuries we've seen him acquire through his time in the series. So upon learning this Ethan limbers up, awakens one last time after getting his literal heart ripped out of his chest, and goes on to have another stereotypical RE boss fight with Mother Miranda herself in which he eventually wins and finds Rose but he cant make it out because he is slowly dying for real and turning into ash like all the mold based enemies he has defeated before. So Chris takes Rose to Mia and they ride out on a helicopter while Ethan stays behind and detonates a bomb that completely obliterates the source of the parasite that Mother Miranda was testing on the people in the village which was also the source of the Lycans. Then after the credits we fast forward to see a grown up Rose Winters on a bus who visits her father Ethans gravesite to say happy birthday, this was a pretty touching scene that I quite enjoyed even if I had just gotten my mind turned into scrambled eggs from the events before hand. But while this is a nice ending it worries me because Rose mentions she has powers and I, and im sure a lot of other people, dont want RE9 to be some Devil May Cry ♥♥♥♥ and completely shift the franchise away from horror AGAIN. Im fine with playing as Rose as long as they dont lazily try to tie together more story like they did at the end of this game.

So all in all I think it was an excellent addition to the series and I will be collecting many many more hours on it in the near future. Also I didnt say anything about Mercenaries because of the character limit but its alright but sadly not an endless wave thing like in RE4.

I'll give this one a 9/10. This is one long and rough review but I felt like this game deserved it. Good job Capcom, please keep listening to fans and trying out new things but dont stray too far from what makes this franchise what it is.

On top of that, I really did love the story and how Ethan Winters grows from blank slate protag of 7 to being up there with Leon and Chris in his own right. I know most people are just in it for Lady D, but there's so much more to discover in this nightmarish theme park of horror. The team said they want to pack as many different types of horror into this game as possible, beyond gothic with the castle, and it shows (contrary to the marketing). WOW .. just WOW. I like to write detailed reviews, so bare with me .. but if you want to jump into action, check out my first gameplay video here - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n4DujwaC6gI

So let's move on, as per Steam rules, I have to disclose that I receive the game for free (courtesy of Gamesplanet - thanks)
But this doesn't mean that I'm bought off or saying good things only because I got it for free. I have always liked the Resident Evil series, I remember playing the very first ones on playstation and moving on to PC. First ones were static camera, but they've always been very good and ahead of their time and RE Village does not disappoint.

Comparing this to other games released in 2019 - 2021 ... most other games don't even come close. I think it's best to just list PROS and CONS rather than writing a long "book" here. So here it is:

PROS:
* Amazing graphics
* Detailed sound effects
* Immersive gameplay
* Good story (at least seems like it)
* Runs very smooth / well optimized
* Haven't had any crashes during 5+ hours
* Unique and challenging enemies / gameplay
* Semi open world

CONS:
* Single player only (could at least have co-op)
* Probably gets boring after you complete it.
* Mouse sensitivity is bugged (hard to explain, but while playing / aiming it's ok, but then when examining items, it's insanely high .. so having DPI button on your mouse is very important, i hope they fix this soon)
* Could have more realism (ability to climb over a table or a chair that is blocking your path)
* Searching / looting is not the best, it only lets you open 1 drawer or cupboard door per unit (like if there's cupboard with 4 doors or drawer unit with 4 drawers, then only 1 is openable)

at this point I can't say much more as I haven't played much, but I will update this review if there's something to add. At this point I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes story-driven and scary action shooter puzzle games. STORY: This game is amazing. In my opinion, Village is the perfect sequel to Ethan Winters' trilogy. All of the current lords in the game fit easily into the story when you find out a little more about the game later on. Seems like the mold can just never leave Ethan alone, throwing him into new problems. RIP.
MUSIC: The scores are good and are placed well into the game while you're playing it. Real thought was out into crafting the music.
GAMEPLAY: Same as its predecessor, although now its in much more open areas compared to the restrictive areas in the Baker house. Guns are good and balanced, except the wolfsbane. that gun in op and cool looking, no wonder it's my favorite.
ENEMIES: Lady Dimitrescu, Lady Donna, Lord Moreau, and Lord Heisenberg have such excellent character designs and personality. Although Miss Dimitrescu turned out to be quite over hyped bc she was the first major boss. (It's not really a spoiler since she was the one in the demo) The Lycans are annoying af, so are the other ones, but it's too many words to type :3 In my opinion, the game as a whole is not as scary as RE7 except for the part with the baby, I'm thankful it was short. 
Overall Score: 9.7/10
Now to wait another 5 years for RE9

Resident Evil Village is a 2021 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom. It is the sequel to Resident Evil 7: Biohazard (2017). Players control Ethan Winters, who searches for his kidnapped daughter in a village filled with mutant creatures. Village maintains survival horror elements from previous Resident Evil games, with players scavenging environments for items and managing resources. However, it adds more action-oriented gameplay, with higher enemy counts and a greater emphasis on combat.

        [td]Reach for the Moon Engine (also known as RE Engine) is absolutely breathtaking. The environments in this game just suck you in into the experience. This is the future for Resident Evil and I couldn’t be any happier. The environments look abandoned and lived in, the architecture is stunning and the lighting is pure next level. The better thing is how good it runs. They truly optimized this game really well. The animations are really well done as well! You can feel the dread in the air, the chills from the cold environments, it's just so well done. The enemy and boss design is superb and the Castle section of the game is so beautiful, and scary at the same time. I can’t find one error in the graphics departments. It’s a true masterpiece![/td]
    [/tr]

        [td]🎮Gameplay[/td]
        [td]Resident Evil Village has a mix of Resident Evil 7, and Resident Evil 4 on the side. Let me explain - You have the merchant bag from RE4. Now I actually enjoyed this a lot. You can upgrade your weapons and inventory from the merchant, and can also buy new and unlocked end game weapons from him as well! You can find currency (just like RE4) that you can use to buy these upgrades and weapons from. You also have collectables to sell and so on, you get the idea. Now this game feels really similar to RE7 in terms of combat, and that's a good thing. The combat felt fluid, and a great balance of action and pace. You have many kinds of weapons in this game and a great amount of enemy variety and I’m really pleased with that. The puzzles were pretty easy and you will have no issues with those, so if you are looking for big brain puzzles here, unfortunately Resident Evil Village is empty in that department.[/td]
    [/tr]

        [td]The story continues from Resident Evil 7 and they do a pretty good job with it to be honest. I was absolutely hooked from the beginning, and all the way to the end. The doll house could have been expanded with more horror elements as I felt that game me the most in terms of psychological horror. The boss fights were a mix bag. Some of the fights were absolutely incredible, and some other ones just felt kinda lazy in my opinion. I also wish Chris had more screen time. Capcom kinda did Chris dirty in this game. He was a bad*ass, but would have been nice to see him interact more with Ethan. The last boss fight was also not great and that’s a true shame. The main antagonist could have done some better writing and more screen time. Besides those negatives, I did enjoy the story and I'm happy it continues from RE7, so if you haven’t played RE7, please play that one first because it’s definitely worth the whole story.[/td]

It’s not the best form of Mercenaries mode in a RE title in my opinion. It's still fun to play, but you probably won’t spend much time on it (only if you are trying to get achievements).[/td]

One of the most well thought out and put together games I've ever played. 

The narrative starts out immediately interesting and manages to sustain that throughout the entire game. The player's knowledge and understanding of events is constantly evolving as new information presents itself without anything being too predictable or seemingly random. The characters are well considered, each having their own perspective on events and their own agendas they pursue. This adds another layer to the story that frankly most games either don't bother with at all or just completely miss the mark. Very good story, now that I think of it, probably the best of any Resident Evil game.

The gameplay is varied and always doing something new and interesting; the game does not feel repetitive or boring at all. The game manages to keep it fresh by introducing new mechanics and enemy designs at a rate such that you'll never feel bored or like the game is just padding its length. (14 hours to beat on hardcore, 9 hours in-game time)

The art direction is simply ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Easily the most impressive part of the whole experience. The setting feels cohesive and seemingly no matter where you look the shot composition looks like a intentional beautiful promotional screenshot. Seriously, it's THAT good. The art team deserve a raise and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ medal of honor for their amazing job on this game.

The graphics themselves are pretty good too. The only minor gripe I have is that the textures are noticeably blurry up close, likely because the textures themselves are fairly large to create a lot of variance within a single texture. It's a trade-off, and one I'm genuinely not sure if I would have made myself put in their position. The game runs pretty well too, I managed around 120fps most of the time on a 3900x and 3080, with RT and everything cranked to ultra. I did notice some pop-in in a few places, and I was able to make my performance drop like a stone when standing in a very specific spot while in a small room. Small hiccups here and there, but ultimately the RE Engine delivers good visuals at generally high framerates.

An interesting and well-told story, varied and engaging gameplay, absolutely stunning art direction, good graphics, and rock-solid game design make this easily my favorite Resident Evil game and a reminder of how great these AAA games can be sometimes.

- SPOILER FREE REVIEW! -

Literally if you enjoyed any of the Resident Evil Games, you have to play this.

It's essentially a mix of RE7 and RE4. How? Well, the moment you get to the Village, you can tell that the whole place reminds a lot of RE4. I wouldn't be surprised if they'll use a lot of the games assets in a potential RE4 Remake or something. Plus, the game is super action heavy.

Although here's something interesting: Unlike most of the action heavy Resident Evil Games, this game still has a lot of horror and puzzle elements to remind you that you're actually playing a survival horror game and not whatever Resident Evil 6 was supposed to be, for example.

The locations look cool and the village slowly becomes kind of a "character" itself, just like the Mansion, the RPD or Raccoon City in the earlier games.

The characters are extremely unique in a very, very good way. I loved every single one of them. They're memorable and some are even really funny.

The puzzles are brilliant. Some are easy and fun/satisfying, but most of them are really challenging and you gotta put your head into some of them in order to actually solve them. Some seem really complicated, but if you don't overthink, they're actually so much easier than you thought which is a very nice way of messing with the player.

The horror aspects - as I said, are brilliant. A few parts of the game - especially one specific one, made me panic quite a bit. Trust me, you'll know which one when you get there. Other than that, this game puts a lot of different types of horror on the table. Classic, yet well executed jumpscares, panic because of being chased, pressure because of a lot of enemies and downright psychological horror, too. It even makes you feel internal pain as the player whenever the main character gets hurt in cutscenes etc. which I've never seen in any other game before and I do believe that this is it's own type of horror.

The weapons are great because they all feel unique. They didn't put that many into the game, but they definitely made them all feel useful and different enough so that you gotta carry a lot of them around with you.

Now here's a few - even if minor, problems with the game:
-The pacing early-game feels a little off/rushed and the late game has a couple of parts that just feel like unnecessary filler. They could've used this filler time to further flesh out some more character interactions or the entire castle section for example. Some of the bosses you fight early game just die and don't even get a cutscene or anything that shows "Wow, you just killed this boss!". Not necessary, but would've made the death of some characters more impactful, even if they're the bad guys. Some parts of the story just feel rushed.

-The backtracking. Hear me out, I love Resident Evil style backtracking. It makes the whole world/map become a character. A place you're familiar with and all. But the backtracking in Resident Evil 8 is just awful in one or two parts of the game because the game makes you run from one part of the map, all the way to the other only to send you back where you came from. And then it does the same thing later in the game in the same locations. You'll see what I mean when you play.

-The enemy design has the same problem as Resident Evil 7. It feels like they put down three enemy types and then also put down 2 more variations for all of them. While older Resident Evil Games had so many BOWs and other types of threats, Resident Evil 8 follows Resident Evil 7's mistake of only putting a few, easily avoidable and boring enemy types into the game. Only in the very late part of the game do you actually get to fight a bunch of really unique enemies, but I wrote this down as a negative aspect anyway because it's disappointing that they actually HAD a lot of/enough different enemies types, but chose not to use them until the very end of the game. 

-The game basically doesn't give you many weapons until the last 1-2 hours of the game where you suddenly get to buy like 5 new weapons you couldn't buy throughout the whole game up until then. 


tl;dr:
10/10 - Absolute must play if you're a fan of the franchise.

This game is a huge disappointment for someone who has played all the main Resident Evil games. There are some spoilers in this review.

They tried really hard to recreate some of the magic that RE4 had but with no success. The tetris inventory serves absolutely no purpose whatsoever in RE8. In RE4, you often were full of items and had to discard some or play tetris to make room. I beat RE8 without having to do that once. There was always room left in my inventory.

Every [i]cool[/i] game has crafting so they thought adding that in RE8 would be cool. Once again, it had no substance. I barely used it. Giving regular ammo instead of crafting materials would have served the same purpose.

They turned my favorite franchise into an open world game and it's a bad one. In RE4, you returned to the big area where you fight Dr.Salvador and you find the shotgun three times. In RE8, half of the game is in the area that is equivalent. Often times, I had to backtrack in this empty world to complete a puzzle with a new key item I just found, only to backtrack there even further after I obtained another key item. To my surprise, a new type of enemy was waiting for me in a little arena. I slightly backtracked in the corridor I came from to see the enemy lose aggro and not attack me anymore. I spent 5 minutes shooting his back while moving up and stepping back like it's Dark Souls 2. At that point, every enemy lost credibility. On that subject, remember the lickers and the hunters? You'll see none of that in RE8. It's only dudes with fur, dudes with no fur, dudes that fly or dudes with a lot of metal on them. I can't believe they didn't integrate a way for enemies to respawn to make this world more alive, especially when the shopkeeper can sell you ammo so you could never run out.

There is a feature where you give food to the shopkeeper and it increases your stats. This means if you do not shoot every animal on sight with your 12 gauge, you are not playing optimally. I thought I purchased Resident Evil 8, not the next Cabela's Big Game Hunter. The animals are just cute chickens, pigs and fishes that don't hurt you. It should be optional to shoot them, not a necessity.

I don't see myself replaying this any time soon due to the forced walking segments, some moments that have nothing going on except running, finding and using items (the puzzles in the doll house and running away from the fish boss) and the set pieces with red barrels all over the place that clearly indicate in advance you're going to fight dudes, ruining any sense of atmosphere this game could have.

Give it a shot when it's cheap, if you're really bored and have nothing else to do.

I still remember when six year old me sat next to my dad for the first time he fired up the first Resident Evil on our Playstation back in the nineties, and I remember even more vividly how terrified I was the first time I saw the first zombie turn it's head to look at me with that dead, stone-like face and blood stained lips. 

At that moment it became my favourite game and as time has gone by and, though the overall quality of the subsequent games has been up and down to say the least over the years, Resident Evil still continues to be perhaps my favourite game ever created, from the characters to the stories, the puzzles and the atmosphere, whether it was traversing the dusty, dimly lit halls of the Spencer Mansion or the zombie-ridden streets of Raccoon City, it all came together to create an experience that I still fondly revisit often and will be with me 'til my last day.

It is no doubt this influence that leaves me to give this game a positive review, as I feel it is a very well put together game for reasons I'll go into greater depth with, but I'll also be including a rather big caveat at the end, keeping the entire thing as spoiler free as I possibly can. 

Please also note that this review is the culmination of my experience after completing the game on Standard difficulty.

So, with all that in mind, here we go:

As mentioned previously, I don't want to risk any spoilers, intentional or otherwise when it comes to the story; suffice it to say that the game is a sequel to Resident Evil VII set in a rural village somewhere in Europe, with the enemies taking on a much more folkloric and gothic flavour, with some stunning art assets and scenery to emphasise it all, from the run down and rotted houses and basements of the village itself to the extravagant and decadent halls and corridors of Castle Dimitrescu.

The story itself I thought was really quite interesting, with plenty of files scattered around the village dropping various hints about what happened there to keep me guessing and drawing theories as to what was going on, with a very satisfying information dump towards the end that tied all those threads together very nicely and had me raising my eyebrows in surprise on more than one occasion.

I am very happy to report that the guns both look and feel incredible, from the recoil to the aesthetics, meaning the combat feels fluid and very satisfying. The guns look, sound and feel fantastic with brilliant recoil and feedback; possibly some of the best gunplay I've seen in a game that I would be willing to put on a par with Hunt: Showdown, and the enemies all react in a very satisfying way that really emphasises the weight behind every carefully, or desperately aimed shot.

During my playthrough I came to see that Capcom has struck a very nice balance between the feel of both Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7; bringing back the attache case style inventory system (big hooray for the Inventory-Tetris OCD gamer like me), the merchant-style economy system of selling treasures for money to buy supplies, weapons and their upgrades along with the overall action of Resident Evil 4, whilst maintaining the first person perspective and atmosphere of Resident Evil 7 and, whilst you are still very much at risk of running out of ammunition if you don't properly aim your shots and get too trigger happy (also much like in 4), the ammunition you find and the materials you need to craft it are plentiful enough that you should rarely find yourself in a situation where you're having to count every single bullet; leaving you much more at liberty than in the previous game to enjoy blowing that wolf man's head into meaty chunks with the hefty shotgun you spent all that sweet, hard earned dosh upgrading; go on, treat yourself!

The puzzles, sadly, are kind of a neutral point for me, never really complex or imaginative enough to make them all that memorable but not exactly stuff you could do with your off-hand pinkie whilst fast asleep either.

So, all that being said, here is that overhanging caveat I mentioned earlier, and that is the overall length of the game. As much of a life-long fan of Resident Evil I am, and despite the wonderfully put together experience that is Capcom's latest entry into a series I've adored since childhood, I can't help but feel a bit stung that I paid £50 GBP for a game that I completed in around 7 hours and 40 minutes, Resident Evil title or not, and that was at a fairly steady pace, taking the time to explore the places I was in, looking for stray items etc.

I have no doubt that more will be added with future DLC, and I look forward to that, but considering the asking price for the amount of game that is currently there, the thumbs up I give in this review should really only apply to the hardcore fans of the series who want to see how the story has progressed since their foray in Louisiana and those, like me, who just really love Resident Evil.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
Coming off the heels of Resident Evil 7, arguably the best in the franchises history, Resident Evil: Village has a lot to live up to. It almost entirely succeeds, blending the action-sensibilities from RE4 (and a small bit of RE5), with the horror and general feel/gameplay of RE7. I'd argue that the middle section of the game is the weakest point, but the very strong beginning and almost-as-strong ending work to offset this feeling very well.

[h1]Here's the good, and the bad:[/h1]

[b][u]The Good:[/u][/b]

[list]
[*]The graphics are phenomenal. The ray-tracing isn't what I'd call cutting-edge or jaw-dropping, but it's a very tasteful implementation that gives the lighting just enough…pizzazz? My favorite is the diffuse lighting coming through lacy white curtains in the mansion.
[*]Character models are the best in the franchise. RE7 had some weird models in my opinion, but this one does a much better job in this department, though the hair leaves a fair bit to be desired.
[*]The performance is fantastic. Though I'm running on very good hardware (AMD 5600 & RTX 3080), I'm able to max all settings at 1440p and get solid 90-115fps in-game. I've also noticed that it seems to run very well on dated hardware as well, which not many games seem to pay attention to anymore, so big plus(es) here.
[*]The level designs/layouts are AMAZING. The mansion(s) and houses and village are all so well laid out and there's so much attention to detail in the decoration and texturing.
[*]The gun upgrade system and weapons you get to use give a great sense of meaningful and well paced progression.
[*]The variety in environments that you visit is incredibly well done. Each area has it's own unique theme.
[/list]

[b][u]The Bad:[/u][/b]

[list]
[*]In general, the pacing of the story feels a bit off, sort of stop-and-go sometimes. Not the worst I've seen, but it could have used a little more TLC. Most notably, the period between the first 1/3 of the game and the last 1/3 of the game feels very quick, but then the last 1/3 of the game feels much longer than the rest of it.
[*]The horror aspects of RE8 took much more of a backseat to the action, and in my opinion, to it's detriment. Something closer to RE7 in terms of horror would have been appreciated, though that all said, what RE8 does, it does well.
[*]Sometimes the game does a poor job of informing you that things you have are important. At one point you'll be able to kill animals and get their meat, but the game doesn't make it abundantly clear that you shouldn't sell that, which can cause some frustration potentially.
[*]It's a bit disappointing that (as far as I could tell), it would be physically impossible to obtain and upgrade every gun in the game on the first playthrough. Some I were really looking forward to that I just barely ever got to use.
[/list]

I was both skeptical and hopeful about this game. I am happy to say that Capcom really outdid themselves with this installment.

Village is a perfect mix between action and horror. Personally, I would have liked for there to be more puzzles involved, but it's not a great loss. The crafting is fun and not particularly unfair. If you take note to try to move around to avoid attacks and use guard, you'll never want for first aids. I never felt like I was running out of bullets etc (keep in mind I played on standard difficulty). 

The enemy design was interesting, the maps are well sized. Though some areas were considerably smaller than others, it never felt like a part was too short, or that a particular boss/area outstayed its welcome.

It is clear that Capcom devs wish to move the franchise away from the main established protagonists (Chris, Claire, Leon, Jill, etc), perhaps to have more freedom to create new characters with new stories, and honestly, so long as they keep on making games like this, or even better, then its okay. [h1] Resident Evil: Village (2021) [/h1]

Resident Evil: Village (2021) is the 8th installment in the Resident Evil series, following the events of Resident Evil 7 (2017) that holds the game three years later. The protagonist, Ethan Winters, is settling among Europe with his family, Mia Winters, and his newborn baby, Rosemary Winters, being supervised consistently by Chris Redfield to further protect the family. Ethan is presumed to be caught off-guard and to further endure his survival and well-being to save and rescue Rosemary Winters from a altered and transformed village society that has been consumed by the evils of leaders among the isolated society. 

[h1] Advantages - Vitality of the Winters Family [/h1]

Resident Evil: Village (2021) brought the ties of Resident Evil 7 (2017) with reappearing game mechanics from the 2017 title into the 2021 title. The game graphically is amazing, while performance is also well-balanced throughout the game. The game also has a mixture of the classics of Resident Evil 4 (2005), while preserving a merchant into the game, the Duke, which you can exchange, buy, do small quests, and be your very own chef with unique benefits, the Duke also intertwines within the plot of the game, which is considerably a cool aspect. Gameplay wise is considerably fun, engaging, and bosses can be difficult among difficulties. 

[h1] Disadvantages - End of the Winters Family Era [/h1]

Resident Evil: Village (2021) has left us in a dark spot, while having Capcom confirm that it's the end of the Winters Family story branch with no indications of another possible installments or hints for another game. The game overhaul seems [i] less [/i] frightening compared to Resident Evil 7 (2017) which holds the behemoth of horrors. In the later parts of the game, you will encounter Alcina Dimitrescu, or Lady Dimitrescu, a inspired vampire within the castles, is [i] not [/i] really a good stalker enemy, compared to Jack Baker in Resident Evil 7 (2017) that inspired everyone's dreams and thoughts of horrors. 

While Resident Evil: Village (2021) is not a bad predecessor, it still serves and concludes the Winters Family saga unfortunately, but brings many feelings back comparing to the other Resident Evil games, including Resident Evil 7 (2017), which successfully tied the story and to further continue it to another level.

It's a pretty damn great game, i honestly wasn't all that hyped for RE8 so my expectations were rather moderate since even though i am a huge RE fan and RE7 was a solid fun game on its own i just didn't really get into it all that much compared to other RE games before the 7th and post 7, heck i only beat RE7 once and never had the desire to go through it again unlike other REs (NOT 6!) which I'd always beat at least 3 or more times or in the case of RE4 like 20 times now in my life probably.

So when i heard that the next numbered game will again feature Ethan and again be first person i was feeling kinda eh about it but it ended up surpassing my expectations, RE8 is a lot more enjoyable than 7 and has a lot better replay value too thanks to Mercenaries being back and the fact the game has basically the merchant and upgrading system from RE4 so multiple runs are needed to fully pimp up all your gear and unlock some hidden things to fool around with for future runs.

Only major weak point I'd fault the game for is one of the areas near the end, it's not much of a spoiler, it's yet again a factory/industrial area with a lab hidden inside of it too, bleh, compared to the rest of the game that had a fantastic village,forest  and castle environment , it kinda blows having to go through that part near the end. It's the same fault every RE game has, one of or the last environments you get to spend your final hours in are just not great. 

Exactly kinda like how in RE4, in which the final area was an industrial island with a hidden lab and it was the weakest part of the game, with the village and castle being the best bits and yes, this game is basically Resident Evil 4 Electric Bogaloo two but in first person. Granted RE4 is still the far better game but RE8 still did a great job trying to mimic that RE4 experience while also doing one thing somewhat better-ish than RE4 and that's feeling more like a horror game however It's not really that scary apart from a few given moments. This is still very much an action game with the horror being more of a well made decoration to set the atmosphere and tone, something which RE4 kinda under delivered with since that game had a far larger focus on just being over the top action which it did rather well. Basically what I'm saying is, RE8 creates a spookier tone than the RE it's mimicing however it's very much still just an action game with the horror being set-decoration.

Visually the game looks pretty fantastic, it runs somewhat worse than RE2 Remake,RE3 Remake and RE7 but that's because it does have some far more detailed and larger environments to handle, granted it still runs fine, i get an average of 70-100 fps, versus the 100-120 fps I'd get in the other titles (i got an RX 580 8GB and a Ryzen 3700x).

Game length is 10 hours, give or take on what kind of player you are. I often went back to older areas to unlock previously locked places and hunted for treasures though it seems i missed a thing or two by the end, so someone who might not do that and just rushes can probably beat it in like 6-8 hours in their first run.
I beat it on Standard, which offered a decent-ish challenge but could've used honestly more unf, i died thrice but that was due to me messing up in a few key linear scene moments where you die instantly if you don't follow or do the exact thing the game wants you, like having to go a specific corner to not get turned into minced meat, so yeah not a single death during actual regular combat. Ammo felt a bit scares at a few periods but more often than not i found myself easily loaded with enough to fight anything in my way really, as long as you're even average at aiming you'll be able to save up on ammo pretty well, so maybe consider making your first run be on Professional perhaps though the downside of doing your first run on pro is that enemies become notably more bullet spongy in the early parts when you don't have many upgrades. However Standard still does offer enough of challenge during your first experience to not get boring at all. 

So yeah, game's pretty good and i'm already gonna start my 2nd run now soon on a harder difficulty, if you liked RE7 then you'll like this even more and if you really disliked the move to first person and a lot of focus being on the new character Ethan than, this might just change your feelings about that since "I" who wasn't into RE7 all that much ended up enjoying this first person RE venture a lot more and even ended up liking Ethan more than in RE7, it also does a great job of explaining at the end some oddities that always bothered me in the previous game and even during this one but i better not say anything more otherwise I'll spoil the surprise.

This is pretty much Resident Evil 4's sequel. There are a lot of homages and the general feel of the game practically emulates it, so I'd definitely recommend playing 4 first if you can and are willing to wait a bit longer to dive into this title.

Gotta start this off by saying that the lack of FoV options is inexcusable. There are mods out there to increase it (I didn't use any) but this needs to be a built-in feature for the sake of comfort for players. Get it together Capcom

The RE engine is producing its best graphics yet and they're ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. I had to stop and just appreciate the visuals and atmosphere every few seconds, I was constantly blown away. There has been a lot of love put into every environment - they're all very unique and are chock-full of detail with impeccable lighting, even in some distant areas and even in small rooms that have little purpose. Everything feels real. It's a shame that the photo mode feels quite limited, but it is what it is. Performance was great for me (GTX 1080Ti) but when I closed the game and re-launched it, the game would run at 20fps with slowdown. A system reboot would cause this issue to vanish until the next time I re-launched the game.

I started on hardcore and hit a wall very early on. And from reading forums discussing the game, it seems like a lot of people had the same issue. After a lot of attempts I had to bump it down to standard difficulty which is a shame because I prefer these games on hard to give me a more survivalist experience. However, I still had an absolute blast with it. I found it very easy, but loved the ride of gunning down enemies since that was its focus. Apparently after this wall, the rest of the game is perfectly fine on hardcore, so in hindsight it may have been better for me to push through and keep trying. There is a cheese tactic out there if you wanted to basically skip it too

Despite this focus on action, it's still surprisingly very tense throughout. Being in tight rooms with the sounds of monsters seemingly all around you is very nerve-wrecking, with my frantically looking back and forth to prevent myself from getting jumped. One part of the game in particular is very creepy and very ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. And I absolutely loved it and would have loved to have seen more areas like it.

I found each area of the game to be good in its own right, and more or less avoided the classic RE trope where the first area is the best, and the end of the game gets pretty bad. So props to them for that. Backtracking and obtaining treasures never felt like much of a slog since the world is fairly condensed and laid out pretty well too.

Mercenaries mode is something I've wanted back for a long time and I've always been a big fan of the mode. It's incredibly fun with great music and some very good replay value. However, there are only 4 levels, with these levels being repeated again but with a smaller arsenal choice (hope you like using the first handgun) and you have much less health. I'm not really a fan of how these levels work, and getting a high score to unlock a special weapon in these levels isn't something I'm particularly thrilled about either.

First Things first: if u were expecting mommy milker lady to be the main villain...boy do I have a spoiler for you x.x

Graphics: 
Beautiful, photorealistic graphics, I highly recommend you use a 3080 or 90 (I'm a 3080 user) if u can get your hands on a decent one (AKA not that ZOTAC poop). The game for some reason at times tried to show me a slideshow of Ethan shooting lycans, but the fix was easy (turning off raytracing, I know, it hurts, but the game still looks almost as beautiful, like 99.6% if what it was). Either way, you can't exactly experience jiggle physics, but you can still get choked by the beautiful Alcina Dimitrescu (said "Dimetrece") and her "daughters" who look pretty fly.

Controls: 
The controls are just about the same as any other FPS out there, and relatively similar to those of RE7. At times, when prompted to grab items from the floor, I would usually spam my F key with the same frustration as I did in my first rocket league match (pls dont judge). The controls are unresponsive at times, even when attempting to shoot lycans or the moroaica my gun wouldn't fire. However I'd rather blame it on my mouse than on the game itself. The only real criticism I got here is that the buttons you press to open the map, inventory and books/readables are all different keys, and each one of these sections is, therefore, separate from one another, which I found quite annoying, mostly when I was being chased by the creatures in Castle Dimitrescu.

Gameplay: 
Very straightforward: Aim(if head)+Shoot= Very good;
Aim(if body)+Shoot(if early in the game)= Good
Loot Room(if red)+Drank coffee before playing= Profit
---//---
Aim+shoot=Ammo waste; therefore: Very good or good= ammo waste
Notice: Ammo is not really a problem, I just wanted to make it a bit more logical.
There are a lot of interesting mechanics I do not want to spoil as they came as a bit of a surprise for me, but always check your surroundings for items, as every single building has its own short story or something to learn with. Gun are smooth to use, well animated, with interesting attachments that improve them in some capacity. There are not as many instances in which you feel like going on a wild goose chase, but the ones that are can prove themselves as tedious as they are profitable from. These usually end up with you getting some sort of treasure or useful item for you to sell to the Duke (whose innability to call me a stranger was rather surprising, much like the time he asked me what I was buying). 

Story: 
I don't want to touch this point for too long, as I intend to keep this as spoiler-free as possible, but here it goes:
1. Rosemary is the baby
2. Not everything is what it seems, also mommy milkers

Resident Evil Village was a ride, from start to finish. It mixes survival horror and action-packed scenes extremely well, with a serviceable plot and really fun gameplay. Mind you, it is  not the most innovative game out there. If you are looking for a horror game with mind-twisting mechanics or a deep and complex narrative, by all means, stay away from this game.

What you will find here is more of the same. But it is an intense, captivating, thrilling experience nonetheless.  The shooting is great, the exploration is FANTASTIC, I never enjoyed back-tracking so much. The map design is outstanding, everything is properly connected and every new tool you get allows you to find more secrets and rewards.

The plot follows from RE 7, with Ethan Winters being the protagonist once again. Not only his quips are really funny, but he now appears as a driven and compelling character. Fortunately, Capcom took the opportunity this time to flesh out Ethan a little more, something that he desesperately needed in the previous game. The rest of cast is really interesting too (the tall vampire mommy gf included) although they dont really have a lot of time to shine in the spotlight. Despite all that, I believe the duration of this is more than fine, wrapping up nicely and setting everything up for a new game in the series!

The first half of this game is a true horror and design masterpiece. 10/10. It can't be faulted. It will go down in video game history as a legitimate testament to the medium.

After that, it gets quite a bit more action-oriented, more about combat and weapons etc- however, it is still incredibly good, and it never really sacrifices the horror and tension for the combat side of things for any longer than a short time at most.

*Nothing* in this game feels cheap. Everything has a very high level of polish and you can tell that everything was designed with a lot of testing and thought involved. Each and every section of the level has amazing detail, interactions and graphical fidelity.

The story is really enjoyable. If you are a fan of the RE-series and the previous games, you will most likely enjoy this one. Without revealing any spoilers, the return of Chris is great and I think that the development of Mia and Ethan's story in this game is also really well done. The character designs here are some of the most creative and unique we have ever seen in the RE franchise.

It is hard to find any real complaints. Obviously there *should* be an FOV slider included at launch. I think that launching a game without one of these in 2021 is completely crazy and ludicrous. I played through almost the entire game using the community-made FOV mod and I had no problems. Another slight complaint I have is that some of the boss-type enemies feel quite damage-spongy. This might just be a problem with my combat approaches, though. I played on Standard difficulty.

Overall, definitely give this game a go if you are a fan of horror, Resident Evil, and good stories. You won't be let down.

RE Village has its moments, but there just isn't enough here to love. 

It has RE4's action focus with a lot of enemies, some bosses, and a merchant that lets you sell treasure and buy upgrades. Other times its puzzles, very scripted, slow paced horror nonsense reminiscent from RE7; that slows the pace down and will make replays dull.

I'm shocked Capcom felt confident to emulate a lot of RE4 but couldn't bring over the same satisfying combat as well; because the shooting in RE8 is pretty abysmal. 

- Movement is too slow and restrictive for a game that sometimes throws a handful of fast moving enemies that take up your entire screen. 
- FOV is too narrow to even get an idea whats happening around you most of the time.
- Weapon sounds are underwhelming and lack punch.
- Enemies have barely any hit reactions, so Its like I'm shooting with a pellet gun. 
- Didn't take the opportunity to add evasive moves, grab counters, melee attacks, etc to flesh out the combat potential. 

I see no benefit to the first person view when it comes to the combat. The camera and movement are better suited for a slow paced horror game; with some enemies and arenas that would benefit if the combat was faster paced and snappy like action RE games. It just doesn't match well at all; Village is two types of games being forced into each other.

Even with the underwhelming combat, the middle section of the game is still great fun. I had a lot of enjoyment upgrading and getting most of the treasures. RE games shine when the player is left to their own pace. Little cutscenes, little dialogue, you are immersed in the gameplay loop and exploration. However it will probably take you about 8 hours to beat the game, so that middle section feels a bit too brief sadly; the game overall feels like it ended too quickly. 

If I can sum up the experience it would be very fun in some places, but overall forgettable. Nothing really happens that's worth talking about. Story is lackluster, characters are underdeveloped/forgettable, music is serviceable, tone has no consistency, voice acting is hit or miss, combat lacks depth, and too many scripted parts for my liking. 

If the combat was much more fleshed out, and if Village was a little longer to accommodate that, than maybe the gameplay would be able to support the game on its own.

I still wanna play more to see what the game offers, or at least to make the most out of the purchase. However the lack of depth in the gameplay and just thinking about replaying some of the slow portions sounds like a chore already. 

RE Village doesn't know what it wants to be. Its a bootleg version of RE4 and its not exactly a great horror game either. It borrows from so many games that in the end it has little of its own identity.

If you insist on getting it, get it on sale.

[h1]Summary:[/h1]Resident Evil Village continues Ethan’s story from VII, it offers similar structure and gameplay as well as a fresh new setting. For better or for worse it is exactly what you would expect from the newer RE-titles. If you like crazy horror imagery, exploration, light puzzle-solving, slow-paced survival FPS gameplay, and a story that makes no sense, this is about as good as it gets. The whole game took me about 9 hours to complete without using guides, I visited most areas but did in no way 100%.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Presentation - [/b]The game just looks great. The aesthetic feels fresh for the series and there is a ton of visual variety, more than in previous games. Each area has its own identity and is full of tiny details. You can tell that every corner of the map is hand-crafted. It runs very well and I encountered no visual glitches, stutters or bugs.
[*][b]Setting and characters - [/b]The village and its inhabitants are interesting and offers a lot of intrigue. Every character is incredibly well modeled, textured, animated and voice-acted.
[*][b]Combat - [/b]Compared to the other RE-games, this combat is the chunkiest by far. Enemies are less bullet spongey (but still sponges nonetheless) and weapons have higher impact. Enemies hit hard but you can move out of the way or block to reduce damage, making combat slow and methodical.
[*][b]Exploration - [/b]There is a lot to find around the village; for example:  ammo, consumables, crafting materials, permanent upgrades, collectibles and lore. The map is closely knit and there will be some backtracking in order to find everything. Finding keys that lead to somewhere new that in turn gives a new lead to follow.
[*][b]Bat-sh!t story - [/b]The story goes all out for better or for worse. There are a lot of surprises and there are a lot of interesting plot points. The story pulls no punches and it goes all over the place.
[/list]

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Bat-sh!t story - [/b]But, the story makes no friggin sense whatsoever! There are so many contradictions, plot holes and internal inconsistencies that everything falls apart as soon as you start thinking about it. Characters act in whatever way is most convenient for the plot in that second and can flip flop motivations in the matter of seconds. The whole horror-setting makes no sense if you remember that this is in essence a sci-fi story but there are frequent uses of basically magic, that is that offhandedly explained away as something completely non-magical in a way that does not really make sense or is in any way interesting. Just make the series actually occult you cowards! No more evil science bullcrap!
[*][b]Pacing - [/b]The beginning is quite slow and has a few false starts. The pacing is either too slow or too fast. It seems like nothing is happening for a long while and then it rushes through several major story beats.
[*][b]Crafting - [/b]Even though RE-games has always had crafting, it has never been that deep. And this game has the shallowest crafting system yet. Many ingredients only have one use and there is seldom meaningful overlap between recipes meaning that there are no interesting decisions in how to use your resources, just craft whatever you can and you will be fine. No more holding out for red herbs in order to make better healing
[*][b]Collectathon - [/b]There is a lot to collect and there is hardly any point to it. I make it through the game without being even slightly thorough and I never ran out of ammo, healing or money. I had several upgrades left to buy, but I managed fine without them. It just felt like most of the rewards were insignificant.
[*][b](Lack of) Inventory management - [/b]You have limited inventory space, but I was never more than half-way full. There was even at least one more inventory upgrade I never got. Crafting materials and plot items do not take up any space so left is weapons and ammo which remains quite static throughout the game. No need to make tough decisions about what to keep or if you should combine items to save space.
[/list]

When I first played Resident Evil 8, I actually enjoyed it quite a bit. But after letting it sit with me for a few years, I’ve come to see it as one of the weaker entries in the series.

It’s not without its strengths—there are some genuinely memorable moments that still stand out. However, the game often feels like a diluted imitation of Resident Evil 4 rather than its own distinct experience. Those RE4-inspired segments overshadow the good parts and drag the overall game down.

On top of that, the story is a bit of a mess, and I don’t feel it does the series’ lore or characters justice.

Overall, it ends up being one of the weaker RE titles for me. Instead of delivering something fresh, it feels like they tried to make RE4 2.0. I can’t quite give it a thumbs down—I still recommend it, just not very strongly.

[h1] Absolute... MASTERPIECE! [/h1]
[b]I expected this game to be absolutely awesome. I don't say this often, but I was wrong. In the end, it exceeded my expectations BY FAR and became probably the best game I've ever played (and I have played A LOT of games). This game has absolutely everything you would want and expect from a game with rating like this. [/b]

You are never bored in this game, the first playthrough will keep you tense through the entire game. There are some really scary parts (don't trust those people who say there's no horror here) and some action oriented parts with perfect balance between each other. The replayability of this game is almost infinite, as you will always come upon something you have missed the last time. I am personally doing my 4th playthrough at the time of writing this review and there's atleast one more I'm planning in the near future. There's also mercenaries mode that's really fun and takes some time to master in order to get the best scores. The visuals are undoubtedly a sight for sore eyes with incredible details and effects. I can only recommend using the photo mode, as it's an endless source of awesome wallpapers.

The characters are really deeply elaborated and in the end, you'll end up liking all of them. In my opinion, this game has no villains, just victims. The main character also got an incredible character developement since RE7, when he was just a regular nobody. The exactly same thing goes for the story, which is just breathtaking. 

You'll feel fear, you'll feel anger, you'll feel remorse and there's no doubt you won't be able to hold tears after everything is over.

Out of all AAA games, you'll never regret paying full price for this one. The rating for me would be at least 15/10.

Whatever this project was meant to be, the result is far from a Resident Evil game.
It looks great and sounds great, it has an impressive atmosphere; astounding, beautifully crafted environments and grotesque creatures, but the frightening and scary aspects are completely gone now and got replaced with disgust and sickening feelings at best.
The gameplay is alright, not much new on that part, but ultimately - in my opinion - the whole package is a strong departure from the franchise.
RE7 was excellent, it sported the classic RE vibe and at the same time, it managed to gently innovate on it.
Village on the other hand, took this too far, and ended up being a hybrid of many other games, such as the later Wolfenstein(s), Call of Duty, The Evil Within, Dark Souls, etc, all that sprinkled with a touch of RE essence.
I went in with adjusted expectations, but as a RE fan, I still got disappointed.
Story-wise, the returning characters were cool, likeable, but the new characters didn't really manage to get my attention. They were mediocre at best, and to be perfectly fair I couldn't care less about who is who, other than Miranda. It would have been interesting to know a bit more about her though, but there wasn't much of an opportunity for that.
I'm not exactly fond of how this story played out. Instead of building on the past and evolving towards the future, it was a case of taking the past and twisting it.
The ending was surprising but also kind of underwhelming. The way it wrapped up seems to be a glimpse into the conflict of the unknown.
Either way, the game is a decent experience, no complaints about that, just not in traditional RE ways. It's not unique anymore.

I would definitely recommend this. I was reluctant to bother with this after the shameless cash-grab that was the Resident Evil 3 Remake, but I can assure anyone wondering it IS worth getting.

Pros:
- Length: It took me roughly 9 hours-ish to complete thoroughly hunting for secrets and there's still the mercenaries mode to do.
- Sounds: Weapons are punchy, ambience is great, what more do I have to say?
- Graphics: Graphics are very nice, not the best out there but far from the worst.
- Weapons: There is a decent roster and with the weapons mods in the game the weapons themselves actually change how they look and operate which is neat.
- Performance: I have a mid range PC now and the game ran far better than I thought it would, frames dropped in certain instances (flies in face - people who have experienced it know what I'm talking about) but ran smoothly apart from that.
-Scenery: The settings of the game is quite varied with each area having it's own unique feel and some parts look downright beautiful.

Cons:
- Sounds: Although the sounds are great I found that pinpointing enemies via my headset was very hit and miss, enemies can sound like they're right on top of you when they are several meters in front, making it difficult to get the drop on them at times.
- Combat: When I started Resi 8 combat felt awkward to get used to, it was only after I realised that acceleration is on by default that I transformed from a no-fingered man into Mr. Marksman himself. My advice? TURN IT OFF. Combat was instantly easier after this. I feel the worst issue plaguing this game in the combat category is how resilient enemies are, even the generic ones are bullet sponges. I was on 'Casual' (normal) on my first run and enemies were still taking 7+ headshots to kill even with the game's most powerful handgun nearly full upgraded. This wouldn't be such an issue if enemies didn't move so erratically making  headshots difficult in a game where  ammo can be scarce.
- FOV: Everyone's favourite complaint and a valid one at that, the FOV is atrocious in this game and there's no way to fix it. This ties in with combat problems as enemies can be stood just off to the side of you and you'll never see them, allowing them to get a cheap free hit.
- Crafting: The crafting system returns from Resi 7 and is one of the features that I have the greatest issue with. The game THROWS crafting components at you in the first couple of hours of the game and then barely any towards the end. Compacting this issue is when you actually need to use the crafting system (I didn't for two thirds of the game) you run out of your hoarded crafting components EXTREMELY quickly. The game then starts throwing poultry amounts at you giving you just enough healing/ ammo to get out of your current scrape but nothing left over afterwards making the next encounter rough, I would have just preferred the ammo or health rather than components.
- Healing: A minor gripe, but the game is so stingy giving out healing items it can hurt. Just before the last boss of the game I had literally one healing item as my crafting supplies were done with!

Although I have listed negatives here the experience was great, A mix of Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7 and definitely worth the purchase.

[h1]Let's keep it simple: the game is a big thumbs up in terms of quality. The story, action, and survival horror elements are all there. If you liked Resident Evil 4 and VII, then you're going to like this too.  [/h1]

I took the long road on this game, creeping around and taking my time, so it took me about 16 hours to complete my first run. 

[b] Pros: [/b] 

- The first half of the game is very survival horror oriented where running is usually your best option and fighting can be difficult. 

- About 1/4 of the game is dedicated toward fighting monsters/bosses that you can't beat with guns. It's nothing too serious, but it can be a little frustrating to repeat those segments on replays. They're fun the first time through, but I can see them being a chore down the road. 

- The last 1/4 of the game is very action-oriented. If you're looking for a game with a big finale... this should do. 

- The story is actually pretty good and focuses on the Winters' family, with some a few predictable twists and at least one very NOT predictable, which comes in early in at the end of the first quarter is absolutely fantastic. That hook had me racing to get to each boss and to the end of the game! 

- The Vendor is back! Weapons, upgrades, crafting recipes... he's got a bunch of great stuff, so if you are hurting for a particular item, you may have options. 

[b] CONS: [/b]

- The Vendor is back! Yes... it's also a bit of a con, since we don't really get a story on the guy and he's actually a bit of a character throughout the game. Also, I liked RE 7's crafting and upgrade system, (you just find the recipes and upgrades), so going back to the RE 4 upgrading of weapons was a bit of a bummer. I'm in the game more for the story and survival, not to be a treasure hunter. 

- Super cheap jump-scares. There's a particular enemy type that hides in the ground that has no indicator. I found that to be pretty cheap. 

- Puzzle boss/Invincible boss. This is mostly something that just kind of annoys me, personally... I'm not a fan of bosses you can't kill with bullets and explosives. Dying because something jumps out of a lake while you're crossing a bridge a second off the timing just pisses me off. 

[h1] Other than that, the game was blast! [/h1]

It was definitely a creepy game where I felt I got my money's worth for being scared and entertained!

Where can I start the over arching story is the great anchor for this title, You follow Ethan Winters, searching for his lost daughter. Throughout the story many obstacles try to stop Ethan in his rescue mission, 4 houses stand in his way, and each house brings new obstacles and challenges to overcome. 

Everyone's favourite 9 ft vampire lady, brings a Gothic chase around her perfectly crafted castle, while Ethan searches for answers, Lady Dimitrescu poses as a Mr X figure, she will follow you around rooms trying to end your existence. However I was a little disappointed at how little we got of her, although my experience with her was fun and heart pumping. 

The next place to search is the doll house of Donna Benevento, the ambience of this area is chilling, and creates great atmosphere to scare the player. Most of this place is psychological, and makes for a great section of puzzling while Ethan searches a doll of his dead wife Mia. Another chase sequence is excellent crafted and is played similar to Outlast, where Ethan is left defenceless while he hides from an attacking foe.

The next place to search is a giant lake, home to a creature called Moreau. Here the combination of puzzle solving and platforming across the lake to dodge a giant lake creature makes for another great change of pace. However if you're too slow, watch out for the water, because you will become fish food.

Last but certainly not least is Heisenberg's factory, the steampunk vibe, and Cybermen-like enemies make for a great new switch upto the game. You will have to be patient and precise to take down these enemies, as they only have small weak spots. The factory is surprisingly giant, many floors, are home to enemies, puzzles and great treasure for the merchant, this is culminates into one of the best boss fights of the franchise, it is fun, hilarious with the dialogue, and epic.

Resident Evil Village is the love child of RE7 & RE4. The chilling atmosphere and first person perspective of RE7, combined with the customisation, upgrade system, and treasures of RE4 make for a a brilliant open world experience. No longer is the lack of backtracking present like RE3R, you can explore previous areas for Special valuable treasure, which the merchant will purchase for a high price,and catch animals for food which you can cook into special recipes to increase health, guarding ability, and speed of Ethan.

This allows for variation in different playthroughs, maybe you want to go with no weapon upgrades, or maybe this time you want to upgrade your whole arsenal to destroy the many enemies varieties which are thrown your way. This is a massive improvement on the previous title, whereas RE7 has roughly about 4 enemies of moulded, RE8 has at least 10+, making how you approach each area different, and how you adjust to it exciting.

When completing the game you will be awarded with shop points for the challenges you have achieved in your playthrough. You will also unlock the hardest difficulty called Village of shadows, here your patience and skills will be put to the test. If you are brave enough and skilled enough to complete this feat, you will be awarded with lots shop points similar to RE3R, here you can buy Figurines, Concept Art, Infinite ammo weapons along with new weapons to enjoy in single player, and also the much wanted return of Mercenaries mode.

Overall In my opinion I would rate this game easily 10/10, this feels like an apology for the lack of content we received with RE3R, and also a beautiful passion project of the many developers who made this title, they clearly took inspiration from RE4 and threw all what was great into the fantastic RE- Engine, which yet again succeeded in bringing to life every horrible BOW this game has to offer. Please if you have the money, do yourself a favour, and buy this game, and invest at least a weekend into enjoying this title. Even if you haven't played RE7, which the developers acknowledge by giving you a short overview of Ethan recounting what previously happened, I would still recommend you buy this!
