Resident evil Village (8) is the next installment in the RE franchise and is the 2nd follow up game to Ethan Winters storyline (previous 7). 3 years after the events at the Baker house, Ethan finds himself in a small backwater decimated village in search of his just recently missing daughter, Rose. Ethan must fight off werewolves, zombies, and attractive vampire ladies.

First off I must say that hats off to CapCom for how well this game runs. I didn't experience a single problem until close to the very end when there were just so many enemies on the screen and my frames dropped. 
It's also incredible just how good this game looks and its not even that demanding in terms of hardware. 
The visuals and level detail are superb, and the audio is sooo good. Doors creaking, wind blowing windows, it's all so immersive. 

The gameplay is almost exactly the same as 7's. there's not too much for me to talk about there essentially. There's a a merchant now (Duke) who you can sell treasures to, and buy various things like ammo, lockpicks, herbs, and even upgrade your weapons. Duke was definitely a highlight, Ethans interactions with him after story mission stuff was pretty nice as it gave Ethan someone to vent too haha.

The story itself is ok. I know RE isn't renown for its storytelling so I don't expect much, just a serviceable one. I will say towards the end that the story gets a bit stupid stupid but oh well. Also to me personally it feels like Heisenberg's, (one of the villains) it feels like his level really drags, and his definitely one of the more frustrating parts of the game just because of the enemy types you are dealing with. 

It's also worth mentioning that Capcom did highly advertise the castle and Lady Dimitrescu and her daughters like they were gonna be main antagonist/setting of the game. This is not the case however. They are dealt with fairly early on in the game, as there are like 4 other main villains in the game besides them. So just be warned. 

Another con I would say is, no FOV slider on a pc port is criminal. Hopefully CC can patch one it but I doubt they will. I've seen people say they can't play the game cause of the motion sickness from it which really sucks. 

Overall RE Village I would say is another hit in the RE franchise, and I'm excited to see where it goes next. 
Would recommend picking it up.

This is really a Maybe rather than a no, but this game is a disappointment for me, and I came into this expecting maybe the BEST RE yet.  Instead all I can say is RUH ROH.

In before clowns leave jester emotes and so on, all because they can't handle someone didn't like their precious take on action RE and can't accept that liking this take on RE is entirely subjective. I didn't hate the game by the way, just found it OK. 

Story

I am not going to say much here, you already know the story if you have watched any footage, Ethan Winters is back and so is Chris, this time it’s personal (at least that is what they want you to think). The story progresses and while it does have some great highs, it also has some REALLY BAD LOWS. With the use of the umbrella logo and such in the trailers and demos, I expected some real deep dive into how umbrella came into existence, do not get me wrong you do find out the link, but it is incredibly underwhelming to say the least.  

I was expecting the story to really go places, and to be honest the ideas in my head make significantly more sense than what Capcom ultimately came up with. There was potential here for so many opportunities for future games set in the past and future, all of it is squandered for what frankly feels pointless and I can honestly say based on the ending I am out when it comes to RE9. RE7 felt like RE was getting back on track and onto something old yet new, but RE has lost its way more than ever with RE8. The final act, as per RE tradition really falls apart, but it wouldn’t be RE without that. It’s just if anything, it falls apart more than normal.

Graphics

Yes, this is a cross gen game, but thanks to RE engine’s great IQ and clean renderer the game is stunning, even sexual to look at times.  The ray tracing is incredibly minimal, but it does add to scenes, especially inside and elevates the game, even if not by as much as one may hope. The overall visual package is a significant step up and the loading stuttering inherent with RE engine is still present but reduced significantly. Overall, I think RE8 artistically is a fantastic game, and while it is ultimately a cross gen game, thanks to all the techniques built upon from RE7 it is still good looking.

Gameplay

This is where the game really falters. In ways it feels better than RE7 for sure, it feels refined, movement feels better, sound is overall improved, animations are solid. However, the guns, which you will be using a lot as this is what I would call an Acton RE, lack feedback, visually and sound. Knockback on enemies from the enemies feel lacking, the guns don’t feel like they have any weight to them, it’s serviceable and good enough, but it sticks out, this is something that should have been a priority for improvement it however is not.

On the action front, this is one of the things that makes the game feel very odd, it has its moments, but it feels like a slow action RE, there are a lot of lulls, and even when things do get going it feels more like RE2 encounter wise for the most part.

I think this may ultimately be the tone in these moments, others may feel different but for me there seems to be a miss match of tone and what you are doing. It is a mish mash of action and horror, but it does not feel like it quite gels most of the time.

This leads me onto the biggest problem of the game. The game is very varied and some of it works, some of it does not, the problem is it never stays with any of these long enough to build on them as soon as it feels it is getting started it is already over. Even lady Dimitrescu does not stay around for long, which really surprised me, if anything she is relegated to an inferior MR X mechanically, and story wise it feels like there should have been much more from her and others.  

The game feels like a compilation of the last 7 REs (yes even 6, there is a tank). It is an RE mash up good and bad, but without focusing on anything for long enough. This ultimately makes it worse than 7, and with its pacing issues, I am not actually sure where I would place it in a list of REs best to worst.  

Sound

Overall, the use of sounds environmentally and everything excluding the guns (which are good but not great), is high quality and used to great, even phenominal effect with their surround sound solution on, however I am in an odd situation here as someone who has listened to the game on PS5 and PC. The mixing and overall quality on PS5 seems higher than that of the PC version. I have had to turn my amp up way higher to hear the environment on PC and the sound quality sounds more compressed and overall worse.

I have played most of the Resident Evil Games now; Only main line entry games I haven't touched are 6, 0 and the original 2 and 3.

This is my personal opinion (for some people they won't like this game) but for me, it is the best Resident Evil game to date. There are many flaws with this game, but what Resident Evil game doesn't. It isn't the scariest game but for me it is the most consistent, the characters are amazing, it is well paced and the story is the most intriguing thing since 2 and 3. Some won't call this a Resident Evil game because it doesn't have your normal zombie enemies, but Resident Evil isn't about zombies, it is about bio-weapons that have been released into the public which have caused people to mutate into terrifying creatures.

Many compare this game to Resident Evil 4 and call it a spiritual sequel; I 100% agree with that but in some ways this game, in my opinion, does things better than what 4 and 7 did, such as the returned inventory management from 4 and the much improved gameplay from 7. 

However, before you play this game, you should play 7 as this is a direct sequel to that game and some things in this game tie in with its predecessor. There will be story beats that will somewhat confuse you if you haven't played 7.

Now onto the Pros and Cons:

Pros:
- The Graphics are beautiful, one of the best looking games this generation.
- The gameplay is fantastic, never gets old or boring.
- Lots of enemy types compared to 7.
- Most of the Boss fights are well made, with the exception of 1 (I won't spoil which one)
- The characters are perfectly made for this type of game.
- The atmosphere is so immersive, I forgot I was playing a game sometimes.
- The setting of the Village is in my top 3 RE settings.
- It correctly blends the horror and action elements together.
- The last hour of the game.
- The music is the best it has been in a RE game.

Cons:
- There is one section of the game which felt a little rushed (You will know what I mean when you get to it).
- This might be a hardware issue for me, but I got a little stuttering when it came to some sections of the game (Don't take my word on this one, it could be different for you).
- The game doesn't really have many puzzles, its more collect this thing, to unlock said thing.
- Big Mummy Milkers isn't in the game that much (Although her presence is perfectly used; this is more of a joke con).
- Some enemies can get a little repetitive further into the game.

Although I have a lot of complaints, they didn't detract my love for this game, like I say this won't be for everyone but if you liked 7 and 4, then this will be right up your alley.

it took me around 12 hours to beat the game, it's about 1/3 longer than 7 so that should tell you if this time is worth your money. For me this game is 100% worth the price but for some the game might seem too short to justify its price.

My final verdict is if you are a massive Resident Evil fan then this is worth its full price, but if you are just trying to get into the series, then I would recommend you wait for a sale or play 7 first and then come back to see if this will be up your alley.

This game draws on a lot of survival horror classics, such as RE4, Haunting Grounds, Silent Hill, and Kuon.  You might even extend its atmosphere to things like the Blair Witch (for occult themes) and Rise of the Tomb Raider (for the eastern European mountain-village setting).  RE7 is the narrative prequel and it's very similar in terms of gameplay as well as starring No-Face Ethan.  

I would argue that it's a really good survival horror game that balances quiet exploration and suspense with frantic action and horrific danger.  I would argue that, like RE7, it's a fantastic survival horror game.  I would argue also that, like RE7, it's not a great RE game, because it's just thematically too different and doesn't really seem to build on the lore enough to satisfy the lack of RE plot continuity since RE6 and Revelations 2.

Pros:  
+  Solid atmosphere and scare factor, with an appropriate use of tension and little in the way of cheap jumpscares.
+  Looks great.  But it's RE engine so yeah.
+  A fair bit of content and replayability.  Mercs mode unlocked by beating the game, and New Game +.
+  A lot more thought than you'd think went into the total game design, as noted by the Concept Art notes.
+  Really good use of treasure hunting and non-plot puzzles like RE4.
+  Some decent puzzles in general.
+  Ethan has a lot of established personality and feels less like a fill-in protagonist.
+  Extra content upon completion includes a LOT of figures (character models) and concept art.  Much more of both than previous titles.
+  A lot of good segments which require quick-thinking or cunning to bypass.  
+  The Village of Shadows cutscene, depicting a story being told to the baby Rose, has some stupidly good Coraline style design.
+  Chris Redfield has a chin again, and looks like he took his whey.

Cons:  (Most of these are nitpicks)
-  The bosses all have ridiculous banter made worse by its incessant nature and voice modulation.  It's just cringe-inducing.
-  The music is forgettable.  No really, I can't remember any of it.
-  Mercs is single player, first-person.  I was secretly hoping for a more classic Mercs with co-op enabled.
-  Lycans are a great early game enemy but become tedious later on and use cheap mob tactics with weapons to just make those segments a chore.  They're not an enemy majority but they are absolutely my least favorite overall.
-  Everyone in this unnamed Eastern European country speaks American English, except for Heisenberg who was taught English by a Dutch parrot.
-  This game continues the REmake traditions of common mooks being absolute bullet sponges.

This is a very good Resident Evil game that feels like a combination of RE 4 and RE 7. The controls are probably the best in the series, very smooth and intuitive.  The game's difficulty settings are great for those who want a challenge versus those who just want to experience the story.  There are enough traditional RE Style puzzles to make this feel like a proper experience despite the lack of traditional zombies.  

The bad is that game is very linear, with a lot of scripted events that will just happen regardless of what you do, but this is hardly new to RE games, so it is only a minor complaint.  The only other complaint I have is that the game just isn't that scary for a "survival Horror" game (With one exception) and RE7 definitely has it beat on that part.

The Story is... well ridiculous.  It's silly, over-the-top, cheesy and fun like all of the resident evil games (especially the later ones) tend to be. The villains are delightfully melodramatic, the voice acting is great and it would seem that the people making these characters come to life really had fun with it.  If you are looking for Resident Evil to provide you with award winning stories grounded in reality, then I do not know what to tell you.  The game is over-the-top and silly and was meant to be.

Resident Evil Village (RE8) is a direct sequel to Resident Evil 7 and a spiritual successor to Resident Evil 4. As it so happens to be, it is also a pretty fantastic game.

RE8 picks up a few years after the events of its prequel. One day while chilling at home, some “boulder punching ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” turns up and straight up murders Ethan’s wife. As if that wasn’t all, the muscular ape-creature also kidnaps him and his daughter. Now finding himself in a strange village, Ethan must go on a quest to save his missing daughter by killing a bunch of monsters.

The setting is immediately familiar to anyone who has played RE4 (with its castles and villages and whatnot). Many aspects of the gameplay have also been lifted from that game. You collect and combine treasures, upgrade your guns at a merchant and keep all your stuff in an attaché case (where [i]do[/i] they keep that by the way?).

The gameplay itself, however, should instead be familiar to anyone who has played RE7. The first-person perspective, the block button, and the way you move through the world is the same. Only this time, it’s much faster. Enemies are more aggressive, often come in large packs, and will weave and dodge your shots constantly. 

I know I bring up RE4 and RE7 a lot here, but that is honestly the best way to describe this game. It’s like a meticulously crafted love child between the two. It’s like RE4, but scarier. It’s like RE7, but with more enjoyable combat. Anyways, the list goes on—but how does the game stand up on its own?

RE8 carries on with the [b]story[/b] as told by RE7. The dialogue is campy, but at the same time, most of the characters feel a lot more “real” than they ever have before. There are some contrivances and convolutions in the scenario writing, but at the end of the day, the game just plays too well for it to detract from the experience. The story itself, while no masterpiece by any stretch of the imagination, is surprisingly engaging. There are enough twists and turns to keep you engaged to the end. RE8 also manages something that no other Resident Evil game has done before it (at least in my experience) by achieving a genuinely heartfelt and touching ending that feels like a proper conclusion to Ethan Winter's story. Then again, I don’t think you should play these games for the story, and RE8 is no exception.

The [b]gameplay[/b] is a rather standard affair for an FPS. What elevates it, is the environments and the well-balanced enemy encounters. While the enemy variety itself is low (still better than RE7), the weapons and locations are many and varied. The puzzle segments are fun enough (at least on a first playthrough) and mixes up the gameplay just the right amount. Bosses are about what you've come to expect from the series but are better than any of the fights in the RE3 remake (and even RE2, I would say). The expanded crafting system, while also pretty standard, adds some spice to the gameplay loop, while also incentivizing backtracking and exploration. You can also hunt animals to cook food, I guess.

The game took me roughly [b]8 hours and 30 minutes[/b] to beat on my leisurely first playthrough on the Village of Shadows (VoS) difficulty. That might seem short to some, but keep in mind that these games are meant to be played multiple times. Even then, this is rather lengthy for a Resident Evil game. I’d have to play through it again to be sure, but I didn’t feel any one particular area to be worse than the other in the usual Resident Evil fashion (where everything falls apart at the end). The game doesn’t feel quite as heavily scripted as RE7 (which made subsequent replays a slog to get through), but still has some railroad-y sections. The reintroduction of the in-game merchant and upgrade system makes new game+ very enticing. Also, mercenaries are back!

My [b]complaints[/b] with the game are relatively minor, and the first one stems solely from my decision to do a VoS playthrough on my first go. RE7’s “Madhouse” difficulty made for a stellar way to experience the game for the first time. The same cannot be said for VoS. Not only do we not get the ink ribbons, but the game is littered with checkpoints and autosaves—as such, dying never feels much like a threat and more like a nuisance. The bosses also become actual chores to kill. Not because they are unfair (you just have to learn and remember the patterns), but because they become bullet sponges. For real, one of the bosses took me almost 20 minutes(!?) to kill (with weapons upgraded). Sure, that’s with me conserving my valuable ammunition by sticking to my handgun and shotgun for the most part, but even then, that’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane.

Another flaw with the game regardless of difficulty level is the blatantly instanced nature of most of the encounters. I imagine this is something that becomes more apparent when you play on VoS where you actively try to avoid fighting—but enemies can (and will) de-spawn right before your eyes just by you walking into the next triggered event. The enemies are heavily restricted to which areas they can and cannot be in, which makes cheesing the game all too easy in many cases. In most areas of the game, enemies can easily (and repeatedly) be pulled to the threshold of their aggro range where they either stop dead in their tracks or start running back to their spawn point. This completely takes the tension out of many encounters when you realize it—and worse still, it even holds true for some of the game’s mini-bosses. Like, did no one playtest this? Is this intended? A game is going to be a game, I get it, but it kinda shatters the illusion when Ethan can obliterate an entire room of enemies by putting his hands on a door. There’s even some cutscenes in which NPCs literally de-spawn in front of your eyes as soon as the cutscene ends (no, a rickety door ridden with holes is not enough to hide the fact that the hag on the other side just popped out of existence mere moments after going through it). As I said, it wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t so blatantly apparent.

On a more technical level there's also the lack of a FoV slider, which is important to mention.

Buuut, with all that said I think RE8 is a pretty damned good game. The aforementioned flaws are my only real gripes with the game as of this writing. That, and maybe the slight overreliance on scripted events, which still isn’t as bad as it was in RE7. Sure, I’ve hardly analyzed the game to the fullest extent here, but I think the best praise I can give is that the game was a genuine blast to play from start to finish. In fact, this is probably one of the best single player experiences I’ve had in quite a while. It’s an improvement of RE7 in almost every aspect (unless you enjoy the horror components exclusively) and is worthy of being talked about in the same breath as RE4. Crazy, I know.

I've just finished my first playthrough of RE: Village.  I had a lot of trouble to begin with getting it to run (see original review below), and wish to preface this review with the caveat that you should remain wary if you are going to purchase before the first patches come out.  

This is especially important if you are using an RTX card and want to use the ray tracing.  It is bugged, and I needed to turn it off to let the game run without crashing.  I still suffered from stuttering, and occasional lag.  During the ending segments I needed to turn down the graphics somewhat as the stuttering kicked in too badly, accompanied by massive fps drops that turned it into a slide show.

That stuff aside, I absolutely loved this game.  I fully intend on playing it through again on the harder difficulty settings (first run was on Normal mode, which was somewhat challenging to me in places, but on the whole pretty easy), because it was a lot of fun.  

The environment designs are really impressive.  The puzzles are stupidly simple.  Some insultingly so.  There's all the classic Resident Evil stuff like needing keys, tank controls, a handful of collectables to smash, chase scenes, etc.  The scripted nature of it allows for some cool set pieces, but it will probably diminish replayability somewhat.

It took me about 11.5 hours to complete the campaign - but I was going real slow just to take in all the detail.  Someone good at fps games, and in a rush, could rattle through the campaign way faster than this.  I've seen complaints about it, but to be fair this is another RE staple.  

It's a mashup gameplay wise of RE 4 and RE 7.  I'm not going to give any of the story away, but I will say it ties things together quite nicely, even though in the beginning I was really confused as to how this was actually an RE game.  It is very much an action shooter with a survival horror theme, rather than an actual survival horror game.  It is pretty tense throughout, but with the exception of one moment, it is not frightening in the least.  Very campy Hammer Horror stuff all around.  That moment though, it caused a sense of dread in me that I've not felt since Silent Hill 1.  

Sadly that moment was all too fleeting.  Had they managed to create that sense of dread all the way through, or even just at many more points along the way, this would have been an incredible game for horror fans.  As it is it is still a really good time if this kind of thing tickles your fancy.  I don't want to give anything away though, so I'll leave it at that.

Thoroughly recommended, with the caveat that you should wait until they patch out the major problems people are currently having running it.

Was really looking forward to this but after finishing it once I have to say I'm a bit disappointed.
The premise seemed really interesting at first but the villains you have to fight were all kinda boring and killing them off seemed a bit rushed. You literally meet the three daughters of the big lady and the big lady herself and kill them in what feels like half an hour playtime. The other big enemies feel the same way. They are introduced and finished way too fast in my opinion. It also bothers me that they toned down the horror aspect in this game compared to the last. The only section that was somewhat unsettling was in the dollmaker's house. The monster baby's sound design was pretty awesome and the overall atmosphere was great. Would have loved to see more of that in the game. 
Gameplay felt alright, you now have a counter move after blocking an attack from basic enemies which can give you some free space. Weapons and gunplay are fine but nothing special. I did enjoy exploring the castle and village, unlocking doors with new keys and collecting treasures and such.
Storywise it is a bit of a letdown for me as well. Ethan is just a boring protagonist. Other main characters in the series weren't especially deep but they worked for what they are - cheesy action heroes - but Ethan isn't even that. He comes across as a normal dude in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up situation but he lacks any charismatic or over-the-top properties a Leon Kennedy or Chris boulder-punching Redfield had in previous titles. The explanation in the end on why Ethan is able to survive all of these injuries felt kinda unnecessary and out of nowhere. Chris's role in all this is weird too. He has yet another organization - the "Hound" group - and his previously found anti-bioterrorist organization BSAA is apparently now an enemy? It's just all presented very poorly in my opinion.
I am going to play it on another difficulty at some point to see how that changes things up, as Resident Evil games are known to do. All in all, I feel like the game tries to combine many things that made previous titles great but fails to do so. The action and gameplay is better in 4, the exploration is more satasfying in 2 and 2 Remake, the horror and villains are more effective in 7 and the story feels underwhelming.

This game combines the main innovative elements from both RE4 and RE7, and combines it like a nice sandwich. This title is heavily inspired by RE4 when it comes to the action, setting, briefcase inventory management, merchant, weapon attribute upgrades, and the lack of an item box. RE7's horror influences (and obvious first person camera) appear nicely as well throughout the game to try to keep you on your toes. I will say that at times it wasn't clear where to go next (specifically at the beginning of the game), and it lessened the tension I was probably supposed to feel when encountering things. I imagine playing on harder difficulties would make you worried more about dying, but possibly lessening the actual fear factor from enemies and areas at the same time since you're always alert. I could be wrong, but that's how I view it when playing. I would say the beginning where you arrive at the village was kind of weird and the least enjoyable part of the game for me, but its not terrible, and things pick up pretty quick and it just gets crazier and crazier as the game goes on.

As a fan who has played most of the Resident Evil games in the franchise, I felt that the game was very satisfying overall and it was done much better than I originally expected! You sorta get a taste of multiple Resident Evil games in one. The castle interior is sort of reminiscent to the mansion from RE1, the overall atmosphere (along with the castle exterior) reminds me of 4, first person from 7, references to previous games (like RE5 as an example), etc. For the most part, the game ran great, but had a few moments where frames would drop randomly during some cutscenes and sometimes when fighting the Dimitrescu vampire ladies. 

Overall, Resident Evil 8 was a very enjoyable experience, and I do recommend it to both new fans and old fans of the franchise. I hope this review was helpful to anyone on the fence about this game!

Spoiler-free pros and cons below.

PROS:
- Direct sequel to RE7 and expands the story in huge ways
- Has new and very impactful plot ties to the rest of the series
- Gameplay has a wonderful mix of mechanics from 7 and 4
- Longer than RE7 (Took me almost 13hrs vs the 7hrs it took me for RE7)
- The graphics are world class. Some of the best I have ever seen
- The game runs like butter (with a few minor exceptions). I average 80-100fps across the game on a Ryzen 5 2600 and GTX 1070 with everything cranked to max. RE engine is made of pixie dust.
- The enemy design is fantastic. They've finally ditched the "vague flesh monster" aesthetic and finally let the art team stretch their legs. Everything from the rank and file enemies to the big bosses are all so cool looking and not to mention actually terrifying. It's breath of fresh air for Resident Evil fans without straying too far from the visual identity of this series
- Same as above for the set design, too
- The game is just so fun from start to finish
- It's seemingly bug-free. Rare for a AAA release on day 1.

Cons:
- Minor FPS issues. There is 1 room in Castle Dimetrescu where my FPS locks to 30fps for no apparent reason. It fixes as soon as I leave the room. Some enemies will also drop your FPS for a second or two if you get hit, but it's not a big deal.
- The first half of the plot leaves you a bit confused and mildly frustrated at Ethan at points. Play to the end though. Trust me.
- No FOV slider. I personally think the default FOV works for the artistic intent of the game, but I understand this will make some people feel a bit sick particularly since it's a first person game.
- Cannot take charms off of your weapons without disabling them entirely in the game settings.
- Some puzzles are far too easy

Yes! Capcom nailed it again. Although I am a fan of the old franchise of Resident Evil games, I do appreciate the  renewal of the series. Resident Evil 7 was a fresh attempt to reboot Resident Evil with many nods and a few Easter eggs to the old series. This game follows that same approach as a direct sequel to RE7. It plays with the idea of vampires and werewolves rather than keeping the same formula of zombies and deadly bio weapons. But the horror is back at full force.

Yes, I know.. You are probably one of the persons who claim to never get scared of horror games and laugh at people who do. But try to border your windows with sheets to get a pitch black room, use headphones with 7.1 surround sound at a relatively high volume and obviously do it all alone. Do that instead of playing the game in a public cafe with your whole peer group behind you listening in using the built in speakers on your laptop a Monday afternoon. The right environment and circumstances will tighten the mood that the game is trying to set. Take it slow and carefully navigate yourself around. Don't rush it as you will most likely miss something important.  

I do appreciate that the still keep that old formula going and are also welcoming this idea. The old games gives you that feeling of constant pressure with moments of relief. You are always fighting off hordes of zombies or bio weapons but can do so with ammunition that will kill them twice. The zombies are slow and easy to predict. The enemies in this game is fast and dodge your bullets as you try to take them down. This game, same as RE7, preys on your senses that heighten your awareness. It rely more so on jump scares but are building them up slowly that keeps you sharp and alert. You know that something is about to happen, you just don't know when.. But when it happens those few bullets you have to spare will be consumed. Saying this is from a viewpoint of only playing the game on Hardcore so far with a controller. Anyone who have played Resident Evil 7 on "Madhouse" difficulty knows what I am talking about. The other two easier options haven't been played and the game is still far from finished. But I do have faith in it and will edit this review if anything less than expected is experienced. I love every second of it and hope that Capcom have plans to keep the games coming for at least a decade more.

Resident Evil 7 was built from the ground up and that took a toll on other aspects of the game, such as the uninspired "molded" enemies. Resident Evil Village does not have that shortcoming, meaning the development was spent more on the game's features, characters, and environments. That doesn't mean to say I like Resident Evil Village more, but gamers need to be cognizant about this.

I make this point because I'm too often seeing the misleading points of "It weighs much more heavily into a shootem up" and "It relies less on the psychological horror of 7." They're brain dead points because they really didn't if you look at the aspects of the game in proportion to each other. This game does have more gun play but it also has much more terrifying scares. 

The game actually follows a lot of the same gameplay beats as RE7, especially when it comes to the ramping up of combat in the later stages of the game. There are even parts that closely mirror the sort of thriller moments from RE7, such as being chased after your hand is lobbed off. However there is nothing in Resident Evil 7 that comes close to how terrifying the baby part in Resident Evil Village is. In short, this game took Resident Evil 7 and made things bigger and gave them more love in all the right ways.

Now what would I give this game? I'd give it a 9/10

The story is intensely engaging, the combat is fun, the thrills will make you scream, and the atmosphere will take what's left of your breath away. The small thing I disliked was the noticeable patchwork in certain story moments, where it felt like they just made a convenient excuse.

After finishing the game I can say that this is easily my favorite RE game. It's got a good mix of the atmospheric horror that shot the series into popularity and intense action sequences that engage the player. There is a recap movie in the game, but I would say playing RE7 is a must before you pick this one up.

Shady business practises aside the game is exceptionally solid. The graphics are wonderful. The game performs well and I experienced 0 bugs throughout my play-through. The gun-play is tight and responsive  and most of the weapons have their place. 
The horror falls off near the mid-point once you become a walking armoury but until then it's pretty scary and that's to be expected of an Resident Evil game by now anyway.
The sound design is extremely well put together, most of the weapons sound great, the environments are audibly spooky and the voice acting is top notch for the most part. Fish-Boy is a bit hard to understand for my liking but that's really my only major gripe with audio.
Overall it's a great game, my only complaint being the game is a little under 8 hours long start to finish on most difficulties. Some might argue for a $100 they would expect at least 10 hours of run-time from it but it was a well crafted and engaging 8 hours and there is some replay-ability to be had from mercenary mode and the harder difficulty. 
I can 100% recommend this game but it is a direct sequel to RE 7 so you might want to play that first which I also recommend as a good game although not as good as this one I should say.

Resident Evil Village is a good sequel to 2016's Resident Evil 7. However, as a mainline entry of this long running series, it falls short in few areas of the greatness of some of the earlier games. 

Pros
- The graphics is awesome
- The village, castle and all the other areas are very well designed. Plenty of variety in the areas as well and backtracking through old areas previously unaccessable to collect new loot was a lot of fun because you run into new mini-bosses.
- Some truly terrifying enemy design
- Some of the boss encounters are epic
- Has possibly the scariest section to play-through in any resident evil game. My heart skipped few beats.

Cons
- Most of the non-optional mini-boss fights were a bummer. Too straightforward and anti-climactic.
-  My biggest con of the game is it's story. Being a resi fan all my life I never truly realized how important even a nonsensical story can be to a mood and feel of a game. Most resident evil games have you play a person trying to escape a nightmare situation. Although most of the time these protatgonists had military or police training, the situation always felt dire and their survival not a certainty. In Re Village, it feels like you are invulnerable. You are not trying to escape but running straight into the pits of hell. You are a professional hitman (not literally), taking out the Lords of the village one by one to save someone. Re Village draws inspiration from RE4 where Leon also faces a nightmare scenario to save Ashley. However, you run into Ashley very early on and spend the majority of the game trying to escape with her. Here, it doesn't feel like that. How can it feel like a survival horror when you are playing as a semi-doom guy? Basically just go into the game thinking this is a survival horror game where the enemies are trying to survive from you than the other way round. Even more so than Re4. Truly effects the feel of the game especially half way through. 

8/10

RE games rarely scare me (let alone scare me real good), but there's this one grotesque creature in a certain dark hallway that honestly spooked me pretty bad the first time I saw it.

I've had small issues like the AI getting stuck on walls and the FOV being locked at 81 (which can be fixed with a program), but other than small nitpicks, this is easily one of the best games from this year.

Resident Evil 7 strayed away from the formula Resident Evil set back in the 90's greatly by adding a FPS perspective as well as  a new cast of characters to familiarise ourselves to. With all that in mind, Resident Evil 7 was a fantastic entry to the series and with a rather weak latter third of the game, the initial opening hours was as close to perfect as Resident Evil has gotten in terms of horror and atmosphere.

Resident Evil 8 has come along, and it's gone even further from the roots of Resident Evil, even more so than my expectations. However, this game is just as good, if not better, than Resident Evil 7. But do be warned, this isn't the claustrophobic horror from 7 at all, this is more action focused with a few horror elements thrown in the mix. With a new set of villains to try rival the Baker family, they don't quite hit the highs as well as the Bakers did unfortunately but they are still pretty good, even if the writing is cringe at times.

The sound design is top notch as usual, you feel the sense of dread of uneasiness as you go around every corner and go into every house in the village. The level design is far better than it was in 7, the ship section in 7 was arse but here the finale section is infinitely superior. Ethan once again is a bit bland, his character feels like he has no emotions he just doesn't sit right in the Resident Evil universe, considering the fact the game is an FPS so you don't see him either.

Both are very well optimised too, my PC is almost ancient now and it still runs the game like a dream. However, there is no FOV slider to speak of in this game. It's 2021 and no FOV slider? I understand they want to keep it a short field of view to enhance the horror experience, but the option is needed for those who suffer from motion sickness, so do be warned.

Overall the game is a solid entry into the series and I cannot wait to see wait to see what Resident Evil 9 brings to the series, I'd consider Resident Evil 8 better than 7 in certain departments and 7 better than 8 in others. They are both vastly different games with the only connection being the FPS. 

Oh, and a boss in the game references Chris Redfield as a "Boulder Punching Arsehole"

I have complicated feelings about Village, but overall I do recommend. Simple Pros and Cons and then a little more in-depth talk below:

Pros:
-The setting is neat. It may be drab and not TOO much variation, but when a series is known for mostly taking place in a facility or two, I'm aight with that.
-Graphics are decent. They ain't the best and won't blow you away completely, but good enough to set a mood, and very atmospheric.
-When it gets tense it gets TENSE. I had a few moments where I needed a breather due to me being a pansy.
-Personally I feel like it was a good length, not super long, but didn't feel like I rushed through it.
-I enjoyed the story and the connections the game made with previous titles.
-I super enjoyed one section where you get to just go ham on some of the enemies. Oh, and the boss fight right before was  super fun.

Cons:
-Pacing felt off, some sections dragged on, others felt like they went by way too quickly.
-Tense, but I wouldn't say scary. Personally I am okay with this, I know some people would not be.
-Takes a lot from one of my least favorite Resident Evil games. (Could be a pro to you, I don't judge)
-Certain weapons felt useless, or ammo. I NEVER used flashbangs, never saw the point.
-Some areas would have TONS of ammo. Some barely any at all. And the barely any at all seemed to be the places I would more commonly burn through the ammo I had.
-One area in particular made me feel like it was there solely to eat through your resources before the end of the game, and I did not find myself enjoying it.

I have mixed feelings, I overall enjoyed the game, but it feels off. Something not quite right. Honestly I still had a lot of fun and plan on playing through on higher difficulties, and playing through Mercenaries mode. This may just seem like rambling, hope it helps make some decisions however!

RE8  is a great action game that improves on the combat and exploration elements from RE7. 
Elements such as enemy variety, boss fights and gunplay make the combat more engaging compared to the 4 molded seen in 7. 
Boss fights are challenging in this game and more engaging than shoot the obvious orange weakspot.
The village and its surrounding areas all have distinct mechanics to help keep the pace of the game moving forward although by the end it basically turns into a slaughter fest mowing down a dozen lychans in one area.

Story is a bit of a mixed bag but overall RE8 is a ambitious followup to RE7.  Tone does start out serious like 7 does but turns into typical resident evil camp similar to 4,5 and 6. 

Overall it took just under 8 hours on hardcore difficulty to beat. I do think RE7 overall is slightly better due to the story structure and how unique of an entry it is. There are moments I will remember in this game but most of it doesn't match the tight pace and shock of the first hour of RE7.

I do want to play more of this game for the mercenaries mode since it will be really hard doing repeat playthroughs going through THAT doll house again.

The game play is essentially RE7 which isn't a bad thing, although i don't care for the new inventory ui. A large plus is key items and such don't take inventory space anymore. The true highlight is the story, which i firmly believe anyone who played 7 will want to see.

Just beat the game before writing this. Capcom still doesn't disappoint. The game was an interesting spin from what resident evil usually throws at us. I will give a spoiler warning to those who haven't finished the game or haven't bought it yet. If you just want the long and short of it, I recommend this product. I'll explain why below in sections and save the story for last so spoilers are easier to avoid.

1. Gameplay - We'll start off here because gameplay can either be a breeze to explain, or a b*tch. First and foremost, gun play is basically the same as Resident Evil 7: Biohazard, but slightly more fast-paced. This might turn off some fans of the horror aspect of the game, but in my opinion, if the gun play was as slow as in RE:7, Village would be a miserable game to play as you will be dealing with enemies that are quick, cunning, and a little unpredictable. You will also see more open environments where you will engage in combat. The village is not as cramped as the halls of the Baker Estate. There is also a wider variety of enemies. Not just four variants of the same thing. You'll be equipped with a map and a decently-sized inventory. In safe zones, storage has been replaced by a merchant who will upgrade your weapons, sell you small amounts of ammo, and will buy "treasure items" that you obtain through breaking objects and slaying monsters. And YES, horror is still very much there. Remember the feeling you got when Jack Baker was stalking you through the beginning portion of RE:7? Now think of the Lady Dimitrescu (the tall vampire lady that the entire internet was in love with before the rise of world-class criminal Chris McLean) she gives you the same feeling but its a little worse as your gunfire, even to her FACE, rarely causes her to flinch. Jack would stagger as a result of a 9x19mm round to the skull. NOT HER. And that isn't even the worst thing you'll face when it comes to the horror aspect. There is a moment that borderline traumatized me. Some serious Outlast sh*t. But I won't spoil the surprise >:)  The short version, gunplay was fun, some moments made me sh*t bricks, enemies were challenging, bosses were spectacular.

2. Visuals - Resident Evil: Village is a beautiful game and its appearance only gets better as you progress. Seeing the light from the sunset stunned me. the environmental design only helps you to feel immersed within the experience. 

3. Story: Not much to say other than WHAT THE F*CK, CAPCOM!!!!!????? You play with my brain, you play with my sanity, and now you play with my feelings!?!?!? I came here to shoot vampires and werewolves. One moment, I'm begging for Geralt of Rivia to come and save my sorry ass, next I'm gunning down lady Dimitrescu's victorian-emo daughters, then I'm fighting her as some dragon-demigorgon abomination, then I find that my daughter is fragmented into several parts and I have to put... her... back together? Then I'm in a smaller house where an overgrown and p*ssed off fetus is trying to murder me in the pitch black, fast-forward to bootleg Walter White and his wolfenstien-esc Soldats, he wants Mother Miranda dead. I forgot to mention that before him was the Hunchback of Notre Dam but he is covered in tumors and can turn into a Metro-Exodus looking fish beast. That and puppet mistress who was a little too much into Emily Wants to Play. Ethan gets his heart ripped out by Mother Miranda and dies. My feelings were hurt and i wished nothing but death on that woman. I took control of Chris Redfield and used a tricked-out AKM to go on a rage/sorrow-fueled rampage through the village. BOOM Ethan's not dead because he was infected with the E-Series mold from RE:7 (we all saw this coming). I take control of Ethan again who kills Mother Miranda, saving his daughter. But he is weakened. Chris tries to get him out, but Ethan gives him the child and takes a detonator meant to blow the village to the Kadingir Sanctum from DOOM. Ethan dies again and my feelings are even more hurt because Morimasa Sato and Antony Johnston gave me hope then ripped it away. YOU BASTARDS!!! Let's just say that after I finished this game I was very happy to see Ethan's daughter alive and potentially an addition to the cast of Resident Evil Characters (she'd better last more than two f*cking games, I swear to ever god that man has worshipped). Pretty sure Mia's still alive too. But at the same time, this game left me a broken man. Ethan Winters is gone. In a nutshell: I love you, Capcom... now go to your room and think about what you've done.

I've noticed there are a lot of diehard Resident Evil fans who resist every change the series makes. Sometimes I'd agree with them, like when RE became completely action oriented in RE5 and scatterbrained and buggy in RE6. 

But if you thought RE7's change to FPS were incredible immersive and the set pieces / graphics were amazing, well, you're going to love RE8. If you liked RE4's wild and ridiculously fun story, then you're going to love what they do in RE8. It's completely over-the-top and doesn't take itself too seriously, just enough for suspense. 

Speaking of suspense, many have suggested this game takes a more action-oriented route. That's true to a degree, but there is a ton of horror here, let me tell you. I actually was surprised at the balance between horror and action. It reminds me of RE4 in that sense. The enemies are so fluid and powerful feeling that this game makes you fear them even if you have ammo. 

I'm just glad that I didn't listen to any negative hype because this is a worthy successor to RE7 so far.

Basically RE4-2, it just did everything RE4 did, but in 7's style. That's not a bad thing to me as 4 and 7 were two of my fav RE games. I played on normal my first play through, completion time said just over 9 hours, steam timer says 14.2 hours. If I'm generous and say I spent about an hour in the pause screen, it took me 13 hours to beat. completion screen doesn't count cutscenes or time spent re-doing sections or bosses when you die and go back to a save or checkpoint. It felt like a long RE game to me, like RE4 did, it's a good length.

Gameplay wise, it felt a lot like 7, but more exploring like RE4, there's treasure, it has RE4's inventory system, you buy more space, no stash and quite a few weapons and upgrades.

The game is broken up into specific sections, quite like RE4 was as well. You start in the village, it makes you uncomfortable right from the start, but you don't spend much time there until you move on to the castle section. You'd think from the marketing that the castle was a large part of the game, I guess it kind of is, but I only spent maybe 2 hours there. 

I have to talk about Lady D though. We all knew she was going to be a stalker type enemy like Mr.X, what I didn't expect was she would just be a reskinned Mr.X. I have played like 150 hours of RE2 Remake and I know Mr.X, Lady D has the exact same walk speed, stands in the same posture and speeds up the same when she sees you. They literally put lady D's mesh on Mr.X's skeleton, changed the sound effects and the attack animation and added an animation for when she see's you and extends her claws and called it a day. Her stalking you is just a tiny portion of the game anyways, but it seemed obvious to me and I had to call it out.

 Next you move back to the village and then it kinda opens up a bit more, you still have to follow a linear path more or less but you're free to explore the village and as you do the other sections you get access to other general areas with more treasure. The sections are all pretty well paced, none of them really over-stay their welcome. There was a moment or two where I was started to get tired of an area and it would end basically right after. 

The game does a good job at keeping the tension throughout the game as well, there are a lot of enemy variety and each section of the game has it's own way of scaring you or keeping you tense.

It gets a little bit into the RE5 and 6 level of over-the-top near the end, but the whole game up to that point was pretty great and it's really just the last 2 boss fights and the section in between, so I'll give it a pass, but you're treading a fine line there Capcom.

The story is pretty good, if you were thorough and read all the notes like I did, the way they slowly tie everything in and bring it full circle with RE7 and the original games was pretty good, twists included.

Honestly in my top 3 RE games probably, I started with 2, played a bit of 3, and 4 was the one I really played all of first. I didn't like 5, didn't play 6 because it was more 5, and I liked 7. RE2 and 3 are great remakes, even if RE3make is only half the game. I think Capcom have done pretty good by me this time around. 

To Capcom: seriously stop making the MP crap, no one wants that because you guys are consistently terrible at it. Make another Outbreak style game with coop if you are going to do multiplayer.

I recommend it for any RE fan (people who played 5 and 6 first and liked those don't count), I doubt we will get any story DLC like we did with 7 since it took them a year to release the free dlc (a chunk of the game that was just removed from the original game to begin with because it wasn't ready in time), and the story doesn't really allow for it, unless we play as chris infiltrating BSAA headquarters which would be the only scenario that makes sense for DLC.

Some misconceptions about RE8!

1. “Short game or it’s 8 hours only.” This is straight up WRONG. The game can easily take more than 10 hours to finish. There are so many people who beat it in 12 to 14 hours, some even more than that. RE8 has more exploration and side optional in-game content more than any previous RE game. The in-game timer literally lies to you, if you’ve played 12 hours, it will tell you that you spent 7 or 8 hours. It’s easily one of the longest RE games. It’s got a perfect length for an RE game, not to mention that it has post-game content and good replay value.

2. “It’s not scary.” hella WRONG! This game has different types of horror. From RE7 type of horror, to RE4 (panicking), and to Silent Hill / PT level of horror + other types. In fact, one section in the game has probably the scariest and creepiest moment in the entire franchise.

3. “It’s RE4+RE7.” This is true, but it also has inspirations from almost every RE game. The game feels like it’s a celebration for RE’s 25th anniversary.

I’ve enjoyed my time playing it and I think it’s A MUST BUY for every RE fan or a survival horror fan.

- Easily and by a huge margin, RE8 is the best looking RE game ever. It's INCREDIBLY detailed, well designed and STUNNING to look at.
- Very atmospheric, and its got a lot of variety in that aspect as well.
- Sound design is also the best in the series. The intro is horrifying!
- From the first few hours, you'll quickly notice how big and diverse the game is.
- Levels are intricately crafted, with more ways to explore them. Really liked how the village was structured with more ways to explore and search its houses.
- The game INSANELY nails the interior design of its levels; I find myself stopping every 5 mins or so just to absorb the beauty of it all.
- The game's setting really makes you feel like you're playing in a horror themed amusement park.
- There is clear emphasis on exploration and side content.
- The game allows you to take control of your own pacing at certain sections. It’s not really a linear game. It has more freedom and exploration than previous RE games as I mentioned before, which I liked very much!
- The game does a really good job of changing its intensity from time to time. Presenting different types of horror along the way, mixing them up with action / adventure elements & sequences while still being within its survival horror medium. It’s well balanced, diverse and refreshing.
- RE8 has some of the highest highs in the franchise. When it hits, it hits real good. :D
- NO LOADING TIMES. That's a technical marvel considering the quality of its graphics, level design and performance. RE Engine strikes again!
- Puzzles are fun and rewarding.
- Backtracking here is the most fun and rewarding in all of the RE games.
- Music is top tier.
- The merchant is cool.
- The story is intriguing and thrilling.
- The characters are some of the best in the series. Really interesting, very well acted and fun to watch. Not including Ethan though lol, however he's honestly better this time.

* Advice: if you're playing with a controller (consoles or on PC), turn off the movement camera acceleration and aiming camera acceleration settings. They somewhat introduce input delay and make the camera movement feel slow. Terrible settings!

This sequel to RE7 was more than what I was hoping for.

My only issues with RE7, was the lack of enemy monsters, types, lack of different weaponry and more depth.

RE8 Succeeded to improve all of those issues in this game.

And the story, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do I love it. You're constantly kept on your feet and everything seems to more or less fit into the logic of the story.

My two issues with the game, is no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FOV slider, which I can assume isn't there to make the player feel more boxed in with what they can and can't see, then there's the boss fights.

Now, the boss fights were super creative, awesome, cool looking, exciting but unfortunately incredibly dull. Hide to avoid enemy attacks or block, shoot weak spot, kill boss. And that is basically almost every single boss fight. Some of them don't even have a weak spot, you just avoid attacks and shoot the boss where you think it'll deal more damage (usually to the head). But I can appreciate the work they put into make these boss fights, there's only so much you can do with the way the game plays when you think about it. You can't exactly do cool manoeuvres and do some weird Devil May Cry level stuff.

So in all honesty I can forgive these two 'issues' because there's not much that can be done in my opinion.

Now my one genuine complaint. There's a particular treasure, which appears when you pass a particular point in the story BUT you have go back to where the particular key to the treasure is and NOT progress the story. Otherwise, the game locks you out and bye bye treasure no chance of you ever seeing it. Not that it's anything major to your gameplay, but that was insanely frustrating, knowing that I progressed so fast past a particular section that i missed a particular treasure. Just make a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puzzle or something, don't do this story gated crap what's wrong with you Capcom.

But as you can see, I barely have any complaints.

You get a gigantic inventory, which you can then make even bigger with purchasable upgrades to the point where you don't need an item box anymore (like Resident Evil 4), references to Resident Evil 5, obviously 7 and probably more I missed somewhere.

Although, to get infinite ammo, you need to fully upgrade a weapon, and buy an unlockable infinite ammo for that particular weapon. However, if you wish to fully upgrade everything, you do so, and to save space you need to sell it to the duke (and to buy it back, it costs DOUBLE). So people know a way to cheese this, save your game with a ton of cash, fully upgrade one, save in a new slot, buy the infinite ammo, then reload old save and there we go no need to upgrade everything. But it's a crappy way of doing things and it'll lower the amount of time you'll have to play the game, Once you unlock the collectibles, sure it'll be fun to go through and steamroll stuff but in all the previous Resident Evil's, I always lost interest once I unlocked everything to unlock and played around a little.

So I'd recommend just playing your way up the ladder.

Start on Standard, then Hardcore, then Village of Shadows.

If you try starting on Village of Shadows, You'll realise that without infinite ammo or some knowledge of the game you're gonna have an insanely difficult time, it is genuinely the hardest RE difficulty to start on first time I've seen in any RE so far. (and it randomizes loot on top of that, exciting.)

So you gotta build up your Ethan, make him nice and stronk then send him and yourself into those difficulties with upgraded weapons and what not.

Now, you could consider the game kind of short, but it seriously did not feel that way. It was paced so well that I thought I spent hours trying to figure stuff out, and it took me 6-7 hours to beat on standard. It felt like 20 hours.

You're constantly doing stuff, and the extra content is, well extra. You're not forced into it but the rewards are nice.

There's a lot more action, but there's sections with pure horror and a mix of both occasionally which keeps the game balanced between the two.

To me, this is a successful sequel and no one can tell me otherwise.

For any long time RE fan, this feels like a combination of RE7 with strong RE4 vibes.  First play through will likely be somewhere around 15 hours depending on how thorough you are collecting things.  There are a few different main areas of the game each with their own theme and feel--I really liked this aspect, they felt distinct from each other.  

Per usual, you'll have access to quite a few weapons and they can all be upgraded via stats or weapon parts that you'll find along the way.  Speaking of weapons, the game has an odd aiming mechanic where you can hip fire a weapon, but ADSing just sort of tightens the spread rather than actually aiming down sights--while this works mostly fine, it didn't feel quite right.  This is definitely something that I wasn't a fan of, but fortunately isn't a deal breaker either.  Melee combat feels par for the course for an RE title, but feels a little under-powered if you're an RE veteran.  

Story has some great characters, some cringe/cheesiness which I've come to expect with any RE title, and is paced overall pretty well. The 1st 70% or so of the game is absolutely amazing for the most part, it's an excellent mix of resi 4s action with the slower paced horror of resi 7.  

You'll spend some quite lengthy periods of time walking about with no enemies in sight, just the slow burn of atmospheric horror (none of that jumpscare trash like Outlast 2) and then be suddenly swarmed by enemies.  It makes for a nice balance between scavenging for ammo at your own pace and frantic fights for your life.  There is also one very noteworthy section of pure horror about half way through the game, if you've played the game you know the one.

However near the end the game really starts to become noticeably worse, with it devolving into wave after wave of samey enemy quite a bit.  I wont spoil anything specific but one of the later sections involving metal and machines is dreadful and the game would be better if it was completely cut.  It does thankfully pick up after that particular section, even going full stupid over the top resi6 for a few minutes before mostly toning it down,  So bad it's good  'merica action can be good as a contrast for 1 or 2 sections and I think it was mostly used well here.

The story is fine, nothing special but it's a RE game what'd you expect.  It also looks and runs beautifully, I'm using an old 1070 and it ran above 60fps on close to ultra with only a few noticeable drops here and there, mostly when grabbed by or killing monsters, with the only real problem being the painfully low FoV.  The gameplay is also good, I've noticed 1 or 2 reviews saying the "game is unplayable without a controller" and I have no idea what they're talking about the K+M controls are perfectly fine, rebind a key or 2 and you're good to go.

The cast of characters and voice acting for the most part is also fantastic, there's no one on Jack baker's level but the main characters do hold up on their own with only 1 real exception.  Ethan is a horrible character, i'm not going into detail (cause he doesn't deserve the effort) but to sum it up he's an unbearably dull moron who just seems to sound bored half the time. 

Overall It is a great game that has issues, I do think it's better than 7 and probably the best resi (not including a certain remake) to come out since resi 4 or even that time Chris punched a boulder.

TLDR its an 8 or 8.5/10 held back by some weaker sections near the end.

Long story:
**First and foremost for most people, if you came to this title for Lady D.  you will be supremely disappointed. She is at best a minor footnote on the entirety of this title. RIP and oofs in the chat for the thirsties.** 
Graphics are pretty nice, didn't notice any graphical bugs, and the game is actually extremely well optimized. This is a moot point for me because in my opinion graphics take a backseat to both style and presentation, after game play.
Game play can be a bit janky, most especially due to controls. Numerous times pop up commands would delay out or just simply not work til you move away and back.
Sound design is super good via atmos surround or atmos headphones, if a bit tin-like from a distance. 
The story actually middle grounds to all fans in a way that doesn't amaze or wow, but just works for everyone. If you are a casual Resident Evil fan, it will feel like playing an Evil Within title. If you are a devoted fan of the series, 8 slaps a lot of new lore to fill in historical gaps in the series that was a real treat. There are immersion breaking things that happen from time to time that get explained away later, but it still sorta festers as something needless to the story. If you loved RE4 then this will likely be your new favorite as it is basically just RE7 with RE4 themes, the big difference is that it actually has a competent story that makes sense. It caters to both survival horror fans of the classics (zero-CVX), and the newer action fans (4-6), though considerably more towards the former. It has its areas where action is highlighted, but for the most part stays true to the core ideals that RE was founded on. Anyway it was pretty aight, give it a go.

So far, this game is everything a RE fan would really want to see, me being included. It's got your action elements like RE4 and RE5, you got your horror of older RE and RE7. (Not to mention a certain part when going after the puppet in the basement, made me have a panic attack and almost broke me). Overall a great RE game that expands upon RE7 in almost every way and enjoyable, plus mercenaries is back! :)

A solid followup to RE7 that satisfied my expectations quite handily. [i]So far, I have finished one playthrough on Standard difficulty.[/i]

As you might be able to guess, [b]this game is a more action oriented sequel to RE7.[/b] While RE7 had a really limited arsenal of weapons (and a smaller arsenal of ones worth using, cough cough burner cough cough), with the shotgun and pistol being your bread and butter, RE8 gives you the shotgun + pistol almost immediately, with an arsenal of upgrades and other viable tools like a sniper rifle or grenade launcher.

It takes heavy cues from Resident Evil 4- There's a merchant, no Item Box, tons of upgrades, and even small details like birds dropping cash are back. There are some differences (dead enemies never drop ammo, usually money and very rarely crafting materials for example) but the homages are clearly there.

First, and this needs to be made absolutely clear to manage expectations: [b]I do NOT think this game is a successor to Resident Evil 4.[/b] This game is a sequel to Resident Evil 7, and THAT is clearly what it was going for. RE4 is a masterpiece IMO, and RE4 Remake will be the one that attempts to improve upon it, NOT this game.

RE8 was very clearly designed with RE7's major criticisms in mind. SO:

[h1]THE GOOD[/h1]

[list]
[*]The game has solid enemy variety. RE7 had literally 4 regular enemies IIRC (not including DLC content) but Village does much better on this front.

[*]The game has solid bossfights, including the final boss. RE7 was much more of a mixed bag in this respect, especially the finale which was a glorified QTE. At most, you could complain that one of the fights is a more cinematic/traditional horror experience with no gunplay, I guess, but I thought it was a good move for the story's pacing.

[*]The game has ample content. Many felt like RE7's general level of quality was good enough (and it did offer genuine bonuses for recompleting the story with challenges, like all modern RE releases) to justify the pricepoint, but here, you get ~12-15 hours of campaign content for your first playthrough, which is very solid for a horror game, especially considering that IMHO, RE8 does NOT lag in terms of pacing or ecetera. Plus all the usual bonus content you can expect from Resident Evil and even an extra in the form of Mercenaries mode coming back.
[/list]


[h1]THE DETAILS[/h1]

[list]
[*]The overwhelming majority of the map takes place in one interconnected world, which is awesome! Instead of leaving the Village after the first 3rd of the game and going into linear times, the game waits until about 2/3rds in before you are locked out of the old areas. This does unfortunately make the areas you [i]can't[/i] revisit stick out like sore thumbs, ([spoiler]the castle[/spoiler]) but this scratches all my backtracking itches so good. There are even a pleasantly solid number of optional nooks and crannies of the map. Good work, RE8, I've wanted other games to do this for a while!

[*]Some people have been talking about the tone/scariness of this game. As I said earlier, you get a gun REALLY early in this. RE7 was a massive abnormality in how long it took you to get any weapons, remember. I do think one of this game's sequences is perhaps the scariest moment for me in RE history ([spoiler]what can I say, I'm a sucker for my means of fighting back being stripped from me and being forced to hide[/spoiler]) but aside from that specific moment, this game is not as toned back as 7 was, which I think is fine. It's not [i]as[/i] arcadey as 4, though, and certainly not as much as 5 or 6, which is the main thing worth noting. It's still [i]ultimately[/i] a horror game, even if it's willing to jump a few (hundred) sharks.

[*]I think the story was solid! Like RE7 it's very twist heavy and I feel like it succeeded, and honestly exceeded my expectations.
[/list]


[h1]THE CRITICISMS[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Compared to RE4, this game isn't as good in terms of economy/item management.[/b] The resource management is Resident Evil quality, but not LEGENDARY Resident Evil quality. It feels like you have too little to spend money on until you get to the final act of the game, for example, then the game springs a boatload of purchases on you. [b]I also never ran out of inventory space once.[/b] Maybe if I had stalled on getting the space upgrades that'd be a different story, but RE8 doesn't really give you stuff to [i]hoard,[/i] unless you're insisting on never selling a weapon.

[*]To explain exactly why you don't run out of inventory space, [i]crafting materials, valuables, and key items don't take up any space.[/i] I'm fine with this design decision, it cuts potential hauling trips and it provides a unique incentive to avoid crafting when you can get stuff wholesale, BUT [b]RE8 could've used some extra items that I had to debate letting go or keeping.[/b] RE4 was filled with all kinds of crazy nonsense like grenade variants and the eggs as a counter example.

[*]Like RE7 and 2 Remake, the game STARTS with a Stalker (Mr X/Nemesis esque) mechanic where a specific monster (Lady D) is following you dynamically, then [i]never[/i] does it again after that first act of the game. They even mix it up by having her daughters sometimes show up first, attack you for a bit, then call their mommy to finish the job (and her daughters are more limited in the areas they can visit). TWO stalker monsters?! It's great, I love it, RE team, you keep striking gold, [b]so why, for the love of god, have you stopped digging?![/b]

[*][b]The enemies/combat is NOT RE4 levels, don't get your hopes up for that.[/b] The Ganados were some of the best enemies in gaming history because of how reactive they were to you, and how you were incentivised to deal with them. One Ganado was no threat, you shoot them in the leg, kick 'em, and knife them to preserve ammo, stunlock heaven. When hordes showed up, when their heads revealed parasites, or when they grabbed instakill chainsaws, you had to adapt your combat style, but each individually was putty in your hands.

RE8's Lycans ARE great, and will be underappreciated IMO, as their animations are [b]perfect[/b] for creating difficulty in landing headshots without making it unfair/unpredictable, [i](seriously, the RE team are some of the only devs I've seen get this balance right)[/i] they are capable of following the player to most places, and they have lots of subtle traits, like how they can choose where to land when they're jumping towards you to ensure they never just queue up to get headshotted. However, this basic formula is still a [i]"risk headshots, or play it safe with center of mass, decide before you run out of ground to kite with"[/i] scenario, not the ultra-tactical ammo conservation strats of 2 Remake or the aforementioned playground of 4. It's most likely a deliberate design decision to preserve some of the game's horror elements, and I like it overall, but you should be aware of it.

[*]RE8 does NOT have a REmake Raccoon City Police Department, or an RE4 village opening, or a ~first 4 hours of RE7, IMO. (in terms of the quality of those game segments) It's an [i]overall[/i] solid game, but it never blew me away with a gameplay segment that on its own sold me. There were moments I loved, but [b]RE8 is clearly focused on giving an overall quality experience, at the expense of not having a singular part that's absolutely perfect.[/b]
[/list]



[b]This is a worthy sequel to RE7, and nothing apart from that.[/b] If you wanted a horror-centric game like the opening of RE7, or a spiritual successor to RE4, those expectations will probably not be met. It seems some people are hitting this game from both sides, saying it's not far enough on one side or the other and therefore isn't "really Resident Evil".


That division is the exact thing that proves this is as Resident Evil as it gets. RE8 is, despite the irony, an 8/10. I highly recommend it.

This is a real banger of a game. It extends on the feeling of RE7, incorporates a lot the best mechanics of RE4, and brings in its own spins and puzzles. Probably one of the best Resident Evil entries to date. Capcom's doing an amazing job with the remakes and the new titles. What a turn around for them, the RE Engine looks great too. I'd also like to address the complaints people have in negative reviews

1.) Performance issues: Follow the specifications and don't play on any older CPUs. This game is NOT designed for older hardware. It functions very well even on lower end Ryzen CPUs. Recommend upgrading to one if you're having issues. Please don't leave a negative review when you didn't bother to read the minimum specs. EDIT: If you have RTX on, turn it off...RTX isn't that good generally speaking and you can do without...it's not very well optimized for the game and that's to be expected. 

2.) Horror and action aspects: The game is plenty horror, if you've only played the first hour or two, you have no idea what you are talking about and should really invest more time. It's probably one of the best entries to date in the series, to knock it is a disservice. 

3.) Complaints about mechanics: The game overall is great and expands on RE7. The naysayers have little to stand on in this regard. It's fine to have an opinion, but people are missing the point of reviews. There's a lot to unpack here and the game, if you take your time, can take longer to beat than RE7. It also carries over some elements from RE4, which is good, because it took the best bits (love the new merchant!) and made them modern. The puzzles are pretty mild but fun as well. 

4.) FOV: Really not a big deal, I don't understand how it makes people "sick". The game is designed to be that close up. It looks VERY weird when you change the FOV via third party tools. It would be decent to have a built in one, but honestly...the game is fine with the default values. 

BONUS: There's also already mods out and they add an extra bit of flair to things. Can't wait to see where those go.

Hopefully this was a decent review, I'm not finished yet and I can't wait to see where the story goes. :)

EDIT: I did finish recently and the end's a banger that made me tear up a bit. Definitely wishlist or buy this game if you're a fan of the series. Now we wait for DLC to come out and maybe add more to the story!

Ok, the "next gen"  is here for resident evil.   The graphics do look pretty, but that is all this game has going for it.      Mia is one of the most unlikable characters in the RE universe.   I didn't like her in 7, and here she is even worse.  They should have called her Millie, she drinks wine, wears ill-fitting yarn cardigans, reads inappropriate material to her children, prepares local european dishes, is on medication and speaks condescendingly to her henpecked husband who went through hell to save her.      

The inappropriate material she read to her daughter is a fairy tale ( a local one! <fawn>), and a poorly told one at that.  But the lack of story telling ability shown in that small local tale of Coraline by way of Tim Burton foreshadows the biggest problem with the game. The Village surrounds an architecture better set in a Castlevania game than Resident Evil, and everyone who complained about the lack of full city exploration in RE3:remake gets exactly what the deserved with this sprawling European town that feels incredibly similar to the farmhouse in RE7. They try to promote this as a spiritual successor to RE4.  NO.   RE4 was great,   This is an uninspired romp down memory lane, as told by people who never experienced the memories for themselves. Weird blend of RE4 and RE7 that mostly works.

Shooting works much like it did in 7, so if you liked that you'll enjoy this. RE8 also addresses the lack of enemy variety in RE7, but your weapon selection is still pretty underwhelming (though upgradable this time around). There are options within each of the weapon classes, but the differences between them are generally just "newer gun does gun better." There will never be a perpetually unresolved "Red9 or Punisher" debate for any of RE8's guns, just use the one with the biggest numbers.

There are also some decent scares, a handful of discomforting sequences that break up the gunplay and exploration nicely. You will know something is about to happen, and you will dread it, but never really on the level of previous horror focused RE games. Yes still spookier than RE4-6, so be wary you're in for a scary. None of these sequences are terribly long, so repeat playthroughs won't be burdened by a now predictable and unscary spookemup area.

The fact that this is still, technically, a "Survival-Horror" game will sneak up on you if you're not careful. It's very easy, thanks to the shop, to have a metric ton of gear, ammo, and supplies saved up. So much so that you start wasting good ammo on junk enemies because you want to, because you want to play with your cool toys instead of your rinky-dink knife and pistol. You will be punished for this, but not at brutally as you might have in RE7.

Puzzles are there, but for the most part the biggest challenge is encountering a thing that needs a thing, and then remembering where it was when you find the thing it needs. Just use key item on slot for 90% of the puzzles, the rest are either time based, box based, or god awful rolling ball physics things. This game is not terribly cerebral, if you pay attention to notes and whatnot it even tells you how you should be preparing for the next new enemy type or gauntlet. "Dear diary, next guy hates explosions," and so you make some extra bombs. Ezpz.

In RE fashion the story is not for everyone. A bit campy but lots of charm. Also short, again this is normal for an RE game. These games are made to be replayed.

Overall, its not an RE6 and it comes with Mercenaries mode. So, its good.
