TL:DR Review:

Graphics: 9/10

Performance: 8/10

Animation: 10/10

Gun work: 10/10

Enemies: 7/10

Boss Fights: 8/10

General: 9.5/10

THOROUGH Review:

GRAPHICS: The graphics were genuinely a major step-up in my opinion, I know some people didn't notice it but it made my top of the line computer get a little lag sometimes. It made the look of the game very enjoyable, while also being my first PC game that had Photo-mode. I enjoyed the overall look of it, and it didn't give me sore eyes at any points...mostly. There is one thing that bothered me and has pretty much always bothered me in terms of Resident Evil games, and that is the textures. The textures aren't noticeable at times but sometimes all that was in your face were P I X E L S! But other than that, the graphics were Amazing.

PERFORMANCE: This is an edit since after my review, Capcom has patched many performance issues, which has taken this rating up a notch, it plays well, and for most parts I keep a pretty smooth framerate on 8 GB ram and a 1650, so not bad, not bad at all.

ANIMATION: The reason I ranked this so high is because compared to what happened with Resident Evil 7?!?!? THIS IS A HUGE IMPROVEMENT!!! The animation of RE7 was so poorly done that sometimes it took away from the experience, the lip syncing was always proper and the movement felt very fluent and non snappy.

GUN WORK: What can I say other than that the upgrades felt relevant and the merchant bought weapons always felt like a proper upgrade from what you have. As a matter of a fact, buying a new pistol from Duke saved my butt in the last boss fight, and actually helped me win! The gun work felt proper and the weapons felt like there was always something that gave them use!

ENEMIES: Enemies were always a threat, always something to be cautious of, they may have been bullet draining but this made them a TRUE danger, and they aren't as easily avoidable, sometimes though the enemy abilities and quantity would make the fight seem fair, and in some parts it just felt like a slow paced DOOM interaction (Which is not good for an Resident Evil game) But they did pose a decent threat, and the thought of them always made you wonder "Do I want to waste ammo or health to go get that item?"

BOSS FIGHTS: In many ways they were similar to RE7 and in many ways they were different, sometimes the way they worked and how to win seemed painfully obvious, but there was a few that I feel like I couldn't have complete without help, one boss fight I probably wouldn't have won had I not went through my documents, and another I would not have won without the help of the Merchant. The boss fights felt fair (Except for the last one) and the movement and patterns felt fluent. (That last boss fight sucked, it was so difficult.)

GENERAL: The game is very good, and compared to what I have seen people say there truly isn't as much to complain about as they say, I will enjoy replaying through this game to see whatever I may have missed, and I will enjoy playing it even after I 100% it. The game is a good feeling like RE4, I love how it is similar to RE4, but upgrades in certain areas, in my opinion if RE4 went with more of the atmosphere that RE8 had it would be much better, as RE8 stuck to the Survival-horror and Action-adventure at the same time, and it felt balanced in that way.

BONUS

A very good survival horror shooter, clearly made for fans of Resident Evil 4. If you enjoyed RE7 or RE4, there's a lot to like here.

It features almost every popular feature from RE4 back in the day, including hidden treasures to sell, a quirky merchant, purchasable weapon and ammo upgrades, a large Tetris-style customizable inventory, an Eastern European setting with castles and catacombs, etc. All of this, but packed into the RE7 first-person formula, with satisfying combat, and fluid controls.

The game strikes a nice balance between tension, action and horror. There are quiet tense parts in the abandoned village with wind howling through cracked windows, large arena-style fights filled with wolf-men crawling on the walls, intense boss battles, and some downright disturbing 'Silent Hill'-style horror scenes. Overall a very good package, and an experience I won't forget!

The combat can be extremely tense at times; especially early on before you have an upgraded arsenal or health upgrades. Enemy counts are a lot higher than more recent RE games, often with 5-6 faster Lycan / wolf-men chasing after you. As you progress, there are also several optional 'mini-boss' enemies which can be extremely tough to take down. You need to make sure you're well stocked up on supplies and upgrades to take them on.

Graphically, it's a beautiful game, and the RE Engine continues to impress with how optimised it is. They made some advances in the lighting and 'density' of objects, so scenes look a lot more dramatic and are very nice to explore. On my PC, it had no trouble running maxed out at 120-144fps (ray tracing off) most of the time, or 60-80fps with RT on. The options menu is identical to RE7, RE2 and RE3, offering toggles for chromatic aberration, film noise, DoF, etc. 

That said, while the options for ray tracing are nice, they are very subtle, and the differences are barely visible unless you have screenshots side-by-side, so I didn't find it worth using at half the frame rate. Having played other games with ray tracing like Metro Exodus or Control, RE Village's RT feels disappointing and not worth using unless you have a 60fps cap or extra GPU headroom.

One major oversight is the lack of any Field Of View adjustment. It's locked to 81 degrees and feels like walking around with binoculars on your face. It's very uncomfortable and makes searching the tight, densely detailed environments cumbersome. RE7 was 90 degrees and even [i]that[/i] felt a little too zoomed in. Thankfully modders have made trainers to fix it, and a wider 90-100 FOV works flawlessly. (Fluffyquack's mod manager works great)

Inventory management is also pretty disappointing on M+KB. To move and rotate items, you need to use the keyboard; there is no clicking and dragging at all. It's very clunky, and baffling because RE2 / RE3 absolutely nailed the inventory controls.

The story is a direct continuation of RE7, following Ethan Winters, his wife Mia and his new baby daughter, Rose. Cutscenes, performance capture and overall production values are very good. Every character is well designed, with some very memorable antagonists.

Any fans of Resident Evil (especially RE4 and RE7) should pick this up!

Of the 5 main villains, Lady Demetrescu is by far the most interesting. The others pale in comparison, which makes the story fall flat after the first third. Same goes for the environments: Apart from the village and the castle, they are largely forgettable. 

House Beneviento was particularly disappointing. This part of the game feels like it is trying to recreate the tension of the Lucas portion of RE:7 but fails and ends up feeling like a poorly-reviewed early-access indie walking simulator horror-themed puzzle game that delivers in neither puzzles nor horror. The pay-off in the end was almost worth it though. Luckily, this portion of the game is fairly short, unless you get stuck on one of the puzzles purely because you fail to get the correct button prompt to come up. (totally didn't happen to me)

The fact that this chapter of the game follows its strongest chapter makes its inadequacy all the more noticeable.

The other two Lords are fine, but fail to measure up to Lady Demetrescu and the castle. The Factory portion was also a bit too long for my taste.

boss fights: There are a lot of them but they ultimately come down to one of two things: kite & do as much damage as needed OR kite & shoot the glowing dots.

gameplay: as i mentioned above this is an action game, survival horror fans better look somewhere else. Enemies are bullet sponges but you needn't worry as you will always have plenty of ammunition at your disposal. Inventory management is a non-issue. 

exploration: exploration of both the castle and the village is fun and rewarding, while the remaining areas of the game drop the ball in this department. 

My favorite moment in this game wasn't a boss fight or one of the encounters with its (literally) larger than life characters, but exploring one particular dungeon, filled up to Ethan's knees with blood, wine or both, dim light reflecting off the smooth surface with a couple of enemies lurking below the opaque liquid . That was awesome.  

One enemy you cannot see in a creepy environment is much more effective than the groups of 5-10 enemies the game lobs at you later. 

These rare moments are when RE: Village shines the most. Sadly there are not many of them.

An excellent game, but don't go in expecting the horror experience to be more on par with that of RE7.

First of all, if you disliked RE4 and RE7, then chances are you'll dislike this game. This game tries to combine both RE 4 and 7 but fails to simulate their charms. But I think RE 8 does enough cool things to outweigh all the questionable stuff it has. 

Some spoiler-ish stuff down below. 

Gameplay is a slightly upgraded version of RE7. It is mostly the same loop, but they added the upgrade system and the inventory of RE4 on top of it. It is alright imo. 

Not much to say about the enemies. They were okay. They aren't as boring as the ones from RE7. 

It is very clear that this game is treating itself as a game first. It wasn't trying to tell a deep narrative or explain something to us. It accomplished what it set out to do and I appreciate that. If you thought RE games had some ridiculous plots, then you'll lose your marbles with one. It is like Didneyworl+Ethan in Wonderland+Silent Hill+Call of Duty+the usual RE madness. 

Speaking of Ethan. He is... still bland. I think it is really hard for the player to connect with Ethan because of how lost he acts all the time and the way he is oblivious to everything that goes on around him. He has more of a character this time around, but he still gets overshadowed by the others. The only relatable thing that came out of his mouth during the entire game was "Eat sh*t"

Villains were a mixed bag. The quality of them deteriorates as the story progresses.But those early hours of the game were the best. 

Game has the replay value of the usual RE games. You unlock stuff and you use it in the new game plus. But you can experience almost everything the game has to offer in one playthrough. I spent a good 9 and half hours trying to explore everything and backtrack. With cutscenes and all the pauses and some restarts. It will come around to 12-13 hours of experience.

Overall, I think this is a good game and it was definitely worth the purchase for me. It had a cool start and an entry but it couldn't keep up its own tempo till the end imo. But still, it was an enjoyable experience. 

I would recommend it. Get it on sale if you can't afford it now.

Review: A Worthy (and Less Stressful) Sequel
Overall Rating: 8.5/10

The Atmosphere & Scares
If you found Resident Evil 7 a bit too intense to handle, this is the game for you. It’s not quite as terrifying as the Baker mansion, but it makes up for it with incredible variety. The shift from horror to action feels more like RE4, which makes it a lot more "fun" to play through without needing to hide under your desk every five minutes.

Combat & Bosses (8/10)
The rogues' gallery in this game is top-tier. From the giant Lady Dimitrescu to the more "industrial" boss fights later on, the encounters are creative and satisfying.

Gameplay Tip: Unlike RE7, your game actually pauses when you open your inventory or map! This is a huge quality-of-life improvement that lets you breathe and plan your next move during a hectic fight.

Story & Characters (9/10)
The strongest part of the game. It does a great job of fleshing out Ethan Winters as a father and sets up high stakes for his daughter, Rose. It feels much more personal than your average "zombie" story.

Shadow of Rose DLC (7/10)
The DLC is a great epilogue, though it’s definitely on the shorter side.

Pros: Great to see the story wrap up; Rose’s powers are a blast to use.

Cons: You can feel a bit too powerful at times, which takes away from the survival horror tension. It goes by very quickly, so savor it while it lasts!

6.5 hours in this game. Before I go into this review (of a game I have not yet completed), I would like to present a recap of my introduction to the series. I've been a big fan of the Resident Evil lore since I was 6 years old (1997) and my big brother showed me how to blast the head of a zombie with a shotgun in the spencer mansion. Didn't understand much at the time, but I knew that the whole thing was kinda creepy with the music, and that the character (Jill) was alone in this big ass house with all of those doors and all the wierd moaning guys walking around with their arms stretched out and reaching towards her. I never got to see my brother complete the game because we didn't have a memory card for our PS1 at the time. Fast forward to 1999, and my brother is playing RE2. And yes, I got to see him complete that masterpiece. I understood most of it and I remember how hard he worked on all those bosses. It was just good times. Again, fast forward to 2006, I've got a PS2, and I've heard many a cool things about RE4. So I bought it for my 15th birthday and started playing that. And I seriously loved it. It took me 1 more year to realize. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I never saw completion of that 1st one! So I got myself a crappy laptop, BUT! I had the opportunities to play RE1, 2 and 3 on that ♥♥♥♥! I got to play the RE1 remake on the gamecube as well! and I got to play RE Zero and Code Veronica. Loved em all! And then... the 5th came... I liked how capcom decided to stick to the 3rd person view. And all in all, the 5th game was a good couch co-op experience! But I felt htat they were going in more of a action, and less horror style in the series. I don't know what they were thinking about the 6th game in the series... I completed it, but I just cringed all the way... and I guess there's alot a RE fans out there who sat with that exact same feeling.

And now, let's get into this. Resident Evil 7... I saw the trailer when it was about to come out. And it looked good. But after the disapointment i felt after the 6th game. I didn't know what to believe. So I thought "man... now they're going for 1st person view? how many changes can be enough?". And you know what? I am so glad I had low expectations for RE7. Because I got to play the demo. It had everything in it. Everything that I now today realize is what capcom really wanted the first Resident Evil to be. Dark cramped hallways where you really do not know what to expect, now in 1st person. So yeah. I bought it and I loved it. Played through it a couple of times. But in the long run, I wasn't to fascinated about the molded. They were scary at first... but they could be so damn boring as well. Now, running around this mysterious village that goes so well into reminding me of how good RE4 was they really made it. THIS!! Resident Evil Village is like Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 4 had a baby. Where there is alot more action and so many monsters to fight, I am satisfied. I really can't wait to play more of this. Village has also taken this type of Farcry approach. Looting means so much more in this game. Hunting as well. Because I have not yet completed this game, I feel like there is not much more for me to say. But! 6.5hrs in it, and I have already lost track of all the jumpscares I've been through! Capcom really ain't losing their touch!

So far I recommend this game to any action/horror fan out there.

THIS REVIEW CONTAINS MILD SPOILERS

Resident Evil: Village is the eighth installment in the Resident Evil franchise and a direct sequel to the 2017 title Resident Evil 7: Biohazard. This survival-horror game takes a majority of its mechanics from previous games in the franchise and blends them together to perfection; some fine tuning of these old mechanics and with the additions of new features — like cooking and the greatly increased catalog of supplies to craft — makes RE: Village feel like one of the most expansive additions to the franchise.

Setting
The setting of a game is imperative to the mood and the feeling of the atmosphere, this is where Resident Evil: Village truly shines. The sense of atmosphere in this game is something I’ve never felt before from a video game; the individual pillars that make up the atmosphere all stand out in their own beautiful way. The level design and art direction of this game is incredible; they achieve this not only through a visual standpoint but also from an auditory perspective. Distant screams and the ringing bells of the castle Demitrescu gives the player a feeling of true involvement in the game. The world feels cold and harsh with gothic-inspired spires and castles, medieval buildings and housing. The level of prestige that the developers have achieved is something of a marvel in the gaming industry.

Graphics
RE: Village shows off the RE engine and the PS5’s graphical capabilities at it’s best. With the power of Capcom’s engine, most people will be able to run the game beautifully whilst still achieving that crispy 60+ fps. This engine allows the display of amazing photorealistic textures in both open and closed environments. The game allows for standard and ultra-wide aspect ratios meaning you won’t be having any black bar trouble if you’re using an ultra-wide monitor. In the settings menu you have a huge assortment of options relating to both performance and visual filters like grain and real time ray tracing. See below for the recommended PC requirements

CPU: Intel Core i7-8700 / AMD Ryzen 5 3600
RAM: 16GB
GPU: Nvidia GeForce GTX 1070 / AMD Radeon RX 5700
DirectX: 12
OS: Windows 10 (64-bit)


Characters

Ethan Winters, the main character of RE:Village might sadly be the dullest and most boring character of the entire franchise. From a character development point of view barely any progress has been made throughout the two games; after the horrors Ethan went through in the last game you’d expect his mentality and the way he reacts to things to be way different. The writing of this game seems to be very inconsistent with different characters; For example, Ethan’s dialogue is flat out boring whilst the few voice lines that The Duke has are extremely descriptive of his character.

The Duke is a merchant from whom you buy supplies, weapon upgrades. After running around the village fighting all sorts of terrifying monsters and exploring for loot you will want to visit The Duke, not only for the sole purpose of buying supplies but he’s also the only friendly face you will run into during the majority of the game. There is just something about the way he talks and his bizarre character design that makes him such an interesting and well crafted character.

Lady Demitrescu has been used as a sort of poster child for this game in all of its marketing and advertising. Sadly her involvement in the game’s story is very short-lived and basically only makes up 20% of the games runtime; This is particularly tragic when you take into consideration that she is probably the most interesting and well written character of the entire game. The intimidating nature of a 2.9 meter tall vampire chasing me through a giant medieval castle really shook me during my playthrough of the game. I found myself longing for that fright again after going past her portion of the game.

8.5 / 10

I'm going to start with the conclusion: This game is not bad. It's fun to play, the story is interesting, the level design is good, and I enjoyed most of what I've experienced so far. However, Steam doesn't have a "meh" or a "yes, BUT" option, so if it's a choice between "yes" or "no", I'm going to go with "no" because it commits the fatal sin of a horror game: Not being scary.

The game looks good, and has decent level design...unfortunately, from what I've seen so far of it (I've just completed the Castle segment, so it's possible later areas are far scarier, but first impressions count for a lot), it might also be the single least scary game in the franchise. Yes, less scary than 5 and 6. (EDIT: I've now beaten the entire game. Wasn't scary at any point.)

After how delightfully freaky Resident Evil 7 was, and how well RE2Make and RE3Make managed to still capture the frightening atmosphere, Village is a huge disappointment. It feels like they're returning to the ill-advised "let's just be a generic shooter" Chris levels from Resident Evil 6 (though of course it's not as bad as 6). 
Honestly, the game reminds me of Resident Evil 6 a lot, and that's...not something you ever want to be reminded of.

Considering the devs have actually said that they intended for it to be less scary than 7, all I can really say there is...well done missing the entire point of a horror franchise? The enemies don't even look that disturbing compared to...basically any other enemy in the series. Morpheus Duvall was scarier. 

The game so far feels like it has only one single trick for being "scary", and that trick is "do something terrible to Ethan's hands." 
Which...after the second time Ethan gets impaled through the hand, it's just silly. Ethan somehow has the durability of Superman in terms of the torture he goes through with little more than a grunt of annoyance.  
By the time his hand gets sliced off, I actually cracked up laughing at how stupid this apparent running gag (running scare?) was. *And then the hand was added to the players inventory*.

I finally beat the game, and I can say that things are better than expected, but...the game has some pretty weird choices in design and story - I might reccomend the game now, but, it's more because there's not a middle option.

I don't think Resident Evil: Village is a *bad* game. I think it's *okay*. There are some issues that really bug me, some little things that make the game frustrating, and the story does very little to really grip me until the end.

Spoiler area:
[spoiler]I got past Lady vampire, puppet gal, and fish guy, and even after the final boss I feel awkward. The first two main "boss" areas, vampire and puppet, feel so out-of-place for a Resident Evil game. Even if the puppet area was interesting because it was 100% puzzle based rather than combat, everything in the story feels slow and plodding up until suddenly you're given tons of exposition through things to read. All the bosses felt very weak and uninteresting (in terms of character), and the only one that succeeded in actually killing me a single time was the fish guy and final boss.[/spoiler]

I still feel like this game is another franchise wearing the skin of Resident Evil. It feels like a thin excuse to introduce more fantastical elements like vampires and hallucinatory creepy moments; which is fine! The thing is though, is that it just barely exists within the realm of Resident Evil. Mold/fungal monsters from Resident Evil 7 felt closer to the series than this - which isn't necessarily a good or bad thing. If the point was to distance themselves from the standard fare of "slow-moving, rotting zombies + the occasional mutant", that's fine. However, everything else surrounding the premise feels a lot weaker than it's predecessors.

Ethan Winters is also, by far, one of the weakest protagonists of the entire franchise up until [spoiler]the end of the game, where his character gets partially deconstructed[/spoiler]. I would prefer meat-headed Chris from Resident Evil 6 to the milquetoast, bland Ethan we get here for a lot of the game. The voice acting for him isn't helping - it's alright, but a lot of the time there's a certain amount of emotion missing (besides pained screaming, of course). On occasions it's witty enough that I crack a smile or emotional enough that I get a bit invested, but he just feels so...weak. It might not be the voice actors fault, maybe the script wasn't fantastic, or maybe direction. Whatever the case, Ethan just is not an interesting character for much of the game...then again, most of the characters aren't very interesting (or funny/campy, as Resident Evil can be sometimes).

If there was a "meh" option, I would use it. I would say that if you want an action survival thriller game, you might like this - if you're looking for an actual action survival *horror*, you will probably be disappointed. I continued playing partially because I couldn't refund by the time I was frustrated with the game, so I may as well see it to the conclusion.

TL;DR - An okay survival shooter with a pretty "meh" story and "meh" characters. Everything is just a lot of "meh" until the end when things come together, so much so that I can only give it a 7/10 at best, and a 5/10 at worst. It's middle of the road. Looks okay, feels okay, but it only gets above "okay" at the end of the game and on repeat playthroughs with toys like unlimited ammo weapons.

Some misconceptions about RE8!

1. “Short game or it’s 8 hours only.” This is straight up WRONG. The game can easily take more than 12 hours to finish. Some even beat it in more than that. The in-game timer literally lies to you, if you’ve played 12 hours, it will tell you that you spent 7 or 8 hours. RE8 has more exploration and side optional in-game content more than any previous RE game. It’s easily one of the longest RE games. It’s got a perfect length for an RE game, not to mention that it has post-game content and good replay value.

2. “It’s not scary.” hella WRONG! This game has different types of horror. From RE7 type of horror, to RE4 (panicking), and to Silent Hill / PT level of horror + other types. In fact, one section in the game has probably the scariest and creepiest moment in the entire franchise.

3. “It’s RE4+RE7.” This is TRUE, but it also has inspirations from almost every RE game. The game feels like it’s a celebration for RE’s 25th anniversary.

I’ve enjoyed my time playing it and I think it’s A MUST BUY for every RE fan or a survival horror fan.

- Easily and by a huge margin, RE8 is the best looking RE game ever. It's INCREDIBLY detailed, well designed and STUNNING to look at.
- Very atmospheric, and its got a lot of variety in that aspect as well.
- Sound design is also the best in the series. The intro is horrifying!
- From the first few hours, you'll quickly notice how big and diverse the game is.
- Levels are intricately crafted, with more ways to explore them. Really liked how the village was structured with more ways to explore and search its houses.
- The game INSANELY nails the interior design of its levels; I find myself stopping every 5 mins or so just to absorb the beauty of it all.
- The game's setting really makes you feel like you're playing in a horror themed amusement park.
- There is clear emphasis on exploration and side content.
- The game allows you to take control of your own pacing at certain sections. It’s not really a linear game. It has more freedom and exploration than previous RE games as I mentioned before, which I liked very much!
- The game does a really good job of changing its intensity from time to time. Presenting different types of horror along the way, mixing them up with action / adventure elements & sequences while still being within its survival horror medium. It’s well balanced, diverse and refreshing.
- RE8 has some of the highest highs in the franchise. When it hits, it hits real good. :D
- NO LOADING TIMES. That's a technical marvel considering the quality of its graphics, level design and performance. RE Engine strikes again!
- Puzzles are fun and rewarding.
- Backtracking here is the most fun and rewarding in all of the RE games.
- Music is top tier.
- The merchant is cool.
- The story is intriguing and thrilling.
- The characters are some of the best in the series. Really interesting, very well acted and fun to watch. Not including Ethan though lol, however he's honestly better this time.

RE7 was, and still is, a masterpiece. Possibly the second best RE ever made, at least in my eyes. And with RE8, they took the legacy of that masterpiece, spat in its face, and then threw it off a bridge. RE8 misses the mark so hard, its actually impressive. The story is AWFUL, and the gameplay feels, as if they couldn't decide on, if they wanted to make RE4, RE5 or RE7, so they just did a bit of all 3, and missed the mark for all 3. The weapon upgrade system is pathetic. Puzzles feel as if they were made for 6 year olds, as in, you can get the right solution, by just spamming random things until it works. Not just that, but some of the puzzles are probably done quicker, if you just spam inputs. And the combat, while technically fun, is just not utilized enough, and its also just too easy. Also, for me personally, a big, psychotic vampire milf, is also just not a valid selling point.

I already mentioned that the story is bad, but its so bad, it had me audibly laugh a few times. Resident Evil has always been B-horror, so a good story was never really the expectation. But the reason why RE4's story worked, and this one does not, is because RE4 realized that its stupid. They leaned on the stupidity, and it felt like laughing with the game, instead of at the game. In RE8, you're just laughing at the game, because it tries to take itself serious, while still having B-horror writing. So it just ends up being cringe, and funny for the wrong reasons. For example, near the end of the game, there is some big plot twist, with a [spoiler]fakeout death of Ethan[/spoiler]. I knew it was going to be a [spoiler]fakeout[/spoiler], the moment it happened, because if that was actually just [spoiler]the end of Ethan[/spoiler], you may have almost thought, that the game's writer did a good job. And then when bro was actually [spoiler]revived a tiny while later[/spoiler], just as expected, I laughed for a good minute. They [spoiler]brought bro back for an entire like 20 minutes[/spoiler], just so they could force a "sad" moment at the very end. Which once again just made me laugh.

The only thing the game did right, was the general atmosphere. The game looks good, and places like the village and the castle were designed well visually. That is, unfortunately, where the pros end. 
Literally the most fun I had in the game, since the horror sections were just NOT scary, and exploration was sub-par at best, were the few sections, where the game just said "♥♥♥♥ it" and started spamming enemies at me. This alone is obviously not good game design, but hey, at least those sections utilized the combat a bit more.

Its also just depressing to see, how well this game did. I know that RE has become a mainstream franchise, and most of these reviews are from the general masses, who wouldn't know good art or good game design, if it jumped at them. But its still sad to see, how easily the masses are satisfied. All it takes, to make a lot of money, are good graphics, and horny baiting deprived people. This games entire marketing was Lady Dimitrescu, and it sold copies faster than RE7 did in its first year. This is even funnier, when you consider, that Lady Dimitrescu was relevant for like the game's first 20%. All this does, is encourage capcom to make even more slop. Resident Evil Village could be best described as a marriage of RE7 and RE4, while the game retains some of the weaker aspects of 7 due to the implementation of first person combat and never quite manages to reach the heights or the exceptional pacing of RE4 - it delivers a fun and interesting hybrid that leans heavily towards the action side of the franchise but still manages to create at least a few of those tense horror moments.

Village continues the story that started in RE7 and delivers a fairly enjoyable even if very over the top, silly and sometimes downright stupid (even by Resident Evil standards) narrative that at times feels like it had perhaps started as another spinoff title but got changed in to a sequel midway development.

Visually the game could be described as inconsistent: Characters, enemies and majority of the interior areas look excellent. However many of the exterior zones look a little dated thanks to the bright lighting that highlights the lower quality assets. Music and sound do their job similar to most RE titles, although this time around nothing really stood out in terms of the soundtrack which is unfortunate but was to be expected as similar to 7 the game relies more on ambient sounds.

Unlike its predecessor Village features a fairly healthy amount of variety when it comes to enemies and bosses while also doing a good job of pacing them so that none of the enemies overstay their welcome for too long.

Unfortunately combat suffers from the inclusion of gun leveling & modding system that works in a similar manner to RE4. Due to it many of the enemies in the early game feel like colossal bullet sponges and as the gunplay is rather weak (poor enemy hit reactions, not enough model deformations to create an illusion of doing much damage) - it doesn't create the best first impression. Fortunately things get a little better once you get a few upgrades and especially in the latter half of the game I started to have a decent amount of fun with the combat.

As mentioned earlier game heavily leans on the action side of the franchise and outside of a couple isolated moments it didn't really manage to create that survival horror atmosphere I was hoping for as you find and are able to craft more than enough ammo to kill everything that moves, literally in this case provided of course that your accuracy is at least a little better than that of stormtroopers.

PC port of the game seems to be a fairly solid one and as expected things ran smoothly on a 3080 + 5900X combination with everything maxed outside of one instance where what seemed to be a memory leak tanked the performance until I restarted the game. Aside from that KB/M feels a little clunky when it comes to menu navigation and unfortunately the PC version does not have a FOV slider which may be a deal breaker to some as the default FOV is rather narrow.

That being said, my playthrough of the game on hardcore difficulty took roughly 12.5 hours and I thoroughly explored every single area. While the replayability of the game may suffer a little from some sections that focus more on spectacle and play out the same way every single time the overall experience was very enjoyable for me and in fact so much so that 
 I'm starting a new playthrough on the Village of Shadows difficulty immediately after.  If you're a fan of the franchise in general or prefer the more action oriented titles from it - I think Village is definitely worth playing.

[h1]Disclaimer[/h1]
Review done after playing the game through on normal and then making through the best part on hardcore with unlocks + doing most of the side content in the main campaign and trying out Mercenaries mode.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
An above average entry to RE series bogged down by a ridiculous lack of FoV options. While it gets compared to both RE7 and RE4 the biggest design problem here is that it doesn’t have a properly focused pacing and instead shifts around from being an action game to being a walking sim Amnesia/Outlast clone.

FoV is locked to 80 degrees and can only be modified through trainers. My 1st playthrough was with the default FoV to ensure I didn’t encounter any bugs related to mods. I’ve experienced weird feelings in my stomach multiple times because of motion sickness. Nothing serious, but I couldn’t play more than a couple hours at a time because of this.
For the 2nd playthrough I’ve increased the FoV to 110 and the game was MUCH more enjoyable. There are some bugs with increased FoV though.

If you don’t care about low FoV then buy it on a discount. Otherwise wait until devs add a way to modify FoV ingame since this is a detrimental lack of feature. People will try to argue that this is an artistic choice to have low FoV, but that’s bullsht – giving players headaches should never be an artistic choice.

I regret not refunding this game on principle and supporting this poor practice against PC players.

[h1]Description[/h1]
Resident Evil Village is a horror action/adventure played from FPP. It’s a direct continuation of the story from RE7, you play as Ethan who will have to rescue his daughter kidnapped by an evil cult that uses mutated monsters to terrorize the titular Village.

There are 3 distinct types of gameplay in this game:
- exploration and puzzles – where you will look around environments to find keys and items to progress
- combat – where you shoot enemies or bosses
- run and hide – where you encounter something you can’t fight and have to run away

Different sections of the game will make use of those 3 gameplay styles in different ways, so every chapter will feel distinct. One area may focus on puzzles and hiding, while another may be filled with combat and running away.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[b]+ Scalable graphics[/b]
This game should run in low detail on a dated hardware.

[b]+ Amount of content[/b]
While main campaign will take you only about 10h to finish, the unlockables, challenges and game modes will provide some replayability. Compared to the 0 replayability of RE7 this is a huge step forward, but still not as good as RE4.

[b]+ Mercenary[/b]
The classic time-kill mode returns with some new features and is IMO the best edition of Mercenaries mode ever made for an RE game. You go through several areas while collecting random abilities like in a roguelike-like and upgrade your stuff in between zones to try and clear everything as fast as possible.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[b]- FoV[/b]
As explained – it’s locked to 80 degrees which is scandalous for a PC game and ruins a lot of the gameplay.

[b]- Audio[/b]
The game is very quiet and has very limited volume options. That wouldn’t be a serious problem, but it also locks your system volume when it’s in focus. In order to change system volume you have to alt-tab out of the game. This does not happen with the console version – it let’s you change system volume on consoles no problem during gameplay. Again – lack of a feature for PC.

[b]- Story[/b]
This game does a seriously fked up thing at the start that will piss off people invested in the established lore. The game only explains things 30 minutes before the end in a huge info dump that arguably places this entry as THE MOST IMPORTANT game in the entire RE franchise to date. And the lengths of plot convenience they had to go to to achieve that level of past story integration results in absurd plot holes that simply destroy any interest I ever had in the story from this point onward. I believe this is due to the criticism that RE7 received with it’s story being poorly incorporated to the series and writers decided to overcompensate to the point that it seems like they just trolled entire established fanbase.

I didn’t like RE7’s story, but I absolutely HATE the story of RE8.

[b]- Pacing[/b]
There are 2 major areas in the game, which are fun to play because they have the right amount of combat and exploration. I am not a fan of Outlast and games that use it’s formula and RE8 has several segments dedicated to the run’n’hide style of gameplay, which kills pacing and isn’t fun or scary. Just tedious.

[b]- Quality/performance[/b]
Looks similar to RE7, but performs notably worse.

[b]- No colorblind options[/b]
The lack of this I could excuse if the game didn't have mechanics that are tied to color. Health display has no clear distinction for your HP state other than color for example.
Thanks to comment section for pointing this out as I am not color blind and don't typically notice these things.

[h1]Lowdown[/h1]
I believe Capcom should leave RE story behind and create a proper anthology-style horror series with different creatures like vampires, mummies, ghosts and the like. It’s clear that they don’t care about past games’ lore. They also need to take more care with PC ports and required features.

Above average game, but not recommended due to technical limitations.

Capcom did it, this is officially my favorite Resident Evil game. Almost every problem i had with RE7 is fixed in this entry, and it was just a complete blast to play through. My expectations were certainly blown away here.
Score: 9/10 

The good:
- Excellent level design offers more exploration than any other RE game.
- Extremely good bosses. I thought the bosses in RE7 were pretty good, but they pale in comparison to the bosses in this game.
- Many appreciated quality-of-life improvements from the previous entry. I think the inclusion of the merchant was brilliant.
- Great combat! Many cool weapons that feel very satisfying, and a lot of enemy variety. So much better than RE7 in this regard.
- The narrative style is really improved upon since RE7, and i actually felt kind of emotional towards the end.

The bad:
- One level towards the end has too much backtracking, and can be really difficult to navigate.
- Carrying over from RE7, I'm still not the biggest fan of Ethan, however i think he seems to act more natural in this entry than in RE7. Not much they could do here, as they would need to change Ethan's character to fix the underlying issues.
- As always for any RE game, the dialouge could be better written.

So rather than going on about a certain lady who's height is a little above average I'm going to give a little review of what I think so far.

The most simple way to explain the game is to describe it as RE4, RE7 and Bloodborne's love child. It is more action packed than 7, but less than 4 yet it keeps the great things about 4 and 7 while leaving the bad things out. It's not as much of a survival horror as 7 or the classics but it is enough to definitely warrant the name. 

There's plenty of backtracking and resource management but the item boxes and limited saves are gone, unless limited saves are unlocked in a harder difficulty than hardcore. So far playing on hardcore hasn't been too difficult except for one section relatively early which feels like a horde chase. If you can get through that you should be fine.

While the game itself doesn't feel overly "Resident Evil"ish it does do a fantastic job with its horror aesthetic being real gothic in nature set in an old town and Romanian castle with more side areas. Coming from an absolute die hard RE fan I'm really enjoying it and think it tops 7 with overall enjoyment. My only negative is I wish the other side areas had as much detail as the castle but if my only complaint is that I want more then I guess that speaks for the game.

Runs like a dream too.

Overall It's a strong recommend for any RE fan or even for newcomers as it does come with a recap of 7's story as this game is set I think 3ish years in the future with 7's main characters. If your unsure, check out the demo.

Is this game "Bad"? No. Not really. 

It's not exactly amazing either. When I play an RE game I want to feel scared, or tense. am I low on ammo? Do I need to conserve ammo? etc? This almost never happens in this game.. and it the game plays out more like a Disney multi part carnival ride than anything.. 

Don't get me wrong, some parts feel like a game, but they are small parts, and almost never like you're in trouble, or on the brink of being in a bad situation. 

You walk through a set, that feels like a set too... you know.. set the mood.. that's the opening with the village..

The whole cinematic scene as you're running down the tunnels, with that big dude with the hammer jumping down, and hitting you off feels exactly like one of those super hero 3D carnival rides you go on on Disney world with those 3D glasses.. 

Then the Castle... same pattern, that makes it dull, and not scary.

No enemies, then an unkillable enemy chases, so you run. Then they stop chasing you,, and that is your trigger that you know little minions will be needing to be dealt with very soon, after dispatching those, you get into the "boss" fight, which you magically figure out how to kill them at that point by sheer dumb luck, Then you go back to the main area of the castle with no enemies, buy stuff, rinse repeat...

There are almost never enemies that just show up that you gotta plan for, It's all so equally scripted that you know what's coming.. You know when it's safe, and you know when you can use items like the land mines and you're not wasting it.

Compare it to gamesl ike RE 1, 2, and others. You never knew what was coming, there was never a pattern, and you never knew when a perfect time to use an item was. Would it be a waste to use this grenade on this group of enemies? Or will there be a bigger group later and no other grenades to find? as an example. Every shot you took, and every item you used was a risk.

That's what made it scary, and thrilling.

--------------

The castle is even worse for the disney ride attraction. You might even have a gun, but you never feel threatened in MOST cases, just like those disney ride thriller attractoins. You never feel like you're on the verge of dieing, or running close to no ammunition, etc.

It's just...

Village attraction, then walk down a scary tunnel to transition into the castle portion of the ride, walk around a beautiful entrance, and go up the stairs to the chase scene, and into the dungeons for another kill the mutants attraction, before you wrap back around to the voyeur area, and onto the next attraction!

It's literally setup exactly like a multi part disney ride thriller..

---------------

Upgrading weapons: 

The upgrading in this game is honestly 99% of the time useless.. 

- The amount of shots it takes to down an enemy with a pistol upgraded, is the same, unless its fully upgraded. You MIGHT get a slightly higher chance to blow the head immediately, but I don't even know. 

And even when you get it fully upgraded and it takes 1 maybe 2 less shots... well you get so much ammo anyway it doesn't matter.. This is playing on Standard Mode. Hardcore is much harder, but still, that just makes the upgrading even less useful. 

- Larger Clip, and Reload speed is again useless.. we're talking 0.2 percent quicker here per upgrade.. At no point is that going be useful. Until again, it's fully upgraded, then it'll slightly help, but with how the maps are setup, and how slow the enemies are in most cases.. You can just kite them, group them up and throw a pipe bomb. Or shoot them down the numerous hallways in the game from afar, even with the pistol. 

- The better weapons you can find laying around, are equal in power to the weapons you just stupidly wasted money on upgrading.. Infact I found the next best pistol, and shotgun before I fully upgraded my previous ones, and they are better in every way.... Making my money I used upgrading entirely waste of money I could of used on bullets instead just so I could spam through the game even faster. 

- This also means the money to buy parts for said weapons is also entirely useless. 

------------

The food buffs are also pretty useless. Except maybe the health ones for Hardcore mode. 

---------------

This means don't waste your money on upgrading anything ever, until you get the best weapon in the game. Then blow your money on upgrading it, with the customizable parts.

Finished the story already and I have to say this is my favourite RE game so far. The story keeps you engaged, and though it gets crazy at some point, it really makes you feel interested on what's going on and it also explains a lot of huge things that so far haven't been explained on the series.

As I said in my past review, I feel like this game is significantly easier than other RE games, since you get a bunch of ammo and pretty powerful weapons. In fact, I got to a certain point where I had 200 pistol ammo and a bunch of ammo for other weapons, so I started wasting them and even that wasn't enough.

Puzzles are not hard at all, but they take time to complete, which is a way to balance things. I personally like more difficult puzzles rather than long ones, but it's up to your taste.
The audiovisual style of the game is one of its strongest points. Of course, it looks insane, even though it can't really get to the level of "new gen" games, but something pretty remarkable are the facial animations, which are crafted carefully. The audio is insanely good, I can notice it right away, it's much better than RE2 Remake which was already at its best.

Once you finish the game, you get points based on your performance that you can spend in some extra gamemodes, like Mercenaries, which is insanely good and fun. You can also buy some other stuff like character and weapon models, which have insane details on them.

I'd definitely recommend this game to everyone. I've seen some comments saying "69USD for a 10 hour game?" but it took me around 12 hours to beat the game without exploring everything and I haven't even touched Mercenaries and other gamemodes that much.

So yeah RE8, very flawed but iam glad it exists. (Spoiler free)

The bad stuff:

First up my biggest issue. There are gameplots that would win oscars if they where movies and then there are Resident Evil games, where the writing is so bad its hard to belive the writer passed elementary school. Every character talks like how an toddler would imagine grown up people would talk, where the finest ladys and the smartest engineers cuss like 13 year old Ellie from the last of us and where the main protagonist is fighting to contain his tourett so he doesnt have to say ♥♥♥♥ every 3 min. And the story it self has some very cool ideas, but the execution can definitly be not credidit to the wirters but the enviormental artis and gameplay designers. Most twist can ben seen miles aways and those that cant are so rediciulous that it feel like the devs had no idea how to impress the players at that point. The characters you ironically care the most about in this game are the ones that talk the least, Rose and Chris. English isnt my first language, it isnt even my second, but even i had to laugh at some of the more serious moments with terrible delivery.
Problem is the gameplay is driven by the plot this time, unlike RE2 remake, which means that no matter how dumb it sounds you have to do it. Player expression is relativly low in this title, where even the action centric RE3 remake had more optional weapon parts to find trough puzzels than this one. Here you either buy them with money you will have in overflux for most of the game or they are placed right in front of you, before or after boss fights. There are just 4 keys in the entire game (!) with the last one being found in the last area, so there are just 3 for 90% of the game.
Where the FPS gameplay of the first game worked perfectly for it due to making you feel powerless, its terrible for making you feel powerful in RE8 something the devs clearly tried to accomplish after the first third. Its way to cluncy with the best tacting beeing to tank most hits with blocking and than shoot people right in the face for most of the time. The core loop clearly wasnt designed for rapid motion and crowds of enemys in re7 so its baffling to see that they just adopted it for this game. Even the devs of their giant insperation (RE4) did know it better 16 years ago, thats why they switched the camera from an slow, RE 2 esque but non static cam to an over the shoulder perspective. All that time and the RE team didnt catch up to Shinji Mikami´s core understanding of game design.

With all the negative critique being handled now, heres the good stuff:

RE survival horror core gameplay loop is still barley contested even 25 years later. The enemy ai wouldnt work if you didnt have to make every bullet count (something a certain part clearly showed *cough*). It makes you more attached to very bullet you find or craft and therefore way more methodical than you tipical fast paced COD or Titanfall. You dont just find a new gun you earned it by surviving everything that has come before and even though its much easier to upgrade them this time around, its still your personal gun at the end of the day. Even though only the cheapest horror ideas has landed for me they contributed toan atmosphere where something that can kill you could always be around the next cornor and even i an horror veteran have to admit that some of the horror stuff was genious (dont think i meant you cliché puppet section).
Where most of the RE4 inspired stuff felt like a cheap way to say "look guys we made that game everyone liked haha you will like this one too", the Heisenberg area, the (intentionally or not) most "RE" area was amazing. Visuals and survival/horror aspects where more than just on point and the level design was sooo good. This is the main reason why i will remeber the game and its sad that only a few reviewers talked about it. Guys it worth powering trough the game for that area alone.
Bossfights, while beeing pretty bland in takling them due to the basic combat system, are some of the best in the series, with even one completly optional Bossfight you will only see if you also want to collect the optional tresuares. It really helps that most of the Bosses are introduced in the first hours so you know whats comming. Unlike in re7 where you had to fight Jack so often you stoped caring and dozed of mentally.
Knowing whats comming from the beging made the game more predictable but it also helped the pacing enormiously, something re4 struggled with big time in my oppinion. You always know what you have to do and how much is still comming so you can balance how you talking it your own way. Unlike Re4 where new areas randomly plopped out of the ground like weed when you really just wanted to push forward.
Character, enviormental and art design in generall is in a league of it own. While you proabaly have seen most of it in differnt media, putting it all together so oganically and making it look so good is something i have barely seen before. The castle and the heisenberg area especially are jawdropping at times, not only because of lady dimitrescu. The fine details in the castles halls make you feel like you are really there and the diviersity in things to so makes t feel like an small journey. The only criticism i have here is that the daughter design was really of for me. Its like they they modeld sexy women and rmembered its a horror game afterwards so they added some blod to there models and gave them insect powers. Horror icons like Junji itos "Tomie" have shown how to darw attractive yet disturbing female character design. (Maybe its time for a Juni ito capcom cross over?).

To summ up now:

Yes RE8 is far from beeing the best title in the series and its kind of a shame that they are going back to its action routes even though they where just praised for going back to RE´s horror routes but Re8 was defintly worth the time i spend with it, something i cant say for many games ive played. While the survival horror gameplay especially the Heisenberg part, was good fun most of the time, the writing and story let the game down overall. Especially the ending left a sour taste in my mouth, not because of what happend but by how it got delivered. Visiting the different houses and and soaking up their atmospheres is definitifly unique to this game.

Deeply disappointing. I only played 90 minutes and refunded. (I edited it down below for my 10 hour review, after rebuying the game on a sale. My opinion barely changed, honestly.)

Headsup for VERY early spoilers.

The game opens up with a decent horror sequence... where they murder the reason that 7 even happened. Mia, a character we may have hoped to finally get to know is dead. They showed us that her and Ethan never actually worked on their relationship ever, and argued with the maturity of teenagers. Thanks, I really wanted to see her die immediately, Shinji. So in this game you're saving Ethan's literal Infant. This doesn't interest me, because I don't connect with characters on a human level; they're just characters to me. This infant doesn't show any character traits to me, so as far as I'm concerned, I'm just running in to rescue a piece of a cardboard. Mia at least had some character, but... well, she's been thrown to the side for the entire duration of this game because of Chris. Somewhere between the last game and the current game, Chris decided that he's going to be a whole new character now with absolutely no development leading up to this. Some people like this plot point, I call it lazy writing.

Speaking of lazy writing, let's talk about how you're in a village in Romania, and everyone speaks perfect english and ALSO has no accent. Capcom, could you really not afford Romanian voice actors? The game literally screams at you that it's not in America but NEVER shows you that it's not in America apart from the castle, as far as I can tell. The characters will all scream at you that you're American with Midwestern and northern accents. This is a serious mood killer for me. If your theme isn't onpoint, then your horror isn't worth anything to me.

Next I wanna talk about fear. RE7 had a singular scary moment for me, and that was the Guest House in the very beginning. Other than that, I loved it for what it was; a love letter to grindhouse horror. Direct references to old 1980s movies with blood and gore, chainsaw duels, humor-filled tense moments, and the best voice acting in the series. RE8 doesn't have anything. It's just not scary to me, and it's not particularly... horror. It has horror tropes up the ass, though! Talking dolls, vampires, werewolves... and atrociously directed drama.

This is the first game I have ever played where characters are very obviously using drama tools that you'd learn in highschool drama class. They angle themselves so that their heads can simply turn towards the audience or the actors, so that their bodies are on display. The presentation of each dramatic moment feels like someone is acting in a highschool play to me. RE7 did this too, but not NEARLY as obviously as Village.

The dialogue is also very poorly worded and awkward. It's hard to get across, but if you've ever watched poorly translated anime, that's what you're getting here. It feels like a teenager wrote everything, I mean, it's just so incredibly amateur.

Resident Evil 7 was a wonderful game, that I'm going to go back and play now. 90 minutes of this ruined any hope I had in capcom, because this is just... this is the furthest thing from what I was expecting, or wanted. They doubled down on the camp, and I just wanted the camp to stay the same and see a bit more of Ethan's story. Instead they killed my girlfriend, threw a piece of cardboard into a castle and said "Have fun, buddy".

Edit: I bought it again on a sale. The gameplay was super fun. The story does not get better. It felt very rushed, and it had a lot of contradictions. I cannot honestly recommend this game, no matter how much I'd like to. Get it on sale; it will never be worth it off a sale.

The default FoV sucks, and you can't change it in the game, so the only option at the moment is to use a mod, or maybe there will be a more permanent solution made by modders in the future. The point is that it's 2021, and Capcom apparently never tested out the game on a computer monitor, because if they had, they would've realized that when you're sitting a little over a foot away from the screen, an FoV this low will make most people sick.

Along with the lack of an FoV slider, there's also a vignette (that black stuff all around the edges of the screen) that can't be disabled without a mod. It's an annoying post-processing effect that doesn't really add much of anything to the game, and just makes the low FoV that much worse.

There are fortunately a lot of other options in the settings menu. Unfortunately, menu navigation is awful, and if you're someone with a monitor that supports any resolution higher than 1080p, you get to experience the joys of cycling through each individual resolution on the way to the one you want, waiting for the game to be rendered in each of those resolutions, and then clicking the "keep changes" button on the little window that pops up. So a basic setting that should take a few seconds to change ends up taking a minute or 2.

The game itself is also much more focused on action this time around. As the producer of the game revealed shortly before release, they toned down on the horror since RE7, which is a shame, because the action was the absolute worst aspect of RE7, and remains the worst aspect of this game. The game is visually stunning, but everything involving player input feels like it belongs in a game released 20 or so years ago.

But I suppose it doesn't matter that the action in this action game sucks, because everybody's gonna give the big vampire lady positive reviews.

The environments and graphics are nothing short of breathtaking and the werewolf creatures at the village portion in the beginning legitimately terrified me. The unusual way that they move, the crazy detail on their teeth, eyes, face, tattered clothes, etc. The effects are also crazy good and everything that came off as a bit janky in RE7 is now fixed here. Even better the cutscenes and action set pieces are incredible and legitimately made my jaw drop. They don't feel like those cheesy "run away or die" QTE scenes you'll see in video games, they feel more detailed and fresher than that. Your hands no longer look ultra glossy and instead are textured with hair follicles and realistic looking veins. Hair physics are very natural and I haven't noticed any clipping at all on the clothing worn by NPCS. The puzzles are much more fleshed out instead of the focus on environment puzzle solving and light puzzles in RE7. They're not incredibly difficult to solve, but they are more creative than RE7. This game just has an incredible amount of polish and I'm really quite shocked. My only complaint would be that I'd like to see some FOV support in the future.

2. Good mechanics, fun to play. 
Just like re7 this version of resident evil is also in first person perspective and it's good for that. The main reason I kept playing and playing this game is because of it's fun gameplay. The guns have personality in it, like an example a freaking rocket pistol which isn't that op but it's fun to use!

3. Guns sounds powerful.
In re7  we get a realistic feel to our guns with a shotgun shell inside the barrel clanking  around when you run. In this game the realistic feel of the guns from re 7 is transferred here and it just sounds and looks powerful. They also added some bits where you can hear cartridges fall down in the floor whenever you  fire your gun. The smokes coming out of the gun just makes it fun to use, the more powerful it is the bigger the smoke is! Also guns emit light though it's just flashes. Overall they made guns great at this game just like in re7 but with more variation.

4.  Werewolves! Vampires! Fishboy?
Unlike re7. re8 has a lot of enemy diversity. In re7 we have the baker family and the molds (with slightly altered variants) but in re8 not only the bosses are unique they also have unique mini bosses which is cool in my opinion. There are a lot of enemy types though some of which acts somewhat the same, it doesn't feel like they just copy and pasted the model, they actually put some thoughts into their character designs.

5. Character Designs are GREAT!
Talking about character designs all of it fits it's purpose. A vampire that owns a castle? Make her tall and a white dress contrast to being a vampire she doesn't have bloodstains in her dress saying that she is a composed  woman and she conceals herself from the villagers. A doll maker that can control doll? Why not make her connected to her doll so in that way she can hide her insecurities. A merman that is the opposite of beautiful but admirable? Make him a grotesque beast that needs love even though he really can't understand why he is not chosen. An literal cowboy that uses magnetic power? Make him one of the coolest characters you've ever seen in resident evil and creates experiments that no one in their right mind would sign up for. Overall I could commend them all, the 3 daughters of Alcina, the creations of heisenberg, lycans and more.

6. RESIDENT EVIL BOSS FIGHTS!!!!
It is pretty standard for resident evil to have boss fights, and this game delivers! The battle with alcina herself is pretty self explanatory. The battle with Donna is pretty much a hide and seek. The battle  with Morou is about patience. The battle with Heisenberg is like a mecha battle and it's in a goodway. The battle with Miranda is pretty much the normal resident evil fight. 

7. Replay?
Just like the older games before this, re8 gives it a lot of replay value. Whenever you finish a challenge you get points which can unlocks perks in the game, like infinite ammo and other stuff. You can get lost in hours and hours of gameplay and still comback for more, either trying your new gun or just abusing enemies in casual difficulty on a new game plus.

All in all the game is splendid! It is a good continuation to 7 story wise delivering answers to unanswered questions in the past games. It having one of the most enjoyable gun mechanics, and giving guns the power they should have feels great. The game doesn't shy on enemy diversity with them having  good designs. And the classic resident evil boss fights is just great. If you're going to buy this game it is fun to play, you can  invest lots of hour and still enjoy it, overall I recommend it!

I picked it up at full price and refunded it, and recently got it as a thank you gift, so here I am again. My initial impressions feel  justified; I wasn’t sold on the opening horde mode, and the narrative contrivance still irritates me. Despite being absolutely at lycan’s mercy the magical timer runs out and they just leave Ethan as it’s time for walkies or something. It was bad design when RE4 and RE5 did it, and it’ll be just as bad when the next game does it. Climbing out of this nadir of horror though, RE8 has some great sections; sadly, outnumbered by the low ones. The high point for me is Castle Dimetrescu and House Beneviento. After that it falls apart in a similar manner to RE7, so all in all, RE8 is a seriously flawed game with two spectacular moments. I can’t recommend it at £25 (current 50% discount) let alone £50, when 2/3 of the game is boring, banal gunplay.  The “free” multiplayer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ doesn’t count in the price tag, as it’s never even getting installed. 

There’s the summary but here’s why.

One of the biggest wastes of potential is the NPCs you encounter early on in the Village. Minor spoiler ahead but one NPC seems to be set up to provide a connection to village, but then dies as a contrivance for Ethan to deliver a stilted “WHY!?” speech while he’s in danger of a protracted painful death. I actually laughed at his response, as it’s completely overblown for someone, we met less than ten minutes ago whose death is completely moronic, and easily survivable.

The reason why Capcom focused all the advertising on Lady Dimetrescu isn’t the reasons bulging out of her dress. She’s the only boss with any level of personality that’s marketable. The daughters of Dimetrescu with their limited screentime as easily dispatched mini-bosses for Castle Dimetrescu outshine the last two bosses in personality. While the RE2RM Tyrant felt like a force of nature, and the RE3RM Nemesis felt like a feral animal; Lady Dimetrescu comes across as more focused and refined. As though running through the halls of Castle Dimetrescu is beneath her status as a noble. Her reactions to her daughter’s deaths adds a layer the others don’t have (or need), but it’s obvious she cares for her daughters, and it adds a parent vs parent motif. The Doll Maker boss is great but couldn’t be advertised as it would ruin the levels atmosphere, and House Beneviento’s got enough trouble being overwhelmed by dumbass mechanical choices. Namely the magical disappearance of your weapons, and Ethan’s movement speed noticeably reducing for no reason. I feel like they could’ve got away with one of the mechanical shifts but together they combined into an irritation I couldn’t shake despite an otherwise fantastically spooky and surreal area; one that can be favourably compared to earlier Silent Hill games. I was left feeling as though the game would’ve worked better ditching the horde mode survival entry point, instead having Ethan fleeing to House Beneviento, before heading to Castle Dimetrescu; at this point the previously mentioned NPC could die as we’ve had time to get to know them, and maybe add a reason for Ethan’s overly dramatic speech. It’d be more coherent narratively for the game. One where you gain your gear at a steadier pace before confronting the last two lords….

Speaking of the final lords they’re little more than rote monster-villains. It’s as this point that the combat ramps up to ridiculous levels, and Heisenberg’s stronghold sees RE8 become a really bad FPS. One other section feels like a werewolf reskin for CoD zombie mode. Finally, while the last part of RE7 ramped up the combat towards the end at least it had the dignity to not feature a combat rig with an unlimited ammo mini-gun and chainsaw…

In case you’re unfamiliar with the game, Resident Evil Village is the 8th game in the Resident Evil main series of games, which has its origins on the Playstation 1 in 1996. The game is a survival horror game in which the player must acquire methods of traversing past a number of enemies. The game features an arsenal of weapons, and was made in a first person perspective, which is the only other game in the series to be in this perspective apart from Resident Evil 7: Biohazard, which came out in 2017.



	Resident Evil Village is a direct continuation of 7, featuring the same characters, but in a wildly different environment, three years after the events of the previous game. The games are functionally similar as well, however, a noticeable difference in Village is the presence of a merchant, and the ability to upgrade your arsenal. This mechanic was derived from an earlier game in the series with quiet fan adoration even today- Resident Evil 4, which came out on the Playstation 2 in 2005. 



	The similarities between both 7 and 4 in Resident Evil Village have caused a number of people to make the association that Village is essentially these two games combined; and while this may be a fair statement- I believe that it leaves the full depth of the game unrealized. Village is a fully standalone point in the series, and seems to not only build from the previous titles in the series, but immensely improve upon them. This is a game newcomers to Resident Evil, as well as diehard fans can both greatly enjoy, even if you haven’t played 7- the game offers a recap of the events, and a refresher of the mechanics.



	Village offers simply stunning visuals, and features a number of diverse areas for the player to explore at their own pace. One of the greatest achievements for this game was keeping the pacing fresh. By dispersing segments of the game from puzzle based and more relaxed segments, to tense combat oriented spaces, and explorative free roam, Resident Evil Village manages to find that perfect distribution and offers a wealth of variety. However- that is not to say that every piece of this game is without criticism. 



	Probably the biggest gripe people have with this game is the enemy repetition. There have been a number of comparisons to the vampire thralls in this game and the molded from the previous title, 7. Which is a very fair criticism. However- there is one seemingly minor difference between these two games that makes these encounters much more different for the player: the presence of currency. 



	When you disperse an enemy in Resident Evil Village, they don’t simply take your ammo and go away, instead- they drop currency, which allows you to purchase items, or upgrade your weapons. This small change subsides the repetition of killing quite a few of the same enemy, as it makes each kill feel more like an investment, or accomplishment.



	The boss fights in this game are absolutely stunning, and each one offers a horrifying encounter to the player- while still being very manageable. The castle looming over the player at nearly every part of the game is such an iconic backdrop, and is a more than impressive representation of the purely magical environment the player traverses. Each building, each item placement feels so painstakingly and tedious handcrafted, and taking that extra time to look around the rooms you encounter will almost always certainly be rewarded.



	There is really not a whole lot that I could say that would concretely discourage you from getting this game if you’re already looking at it- but a wealth of things I could say that might interest you in it. This is by far the most solid addition to the franchise since 4, and if you loved the classic survival horrors of Resident Evil, I have no doubt you’ll find something to love in this game.

This is rather be called Resident Evil: "Theme park" than "village". To the level of how I wonder I still recommended this game. I don't think it has problems but the idea they pulled from other RE games is a bit... underdeveloped.

It has collecting-based puzzle-solving from RE1, 2, and 3 but the area the game gives is not large enough to make players feel like they have found the key items. It rather feels like the game doesn't want you to spend too much time on each zone.

It has Mr.x and Nemesis type of hunter boss that follows you throughout the area but the area itself is not as well planned out as RE2. They might make you jump a couple of times but hardly has a stressful situation like in RE2 that you have to plan out your route and sometimes even improvise your escape route not to stuck in a death trap with Mr.X and lickers in the same room.

It has a scary situation with puzzle-solving but the solution and route are always the same (Play the game and you will know where I am talking about.) It feels great the first time and becomes a drag after that.

It has RE4 kind of mindless shooty shooty bang bang moment. But there are too few moments about that.

Other than that, It feels like the game is on a rail rollercoaster that tries so hard not to make you stuck and challenge you with real obstacles and drive you through each area as fast as possible.

Then again, just like the director said that they want to make a "Theme park ride style of Resident Evil." How can you blame them?

This game feels like a medium pie of pizza that has each slice different toppings. It has almost every main RE series idea in it (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and even Revelations.) 10 hours of playtime can't fit this many ideas inside it and make it feel substantial for everyone. The part you like ends too fast but the part you don't like also doesn't overstay it welcomes. When people say "This resident evil take it back to its root." there is a fact that should be clarified. Resident Evil series has two roots. survival horror RE, and Action RE. While the implementation of Classic RE1 is not fleshed out. The fleshed-out part of Action RE4 feels lacking in quantity.

The mercenaries mode also has a weird design that kinda reminded me of
a raid mode rather than real mercenaries modes like RE4, 5, and 6.  It's not about survival and improvisation. It's about optimizing your route and not breaking your combos. Which older RE mercenaries mode is about keeping yourself alive first and then try to keep your combo going because enemies are out hunting for you while Village is waiting for you to find them.

Ethan is also a boring character. While the plot is good (for a goofy type of RE game.) Ethan is not made for this caliber of silliness. At least the ending gives him a high note to brings the curtain down.

Then Why I still recommended this game? Let go back to the quote "Theme park ride style of Resident Evil".  While this game feels lacking to be either RE1 or RE4 type of games. If you look at it as a theme park, It actually impressively represent itself as a grand nostalgic ride. It missing the point that making RE1 and RE4 in the term of design but it also in really high quality you could just play and enjoy it. [h1]Resident Evil Village is Truly Amazing[/h1]
It's honestly crazy how good the Resident Evil games have become. Each entry feels special in its own way, yet they all consistently manage to deliver a captivating story. Village is definitely one of those standout titles. When it first released, I was genuinely blown away by the graphics and especially the art direction. Even today, the atmosphere and visual design still hold up incredibly well.

[h1]Story[/h1]
The story is exceptional once again. It builds directly on the strong foundation set by RE7 and answers many of the lingering questions from that game. At the same time, it gives the main protagonist a meaningful and satisfying conclusion. The storytelling is handled extremely well and ties everything together in a powerful way.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
At its core, the gameplay is a fairly straightforward first-person shooter, but it works perfectly for what the game is trying to do. Interestingly, the slightly clunky shooting mechanics and overall combat actually make the experience feel unique rather than frustrating. Somehow it adds tension and personality to every encounter, which makes the gameplay genuinely enjoyable.

[h1]Performance[/h1]
Performance is top-notch, which is exactly what you'd expect from the RE Engine. The game runs incredibly smoothly, and the graphics still look better than some of the AAA titles I've played even in 2026.

[h1]Overall[/h1]
Resident Evil Village is another fantastic entry in Capcom's legendary franchise. With every release, they continue to refine the RE Engine while still delivering strong storytelling and memorable single-player experiences. This is a truly special game and an easy recommendation.
