This game puts off vibes of Resident Evil 4 and Bioshock 1. There's a lot of combat for a mainline RE game, but it's not so frequent that the game ever really feels like it boils down to a mindless shooting gallery. Playing at a normal pace, doing some exploring but not checking every nook and cranny on Standard difficulty you're looking at a 10 - 12  hour experience, and unless you start out on Hardcore mode you're probably going to want to do a replay either on VotS or Hardcore mode if anything just to go back through and get all of the unique items, but I think Hardcore is the most balanced difficulty mode personally. If you do your first playthrough on Hardcore you're probably gonna extend your campaign by another 2 hours at least just by needing to scrounge around for ammo and heals. 

Atmosphere across the board is really solid, less so than RE7 but atmosphere was a primary focus of that game and the explorative combat is the focus of Village. Still the castle is gorgeous and feels like a completely real place, the village is spooky at first but does a good job of being a central point between the 4 main outer areas. The other two locations not already spoiled through trailers and the demos I'll keep secret, but one of them is your worst nightmare and one of them is just really theatrical and cool. There's one with windmills that's meh to me, but only relative to the rest of the game being so good. 

The combat is very similar to the first one, but you have more movement and larger areas to play around in, with massive buffs you can get from the hunting and cooking system. It's balanced enough that it never feels like you're helpless, but that also takes away from the anxiety combat had in the first game. That could be seen as a pro or a con depending on why you play RE, I really like both honestly.

Overall this game is a must play for long time fans of the Resident Evil franchise. If you really liked Bioshock this also could be right up your ally. The graphics are gorgeous, the story and world building is consistent with the previous game and there's plenty of content to get your moneys worth out of it at most price points for most people I think.

[h1]Actual review[/h1]
Now that I've played through the story mode, i can finally give you my thoughts on Resident Evil: Village. [i][b]TL;DR:[/b] Fantastic title with and authentic setting and plot; I would go as far as to say that this is the definition of what a RE game should be. Must-have for franchise fans and highly recommended for everyone else.[/i]
[h1]Story (No Spoilers)[/h1]
With the internet going "Tall lady this, tall lady that", it's easy to overlook the story aspect of this game, mistaking it for something it isn't. Sure, you do get chased by her for a while, but that's about it. She's but an obstacle in your way, and in classic RE fashion, all obstacles must be overcome. The story runs deep, and having played the previous installment, RE7, will give you a great foundation for understanding this one. That is, however, not necessary, as the game offers a recap of all the major events that led up to where you are at the start of the campaign. The files, pictures, specimens and many other hints in the environment will sometimes give answers to the player's ever growing list of questions, which helps strengthen the narrative. The story in this game is a definite strong point.
[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The gameplay loop is great. You find new weapons, new recipes and new types of enemies rather often. The game is not long enough for it to become repetitive, which is a good thing. The duke, which is inspired by the merchant from RE4, makes an appearance here and is willing to trade you all sorts of goods, for a fair price of course. This blends exceptionally well with the fact that there are all sorts of rewards/treasures to be gained, all of which can be sold  to him. The control scheme is good, with most of the binds being what you would normally expect to find in a modern game. I can't say much for the controller side of things, but Capcom has a good history of making intuitive controls for consoles, so i would assume the game can be enjoyed that way too. The crafting system is okay and does its job, requiring you to gain materials and use them to craft whatever it is you desire. 
[h1]Performance[/h1]
This game is well optimized. On my RTX 2070, it was staying at around 160-170 fps in the earlier part of the game, although the larger areas were seeing lower fps, at around 120. This was with all the settings cranked to max and [i]no raytracing[/i].You might think that a 50 fps drop is huge, but the drops were never instantaneous, so transitioning from a smaller, inside area, to the larger outside areas was smooth every single time. During my playthrough, I've encountered zero bugs, glitches or crashes, which was a great relief considering the experience I've had with some other recent releases. 

[u][i]Resident Evil Village is a great successor to RE7, both in terms of story and gameplay. For long time fans of the franchise this is basically a modern game that somehow manages to give a very familiar feeling, to us, the players[/i].[/u]
[h1]Overall: 10/10, A classic in disguise[/h1]

[h1] A Step in the Right Direction [/h1]
I initially gave this game a thumbs down because of its rough start. I was about 2 hours in, yet I was still stuck on the first wave based encounter. However, after completing the game on Hard, I have to say, this new RE entry is as Resident Evil as it gets. It's not perfect and it definitely has some flaws, but I am definitely revisiting this game for another play through.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] My Original Impression [/h1]
I'll be honest, I hated the beginning of this game. When I first played RE7, I was excited to see Capcom return Resident Evil to its roots. The game was a lot more slow paced than the RE titles we received before it, yet it made the survival horror and mystery aspect that much more intriguing. So when I tried to play RE8 the same way as RE7, I was left with a VERY bitter taste in my mouth. Enemies are much more fast paced here, and they EAT bullets on Hard (at least in the beginning). I was very disappointed to see my headshots doing nothing, and was amazed at how much ammo the game expected me to waste. I kept dying for two hours during the first encounter because I was trying my best to conserve ammo and only get headshots.

As it turns out, ammo is not something you need to worry much about, even on Hard. You can find it, craft it and buy it pretty frequently. What was throwing me off was how much the game wants you to play aggressively. It's not just the Village aspect that this game will remind you of RE4, it's also the gameplay (more on this in a sec). In general though, this change in gameplay from RE7 to RE8 + the extremely low FoV + poor PC controls (will go over these last two later) is what pushed me to originally give this game a thumbs down.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] Combat [/h1]
The combat in this game is so much more satisfying than RE7. Where before you didn't really feel the impact of your guns shooting big blobs of nothing, it's in RE8 where you will see enemies react to the way you shoot them. Do enough damage and you'll stagger them. Pump enough headshot damage and their heads will blow right off. What I don't really like is how much headshot damage it initially takes to stagger an enemy on Hard. After some upgrades, this is less of a problem, but it will definitely throw people off, especially if they expect it to be exactly like RE4 where a headshot is an instant stun. If you're an RE vet, do yourself a favor and go in with an open mind to combat. Don't expect it to be exactly like RE4 or RE7. It really comes into its own style.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] FoV [/h1]
When I first booted the game up I went straight to the settings to find no FoV option. It's 2021, seriously? That's fine though, right?... No. The way enemies move in this game is pretty erratic. So much that your FoV being low makes it hard to get clean shots. Capcom, I don't know what you were smoking when you thought a lower FoV made games scarier, but you're wrong, it doesn't. If I wanted to play the game like I was looking through a telescope I wouldn't play Resident Evil, yet here we are... Just as an example, I was walking through the opening area and thought some kind of cutscene had started to play since it looked like a house was being zoomed in on... Turns out that was just me walking towards it. So off to Nexus mods I went and downloaded a mod for FoV. RIP console players.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] Controls [/h1]
I don't know what went wrong with the PC's controls for this game, but they feel VERY clunky. It feels so bad to use a mouse and keyboard to the point that inputs become unresponsive and you will stand still randomly even when you are holding forward. And no, it's not my keyboard since this doesn't happen on any other game and the keyboard is a month old. Even aiming with a mouse feels horrible. I had to plug in an Xbox controller and right away the game felt 100 times better. How does an FPS feel WORSE to aim on a mouse than a controller? I never had this issue with the PC version of Resident Evil 7.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Aside from the issues mentioned, I am overall very satisfied with this game. There are a lot of parallels to RE4, which makes this game really shine. The story is great, the combat is great, and all the puzzles/mysteries really give this game that Resident Evil vibe that the classics are known for. Please do yourself a favor and play this game with an open mind to combat, an FoV mod, and if possible a gamepad. The game will feel right at home and hopefully you can have a blast with it!

If you're cool with that & it simply makes you happy to know there's more to go? Go ahead & dive in.

After finishing the game once: I'm in love. Will every RE fan also love it? No, absolutely not. This absolutely feels like Capcom trying to take some of RE4 & blend it with some RE7. I honestly think it works. If you liked the gameplay of 7, no reason to suspect you would be disappointed here. Yet to try out The Mercenaries but happy it's back. Plenty of replayability both in difficulty levels & things to unlock for further runs such as yes, infinite ammo weapons. Same purchase model as the 2 & 3 remake. Complete in game challenges, use that currency.

I do disagree with some reviews that this game doesn't stick the landing. Though that one of course is more personal taste. Hard for me to talk about the story at the moment in a non spoiler way. 7 I felt meh on that third act. Not so much here. 

So final word is this: If you enjoy most of this series, 7 included, I think you'll be happy with your purchase if you did so now. If you're on the fence, probably wait for a sale & you'll be happier. I'm a fanboy of this series, so I'm relatively easy to please. Trying to think of people that are harder to please, especially other fans, I feel you have to enjoy the combat of 7, not be turned off by first person, not be turned off by monster choices, & be okay with marketing possibly leading you to believe that certain characters the internet loves, are so not the central plot of the game. If that is one of your big selling points, absolutely wait on a discount. Even if you go through RE at a slower pace, sure, you could spend plenty more time than I did with Lady D & her daughters. But in the grand scheme of things, while happy, even I wanted more in that department. 

So once more, if your gut says yes, go for it. If you're on the fence, wait. I recommended it regardless, only trying to help those that could regret it at the current price point & possibly hate the game at this price point vs enjoying it later for a different price.

You take the shoes as Ethan Winters from Resident Evil 7, trying to rescue your daughter from a woman named Mother Miranda and her children. I've become a huge fan of resident evil games, after being able to experience such a masterpiece. When you have 43 hrs in a single player game you can most likely have an idea to express what sort of bliss you've had in it. I've played RE7 fully and finished all of it's difficulties, so when i got the whole bundle of both RE7 and RE8 i thought why not beat RE8 on it's every difficulty, thus i started it. Played the game over 4 times and did not regret any second of it. Usually these "titles" or you could say beginning of my reviews are quit nonsense, therefore i will cut the chase!

Environment:
I've played quite a lot of Horror games and others that are just story driven, but only a few could compete with RE8. Such an immersive environment, everything you can see you can touch it (not literally, but you get the point). Every boss fight was a blast, i did not want them to end, it was really enjoyable, because of the surroundings. Capcom did not just randomly put bosses nor normal monsters in places and said "yep that sounds good and we will keep it there" no, they worked a lot on the environment to make things twice more enjoyable. Everything in the game makes you like you are experiencing it. Since i am from eastern Europe country and since the game is based in Romania i felt in love with it even more, because for some reason interior of the village houses remind me of soviet union furniture, carpets and etc (if your country is ex soviet then you will know what im trying to say)

"colorfulness"
colorfulness i mean in terms a lot of abilities, modifications, craftable items, biomes, guns and etc. You will be surprised how much this game has to offer. there're tons of guns for a single player game and parts of these weapons to make them even more powerful. After you've finished the game you obtain extra content from where you can gain infinity ammo on any gun you wont, however you should have that gun fully upgraded and modified, which actually adds more to the game and it does not get boring! There are a few "biomes" too, first being Castle, Village, House that is close to a waterfall (dont know how to put it properly), swamp, factory and the last boss dwelling (which i am not aware what is the name of) All of these have their own types of bosses, monsters, hidden guns that can be unlocked, crystals being hidden into walls and more (i think i should have said it in environment but anyway!). I would keep going but this should be enough, otherwise not even a few people will read the review.

Boss fights:
As mentioned, i loved all the bosses and mini-bosses along with their surroundings. However, what i did not like was the places you have to work around. It is firm and you dont have much places to move. Sometimes you get stuck into animations as well, as you are being hit by a boss, and that makes it even worse. However (again), if you somehow (its not as hard) gain enough skill to run around and time the attacks to dodge/block them its no problem.

Difficulties:
There are 4 difficulties. All of them obviously different from each other completely. We have: Casual, Normal, Hardcore and village of shadow. The last one will be unlocked after you've finished the game on normal or hardcore (not sure about casual). People say that you should play the game on hardcore to fully immerse yourself, but i would have to disagree. To fully enjoy its glory you have to play the game on normal, get to know all the places, and then try to do hardcore Otherwise you would end up dying a lot and it would not be fun at all. On hardcore it took at least 15-13 handgun bullets to kill  monster but on Village of shadow it took me over 20 bullets to kill them. Easy solution for this, play the game on normal again get all the modifications and upgrades on revolver then buy infinity bullets and that is it. With that gun, especially while you have infinity ammo, you can kill everyone (pretty much, but not bosses) in a single hit. also after you've finished the game save it and load a new one, which will make all the previous progress to transfer into the new game.

Mercenaries: 
People are saying that RE games should not have such gamemodes and nobody cares about these, but i would say that is a wrong assumption. I enjoyed it quite a lot, even tho i have not actually finished it fully. Such game modes are a lot of fun, but RE resistance was truly bad and i agree. After you've finished the main story multiple times and you dont know what else to do you can always get into mercenaries and blast some monsters there. They even added mini-bosses in there which makes things even more fun! also if you get good score you may even unlock lightsaber and other guns.

To sum up, this game is the best resident evil game i have ever played. As many fans say it is basically a mix of all the RE mixed together, which i agree on. I highly recommend you check this game out! and give it a try. I may have missed a few things but its because i cant write a lot here nor will anybody read a bible about RE8, so... Have not mentioned bad scenarios because there was basically non.
P.S Voice acting is fokin' amazing.

An absolutely fantastic game and might I say it's an improvement over RE7 in all aspects. The game reminds you of Resident Evil 4 but somehow manages to do more and better despite being on the shorter side (took me 13 hours to finish along with moderate exploration).

The graphics are absolutely breathtaking due to its photorealism and the game isn't even taxing, even if you turn Ray Tracing on. (Though there is a frame drop issue that capcom needs to address.)

The biggest complaint that I've heard that Village is more action oriented, but I think this is false. Sure, the game has way more combat and action set pieces than Biohazard, but the game has some well-done horror elements and scenes and managed to terrify me more than Biohazard did.

Along with the Campaign, you get access to the Merceneries mode which is a fan-favourite horde mode and adds a lot of replayability value to the game. (The campaign itself has many challenges and collectibles so the entire package can be revisited to tackle them.)

Overall it's a fantastic game, though a bit overpriced at $79.

I've always reserved special spots for the Resident Evil series in my heart.

Being one of the longest running horror franchise, it has crafted many great moments, characters and stories. Whilst RE8 can be played as a standalone game, having played the previous games in the franchise or at the very least, RE7 will enrich your experience by providing you with a much more complete story. 

The moment I completed RE8, I'm very confident that this is a very solid 9 out of 10 and is easily one of the best game in 2021. Let's break it down!

In terms of horror, RE8 is not as scary as RE7. However, it makes up by providing you with a more unique and larger environments to explore. There are several areas in the game such as the celler and the doll house which really creeped me out. The sense of dread and helplessness is further enhanced by the fact that there are 0 jump scares throughout the game and always low ammo count. 

In the doll house area specifically, the game even removed your weapons and introduced outlast-like gameplay mechanic. I must say this area is the scariest area I've experienced in games in recent years. 

The action oriented gameplay ramped up in the second half of the game but it is highly polished and tells a great story that even answered some of my long time questions about the characters and settings. 

Upon completion, you will unlock the mercenary mode offers additional challenges and as RE traditions go, replayability is high with unlockable infinite ammo weapons intended for higher difficulties. 

Overall, I'm very satisfied with RE8 and I'm looking forward to the eventual sequel.
